Defining General Ledger Accounts

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Corporate/GL_Account_Definition_Corp.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Corporate/GL_Account_Definition_Corp.htm

Defining General Ledger Accounts

Use the G/L Account Definition (Corporate form to define general ledger accounts. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To define general ledger accounts:

  1. Enter the Account code to distribute.

  2. Select the Prefix Values that you want to attach to the beginning of the G/L account code.

  3. Select the Suffix Values that you want to append to the end of G/L account code.

  4. Enter the Segment Delimiter to use. Valid delimiters are: *, - , ., or ! If you leave the field blank, there will be no mark or spaces between the account number and any prefix or suffix.

  5. Enter any Prefix/Suffix Overrides:

a. Select the Override When Prefix/Suffix term.
b. Enter the is equal to term.
— —
c. Enter the Replace with value to append to the account number instead.
— —
d. Click Save.
— —
  1. Enter any Account Value Overrides:
a. Select the When Field Equals term.
b. Enter the is equal to term.
— —
c. Enter the Replace Account # With value to append to the account number instead.
— —
  1. Click Save.

Defining Periods for Your General Ledger

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Corporate/GL_Periods_Corp.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Corporate/GL_Periods_Corp.htm

Defining Periods for Your General Ledger

Use the G/L Periods form to define the periods for your general ledger.

To define periods for your general ledger:

  1. Enter the Period code, ensuring that it conforms to the format used by your general ledger.

  2. Enter a Description of this G/L period.

  3. Enter the calendar Year.

  4. Enter the Month or G/L period within the year.

  5. Enter the External G/L Period to be passed to an external general ledger.

  6. Click Save.

Defining Global G/L Accounts

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Corporate/Global_GL_Account_Definition_Corp.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Corporate/Global_GL_Account_Definition_Corp.htm

Defining Global G/L Accounts

Use the Global G/L Account Definition (Corporate) form to define global G/L accounts.

To define global G/L accounts:

  1. Select the Prefix Values that you want to attach to the beginning of G/L account codes that allow prefixes.

  2. Select the Suffix Values that you want to append to the end of G/L account codes that allow suffixes.

  3. Enter the Segment Delimiter to use. Valid delimiters are: *, - , ., or ! If you leave the field blank, there will be no mark or spaces between the account number and any prefix or suffix.

  4. Enter the Code Acct Segment No, which is the segment where the “core” account number is found.

  5. Enter any Account Value Overrides:

a. Select the When Field Equals term.
b. Enter the is equal to term.
— —
c. Enter the Replace Account # With value to append to the account number instead.
— —
  1. Click Save.

Defining Codes for Corporate Payroll Accounts

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Corporate/Payroll_Account_Codes_Corp.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Corporate/Payroll_Account_Codes_Corp.htm

Defining Codes for Corporate Payroll Accounts

Use the Payroll Account Codes form to define codes for your corporate payroll accounts.

To define codes for corporate payroll accounts:

  1. Enter the unique payroll Account number.

  2. Enter a short Account Name, such as Payroll Tax Expense or FICA Liability.

  3. Select Prefix/Suffix Allowed if the G/L account code can take prefixes and suffixes using the variables set up in the account definitions.

  4. Click Save.

Working with 1099 Forms

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/1099%20Reports.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/1099 Reports.htm

Working with 1099 Forms

Use this form to open, reprint, or delete 1099 forms that were printed using the Printing Employee 1099 Formsoption. When you print an employee 1099 form using the Printing Employee 1099 Forms option, the output file generates a corresponding entry here. These files will auto-delete after 60 days.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To access this form, click Work Centers. In the Work Centers|Tax section, click 1099 Processing, then click 1099 Reports.

To use this form:

  1. In the Show Reports Dated On or After field, enter the appropriate date.

  2. Select the appropriate Sort By option:

  • Report Date

  • Report Title

  • User ID

The 1099 Tax Reports panel displays information matching the attributes selected above. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: Click Next Page to go to the next page. If you cannot find your entry, click the

[Image: screenshot]

icon to refresh the window.

Note: Note the following:

  • Each time a file is generated by selecting Print from the Printing Employee 1099 Formsoption, this section produces a newly generated file.

  • Historical reports remain in this section. Every entry in this section reflects the following:

  • Date and time the process was run.

  • The Report Title reflects the form type, year, employer, and client information and sort option.

  • The User ID and User Name who initiated the process, and the report title that reflects the Form Type - Year - ER or Client information.

  • Click Delete to remove all output and control records related to that report.

  • Click Reprint to rerun the report with the original Payroll/Parameters provided.

Note: Note: If the report parameters change, the resulting report could be different.

Building the 941 Quarterly Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/941-Quarterly-Report.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/941-Quarterly-Report.htm

Building the 941 Quarterly Report

Use the 941 Quarterly report option to build a CSV file (no on screen report) to report income taxes, Social Security tax, or Medicare tax withheld from employee’s paychecks. It also reports Schedule R credit for the disabled or elderly. You can also define the format for Schedule B (income tax due on interest and dividends earned). An icon is available for downloading the file.

Note: Note: The wages and tax withholding for a 1099 contractor will not be included in the Employer 941 Quarterly Report for any employer who is withholding federal or state income taxes from a 1099 contractor as defined under the Work tab of the Employee Details form. Evidently, such wages and tax withholding for a 1099 contractor will also not appear in Employer 941 Register, Employer 941 Schedule R, 941 File Processing download etc.

An expandable History section is available for you to see historical reports.

To build the 941 Quarterly report:

  1. In the Work Centers panel, select Quarterly Tax Processing > Quarterly Tax Reports > 941 Quarterly Report.

  2. In Build 941 Files By, select one of the following options:

  • Employer -Generates a 941 and Schedule B and totals by employer

  • All Clients - Generates a 941 and Schedule B for every client that is associated with a specified employer

  • Client - Generates an individual 941 and Schedule B for individual clients

  • Schedule R

  1. If you selected Employer or All Clients, provide the following parameters for the report:

  • Employer

  • Tax Year

  • Tax Quarter

  • Schedule B Format (Standard or Post COVID-19)

  1. If you selected Client, provide the following parameters for the report:

  • Client

  • Employer

  • Tax Year

  • Tax Quarter

  • Schedule B Format (Standard or Post COVID-19)

  1. If you selected Schedule R, provide the following parameters for the report:

  • Employer

  • Tax Year

  • Tax Quarter

  1. Click Build. If errors occur, fix them and then rebuild the download.

  2. When the process is complete, click Close to return to the 941 Quarterly Report page. The system sends you an email notification that the process competed successfully.

  3. Click the Download 941 link to download the file.

Note: Note: On, the 941 Quarterly Report built either by Employer, All Clients, a specific Client or with Schedule R breakout will not include wages and tax withholdings for any W-8 employee. A W-8 employee in PrismHR is one who according to the Employee Details form, under Tax tab, under the Federal Tax Filing section has the Form W8 Filed field checked. This change will also affect the following:

  • Employer 941 Register

  • Employer 941 Schedule R

  • 941 File Processing

To view historical reports:

  1. Expand the 941 File History section.

  2. Select the Tax Year, Quarter, and 941 Type for the reports you want to see. The list of reports is shown as in the following example.

  3. To download a report, click the link in the Report column.

[Image: screenshot]

Adding or Updating an Employee 1099 Record

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Add-Update-1099.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Add-Update-1099.htm

Adding or Updating an Employee 1099 Record

Use the Add/Update 1099 form to add or update an employee’s 1099 record.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To add or update an employee 1099:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, select Tax > 1099 Processing > 1099 Processes > Add/Update Employee 1099.

  2. In the Add/Update Employee 1099 section, complete these fields as required.

Field — Description

Employer — The Employer ID for whom to generate 1099 data.

SBEA Entity — An optional field that is available only when Build W2s from Client Federal Tax Registers is checked in the Global Configuration form. This is a client federal entity who represents a client of your organization that is included in SBEA reporting.

Employee — The employee whose record is being added or updated. If a 1099 record is found for the specified employer ID and employee ID, the record is displayed so that you can make the necessary changes. If a 1099 record is not found for the specified employer ID and employee ID, the system prompts you to specify whether to add a 1099 record for that employee. Click Yes or No.

Tax Year — The tax year for which to generate 1099 data. Typically this is the year before the current year.

1099 Manually Updated — When the record is manually updated. The system selects this option when you make manual changes to the record.

  1. In the Federal Form 1099 Misc section, add or change these fields as necessary.

Field — Description

Recipient’s TIN — The recipient’s tax ID number.

Recipient’s Name — The recipient’s name.

Employee Address — The employee’s street address.

City, State & Zip — The employee’s city, state, and zip code.

Non-employee Compensation — Whether the record was manually updated. The system selects this option when you make manual changes to the record.

Federal Income Tax Withheld — The amount of federal income tax withheld.

Federal Income Taxable — The amount of taxable federal income.

State Tax Withheld — The amount of state tax withheld.

State Income — The amount of state income.

State/Payer’s State No. — The number for the state or payer.

  1. Click Save and then Yes when prompted to continue. When the data is saved, the system writes these changes to the status change log and flags the 1099 as manually updated. See Viewing the 1099 Record Change Log

  2. Click Delete to delete the record.

Note: Note: From tax year 2024, for an employee who is a 1099 contractor and has federal or state income tax withheld by the employer, the employee 1099 Build process in PrismHR will include the following information apart from Non-Employee Compensation:

  • Federal Income Tax Withheld

  • Federal Income Taxable

  • State Tax Withheld

  • State Income Taxable

Generating the ADP Quarterly Tax Download

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/ADP-Quarterly-Tax-Download.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/ADP-Quarterly-Tax-Download.htm

Generating the ADP Quarterly Tax Download

This form generates a quarterly fixed width file similar to the MasterTax RTS file, only with slight variations in the format.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To generate a quarterly report:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click Tax > Quarterly Tax Processing > 3rd-Party Exports > ADP Quarterly Export.

  2. Select a Tax Year.

  3. Select a Tax Quarter.

  4. Click Build to generate a report for download. A dialog box opens showing steps to process this file. This process may take time so wait for a status update that the build has completed.

  5. Click Close, then click Download ADP Quarterly Tax Export file to download a .txt file to your local system.

Running the Benefit Plan W-2 Reporting Status Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Benefit-Plan-W2-Report.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Benefit-Plan-W2-Report.htm

Running the Benefit Plan W-2 Reporting Status Report

This report provides information about the W-2 reporting status for your organization’s benefit plans. You specify whether the report includes only plans that are reported, only plans that are not reported, or both benefit plans that are reported and those that are not reported

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To run the Benefit Plan W-2 Reporting Status report:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click Tax > W-2 Processing > W-2 Reporting > W-2 Setup Reports > Benefit Plan W-2 Reporting Status.

  2. In Is Benefit Plan Reported on W2? select one of the following options:

  • Yes - The report includes only benefit plans that are reported.

  • No - The report includes only benefit plans that are not reported.

  • Both - The report includes both benefit plans that are reported and those that are not reported.

  1. Click Process to run the report. The system displays the report. You can click the XLS link to download the report.

Building the Massachusetts (CSV) Download

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Building%20the%20Massachusetts%20(CSV)%20Report.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Building the Massachusetts (CSV) Report.htm

Building the Massachusetts (CSV) Download

Use the Massachusetts (CSV) form to generate unemployment insurance reports in CSV (comm-separated value) format. The reports are used to electronically transmit both employer tax data and employee wage data, eliminating the need to print paper reports.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access this form and build a report:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click Tax > Quarterly Tax Processing > Government Exports > Client Reporting > Massachusetts (CSV).

  2. Complete these fields as required:

In this field — Enter this

Report Year — The year for the download.

Quarter — The quarter for the download. Defaults to the previous quarter based on the current date.

Client ID — Leave blank to select all clients or click the link to make a selection from the Select Client list. The list shows the Client ID, Client Name, Legal Name, Service Type, Employer, and Status. You can filter the list by Client ID or Client Name, Service Type, Status, or Employer. To close the list, click Done.

  1. Click Run. If errors occur, fix them and then rebuild the download.

  2. Click Close when the process is complete to return to the Massachusetts (CSV) page.

  3. Click the Download link to download the file.

Clearing Employee SSN Verification Reporting Dates

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Clear%20Employee%20SSN%20Verification%20Reporting%20Dates.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Clear Employee SSN Verification Reporting Dates.htm

Clearing Employee SSN Verification Reporting Dates

Use this process to reset the Employment Verification Service (EVS) reporting dates. These Employee SSN Verification Reporting Dates are used when processing the EVS download file that is generated from the W-2 work center (W-2 Processing > W-2 Processes > Create Employee SSN Verification Download). If a reporting date is entered in the Employment Verification Service (EVS) reporting date, the employee is not shown on the EVS download. This process resets the EVS reporting dates so that the employees will be shown on the EVS download file.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, in the Work Centers panel, under the heading Complianceclick on New Hire and Termination Reporting. Then under the heading Reporting Date Overrides click on Clear Employee SSN Verification Reporting Dates.

To clear employee SSN verification reporting dates:

  1. Enter Starting EVS Report Date which is a mandatory date field. Please enter the date from which you want to clear the employee SSN Verification reporting.

  2. Enter Ending EVS Report Date which is a mandatory date field. Please enter the date upto which you want to clear the employee SSN Verification reporting.

  3. Company ID is an optional free text field. Leave it blank to select all clients.

  4. Click Process. A progress window opens that shows the number of records read and the number of records cleared and notifies you when the process is complete. The Close and Report buttons remain disabled while the report is being generated.

  5. Click Close to close the window.

  6. Click Report to display the Job Control Status Report window.

  7. In the Job Control Status Report window, click the XLS link to download the report.

Running Client Tax Register Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Client%20Tax%20Register%20Report.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Client Tax Register Report.htm

Running Client Tax Register Report

Use the Client Tax Register Report form to generate a report that produces a detailed or summary output of client-reported tax amounts. This informational report includes gross pay, taxable hours, gross taxable, and tax withheld amounts.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access this form, clickReports menu. Under Employer|Report, click Client Tax Register Report.

To generate the Client Tax Register Report:

  1. Complete the following fields:
Field Name Description
Starting Date Enter or select the starting date of the reporting period.
Ending Date Enter or select the ending date of the reporting period.
Client ID This field is not mandatory. Leave this field blank to select allclients. If you want to run this report for specific clients, enter the Client IDs here or click the Client ID link and select them from the Select Clients list. The corresponding Client Name displays.
Tax Authority This field is not mandatory. Leave this field blank to select all tax authorities. If you want to run this report for specific tax authorities, enter the tax authority IDs here or click the Tax Authority link and select them from the Select Tax Authority ID list. The corresponding Tax Authority Name displays. (This entry could be a state, county, or city tax authority.)
Tax Identifier This field is not mandatory. Leave this field blank to report all tax types. If you want to run this report for specific tax identifiers, enter the tax identifier IDs here or click the Tax Identifier link and select them from the Select Tax Identifier ID list. The corresponding Tax Identifier Name displays.
And Other Tax Auth = This field is not mandatory. If you enter a tax authority code here it will not display on the report, but only records that have this tax authority will be included in the report. Enter the tax authority IDs here or click the And Other Tax Auth = link and select them from the Select Tax Authority ID list. The corresponding Tax Authority Name displays. (This entry could be a state, county, or city tax authority.)
And Other Tax ID = This field is not mandatory. If you enter a tax identifier ID here it will not display on the report, but only records that have this tax identifier ID are included in the report. Enter the tax identifier IDs here or click the And Other Tax ID = link and select them from the Select Tax Identifier ID list. The corresponding Tax Identifier Name displays.
Include Client SUI Report Only Register This field is not mandatory. By default, this box is disabled. Select this field if you want to include client SUI report only register.
Report Type Select the type of report that you want to generate from the following options: - Summary (Default) - Detail
  • Summary (Default)
  • Detail

  1. Click Run to generate the report on-screen.

  2. Click Clear to clear this form at any time.

  3. Click Close to close this form at any time.

Report Outputs

The ClientTax Register Report displays the following columns:

Report Name Columns
Summary Report - Client ID - Auth ID - Tax Authority Name - Tax ID - Tax Description - Gross Pay - Taxable Hours - Gross Taxable - Tax Withheld - EE Count - Totals (per Client ID) - Grand Totals
  • Client ID
  • Auth ID
  • Tax Authority Name
  • Tax ID
  • Tax Description
  • Gross Pay
  • Taxable Hours
  • Gross Taxable
  • Tax Withheld
  • EE Count
  • Totals (per Client ID)
  • Grand Totals | Detail Report | Client ID - Auth ID - Tax Authority Name - Tax ID - Tax Description - Employee Name - SSN: You can control whether to display SSN numbers by enabling the SHOWSSNFORTAX custom feature code on the System Parameters form and setting up a Conversion User in the Account Management Roles panel on the Users form. - Gross Pay - Taxable Hours - Gross Taxable - Tax Withheld - Totals (per Tax ID) - Grand Totals |
  • Auth ID
  • Tax Authority Name

Cloning Employer Details

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Clone%20Employer%20Detail.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Clone Employer Detail.htm

Cloning Employer Details

Use this form to copy an existing Employer Detail record to a new Employer Detail Record. This is especially helpful for customers in the entertainment industry where each new show is a separate PEO clientwith a corresponding employer record that is identical to the other employers in the system. Using this form, you can avoid setting up all the state information for a new employer. You can just clone it from an existing employer.

Note: Note: Client Access Group security is not enabled on this form.

To access this form, click the Back Office menu. Under Employer|Action, click Clone Employer Detail.

To clone an existing employer record to a new employer:

  1. Complete the following fields:

Field Name — Description

From Employer ID — Enter the existing Employer ID from whom you want to clone the employer record, or click the From Employer ID hyperlink and select it from the Select Employer dialog box. If you enter an employer ID that does not exist, you will receive an error stating Record is not on file EMPLOYER.MASTER.

New Employer ID — Enter the Employer ID of the new employer. If you enter an employer ID that already exists, you will receive an error stating Employer ID already exists.

New Employer Name — Enter the name of the new employer

  1. Click Clone to copy the existing employer details to the new employer. All information on the original employer record will clone to the new employer except Init History. This is because you would not want to clone the init history from prior years for another employer as this is a new employer.

  2. Click Clear to clear this form at any time.

The following information of the existing employer will be copied to the new employer:

  • Address, City, State, Zip

  • Telephone

  • G/L Setup

  • Federal Deposit Method

  • Certified PEO

  • Tax Contact Information

  • State Tax ID Numbers

  • Heading

  • Masked SSN on Form W-2s. (If Exists)

  • Common Pay Agent

  • Invoice Information Maintenance

  • Local Tax Identifiers

  • SBEA W2/1099 Name Control

Creating Employee W-2C Forms

Use Create Employee W-2C Forms to create the electronic W-2c form data that needs to be uploaded to federal, state, and local government agencies. If the system detects any errors that will prevent processing, it displays an error message when you select the option. Click OK to dismiss the message and then resolve the errors. Click Pre-Process Error Report to download errors if any before you create the W-2c forms.

To create employee W-2c form data:

  1. Open the Work Centers menu and select Work Centers|Tax > W-2 Processing.

  2. Under W-2 Processes, select Create Employee W-2C Forms.

  3. Complete the form.

Option Description
Clear options: Select one of the following options: - Do not clear existing forms - This is the default option. This option provides the following two options: - Only create W-2C forms for employees without an existing W-2C record. This is the default option. - Overwrite W-2C form if values are different. Any Form W-2c included in an EFW2C export file that is not in a status of regenerate or canceled will be skipped. - Clear all existing forms - This option will delete all W2-C records. Any Form W-2c included in an EFW2C export file that is not in a status of regenerate or canceled will be skipped. This process does not create W2-C automatically after clearing. You will need to create W2-C records separately.
  • Do not clear existing forms - This is the default option. This option provides the following two options:
  • Only create W-2C forms for employees without an existing W-2C record. This is the default option.
  • Overwrite W-2C form if values are different. Any Form W-2c included in an EFW2C export file that is not in a status of regenerate or canceled will be skipped.
  • Clear all existing forms - This option will delete all W2-C records. Any Form W-2c included in an EFW2C export file that is not in a status of regenerate or canceled will be skipped. This process does not create W2-C automatically after clearing. You will need to create W2-C records separately. | Tax Year | Select the year for which to generate W-2c data. Typically, this is the year before the current year. | | Employer ID | Select one or more Employer IDs for whom to generate W-2c data. You will need to enter at least one Employer ID to Create Forms. | | Load All Employers | Click this option to process W-2c data for all employers. | | Employee ID | This field is optional. Select one or more employees for whom to generate W-2c data. You can enter them manually in the Employee table or click the Upload Employees button to import them from a list. - If you have full access to the Create Employee W-2C Forms form, you will be able to see this button and use it to upload employees. Use the File Upload dialog box to upload your list of employees for whom you need to generate Form W-2cs. Click the Add Files button to select the import file from your system. Click the File Upload button to upload the employers and employees. - When uploading an employee list containing an invalid Employer ID / Employee ID combination, the Employee ID is not added to the Employee Table but is noted on the upload Transaction Report as “Failing” the upload process. - When uploading a list containing a valid Employer ID/ Employee ID combination where the Employer ID had not yet been added to the Employer Table, the upload process adds both the Employer ID and the Employee ID to their respective tables. - When uploading a list containing a valid Employer ID/ Employee ID combination where the Employer ID has already been added to the Employer Table, the upload process adds only the Employee ID to its respective table. - Your import file should: - be a csv or text-tab-delimited file - have two columns namely: - Employee ID - Employer ID - not contain more than 500 employees - If you have inquiry access to the Create Employee W-2C Forms form, you will be able to see this button but you cannot use it. |

Click the File Upload button to upload the employers and employees.

  • When uploading a list containing a valid Employer ID/ Employee ID combination where the Employer ID had not yet been added to the Employer Table, the upload process adds both the Employer ID and the Employee ID to their respective tables.

Updates to Form W-2 build

The State Income Tax Account Number on the employee Form W-2 will now be pulled from the Client Details form or the Employer Details form based on the tax deduction code, unless an override exists on the Employer Details form on the SIT Rpt Entity field for that state under the State Tax section.

The State Income Tax Account Number on the employee Form W-2 will be:

  • Client State Tax ID when:

  • Tax deduction code set to report at Client Level and ER Details, State is set to -select- or Client

  • Tax deduction code NOT set to report at Client Level, but ER Details, State is set to Client

  • Employer State Tax ID:

  • Tax deduction code NOT set to report at Client Level and ER Details, State is set to -select- or Employer

  • Tax deduction code set to report at Client Level, but ER Details, State is set to Employer

Note: If the State Tax ID is not available on the corresponding reporting entity, the Form W-2 will not be built, and an error will appear in the W2 Error Report stating State Employer ID not found for Client # for State XX OR State Employer ID not found for Employer for State XX

Creating Payroll Tax Summary Export Files

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Create-Payroll-Tax-Summary-Export.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Create-Payroll-Tax-Summary-Export.htm

Creating Payroll Tax Summary Export Files

The MasterTax PTS (Payroll Tax Summary) File Build transmits data from the TAX.JOURNAL file to MasterTax. MasterTax is a third party vendor that handles the tax payments for many service providers.

This file is typically generated once per day and uploaded to MasterTax. There are multiple versions of the PTS file. There are also SBEA and Non-SBEA versions of this file, depending on the settings on the MasterTax Interface Parameter form. A process lock on the TAX.JOURNAL file prevents multiple users from running this file concurrently.

In the past, PTS files contained deleted data. PTS files created out of PrismHR archive that data for 45 days, and then it is deleted.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To build the PTS file:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click MasterTax Processing. > File Exports > Mastertax PTS File Build.

  2. Select Build File by:

  • All Clients and Employers – When this option is selected, the Employer and Client options are disabled.

  • Employer – Click the Employer link and select an employer from the list that displays.

  • Client – Click the Client link and select a client from the list that displays. You can search by Client ID/Name, Service Type, Employer, or Status.

  • Re-process Previous File – Select a file from the drop-down. This regenerates data that was contained on that file using updated parameters from the MasterTax Interface Parameters form.

  1. Click Build to generate the PTS file. A progress window opens and displays process steps and a date/time stamp. When the build is finished, it automatically downloads to a local drive and appears on the PTS File History list.

If a PTS file is already being generated, a process lock is applied to prevent others from attempting builds. You can clear the lock, but it should be cleared only if the process is frozen.

  1. Check the MasterTax version by expanding the Configuration Information panel.

  2. Check the PTS File History for a build status. The system displays a time and date stamp, the user who ran the build, and what the file name is.

  3. Click a File Name link to download that file. You can also view an audit report by clicking View next to one of the file names.

Creating the Employee SSN Verification Service Download

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Creating-The-Employee-SSN-Verification-Service-Download.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Creating-The-Employee-SSN-Verification-Service-Download.htm

Creating the Employee SSN Verification Service Download

The Employee SSN Verification Service Download builds an electronic file that you can upload to the Social Security Number Verification Service, which verifies names and SSNs before generating Employee W-2s. It also updates employee records with an Eligibility Verification System (EVS) date. Once this process is complete, you are notified with a pop-up window.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To access this form and run the report:

  1. Open the Work Centers menu and select Work Centers|Tax > W-2 Processing.

  2. Under W-2 Processes, select Create Employee SSN Verification Download.

  3. Complete these fields as required:

Field — Description

Requester ID — ID of the person requesting the file. This required field is limited to 4 alphanumeric characters (no special characters).

Starting Report Date — Starting date of the date range for creating this file.

Ending Report Date — Ending date of date range for creating this file.

Client ID — Click the link to display a list from which you can select a specific client for the report. If left blank, the file includes all clients.

  1. Click Generate File. If errors occur, fix them and then regenerate the download.

  2. Click Close to download the file.

If you return to the Create Employee SSN Verification Download screen, a Re-Download Verification File option is available.

Edit EFW2C File Status

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Edit%20EFW2C%20File%20Status.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Edit EFW2C File Status.htm

Edit EFW2C File Status

Use this form to change/update the Status of the EFW2C download file in the Generated EFW2C Files grid on the EFW2C Download and Maintenance form. The Status of the EFW2C download file in the Generated EFW2C Files grid on the EFW2C Download and Maintenance form reflects the current Status of the file. Depending on your external processes, use this form to change/update the Status of the EFW2C download file along the life cycle of the file. For example, once you generated a download file, it will be in the Unsent status. Once you submit it to the SSA you will need to change the Status to In-Process.

Click any Status on the Generated EFW2C Files grid on the EFW2C Download and Maintenance form to open this form for that particular download file. The following fields will be read only on this form:

  • Tax Year

  • Submitter ID

  • File Name

  • File Description

  • Status - You can change/updated the current Status (shown in parenthesis) using the drop-down to one of the following options:

  • In Process - Select this option once you have submitted the file to SSA. You have the option to enter/update the Receipt ID for that file. On the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you can view the EFW2C data for this employee but you cannot edit it.

  • Accepted - Select this option once SSA has accepted your download file submission. On the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you can view the EFW2C data for this employee but you cannot edit it.

  • Rejected - Select this option once SSA has rejected your submission of the download file. You have to enter/update the Resubmission WFID for that file.

  • Regenerate - Select this option once you need to regenerate a download file with corrected data. On the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you can view the EFW2C data for this employee and you can edit it.

  • Cancelled - Select this option once you need to cancel a download file and want to redo the data. On the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you can view the EFW2C data for this employee will be blank and you will need to fill in from the scratch..

  • New File Description - You can also change/update the file description using this field.

Click Save to save the changes made on this form so that it reflects correctly on the Generated EFW2C Files grid on the EFW2C Download and Maintenance form. If you do no wish to save the changes, then you can close this form using the Close button on the top right of this form.

Building EEO-1 and Pay Data

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/EEO/Build_EEO-1_Data.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/EEO/Build_EEO-1_Data.htm

Building EEO-1 and Pay Data

Before creating the EEO-1 download file, you must build the appropriate pay data into the database. The build process will progress differently depending on the settings you configure here.

Configuring EEO-1 Report Settings

In PrismHR, open the Work Centers menu and select EEO Processing under Work Centers|Compliance. In the EEO-1 Report Processing category, select Build EEO-1 & Pay Data.

Then, fill out each section of the form specified below. When you are ready to start the data build, see Running the Build.

EEO-1 Information

Set up the following fields according to your reporting needs. This data will display in Consolidated record of the EEO-1 reporting file.

Field — Action

Unit number Assigned by the EEOC — Enter the unit number assigned by the EEOC.

Headquarters Company — Enter the company headquarters ID number.

Headquarters Location — Enter the company headquarters location ID number.

Is Federal Contractor or Financial Institution — Select this option if the company counts as a financial institution or does contract work for the federal government.

Dun & Bradstreet Number — If the company has a Dun & Bradstreet number, enter it here.

Unique Entity ID — This field is not mandatory. You may enter the 12 character (no special characters) Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number issued by the System for Award Management (SAM) to identify businesses and other entities that do business with the federal government.

Client Settings

Use this section to determine the inclusion and exclusion of client data in the data build process.

Field Action
Exclude ASO Companies Select this option to exclude clients set up as Administrative Services Organizations.
Build Data For Specify whether the system will build data for: - All clients - All clients except for ASOs - Only specific clients (a grid displays for you to specify the clients) - All clients except specific clients (a grid displays for you to specify the clients)
  • All clients
  • All clients except for ASOs
  • Only specific clients (a grid displays for you to specify the clients)
  • All clients except specific clients (a grid displays for you to specify the clients) ### Running the Build

To build EEO data:

  1. Complete the following setup fields in the Build Options panel:
Field Action
Report As‑of Date The date for the report, based on year and employee-related information (such as active/inactive status and position). > Note: Note: As a best practice, PrismHR recommends using the date for the last scheduled payroll batch of the reporting year.
Employee Filter Select the rule to use when the system determines whether to include an employee in the data build: - Active during reporting period - Paid more than $0 during reporting period
  • Active during reporting period
  • Paid more than $0 during reporting period | Build Only if 100/50 Threshold Met | Select this option to only build data for the following clients: - Clients who are not Federal Contractors and who have 100+ employees - Clients who are Federal Contractors and who have 50+ employees > Note: Note: The values 100 and 50, above, are defined based on the EEO-1 build logic (specifically the Report As Of Date). These values do not refer to employee counts in general. |
  • Clients who are not Federal Contractors and who have 100+ employees
  • Clients who are Federal Contractors and who have 50+ employees | Use 40/20 Hours Worked Approximation | For FLSA exempt employees: - To display an approximation of hours worked based on full/part‑time status and weeks worked, enable this option. Full-time exempt employees display 40 hours a week. Part-time exempt employees display 20 hours a week. - To display the actual number of hours worked, leave this option unchecked. |
  • To display an approximation of hours worked based on full/part‑time status and weeks worked, enable this option. Full-time exempt employees display 40 hours a week. Part-time exempt employees display 20 hours a week.
  • To display the actual number of hours worked, leave this option unchecked. | Build Component 2 Data | Whether to include “Component 2” data (as defined by the EEOC) in the build. Component 2 requires a more fine-grained breakdown of employee information. | | Build Labor Contractor Data | - This field is a check box which is unchecked by default. When selected an additional data set will be built to support the California Labor Contractor Pay Data Report. - This field will only appear when the Employee Filter field is set to Paid more than $0 during reporting period. - This will build a separate set of data to support the new requirement related to Labor Contractors for the state of California. In addition to the existing “Payroll Employee Report”, for the reporting year 2022 filed in 2023, the state of California now requires a private employer with 100 or more workers hired through labor contractors in the prior calendar year (with at least one worker based in California) must file a separate “Labor Contractor Employee Report” that covers workers hired through labor contractors in the prior calendar year. - When selected, the standard YTD data will build based on the Report As-of Date supplied. In addition to the standard YTD data, a separate set of data specific to the worksite location in which the employee has a voucher greater than $0 on the report as of data will be built. This is most commonly used by staffing companies. |
  • This field is a check box which is unchecked by default. When selected an additional data set will be built to support the California Labor Contractor Pay Data Report.
  • This field will only appear when the Employee Filter field is set to Paid more than $0 during reporting period.
  • This will build a separate set of data to support the new requirement related to Labor Contractors for the state of California. In addition to the existing “Payroll Employee Report”, for the reporting year 2022 filed in 2023, the state of California now requires a private employer with 100 or more workers hired through labor contractors in the prior calendar year (with at least one worker based in California) must file a separate “Labor Contractor Employee Report” that covers workers hired through labor contractors in the prior calendar year.
  • When selected, the standard YTD data will build based on the Report As-of Date supplied. In addition to the standard YTD data, a separate set of data specific to the worksite location in which the employee has a voucher greater than $0 on the report as of data will be built. This is most commonly used by staffing companies.
  1. Click Build. The Job Control form displays the progress of the build process.

Creating the EEO-1 Download Report

This form produces a report in .csv format, summarizing EEO-1 and, if applicable, Component 2 data.

To run the report:

  1. In the Work Centers menu, navigate to Work Centers|Compliance > EEO-1 Processing.

  2. Under the EEO-1 Report Processing category, under Reports, select EEO-1 Download Report.

  3. Select the report Year.

  4. To generate a report that contains Component 2 reporting data, select Build Component 2 Format.

  5. Click Generate Report: the Job Control form displays the progress of the report generation.

  6. Review the Job Control details and the click Close.

  7. Click Download Report to obtain the report download through your web browser.

The generated .csv file will contain labeled counts for each EEO-1 reporting category.

Note:

Client and Worksite Location level federal contractor settings are now applied to the EEO-1 Download Report.

If in the Client EEO-1 & Pay Data Files form Additional Companies are included, and:

  • If the headquarters client is a federal contractor and any listed additional clients are not, then the specific additional clients who are not federal contractors are not reported as a federal contractor on the EEO-1 Download Report.

  • However, if those additional clients who are not federal contractors are flagged as federal contractors on their Worksite Locations form, then those specific those worksite locations will be reported as federal contractors.

  • If the headquarters client is a federal contractor and one or more of the listed additional clients are also federal contractors, then the additional client or clients will be reported as federal contractors using the client specific Unique Entity Identity (UEI).

Running the EEO Detail Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/EEO/EEO_Detail_Report.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/EEO/EEO_Detail_Report.htm

Running the EEO Detail Report

Use the EEO Detail Report to view detailed employee information relevant for EEO-1 reporting.

  • The Report Filters panel restricts the report output to employees associated with particular entities (such as categories, departments, or cost centers). Leave the grids blank to include all applicable entities (for example, all worksite locations under the specified client).

  • The Report Parameters panel filters out employees based on status, status classification, or type.

To run the report:

  1. In the Work Centers menu, navigate to Work Centers|Compliance > EEO-1 Processing.

  2. Under EEO Reports, select EEO Detail Report.

  3. Specify whether to produce a report for All Clients or the Currently Selected Client.

  4. Use the Report Filters panel to restrict the report output to specific entities within the client or clients. If you run the report for a single client, there are additional filter options.

  • Department Code — Selected Client only

  • Worksite Code — Selected Client only

  • State Code — Selected Client only

  • Category Code — All Clients or Selected Client

  • Cost Center (Sub-Cost Centers are not allowed) — All Clients or Selected Client

  1. Use the Report Parameters panel to restrict the output to employees of one or more Status Codes, Status Classes, or Employee Type Codes.

  2. Enter the As Of Date, which is the start date for the range of data that the report selects and displays (the end date is today’s date).

  3. Click Generate Report: the Job Control form displays the progress of the report generation.

  4. Review the Job Control details and the click Close.

  5. Click Download Report to obtain the report download through your web browser.

Analyzing the Report Output

The report output includes much of the data necessary for generating the EEO-1 output file. Use this output to review employee data and ensure that it is ready for filing.

  • EEO-1 Download Report ## About the EEO-1 Report

Employers must annually file the Employer Information Report (EEO-1 Report) with the Joint Reporting Committee of the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. The report provides a count of company employees by job class, ethnicity, race, and gender.

This document describes how to create a download file that contains a multi-establishment report for all employers. The data file includes:

  • A consolidated record for the PEO or employer

  • A headquarters record for a single client or worksite location

  • Establishment records for each client that has 100 or more employees. Note that if a company has government contracts for $50,000 or more, the threshold for establishment records is 50 or more employees.

Where applicable, clients can report each location as a separate establishment record, regardless of the number of employees working at the location. These line items will use EEOC status codes as detailed in the table below.

Note: Note: The Unit Number mentioned in the table below refers to the field under Client > Change > Worksite Location > Other Parameters, called EEO Unit Number.

EEOC Status Code — Description

2 — Consolidated report record This only displays in the first record of the download. > Note: Note: If your download is for single-establishment reporting, you must manually change this value to 1 and ensure that any worksite locations are linked (contact Customer Support for details).

3 — Headquarters record This only displays in the second record of the download. > Note: Note: If your download is for single-establishment reporting, you can remove this record.

4 — Establishment has 50+ employees and it is not first time reporting (a Unit Number exists for the establishment).

8 — Establishment has fewer than 50 employees (a Unit Number does not exist).

9 — Establishment has 50+ employees and it is the first time reporting (a Unit Number does not exist).

Other Documentation

For more general information about EEO-1 filing and Component 1 of the report, please consult the following official resources:

  • Preparing Data – Single-Establishment Companies

  • Preparing Data – Multi-Establishment Companies

Exporting EEO-1 Data

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

Use the Export EEO-1 Data feature to create .csv export files of employee-level EEO-1 data from the latest build.

  • After exporting this data, you can review the export file for data errors.

  • After correcting the error fields on the export file, re-upload it using the EEO-1 import process to correct the data in the system. For details, see Importing EEO-1 Data.

Note: Note: The export file is not valid for submission to the EEOC.

If you export all employees, employees with errors will display at the top of the output file.

  1. Click Export Data. A new form displays the progress of the export.

  2. Review the export progress and click Close when finished.

  3. On the Export EEO-1 Data form, click Download EEO-1 Data. Your browser displays the downloaded .csv file.

Importing EEO-1 Data

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/EEO/Import_EEO-1_Data.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/EEO/Import_EEO-1_Data.htm

Importing EEO-1 Data

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

Use the Import EEO-1 Data form to correct any errors that were identified by the Export EEO-1 Data feature. The form also provides some import preferences you can customize.

Note: Note: Use either .txt. or .csv files with this feature. The format of the input file must match the format generated by the EEO-1 data export feature. For details, see Exporting EEO-1 Data.

File Requirements

Note: Note: This form accepts input files that follow the format of the EEO-1 export file. The import will ignore any data in columns to the right of the System column, as these are informational only.

You can import employees who do not already have records in the system. There is a setting on this form that determines whether to include them in the report. See the procedure below for more information.

If you want to import data for employees that are not already in the system, you must assign each of these employees a unique ID on the import file. For example, you can use their SSN, a unique number, or some form of their name. This ID will act as their employee ID on the report.

Requirements for the EEO-1 import file:

  • It can be a .txt file with tab delimiters OR a .csv file.

  • Employee names must not contain any special characters, such as commas, periods, apostrophes, or quotation marks.

  • Employee names must be formatted: FirstName MiddleName LastName Suffix.

  • Give the import file a unique name.

  • If you are importing employees that are not in the system, give them a unique Employee ID. See the note above.

Procedure

To import EEO-1 data into PrismHR:

  1. Open the Work Centers menu and select Work Centers|Compliance > EEO Processing.

  2. Under the EEO-1 Report Processing category, select Import EEO-1 Data.

  3. The EEO-1 Report As Of Date populates automatically from the EEO-1 configuration. Change this value if necessary.

  4. Use the Replace Behavior option to specify how the import process works:

  • Modify and Replace Existing Data – if data exists in the system for employees listed in the file, PrismHR overwrites that data with the data from the import file.

  • Clear All Data and Replace – PrismHR deletes all EEO-1 register data for all employees (even employees not listed in the import file) and creates new EEO-1 registers using only data from the import file.

  1. Select whether to Import Employees That Are Not in Prism. Otherwise, PrismHR will ignore data for any employees not already in the EEO-1 registers.

For details, review the Import File Requirements section, above.

  1. In the Import File panel, specify the number of Header Lines to Skip. For example, enter 1 if the import file has header data or labels in the first row.

  2. Click Choose File. A new form displays where you can upload the import file.

  3. Upload the file and click submit.

  4. Click Import Data to run the import. The Job Control form displays the imported employees.

  5. After the process completes, select Error Report to review any errors.

  • Social Security Number

  • Gross Earnings

  • Federal Taxable/Withheld

  • OASDI Taxable/Withheld

  • Medicare Taxable/Withheld

  • State

  • State Taxable

  • State Withheld

  • Locality

  • Local Taxable

  • Local Withheld

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To run the W-2 Local Detail report:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click Tax > W-2 Processing > W-2 Reporting > W-2 Local Detail Report.

  2. Complete these fields as required:

Field — Description

Employer ID — When you select the client’s employer, the system displays the Employer ID and Name.

Client ID — When you select the client ID, the system displays the name of the client for whom the report will be generated.

Tax Year — Year for which the report is run. The default is the current year.

State Code — The state of which the client is a resident.

Local Tax Authority ID — The local tax authority for the area where the client resides (if any).

Zip Code Above or Equal To — Five digit client zip code that is above or equal to a specific value.

Zip Code Below or Equal To — Five digit client zip code that is below or equal to a specific value.

Box 12 Code — Code for the amount to be reported in Box 12 of the federal W-2 form. This code is two alpha characters only.

  1. Click Run. When complete, the report is displayed. You can download the report in XLS format by clicking the XLS link.

Date. - SIT Rpt Entity – Any one of the following options only: - C – Client - E – Employer - Blank - SIT Eff Date – Must be a valid date. - SIT End Date – Must be a valid date after the SIT Eff. Date. - GL Segment EEHL – Only Alpha-Numeric characters are allowed for this field.

Maintaining Employer Details

Setting Employer Details

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Employer_Details_and_General.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Employer_Details_and_General.htm

Setting Employer Details

Use the Employer Details panel to create new employer IDs and add basic employer information, or to edit information for an existing Employer ID.

Setup Procedure

To configure employer details:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From Employer|Change, select Employer Details.

  3. Change these fields as required.

Field Description
Employer To create or edit an employer, enter an employer ID. IDs must be an integer up to 6 digits long. For ASO clients, this ID is the same as the client ID.
Employer Name Name that displays in PrismHR.
Employer Print Name Name that displays on checks and reports.
Federal EIN Federal Employee Identification Number issued to employers by the IRS, in one of the following formats: ##-####### (two numbers, dash, seven numbers) or ######### (nine numbers).
Address, City, State, ZIp Code, Zip Extension, Telephone Enter the employer’s basic contact information.
Obsolete Select this option if the employer is no longer active. If there are payrolls that still exist for this employer, a message displays during calculation that indicates the employer is discontinued.
G/L Company Number Prefix to the general ledger account number. > Note: Note: PrismHR accounting files put the company number before the account number. QuickBooks and PeachTree cannot process the numbers, so the system removes the company number when it builds files for those programs. You can use the G/L Company Number to group data for accounting purposes, such as for an ASO.
G/L Cost Center General ledger cost center, if any.
G/L Sub-Cost Center General ledger sub-cost center. Use this field for generating G/L accounts, if any.
New York City Public Entity Select this option if the employer is a public entity in New York City. This enables special Section 125 handling for New York City public employee health deductions, because New York State does not allow those plans to be deducted pre-tax.
ESS URL Employer Override ESS override URL for this employer.
EP URL Employer Override Employee Portal (EP) override URL for this employer.
Prism URL Employer Override PrismHR URL for this employer.
Federal Deposit Method Federal deposit method in use. Options include: - MasterTax - Select to include tax data on the MasterTax PTS file. Then, enter the MasterTax Employer ID and the EFTPS PIN code. - Other - Select if tax data on the MasterTax PTS file is not required. These fields only display if the SBEA feature set is enabled. Contact your system administrator or consult the SBEA User Guide for more information.
Certified PEO This field and the following three fields apply to the SBEA features. Select if the employer is certified by the IRS as a PEO according to the provisions of the SBEA.
Certified Start Date Date when the SBEA certification went into effect.
Certified End Date Date when the SBEA certification expires.
Limit Testing on Employer Register When the Certified PEO functionality is enabled, select this field if you want to build client entity registers, but test for federal taxes at the employer level. Select this option if you need to set the Certified PEO flag mid-year. It enables you to produce Schedule R Reports without interfering with payroll and tax processing.
PTM Identifier Number Enter the PTM Identifier Number of the employer here. This field is optional and supports alpha numeric characters. - The PTM Identifier Number field must be set at the system level on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, so that the PTM Identifier Number field is available on the Employer Details form here. - If no PTM Identifier Number is set at the system level on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, then no PTM Identifier Number will display on the files. - If an employer PTM Identifier Number on the Employer Details form exists for an employer and the same or a different PTM Identifier Number is set at the system level on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, then the employer PTM Identifier Number will override the system level PTM Identifier Number. Then: - The employer PTM Identifier Number on the Employer Details form will appear on all PTM reports including the Daily Tax Export (including PTM Agency export), the Monthly Tax Export and the Quarterly Tax Export reports. - If an employer PTM Identifier Number does not exist on the Employer Details form, but a system level PTM Identifier Number exists on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, then the system level PTM Identifier Number on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form will appear on all PTM reports like the Daily Tax Export (including PTM Agency export), the Monthly Tax Export and the Quarterly Tax Export reports.
  • The PTM Identifier Number field must be set at the system level on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, so that the PTM Identifier Number field is available on the Employer Details form here.
  • If no PTM Identifier Number is set at the system level on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, then no PTM Identifier Number will display on the files.
  • If an employer PTM Identifier Number on the Employer Details form exists for an employer and the same or a different PTM Identifier Number is set at the system level on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, then the employer PTM Identifier Number will override the system level PTM Identifier Number. Then:
  • The employer PTM Identifier Number on the Employer Details form will appear on all PTM reports including the Daily Tax Export (including PTM Agency export), the Monthly Tax Export and the Quarterly Tax Export reports.
  • If an employer PTM Identifier Number does not exist on the Employer Details form, but a system level PTM Identifier Number exists on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, then the system level PTM Identifier Number on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form will appear on all PTM reports like the Daily Tax Export (including PTM Agency export), the Monthly Tax Export and the Quarterly Tax Export reports. | Tax Contact Name | Contact for quarterly reporting. | | Tax Contact Title | Company contact title | | Tax Contact Phone | Phone number, and extension if applicable. | | Tax Contact Email | Contact email address. | | Suppress W2 Printing | Prevents Form W-2 printing for an employer. Select if the employer processes W-2s on a different system. | | Exclude from BLS 3020 | Excludes this employer from the BLS 3020 Multiple Worksite Report. |
  1. Click Save.

Note about deleting employers

Note: If you try to delete an employer who has active employees or employees on leave, the following confirmation message displays:

[Image: screenshot]

Do the following if this message displays:

  • Click Yes to permanently delete the employer record. The Employer Details form clears.

  • Click No to close the message and return to the form. The employer data remains on the form.

Setting Online Access for Form W-2

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Employer_Form_W-2_Audit.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Employer_Form_W-2_Audit.htm

Setting Online Access for Form W-2

Set up employer online access to Form W-2, Form W-2c, and Form 1099 using the Form W-2/1099 Initialization Audit & Control panel under Employer Details.

To configure online tax form access:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From Employer|Change, select Employer Details and expand the Form W-2/1099 Initialization Audit & Control panel.

  3. Fill out these fields as required:

Field Description
Year Enter a tax year. The grid displays the Last Init Date, Last Init Time, and Last Init By fields. Use the Create Employee W-2 Forms (found under Work Centers > W-2 Processing) to perform these initializations.
Allow Web Access Provide web access permissions for Form W-2. Options include: - Yes - All employees can access Forms W-2 for the year. - No - No employees can access Forms W-2 for the year. - Electronic - Employees who elected early online access to their W-2s can see the forms. This is controlled by the Electronic Form W-2 option in the Employee Details > Tax tab. To see which employees have elected electronic Form W‑2 access, use the Client Master report or the Employee General Information report in Report Center.
These steps make Form W-2c/Form 1099 accessible from both Employee Details and Employee Portal (EP):
1099 Web Access Set to Yes to allow employees to view and print Form 1099.
W2C Web Access Set to Yes to allow employees to view and print Form W-2c.
Mask SSN on W-2’s Beginning In Specify a reporting year. If this field: - has a year selected then: - from that selected year onwards the Social Security Number for an employee will be masked and only the last 4 digits will display on both Form W-2 and Form W-2c PDFs. This functionality has been extended to the Employee Portal PDF. - for any prior year the Social Security Number for an employee will not be masked on both Form W-2 and Form W-2c PDFs. - does not have a year selected then: - for any year the Social Security Number for an employee will not be masked either on Form W-2 or Form W-2c PDFs.
  • has a year selected then:
  • from that selected year onwards the Social Security Number for an employee will be masked and only the last 4 digits will display on both Form W-2 and Form W-2c PDFs. This functionality has been extended to the Employee Portal PDF.
  • for any prior year the Social Security Number for an employee will not be masked on both Form W-2 and Form W-2c PDFs.
  • does not have a year selected then:
  • for any year the Social Security Number for an employee will not be masked either on Form W-2 or Form W-2c PDFs.
  1. Click Save.

Processing Form W-2 with a Common Pay Agent

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Employer_Pay_Agent_Form_W-2.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Employer_Pay_Agent_Form_W-2.htm

Processing Form W-2 with a Common Pay Agent

Common Pay Agents provide FICA consolidation and also handle income tax withholding, reporting and remittance under their Federal Employer Identification Number (FEIN). Common Pay Agent Name Control is not applied to Form W-2’s built by Client Federal Entity Registers for SBEA W2 Reporting. Common Pay Agent PDF only applies to 2023 and forward.

If an employer has registered with the IRS as using a common pay agent for remittance of federal withholding taxes, use the Employer Details > Common Pay Agent for Form W-2 Processing panel to identify the common pay agent contracted to process W-2s.

To set Common Pay Agent details:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From Employer|Change, select Employer Details and expand the Common Pay Agent for Form W-2 Processing panel.

  3. Complete the following fields:

Field Name Description
Year The year for which this setup will apply. For example, for 2023 you have a common pay agent and reporting option is Agent only. For every year starting 2023 the Form W-2 or Form W-2c will report only the common pay agent information until you change it. If you make any changes later, you will need to add a line, enter the year and make the changes. For example, for 2025 you change the Report Option to *Agent\ Employer. You would then see the Common Pay Agent information reported on the Form W-2 only for 2023, 2024, and in 2025 you would see the Agent\ Employer* information reported on the Form W-2 or Form W-2c. (It is not required to add the 2024 record for common pay agent to continue)
Agent FEIN Enter the common pay agent’s FEIN (or Federal Tax Identification Number). FEIN format must be either ##-####### (two digits, dash, seven digits) or ######### (nine consecutive digits).
Agent Name The name of the agent.
Address The street address of the agent.
City The city of the agent.
State The two digit state of the agent.
Zip The zip code of the agent.
Report Option Select is the default option which will only report the employer information. You need to select one of the following options: - *Agent\ Employer* - Select this option to report the Common Pay Agent and Agent for {Employer}. - Agent only - Select this option to report only the Common Pay Agent. > Note: Note: To display Common Pay Agent information on the Form W-2 or Form W-2c PDF, even if this was used in the past, you will need to select a Report Option and Save the changes on the Employer Details form.
  • Agent|Employer - Select this option to report the Common Pay Agent and Agent for {Employer}.
  • Agent only - Select this option to report only the Common Pay Agent.
  1. Click Save.

PrismHR now supports Common Pay Agent reporting within the Form W-2 and Form W-2c. Previously, this information was used in third party downloads for W-2 printing. With the 2023 November QR, you will now see this information applied to the PDF generated within PrismHR and Employee Portal.

  • This will only apply to the NON SBEA W-2 build.

  • SBEA W-2 will reflect the client federal entity information as it does within the EFW2 currently.

  • This will not apply to W-2 that are printed in-house.

Setting State Tax Information

Setting State Tax Information

Maintain state tax information in Employer Details with the State Tax panel.

To set up tax information:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From Employer|Change, select Employer Details and expand the State Tax panel.

  3. In the State Tax ID Numbers table, set tax information for each state where an employer does business:

Note: Note: SUTA Rpt Entity and SIT Rpt Entity must have equivalent values. You cannot set one to report at the client level and the other to report on the employer level.

Field Description
State Two-character postal code. States will display in alphabetical order once any changes are saved.
State Name The full state name displays when you enter a postal code. For example, enter CA in the State field and the State Name of California displays.
Licensed Select Yes if an employer is a licensed PEO in a specific state.
Taxpayer ID/UI Account Employer Taxpayer ID number for a specific state. Enter APPLIED FOR if you are awaiting an ID.
State Tax Nbr State number for reporting income taxes that appears on W-2 forms.
Mag Authority ID Magnetic authorization number for a state.
Misc ID1 - California: Enter the Wage Plan Code. - Iowa: Enter the 3 digit suffix location number. If an employer has multiple locations that requires the 3-digit suffix for the location they are filing from, they should enter the 3-digit suffix location number here to capture the employer 9 digit FEIN along with the 3 digit suffix when generating the Iowa New Hire Report. Iowa New Hire reporting file will be rejected if the FEIN is not 12 digits long. - New Jersey: Enter the Disability Insurance Private Plan Number.
  • California: Enter the Wage Plan Code.
  • Iowa: Enter the 3 digit suffix location number. If an employer has multiple locations that requires the 3-digit suffix for the location they are filing from, they should enter the 3-digit suffix location number here to capture the employer 9 digit FEIN along with the 3 digit suffix when generating the Iowa New Hire Report. Iowa New Hire reporting file will be rejected if the FEIN is not 12 digits long.
  • New Jersey: Enter the Disability Insurance Private Plan Number. | Misc ID2 | - New Jersey: Enter the FLIPP Number. - Iowa: Enter the 8-digit Business E-File Number provided by the state. |
  • New Jersey: Enter the FLIPP Number.
  • Iowa: Enter the 8-digit Business E-File Number provided by the state. | GL Segment EEHL | Enter substitute data for the Employee Home Location ID. | | SUTA Rpt Entity | Select whether the PEO or Company (client) is the designated SUTA reporting entity in the state. This overrides the setting on the State Rules form. | | Rpt Entity Eff. Date | Effective date for the SUTA reporting entity. | | SIT Rpt Entity | Select whether the Employer or Client is the designated income tax reporting entity for the state. If you do not select an entity, or if the reporting date is in the future, state income tax accrues and reports according to any Tax Deduction settings. If no Tax Deduction settings exist, state income tax accrues and reports under the employer, by default. | | SIT Eff Date | Effective date for the SIT reporting entity. | | FUTA Override View | Click to display state FUTA information. See the rest of the procedure for details. | | FUTA Override Edit | Click to open a form that allows edits to FUTA override rates. FUTA override rate information displays in its own grid at the bottom of the panel. See the rest of the procedure for details. |
  1. Set up invoice and fax headings using the Heading table:

Field — Description

Heading Information — Information that prints on the invoice or fax.

Used On — Select whether the heading is used on invoices, faxes, or both.

X Coor / Y Coor — Printer Command Language/PCL coordinates for invoice headings that do not appear on a fax form.

  1. Edit and review any Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) overrides. You can override FUTA rates using the FUTA Override form: click the FUTA Override Edit field in the State Tax ID Numbers grid to edit override information.

Field — Description

Year — Tax year for the override.

Override FUTA Rate — Override tax rate.

Suppress Self-Adjust — Suppresses year-to-date self-adjustments. Select Yes to suppress for both Accrual and Billing, or select Accrual Only or Billing Only. Leave blank for neither self-adjustment type.

  1. Click Save.

Updates to Form W-2 build

The State Income Tax Account Number on the employee Form W-2 will now be pulled from the Client Details form or the Employer Details form based on the tax deduction code, unless an override exists on the Employer Details form on the SIT Rpt Entity field for that state under the State Tax section.

The State Income Tax Account Number on the employee Form W-2 will be:

  • Client State Tax ID when:

  • Tax deduction code set to report at Client Level and ER Details, State is set to -select- or Client

  • Tax deduction code NOT set to report at Client Level, but ER Details, State is set to Client

  • Employer State Tax ID:

  • Tax deduction code NOT set to report at Client Level and ER Details, State is set to -select- or Employer

  • Tax deduction code set to report at Client Level, but ER Details, State is set to Employer

Note: If the State Tax ID is not available on the corresponding reporting entity, the Form W-2 will not be built, and an error will appear in the W2 Error Report stating State Employer ID not found for Client # for State XX OR State Employer ID not found for Employer for State XX

Establishing Employer Tax Rates (SUTA)

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Employer_Tax_Rates_SUTA.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Employer_Tax_Rates_SUTA.htm

Establishing Employer Tax Rates (SUTA)

Use the Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) form to set up State Unemployment Tax Act (SUTA) and State Disability Insurance (SDI) rates for an employer and the states where they do business. (In PrismHR, SUTA is based on employee home location.)

Note: Click the Data Import Tool icon (

[Image: screenshot]

) to upload a database file and import data. (This icon displays for all user roles, except “Inquiry Only.”)

Note: Note: For more information about the Data Import Tool form, see the Payroll Administration Guide.

To set rates:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From Employer|Change, select Employer Details to view the Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) panel.

  3. Fill in these fields as required.

Panel Description

Setting Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Employer_WC_Accrual_Modifiers.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Employer_WC_Accrual_Modifiers.htm

Setting Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers

Set Workers’ Compensation rates for a selected employer and state with the Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers form.

Importing an Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers File

Clicking the Import button

[Image: screenshot]

displays the Data Import Tool form, which allows you to import an Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers template file that contains the following fields (this file must be in .txt format):

  • Employer (required): Must be a valid employer that is currently in the system.

  • State Code (required): Enter a two-digit state name (do not enter the whole state name). For example, enter TX for the state of Texas.

  • Effective Date (required): Must be a valid date.

  • Discount/Debit (required): Must be a valid number.

  • Modifier (required): Must be a valid number.

  • W/C Policy: Must be a valid W/C policy in the system.

  • W/C Policy Discount/Debit: Must be a valid number.

  • W/C Policy Modifier: Must be a valid number.

The Import button displays on the Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers form for all service provider user roles except the “Deny” and “Inquiry-only” roles. Imports can be performed for multiple clients at the operations level.

Note: Note: For more information about the Data Import Tool form, refer to the PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide.

To set rates:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From Employer|Change, select Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers.

  3. Complete the following fields:

Field Description
Employer Enter or select the employer ID.
State Code State code where the employer does business.
Effective Date Date when workers’ compensation is effective. Enter a new date or select an existing date.
Discount/Debit Employer discount/debit rate for the state.
Modifier Modifier rate for the state.
Effective Rate This value is determined by the Discount/Debit and Modifier rates.
Override by W/C Policy You can override the rates by policy in the Override by W/C Policy panel: - Enter the W/C Policy. - Enter the Discount/Debit rate for the policy. - Enter the Modifier for the policy.
  • Enter the W/C Policy.
  • Enter the Discount/Debit rate for the policy.
  • Enter the Modifier for the policy.
  1. Click Save.

Creating the ESAC Client Export

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/ESAC%20Client%20Export.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/ESAC Client Export.htm

Creating the ESAC Client Export

The Employer Services Assurance Corporation (ESAC) is an independent non-profit corporation; it is the official accreditation and financial assurance organization for the PEO industry. The ESAC Client Export process creates a file that contains a list of clients for a specified PEO, which can be sent to ESAC for accreditation verification.

Note: Note: This process does not use Client Access Group security.

To access this form, click the Back Office menu. Under Operations|Action, select ESAC Client Export.

To download the ESAC Client export:

  1. Complete the following fields:
Field Description
Start Date Enter the start date of the export period.
End Date Enter the end date of the export period. > Note: Note: The End Date must be after the Start Date and must be the last day of the month.
Include PEO Clients Only? This field is optional. Select one of the following options from the drop-down: - Yes (Default) - Only PEO clients are included in the export. - No - All clients
  • Yes (Default) - Only PEO clients are included in the export.
  • No - All clients | Exclude Clients Terminated | Enter the number of months in numbers. You can enter any number of months. This will exclude clients who were terminated the specified number of months before the Start Date. |

  1. Click Build. The ESAC Client Export processing starts. If errors occur, fix them and then rebuild the export file.

  2. When the process is complete, click Close to return to the ESAC Client Export page

  3. Click the Download link to download the export file.

  4. Click Clear to clear the screen at any time.
