BLS Multiple Worksite Electronic File

Use this form to generate the BLS-3020 electronic file to be submitted to the federal or state Bureau of Labor Statistics.

BLS Reports provide analytical information related to the labor force, consumer spending, earnings, and work injuries and illnesses. Typically, reports contain a few pages of written analysis followed by statistical tables, which allow you to gather detailed information on economic conditions. Most reports have an annual cycle.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group security.

To access this form, in the Work Centers panel, under Tax, click Quarterly Tax Processing. Under Government Exports, click BLS Multiple Worksite Electronic File.

To generate the BLS Multiple Worksite Electronic file:

  1. Fill in the following fields:
Field Description
BLS Type Select the BLS type from the following: - PEO (Default) - ASO
  • PEO (Default)
  • ASO | Report Year | Enter the year to report on. Valid values are between 2020-2055. | | Quarter | Enter the quarter to run the report on. Select it from the drop-down. | | Employer ID | This field is optional. If you want to run this report for a particular employer, enter the Employer ID or click the Employer ID link and select one from the Select Employer dialog box. | | State | Default is All States. If you want to run this report for a specific state, select it from the drop-down. |

  1. Click Build.

  2. Click Yes in the dialog box when asked Are you sure you wish to build the BLS Multiple Worksite Report at this time?

  4. Click Close to close the job progress window

  5. The report is downloaded on your system in a .txt format.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Federal%20940%20Credit%20Reduction%20Report.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Federal 940 Credit Reduction Report.htm

Federal 940 Credit Reduction Report

Use this form to generate a report to display the FUTA taxable amount by state for a calendar year. You can run this report by Clients, Client Federal Entity or Employer.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, click Reports. Under Employer|Report, click Federal 940 Credit Reduction Report.

To generate the Federal 940 Credit Reduction Report:

  1. Complete the following:
Field Name Description
Year Select the calendar year you want to run this report for from the drop-down. The default option is the current year. The drop-down has a ten year look back starting from the current year.
Employer ID This field is optional. Leave this field blank to run this report for all employers. If you want to run this report for a particular employer, enter the employer ID here or click the Employer ID link and select it from the Select Employer dialog box.
SUI State This field is optional. Leave this field blank to run this report for all states. If you want to run this report for a particular state, enter the two digit state code here or click the SUI State link and select it from the Select States dialog box.
Report Type Select the type of report you want from the following options: - Client – This is the default option. - Client Federal Entity - Employer
  • Client – This is the default option.
  • Client Federal Entity
  • Employer | Report Output | Select the report output from the following options: - Summary – This is the default option. Select Summary to provide Report Type Totals by State. - Detail – Select Detail to provide Report Type Totals by State and Employee. |
  • Summary – This is the default option. Select Summary to provide Report Type Totals by State.
  • Detail – Select Detail to provide Report Type Totals by State and Employee. | Include Adjustments | By default this option is disabled. Enable this option to report adjusted FUTA wages. - When disabled – The report only outputs the total of all vouchers that have combined SUTA and FUTA taxable wages for the year. Any data entered in the grid in the FUTA Credit Adjustment Entry form will NOT reflect in the totals. - When enabled – The report outputs the total of all vouchers with combined SUTA and FUTA taxable wages for the year AND includes any adjustments entered directly into the grid in the FUTA Credit Adjustment Entry form. > Note: Note: The accrued and billed are not modified by the grid in the FUTA Credit Adjustment Entry form. Only the wages are moved to a new state. The accrued and billed amounts are still reflected in the original state. This will be modified in a subsequent enhancement. |
  • When disabled – The report only outputs the total of all vouchers that have combined SUTA and FUTA taxable wages for the year. Any data entered in the grid in the FUTA Credit Adjustment Entry form will NOT reflect in the totals.
  • When enabled – The report outputs the total of all vouchers with combined SUTA and FUTA taxable wages for the year AND includes any adjustments entered directly into the grid in the FUTA Credit Adjustment Entry form.
  1. Click Run to generate the report. The report shows up on screen.

If you run this report by Client, then this report shows the following columns:

  • Client ID

  • Client Name

  • State

  • Employee Count

  • FUTA Taxable

  • FUTA Accrued

  • FUTA Credit Amount – This column will display a calculated amount of the FUTA taxable wages X 0.6%.

  • FUTA Credit Reduction Amount – This will display a calculated amount of the FUTA Taxable wages X the FUTA override amount for the reporting year found in the Back Office>System|Change>State Rules form.

  • FUTA Credit Billed Amount – This will display a calculated amount from payroll vouchers with both FUTA and SUTA taxable amounts. The value is the total amount of FUTA tax billed to the client on those payroll vouchers

If you run this report by Client Federal Entity, then this report shows the following columns:

  • Client ID

  • Client Federal Entity

  • Client Name

  • State

  • Employee Count

  • FUTA Taxable

  • FUTA Accrued

  • FUTA Credit Amount – This column will display a calculated amount of the FUTA taxable wages X 0.6%.

  • FUTA Credit Reduction Amount – This will display a calculated amount of the FUTA Taxable wages X the FUTA override amount for the reporting year found in the Back Office>System|Change>State Rules form.

  • MasterTax F Code

  • FUTA Credit Billed Amount – This will display a calculated amount from payroll vouchers with both FUTA and SUTA taxable amounts. The value is the total amount of FUTA tax billed to the client on those payroll vouchers

If you run this report by Employer, then this report shows the following columns:

  • Employer ID

  • Employer Name

  • State

  • Employee Count

  • FUTA Taxable

  • FUTA Accrued

  • FUTA Credit Amount – This column will display a calculated amount of the FUTA taxable wages X 0.6%.

  • FUTA Credit Reduction Amount – This will display a calculated amount of the FUTA Taxable wages X the FUTA override amount for the reporting year found in the Back Office>System|Change>State Rules form.

  • FUTA Credit Billed Amount – This will display a calculated amount from payroll vouchers with both FUTA and SUTA taxable amounts. The value is the total amount of FUTA tax billed to the client on those payroll vouchers

Building FUTA Credit Reduction Registers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/FUTA-Credit-Registers.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/FUTA-Credit-Registers.htm

Building FUTA Credit Reduction Registers

You can build Federal Unemployment Tax Act credit registers with the FUTA Credit Reduction Register Build form. This process also creates the - 17 record.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To rebuild FUTA credit registers:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click MasterTax Processing. > Setup Forms > FUTA Credit Reduction Register Build.

  2. Complete these fields as required.

Field — Description

Tax Year — Tax year for this register build.

SUI State — State that this report is being generated for.

Employers — Select an employer ID to limit the report to a specific employer. Leave the field blank to include all employers in the report.

  1. Click Build. The system asks if you want to proceed.

  2. Click Yes to confirm the register build. The system displays a status for the rebuild operation.

Building the EES Authentication File

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Generating%20the%20EES%20Authentication%20report.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Generating the EES Authentication report.htm

Building the EES Authentication File

Use the EES Authentication File form to download an authentication file for EES Plus. This enables employees to create accounts on the EES Plus website.

To download the EES Authentication file:

  1. Click the Back Office menu.

  2. From Employer|Action, select EES Authentication File. The EES Authentication File page opens.

  3. Complete the appropriate information:

Field — Description

Use SSN or EEID in Field1 — Select whether to include social security number or employee ID in Field 1.

Use SSN or EEID in Field2 — Select whether to include social security number or employee ID in Field 2.

Use DOB or PIN in Field3 — Select whether to include date of birth or PIN in Field 3.

Year — Select the year for the report. This will default to the current year, but the drop down will provide the option to select the following year as well to not prevent you from working ahead. The download does not report employees that were terminated in previous years.

  1. Click Build. The following warning displays:

[Image: EES Authentication File Warning]

  1. Click Yes. A job progress window opens and the system creates the download file.

  2. Click Close to close the job progress window. The CSV file named EES.AUTH is downloaded to your system.

Maintaining the Quarterly Download

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Maintain-Quarterly-Download.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Maintain-Quarterly-Download.htm

Maintaining the Quarterly Download

Use this form to update two SUTA downloads for missed payments in previous quarters and to update the quarterly register without having to re-run the previous quarter.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To update the SUTA downloads for missed payments:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click Tax > Quarterly Tax Processing > Government Exports > Maintain Quarterly Download.

  2. Complete these fields as required:

Field — Description

Reporting Entity — Select Employer or Client.

State — Select the state.

Employer ID/Company ID — Select the employer or company ID. This changes to Company ID if Client is selected as the Reporting Entity.

Year — Select the tax year.

Quarter — Select the quarter.

Tax Rate — Enter the tax rate.

Previous Quarter(s) Underpayment — Enter underpayments for the previous quarters, including previously due penalty and interest).

Interest Due — Enter the amount of interest due.

Penalty Due — Enter the amount of the penalty due.

Credit/Overpayment — Enter the previous credit or overpayment to apply to the balance due.

Employer Assessment Amount — If applicable, enter the employer assessment amount, as levied by the state.

Amount Remitted — Enter the amount remitted to the state.

  1. Select one of the following options:

  • Click Save to save the information you entered.

  • Click Clear to clear the information you entered.

  • Click Delete to delete the record.

Maintaining Employee Lock-in Information

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Maintaining-Employee-LockIn.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Maintaining-Employee-LockIn.htm

Maintaining Employee Lock-in Information

Employers and employees might receive a lock-in letter from the IRS if they are in debt to that organization. This letter states how much withholding allowance the employee can claim — typically zero. Employees who have a lock-in letter cannot change their allowances in Employee Portal. A lock-in can also be set for a particular state.

When an IRS employee lock-in is set, any users who are not Service Providers will see the following message when they try to change their withholding amount:

Note: Federal taxes for this employee are locked and may not be changed.

To maintain employee lock-in information:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From Employer|Change, select IRS Employee Lock In Letter. The IRS Employee Lock In Letter form opens.

  3. Fill in the form as shown in the following table. When searching for information, you have the following options for displaying search results:

  • Display the previous or next page.

  • Go to a particular page.

  • Narrow your search by entering information in any of the available text boxes and then click Refine.

  • Return to the default display by clicking Reset.

Field Description
Client ID Click the link and select a Client ID. The form displays the Client ID and Name.
Employee ID Click the link and select an Employee ID. The form displays the Employee ID and Name.
IRS Lock-In Date Click and select the IRS Lock-In Date. > Note: Note: The system will ignore any future dates entered in this field. The lock will go into effect immediately, even if a future date is entered.
Lock-In State If applicable, expand the list and select the Lock-In State.
Lock-In Date If applicable, click and select the Lock-In Date for the state.
Lock-In Auth User Click the link and select a service provider who is authorized to change the withholding amount for an employee who has a lock-in letter. The system displays the ID and username of the service provider in the list. - Click + in the header or > in any row to display an additional row where you can select another service provider. - Click x to delete a service provider from the list.
  • Click + in the header or > in any row to display an additional row where you can select another service provider.
  • Click x to delete a service provider from the list.
  1. Click Save.

Mass Update W-2 Access

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Mass_Update_W2_Access.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Mass_Update_W2_Access.htm

Providing Employee Access to W-2 Forms

Set employee access to electronic W-2 forms for multiple employers using the Bulk Update W-2 Access form. You must initialize the W-2s before you can provide access.

Note: Note: In Employer Details, users must provide the employer with online access to W‑2s. See Setting Online Access for Form W-2

To set employee W-2 access:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click Tax > W-2 Processing > W-2 Printing > Bulk Update W-2 Access. [Image: screenshot]

  2. Complete the fields as required.

Field — Description

Tax Year — Tax year for a W-2.

Search for Employer Name — Displays a list of employers after an employer name is entered.

Action — Sets access for W-2s. Options include: - Set all to Show W-2: All employees can access their W-2s for the tax year. - Set all to Hide W-2: No employees can access their W-2s for the tax year. - Set all to Early Access: Only employees who elected early online W-2 access can view their forms. This is set in the Electronic Form W-2 option in the Employee DetailsTax tab. To see which employees have elected electronic Form W‑2 access, use the Client Master report or the Employee General Information report in Report Center. You can also click the links in the W2 Web Access column to change the settings for individual employers.

If most employers are set to one access level and some are not, use the Action drop-down for the most common setting and then click the links for the exceptions. For example, you could use the drop-down to apply Set all to Early Access to the entire list and then use the links to change the access for the employers who are not ready for early access.

  1. Click Save.

Setting MasterTax Interface Parameters

This form controls the version number, SBEA vs Non-SBEA reporting breakouts, File IDs and Customer codes for MasterTax. It also features options that control how data is generated on MasterTax reporting files.

To set MasterTax interface parameters:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click MasterTax Processing > Setup Forms > Mastertax Interface Parameters.

  2. Complete these fields as required:

Field Description
Mastertax Interface Active Activates the MasterTax interface. Enable this to have the system write transactions to the TAX.JOURNAL file automatically during batch posts, voucher reversals, or tax adjustment posts.
Mastertax PTS Import File Version Select the appropriate version of the PTS import file. PrismHR setting this to Version 29, the most recent supported version. If you are running a version of the MasterTax PTS Import File that is version 28 or older, you will receive and the following error message: [Image: screenshot] Position 57-58 on the header record Line 1 in 000 record will reflect “29”. > Note: Note: MasterTax PTS has required updates for Alabama withholding overtime wage reporting changes in record 500 - starting in Q1 2024. PrismHR now supports this when using version 28 in the MasterTax PTS Import File Version field in the MasterTax Interface Parameters form. These changes should only appear when using Version 28 in the MasterTax PTS Import File Version field. If you are using Version 20 or earlier, you will not see the updates. - For both SBEA and non-SBEA clients, the MasterTax v29 PTS will include Work Out of State Flag which is either Y or N in position 15 for the 210 and 500 records for PA resident tax codes not including Philadelphia. This does not apply to Philadelphia residents and this position will remain blank for Philadelphia and all other locality taxes. For example: - If an employee has a resident address and the Courtesy EIT is withheld for Lancaster, PA - position 15 for the tax code 39711930-31 will report Y for all records. - If an employee has a resident and work address in Lancaster, PA - position 15 for the tax code 39711930-31 will report N for all records.
  • For both SBEA and non-SBEA clients, the MasterTax v29 PTS will include Work Out of State Flag which is either Y or N in position 15 for the 210 and 500 records for PA resident tax codes not including Philadelphia. This does not apply to Philadelphia residents and this position will remain blank for Philadelphia and all other locality taxes. For example:
  • If an employee has a resident address and the Courtesy EIT is withheld for Lancaster, PA - position 15 for the tax code 39711930-31 will report Y for all records.
  • If an employee has a resident and work address in Lancaster, PA - position 15 for the tax code 39711930-31 will report N for all records. | Include Dashes on all Eins and Feins | Enable this option to include dashes in both federal and client federal entity Employer Identification Numbers (EINs) on the PTS file. > Note: Note: You cannot enable this field if Include Dashes on Non Federal Eins Only is already enabled. | | Include Dashes on Non Federal Eins Only | Enable this option to include dashes only in the EINs of client federal entities (F codes) on the PTS file. The file will not print dashes in any FEINs. > Note: Note: You cannot enable this field if Include Dashes on all Eins and Feins is already enabled. | | Provide SBEA Payroll Breakout | Enable this option to create F codes on the PTS file for clients that are under a certified employer. This includes creating tax liabilities, by client, for federal taxes. | | SBEA Breakout Start Date | Date when the SBEA payroll breakout occurs. | | Include Certified Relationship Setups | Enable this item to create 210 records for the F codes. The 210 record is required to set up company and pay agent linking in MasterTax. | | Mastertax RTS Import File Version | Select the MasterTax RTS file version used by your system. PrismHR recommends setting this to the highest possible value, which corresponds to the most recent supported version. The header on the MasterTax RTS file now also reflects 48 in Line 1 in 000 record in positions 57-58, with or without the Schedule R Breakout field selected. - For both SBEA and non-SBEA clients, the MasterTax v47 RTS will include Work Out of State Flag which is either Y or N in position 15 for the 500, 501, 601, and 616 records for PA resident tax codes not including Philadelphia. This does not apply to Philadelphia residents and this position will remain blank for Philadelphia and all other locality taxes. Building the MasterTax Monthly Tax Export

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/MasterTax-Monthly-Tax-Export.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/MasterTax-Monthly-Tax-Export.htm

Building the MasterTax Monthly Tax Export

Use this form to build a monthly tax summary, which provides a breakdown of an employee’s monthly tax information.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To build the monthly tax summary:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click MasterTax Processing > File Exports > MasterTax MTS File Build.

  2. Complete these fields as required:

Field Description
Tax Year Year the tax summary is based on.
Tax Month Month the tax summary is based on.
State State the tax summary is based on. If Pennsylvania is selected: - All tax codes that start with 39 are added to the Monthly Tax Summary file. - If the MasterTax version is set to a value lower than 25, the system displays this warning: You must be on version 25 to generate the file for Pennsylvania. This version can be edited on the MasterTax Interface Parameters. - The MTS file is only generated for LTS taxes. This includes any tax code that starts with 39, but it has 7 digits for the first part of the tax code and -31 for the second part of the tax code. For example, 390950320-31. - Excludes any taxes with an authority ID of 391013000 in the tax code because these are not monthly reported taxes for Philadelphia.
  • All tax codes that start with 39 are added to the Monthly Tax Summary file.
  • If the MasterTax version is set to a value lower than 25, the system displays this warning: You must be on version 25 to generate the file for Pennsylvania. This version can be edited on the MasterTax Interface Parameters.
  • The MTS file is only generated for LTS taxes. This includes any tax code that starts with 39, but it has 7 digits for the first part of the tax code and -31 for the second part of the tax code. For example, 390950320-31.
  • Excludes any taxes with an authority ID of 391013000 in the tax code because these are not monthly reported taxes for Philadelphia. | Limit to Employer | Click the link to select an Employer ID that this tax summary is limited to. | | Limit to Company | Click the link to select the Company ID that this tax summary is limited to. | | Reporting | Select Employer to process Employer tax registers and report by Employer. Select Client to process Client tax registers and report by Client. > Note: Note: If an Employer or Company is specified with Limit to Employer / Limit to Company, this field is set to either Employer or Client and is read-only. |

  1. Click Build. A progress window opens.

  2. Click Close when the export is finished. You are presented with these export options:

  • Download MTS File

  • View Summary Report (.txt or .csv)

  • View Detail Report (.txt or .csv)

MTS File History

MTS File History provides a way to save historical files and download them more than once. MTS File History is closed by default, but can be expanded by clicking +. Filters let you narrow down search options by State, Tax Year, or Tax Month.

The history displays the date and time the process was started, the person who started the process, the file name, and both detailed and summary reports.

You can download reports as .txt or .csv by clicking the hyperlinks. In this example, if you click the first link under Detailed Report, the report is displayed and you can print it, save as PDF, or download in .XLS format.

MasterTax PTS Clear Lock

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/MasterTax-PTS-Clear-Lock.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/MasterTax-PTS-Clear-Lock.htm

MasterTax PTS Clear Lock

A process lock is applied to the Mastertax PTS (Payroll Tax Summary) file during its build process to prevent other users from attempting builds. However, it is possible that the process that generates the file can hang, preventing generation of a new file. This function removes the lock on the PTS generation process so the file can be recreated.

To remove the lock on a PTS file being built:

  1. From the Work Centers panel, click MasterTax Processing.

  2. From File Exports, click Mastertax PTS File Build.

  3. Click Build. If a PTS build is already in progress, this message displays: [Image: screenshot]

  4. Click Yes to remove the lock.

  5. Click Build again to start the build process.

Tax Year Select the tax year from the drop-down for which you want to run this report. This field defaults to the current year based on today’s date.
Tax Quarter Select the tax quarter from the drop-down for which you want to run this report.
Report Type Select the report type that you want from the following options: - Schedule R - This report type provides a breakout of the Employer ID, Client ID, Client Federal Entity and Employee ID. - Non Schedule R - This report type provides a breakout of Employer ID and Employee ID.

New York Quarterly Combined Wage Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/New%20York%20Quarterly%20Combined%20Wage%20Report.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/New York Quarterly Combined Wage Report.htm

New York Quarterly Combined Wage Report

Use this form to generate a report to display the original and amended NY Quarterly Combined Wages Report, as well as an employee detail download of those employees with NY SUTA / Income Tax and an exception report (when an employee has negative wages in the reporting quarter) for an employer for a quarter.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

The state of New York has updated their combined reporting file specifications as of 01/01/2025. Click thislinkto visit the official website of New York State for the changes to withholding tax and wage reporting.

As this report can be created in Report Center in CSV format as per the updated specifications, you will need to use the Report Center only to generate this report for Q1 2025 and beyond. However, you can still generate this report in PrismHR for Q4 2024 and prior for past filings and verification of data.

To access the form, under Work Centers, under Tax, click Quarterly Tax Processing. Under Quarterly Tax Reports, under NEW YORK QUARTERLY REPORTS, click New York Quarterly Combined Wage Report.

To generate the New York Quarterly Combined Wage Report for Q1 2025 and beyond:

Use Report Center only to generate this report for any period starting Q1 2025 and beyond. For information on how to generate this report in Report Center, consult the Report Center help documentation located on the Report Center sidebar. If this report is not available for your User ID in Report Center, contact your Report Center Administrator for assistance.

To generate the New York Quarterly Combined Wage Report for Q4 2024 or prior:

  1. Complete the following:
Field Name Description
Report Type Select the report type that you want to run from the following options: - Original - This is the default option. Line 2 Position 127 displays an O in the download file. - Amended - Line 2 Position 127 displays an A in the download file.
  • Original - This is the default option. Line 2 Position 127 displays an O in the download file.
  • Amended - Line 2 Position 127 displays an A in the download file. | Reporting Entity | Select the reporting entity here from the following options: Employer - This is the default option. | | Employer ID | Enter the employer ID here for whom you want to run this report or click the Employer ID link and select it from the Select Employer dialog box. | | Year | Select the year from the drop-down for which you want to run this report. The default is the current year. The drop-down has a 10 year look back starting from the current year. > Note: Note: If you try to generate a report for any quarter for tax year 2025 and beyond by clicking the Generate Report button, you will receive the following notification. No report will be generated. [Image: System message when running report for Q1 2025 and later.] | | Quarter | Select the quarter from the drop-down for which you want to run this report. |
  1. Click Generate Report to generate the report. A job progress window open up. Click Close to close the job progress window. In case of any errors, redo the process. The following three links become visible on the form.

  • Download New York Tax Export File - Click the link to download the report in a .TXT format to your system.

  • View Detail Report - Click the link to view the report on screen.

  • View Exception Report - This exception report generates only when an employee has negative wages in the reporting quarter. Click the link to view the report on screen. If no employee has a negative wage, then this report is not generated.

The Detail report in PrismHR shows the following columns:

  • Employer ID

  • Employee ID

  • Last Name

  • First Name

  • Suta Wages

  • State Taxable

  • Tax Withheld

Pennsylvania Local EIT Quarterly Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Pennsylvania%20Local%20EIT%20Quarterly%20Report.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Pennsylvania Local EIT Quarterly Report.htm

Pennsylvania Local EIT Quarterly Report

Use this form to generate a quarterly report to show the details for one or more Employers of Pennsylvania Local EIT Taxes. This is a single page report for each Municipal Taxing Authority and those employees who have Pennsylvania Local EIT taxes under that authority with a subtotal for the authority. It includes the Gross Pay, Taxable Wages, EIT Withheld, and the Resident PSD code per employee.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, under Work Centers, under Tax, click Quarterly Tax Processing. Under Quarterly Tax Reports, click Pennsylvania Local EIT Quarterly Report.

To generate the Pennsylvania Local EIT Quarterly Report:

  1. Complete the Report Period using the following:
Field Name Description
Tax Year Select the tax year for which you want to run this report. The tax year defaults to the current year, or you may select another one from the drop-down which has a ten year look back.
Tax Quarter Select the tax quarter for which you want to run this report. The tax quarter defaults to the previous quarter, or you may select another one from the drop-down. Valid options between 1, 2, 3 and 4.
Sort Select one of the following sort options for your report: - Employer ID - this is the default option - Client ID
  • Employer ID - this is the default option
  • Client ID | Employer ID | This field is optional. Leave this field blank to run the report for all employers or click the Employer ID link and select the employers from the Select Employer dialog box. |
  1. Click Run to generate the report. The report shows up on screen.

This report shows the following columns:

  • Employee Name/addresses

  • Gross Wages

  • Taxable Wages

  • PA EIT Tax Withheld

  • Resident PSD Code

Exporting Pennsylvania Local Taxes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Pennsylvania-Local-Tax-Exports.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Pennsylvania-Local-Tax-Exports.htm

Exporting Pennsylvania Local Taxes

Use this form to create the following local tax downloads for Pennsylvania:

  • EIT (Earned Income Tax) - For Berkheimer and Keystone

  • LST (Local State Tax) - For Berkheimer

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To build the EIT (Earned Income Tax) download for Keystone:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click Tax > Quarterly Tax Processing > Government Export > Pennsylvania Local Tax Exports.

  2. In the Vendor/Template list, select Keystone.

  3. Complete these fields as required:

In this field — Enter this

Tax Type — Select EIT.

Employer ID — Click the link and select the employer for the download

Year — Select the year for the download. Defaults to the current year.

Reporting Period — Select Quarter or Month

Quarter/Month — If Quarter is selected as the reporting period, select the quarter. If Month is selected, select the month.

  1. Click Generate File. If errors occur, fix them and then rebuild the download.

  2. When the process is complete, click Close to return to the Pennsylvania Local Tax Exports page. You can see a preview of the file by expanding the Preview panel.

  3. Click the Download File to download the file.

To build the EIT (Earned Income Tax) download for Berkheimer:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click Tax > Quarterly Tax Processing > Government Export > Pennsylvania Local Tax Exports.

  2. In the Vendor/Template list, select Berkheimer.

  3. Complete these fields as required:

In this field — Enter this

Tax Type — Select EIT.

Employers — If blank, the download includes all employers. If you want to restrict the download to specific employers, click the Employer ID link and select the employers. Click Done when finished.

Year — Select the year for the download. Defaults to the current year.

Reporting Period — Select Quarter or Month

Quarter/Month — If Quarter is selected as the reporting period, select the quarter. If Month is selected, select the month.

Report by Company — Specify whether to organize the download by company.

Suppress District Limiter — Select this option if you want to send all tax records regardless of the district. Expand the PA Local Districts panel if you want to specify the local districts and then click Save.

  1. Click Generate File. If errors occur, fix them and then rebuild the download.

  2. When the process is complete, click Close to return to the Pennsylvania Local Tax Exports page. You can see a preview of the file by expanding the Preview panel.

  3. Click the Download File to download the file.

To build the Berkheimer LST (Local State Tax) download:

  1. In the Vendor/Template list, select Berkheimer.

  2. Complete these fields as required:

In this field — Enter this

Tax Type — Select LST.

Employers — If blank, the download includes all employers. If you want to restrict the download to specific employers, click the Employer ID link and select the employers. Click Done when finished.

Year — Select the year for the download. Defaults to the current year.

Quarter — Select the quarter for the download.

Report by Company — If selected, the report is organized by company rather than employer.

Suppress District Limiter — Select this option if you want to send all tax records regardless of the district. Expand the PA Local Districts panel if you want to specify the local districts and then click Save.

  1. Click Generate File. If errors occur, fix them and then rebuild the download.

  2. When the process is complete, click Close to return to the Pennsylvania Local Tax Exports page. You can see a preview of the file by expanding the Preview panel.

  3. Click the Download File to download the file.

Periodic Tax JSON Export

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Periodic%20Tax%20JSON%20Export.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Periodic Tax JSON Export.htm

Periodic Tax JSON Export

Use the Periodic Tax JSON Export form to generate PrismHR Tax Periodic JSON export file or to regenerate a processed PTS file in the PrismHR Tax JSON Format.

Note: Note: Client Access Group security is not enabled on this form. PrismHR

To access this form, on the Work Centers under Tax, click PrismHR Tax Processing. Under File Exports, click Periodic Tax JSON Export.

To build the periodic tax JSON export file:

  1. Complete the following fields:
Field Name Description
Build File by Select one of the following options from the following: - All Clients and Employers - This is the default option. Select this option to build the Periodic Payroll Tax Export file for all clients and employers. - Employer ID - Select this option if you want to build the Periodic Payroll Tax Export file for all employers, all employers except some or some employers. Enter the specific Employer IDs in the box on the right or click the Employer ID hyperlink to select them from the Select Employer dialog box. Set the Filter Option field to: - Limit To from the drop-down to build the Periodic Payroll Tax Export file for the specified employers. - Exclude From from the drop-down, to build the Periodic Payroll Tax Export file for all employers except the specified employers. - Client ID - Select this option if you want to build the Periodic Payroll Tax Export file for all client or for all clients except some clients or for some clients. Enter the specific Client IDs in the box on the right or click the Client ID hyperlink to select them from the Client Master Search dialog box. Set the Filter Option field to: - Limit To from the drop-down to build the Periodic Payroll Tax Export file for the specified clients. - Exclude From from the drop-down to build the Periodic Payroll Tax Export file for all clients except the specified clients. - Regenerate Processed PTS File - Select this option to regenerate a processed PTS file in JSON format. Select the appropriate Processed PTS File from the drop-down to regenerate.
  • All Clients and Employers - This is the default option. Select this option to build the Periodic Payroll Tax Export file for all clients and employers.
  • Employer ID - Select this option if you want to build the Periodic Payroll Tax Export file for all employers, all employers except some or some employers. Enter the specific Employer IDs in the box on the right or click the Employer ID hyperlink to select them from the Select Employer dialog box. Set the Filter Option field to:
  • Limit To from the drop-down to build the Periodic Payroll Tax Export file for the specified employers.
  • Exclude From from the drop-down, to build the Periodic Payroll Tax Export file for all employers except the specified employers.
  • Client ID - Select this option if you want to build the Periodic Payroll Tax Export file for all client or for all clients except some clients or for some clients. Enter the specific Client IDs in the box on the right or click the Client ID hyperlink to select them from the Client Master Search dialog box. Set the Filter Option field to:
  • Limit To from the drop-down to build the Periodic Payroll Tax Export file for the specified clients.
  • Exclude From from the drop-down to build the Periodic Payroll Tax Export file for all clients except the specified clients.
  • Regenerate Processed PTS File - Select this option to regenerate a processed PTS file in JSON format. Select the appropriate Processed PTS File from the drop-down to regenerate. | Report Period | - Include All - Select this option to run the periodic tax export for all new TAX.JOURNAL records. - Pay Date Range - Select this option if you want to build the PrismHR Tax Export file for a specific pay date range. Complete the following fields: - Tax Date Start - Select the start date of the pay date range for the PrismHR Tax Export file that you want to generate. - Tax Date End - Select the end date of the pay date range for the PrismHR Tax Export file that you want to generate. Note: Once a file is generated, unless the Run in Test Mode option is selected, the records included will be cleared from the TAX.JOURNAL file to prevent duplicated data. |
  • Include All - Select this option to run the periodic tax export for all new TAX.JOURNAL records.
  • Pay Date Range - Select this option if you want to build the PrismHR Tax Export file for a specific pay date range. Complete the following fields:
  • Tax Date Start - Select the start date of the pay date range for the PrismHR Tax Export file that you want to generate.
  • Tax Date End - Select the end date of the pay date range for the PrismHR Tax Export file that you want to generate. | Run in Test Mode | Select one of the following from the drop-down: - No - This is the default option. If you select this option, the records included will be cleared from the TAX.JOURNAL file to prevent duplicated data. - Yes - If you select this option, the tax journal will not be cleared. These records will be picked up in a future file. > Note: Note: This field should not be set to Yes if the file is being uploaded for processing. |
  • No - This is the default option. If you select this option, the records included will be cleared from the TAX.JOURNAL file to prevent duplicated data.
  • Yes - If you select this option, the tax journal will not be cleared. These records will be picked up in a future file. | Include Audit Report | By default, this checkbox is unchecked. Select this checkbox if you want to include the audit tax report in the JSON tax export. | | Include PrismHR Tax Agency Export | By default, this checkbox is unchecked. Select this checkbox if you want to include the PrismHR Tax Agency Export in the JSON tax export. Selecting this option will create a secondary JSON file for setting up new employers and clients in PrismHR Tax. | | Periodic JSON Export History | This feature helps customers and Support teams quickly locate and re-download previously generated Periodic Tax JSON/PTS export files, reducing the likelihood that processed files are lost. Previously, you had to navigate to Transfer Downloads to PC to retrieve periodic JSON exports. The export history is now available directly on the Periodic Tax JSON Export form. If no historical exports exist, the Periodic JSON Export History subsection displays an empty state message stating No export history found. This subsection renders a table with the following columns (left to right) : - Date/Time - The date and time the file was generated. - Created By - The username of the user who initiated the build. - File Name - The JSON file name is displayed as a hyperlink. Please note that the PTS files are deleted after 60 days. - Audit Report - Click the View hyperlink to access the audit report associated with the export history entry. |
  • Date/Time - The date and time the file was generated.
  • Created By - The username of the user who initiated the build.
  • File Name - The JSON file name is displayed as a hyperlink. Please note that the PTS files are deleted after 60 days.
  • Audit Report - Click the View hyperlink to access the audit report associated with the export history entry.
  1. Click Build to generate the export file. The following hyperlinks appear on the form depending on the selections made:

  • Download PrismHR Tax Export File

  • View Audit Report

  • View Audit Report (CSV)

  • Download PrismHR Tax Agency Export File (If an Account No. and a Routing No. is available on the PrismHR Tax Parameters form, then this report will include the override fields.)Click the appropriate hyperlink to download.

Note: If you are running this build for All Clients and Employers and set the Report Period as Include All, then the build process might take a while.

  1. Click Cancel to clear this form at any time.

Printing Employee W-2 Forms

You can print all Forms W‑2 together or specify ones printed to a particular group by setting certain criteria.

Note: Client Access Group security is not enabled on this form.

To access this form, click Work Centers. In the Work Centers|Tax section, click W-2 Processing, then click Print W-2 Forms.

To print W-2 forms for employees:

  1. Complete the following fields:
Field Name Description
Tax Year Select the tax year to be processed. The default tax year will the prior year based upon today’s date.
Create Forms By Select if you want to generate Form W-2 for employees for: - Employer: Select this option if you want to print Form W-2 for employees for certain employers. Enter the employer IDs here or click the Employer ID link and select the employers from the Select Employer dialog box. - Client: Select this option if you want to print Form W-2 for employees for certain clients. Enter the client IDs here or click the Client ID link and select the clients from the Select Client dialog box. - All (default)
  • Employer: Select this option if you want to print Form W-2 for employees for certain employers. Enter the employer IDs here or click the Employer ID link and select the employers from the Select Employer dialog box.
  • Client: Select this option if you want to print Form W-2 for employees for certain clients. Enter the client IDs here or click the Client ID link and select the clients from the Select Client dialog box.
  • All (default) | Employees | This field is optional. If you want to restrict generating Form W-2 for certain employees, enter them here or click the Employee ID link and select them from the Select Employee dialog box. Leave this field blank to generate Form W-2 for all employees as per selection above. | | Form Type | Select the form type that you want to print from the following options: - S – Simplex, Four (4 panes per employee per page) - D – Duplex, Four - L – Legal Size, Simplex, Four - LB – Legal Size, Simplex, Four - E – Simplex, Four (1 pane per employee per page) - T – Simplex, Two - TS – Simplex, Two (TS) - TA – Simplex, Two (copy A) - GHF – LB Custom Legal Size, Simplex, Four - SPDF - Simplex, Four-Up, Not Self-Mailer PDF - LBPDF - Legal Size, Simplex, Four-Up, Self-Mailer with address panel on bottom > Note: Note: When SPDF or LBPDF is selected, W-2 forms are generated as fillable PDFs and made available for download from W-2 Processing > W-2 Reporting > W-2 Reports. Existing electronic W-2 suppression logic continues to apply. The W2 batch download process has been enhanced to support larger data sets. Starting in 2025 you have the ability to suppress the instruction page when generating the W2 batch. Customers who print and mail Form W-2s in-house will have an enhanced process for 2026 tax year reporting. To reduce challenges reported by alignment and printer settings, PrismHR will now print the complete 4 quadrant Form W-2 which should be used on Blank W2 stock to replace the prior 4-Quad W2 stock. This blank W2 stock produces the IRS instructions and has 4 blank perforated sections that will print directly fromPrismHR. Customers who will be printing Form W-2 in house in 2026 are encouraged to review the enhanced 2025 Form W-2 formats for alignment, data formatting, and functionality prior to printing 2026 Form W-2s at year end. This new functionality currently has the following known issues which will be resolved in an upcoming release prior to Q4. - Printing Form W-2 should ignore electronic Form W-2 employees unless using the reprint - include electronic option – this currently does not work. - Box 14 does not adjust the font size when words fit outside the box and instead cuts off at the box line - this will be fixed. - Control number prints but does not start at 1 and instead starts at 2, this also affects the sort which does not work. - Reprint - Reissued statement does not appear. - When sorting by any option other than name, the generated zip file references the alpha range for names. The 2025 PDF forms have been added to support the current development towards the new 2026 Form W-2 format. Please note the following process change if testing the 2025 W2 PDF forms: - Do not rebuild Form W-2 data as this will reset already processed Form W-2 data - Print W-2 Forms: - Print W2 Form Type S or LB (previously supported format) before printing new PDF form type - Print W2 Form Type SPDF or LBPDF When printing the new PDF form type, if previously supported format is not printed first an error will appear “No W2 Forms selected”. This will be resolved for 2026 Form W-2 year-end printing. |

Setting Up Tax Parameters

Use the PrismHR Tax Parameters form to set up parameters to be used for various needs in the PrismHR Tax files. This form is currently informational only with future development planned for future quarters.

Note: Note: Client Access Group security is not enabled on this form.

To access this form, on the Work Centers under Tax, click PrismHR Tax Processing. Under Setup, click PrismHR Tax Parameters.

To set up PrismHR Tax Parameters:

  1. Complete the following fields:
Field Name Description
PrismHR Tax Interface Active This field is currently inactive. Functionality will be released later in 2025.
PrismHR Periodic File Version Select one of the following options: - Version 01 - This is the only options available at this time.
  • Version 01 - This is the only options available at this time. | PrismHR Quarterly File Version | Select one of the following options: - Version 01 - This is the only options available at this time. |
  • Version 01 - This is the only options available at this time. | Include Schedule R Reporting | This field is currently inactive. Functionality will be released later in 2025. | | Regenerate processed PTS file record count | By default, the regenerate processed PTS will present the last ten pts files. Entering a number here allows you to expand that number to a larger look-back. > Note: Note: Do not enter more than 20 here. | | PrismHRTax Override Parameters For PrismHR Tax customers, the PrismHR Tax Parameters include this option to override the default banking information in the Client Setup files. The banking information entered here will be used for future debits and payments. | | | Include PrismHR Tax ID in Override Client ID | This field is optional. This field is unchecked by default. - Unchecked - When unchecked the OverrideClientId field in the JSON output will NOT include the Prism Tax ID whether assigned to the System or Employer. This means the system will also not pick up the Override Employer Suffix Code. Example - Checked - When checked the OverrideClientId field in the JSON output will include the Prism Tax ID whether assigned to the System or Employer. This means the system will also pick up the Override Employer Suffix Code. |
  • Unchecked - When unchecked the OverrideClientId field in the JSON output will NOT include the Prism Tax ID whether assigned to the System or Employer. This means the system will also not pick up the Override Employer Suffix Code. Example
  • Checked - When checked the OverrideClientId field in the JSON output will include the Prism Tax ID whether assigned to the System or Employer. This means the system will also pick up the Override Employer Suffix Code. | Override Employer Suffix Code | This code will append to any employer record with an identifier override. All other records will not include a suffix code. - If there is a PTM Identifier Number (for example ABC) entered on the Employer Details form (Emp ID 6485), and an Override Employer Suffix Code (for example XYZ) is entered on this form, then this suffix code will append to the client code (for example E6485XYX) for any employer record with an override identifier. - If no PTM Identifier Number is entered on the Employer Details form, then the client code will not add the Override Employer Suffix Code and will remain as is (from the above example E6485). Any employer that does not have the employer override will continue to use the System PTM code as the Processor ID. - This will also apply to the Daily Tax Export JSON output and to both the stand alone file and the Include PTM Tax Agency Export file output using the Daily Tax Export form. |
  • If there is a PTM Identifier Number (for example ABC) entered on the Employer Details form (Emp ID 6485), and an Override Employer Suffix Code (for example XYZ) is entered on this form, then this suffix code will append to the client code (for example E6485XYX) for any employer record with an override identifier.
  • If no PTM Identifier Number is entered on the Employer Details form, then the client code will not add the Override Employer Suffix Code and will remain as is (from the above example E6485). Any employer that does not have the employer override will continue to use the System PTM code as the Processor ID.
  • This will also apply to the Daily Tax Export JSON output and to both the stand alone file and the Include PTM Tax Agency Export file output using the Daily Tax Export form. | Bank Name | This field is optional. Enter the name of the bank of the client. | | Bank Address | This field is optional. Enter the address of the bank. | | City | This field is optional. Enter the city of the bank. | | State | This field is optional. Enter the two digit state code of the bank. | | Zip Code | This field is optional. Enter the two digit state code of the bank. | | Bank Contact | This field is optional. Enter the name of the contact person of the bank. | | Bank Phone No | This field is optional. Enter the phone number of the bank. | | Account No. | This field is optional. Enter the account number of the client in this bank. This field cannot be blank if a Routing No. is provided. You will get an error stating Account Number is required. When this field has a value, the PrismHRTax Agency Report generated using either the PrismHR Tax Client Setup Export form or the Periodic Tax JSON Export form will include the override fields. | | Routing No. | This field is optional. Enter the ABA routing number of this bank. This field cannot be blank if an Account No. is provided. You will get an error stating Transit Number is required. When this field has a value, the PrismHRTax Agency Report generated using either the PrismHR Tax Client Setup Export form or the Periodic Tax JSON Export form will include the override fields. | | Fractional No. | This field is optional. Enter the fractional number of the ABA routing number of this bank. |
  1. Click Save to save the parameters set on this form.

Working with PrismHR Tax Processing

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/PrismHR%20Tax%20Processing.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/PrismHR Tax Processing.htm

Working with PrismHR Tax Processing

Under the Work Centers menu, under the Tax section, a new group named PrismHR Tax Processing is added. This is a central location to access the PrismHR tax setup and reporting forms.

[Image: screenshot]

The following two sections are available under PrismHR Tax Processing work center:

  • Setup - this section contains the following two forms:

  • PrismHR Tax Client Setup Export - Use this form to build the PrismHR Client Setup JSON export file. This will create an initial JSON export for setting up an initial group of client data in PrismHR Tax.

  • PrismHR Tax Parameters - Use this form to set up parameters to be used for various needs in the PrismHR Tax files. This form is currently informational only with future development planned for future quarters.

  • File Exports

  • Periodic Tax JSON Export - Use the Periodic Tax JSON Export form to generate PTS periodic tax JSON export file or to regenerate processed PTS periodic tax JSON export file.

  • Quarterly Tax JSON Export - The quarterly tax JSON export will be supported in a future release. More information will be available in a future release.

Exporting the QEX Plus 941 File

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/QEX-941-Export.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/QEX-941-Export.htm

Exporting the QEX Plus 941 File

QEX Plus is a third-party software application that imports information and processes IRS tax payments for certified PEOs. The QEX Plus 941 Export form builds three .csv files that are uploaded to QEX Plus for processing.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To export and process the QEX Plus 941 file:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click Tax > Quarterly Tax Processing > 3rd-Party Exports > 941 File Processing.

  2. Complete these fields as required:

Field — Description

Employer ID — Click the link and select the ID of the employer whose information is being uploaded and processed.

Year — Year for the tax information.

Quarter — Quarter of the year for this tax information. For example, 1 indicates first quarter, and so forth.

Include Schedule R? — Generates a third, optional file that breaks out federal taxes by client. Enabling this field displays the Schedule R Report field.

Deposit Schedule — Specifies the frequency at which the employer makes deposits. Options are Monthly and Semi-Monthly.

941 Worksheet — Builds the Form 941 worksheet.

941 Schedule B — Builds Form 941 Schedule B.

Schedule R Report — Builds the Schedule R report.

  1. Click Build.

Reporting Qualified Overtime and Tips

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Qualified%20Tips.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Qualified Tips.htm

Reporting Qualified Overtime and Tips

Use the Qualified Tips and Overtime form to update the annual data for qualified overtime and qualified tips to report them in the employee Form W-2 for the tax year This option is provided to support federal reporting and compliance requirements supporting the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA). For more information, please visit the article named OBBBA No Tax Setup Guide on the Customer Resource Center. If an employee works for multiple clients in a tax year, this form will report information for the activeclient only. If an employee works for multiple clients in the same employer, then Box 14 will have combined amounts when built on the employer. W2 data will be aggregated by employer if applicable. If an employee works between multiple positions, you should determine a single TTO Code for reporting purposes.

Box 14 of the employee Form W-2 reports the qualified tips and overtime dollar amounts against the following applicable designations for SBEA and employer builds:

  • Approx Qualified OT

  • TTOC <TTO Code1>; Cash Tips

Note: Note: You cannot access this form using the search bar.

To access this form for an employee, select the employee in the Employee Details form. From the Actions menu, select the Qualified Tips and Overtime form for the employee for the client.

Note: This information can also be added via the Data Import Tool.

To report qualified overtime and tips for an employee for an active client:

  1. Complete the following fields:

Field Name — Description

Employee ID — This field is auto-populated with the Employee ID from the Employee Details form.

Client ID — This field is auto-populated with the active Client ID.

Employer ID — If the employee has more than one employer for the active client in the tax year, select the Employer ID for the list of employer IDs available in the drop-down. This list will populate the main employer for the client and any alternate employer assigned to the client.

Entity ID — If the active client is set up to have a Client Federal Entity, it will display here. Note: If the client was cloned from another client prior to the option to clone the Client Federal Entity on the utility, you may see a federal entity when there should not be. If this occurs you should remove the entity on the client by following the steps listed here.

Year — Select the tax year.

TTO Code — Enter the TTO Code (Tipped Taxable Occupation Code) manually, or you can click the TTO Code hyperlink and select it from the TTO Codes dialog.

TTOC Tip Amount — Enter the TTOC Tip Amount for the corresponding TTO Code.

Premium OT Amount — Enter an approximate premium portion of overtime, if applicable.

  1. Click Save to save the record.

  2. Click Cancel to clear the form. Changes made to this form will be removed, but the auto-populated fields will display as is.

  3. Click Delete to delete the record.

  4. Click Close to close this form at any time.

Exporting Quarterly Tax JSON File

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Quarterly%20Tax%20JSON%20Export.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Quarterly Tax JSON Export.htm

Exporting Quarterly Tax JSON File

Use the Quarterly Tax JSON Export form to review the various tax registers and generate a file in a JSON format for PrismHR Tax processing. Run this process quarterly and use it to reconcile the wage and tax amounts that were reported through the Periodic JSON Tax report for the previous quarter. This format currently only supports the non-SBEA required output. The SBEA format will be released in 2025. More information will be available in a future release.

State specific information has been added to the JSON quarterly download. If data point is missing that state specific field is not populated for example, if LASUI is missing, then that position will not be populated.

PSD codes have been applied to the quarterly tax JSON export to ensure the data matches the daily tax JSON export.

Note: Note: Client Access Group security is not enabled on this form.

To access this form, on the Work Centers under Tax, click PrismHR Tax Processing. Under File Exports, click Quarterly Tax JSON Export.

To build the quarterly tax JSON export file:

  1. Complete the following fields:
Field Name Description
Tax Year Select the appropriate tax year from the drop-down menu. The default is the current year with a 10 year look back.
Tax Quarter Select the appropriate tax quarter for which you want to build export from the following options: - 1 (default) - 2 - 3 - 4
  • 1 (default)
  • 2
  • 3
  • 4 | #### Reporting Filters | | | All Clients and Employers | This is the default option. | | Limit to Client ID | If you want to limit this export to a particular client, enter the Client ID here. Leave this field blank to build the export file for all clients. | | Limit to Employer ID | If you want to limit this export to certain employers, then select this option and enter their Employer IDs here. Leave this field blank to build the export file for all employers. > Note: Note: When you select this option, a new field named Includeclientreportable taxes for PEOclients displays. This field is a checkbox. By default this field is unchecked. |

  1. Click Build to build the quarterly tax JSON export file for the selected tax year and the tax quarter.

  2. Click Clear to clear this form at any time.

On the File History section, you can select the following fields:

  • Tax Year - Select the tax year for which you want to view the file history.

  • Tax Quarter - Select the tax quarter for the corresponding tax year selected above to display the corresponding quarterly tax JSON export files.

Note: Note: Development is already in progress after which this File History section on the Quarterly Tax JSON Export form will have more reports added to it in future releases.

Building the Employer Quarterly SUTA Tax Export

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Quarterly-SUTA-Exports/Employer-Quarterly-SUTA-Tax-Export.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Quarterly-SUTA-Exports/Employer-Quarterly-SUTA-Tax-Export.htm

Building the Employer Quarterly SUTA Tax Export

Use this form to create electronic files that contain state unemployment data that will be sent to the various states. Each state has a different format.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To build the quarterly SUTA tax processing file for download:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click Tax > Quarterly Tax Processing > Government Exports > Employer Quarterly SUTA Tax Export.

  2. Complete these fields as required:

Field Description
State State that the quarterly SUTA tax file is based on. If South Carolina is selected, these fields appear: - Taxable Gross Wages (Gross Wages minus non taxable earnings and section 125 sheltered earnings) - Report Gross Wages If Louisiana is selected, the system displays: Do any of your employee’s report wages to other states in addition to Louisiana?
  • Taxable Gross Wages (Gross Wages minus non taxable earnings and section 125 sheltered earnings)
  • Report Gross Wages | File Format | Select a file format relevant to the selected state. The state selected limits the available file formats. | | Employers | You can select from All Employers, All ASOs, All PEOs, or Selected Employers (default). If you select multiple employers, you can generate individual files for each employer or consolidate all employers into a single file. | | Employer / Employer Name | ID and name of the employer to be processed on this download. You can search by Employer ID or Employer Name. | | Tax Year | Year the quarterly download is based on. | | Tax Quarter | Quarter the quarterly download is based on. | | Output Filename | Name of the file to be downloaded. This is determined during the build. |

  1. Click Build. A progress window opens.

  2. Click Close when the report building is finished. You are presented with these options:

  • Download File

  • Download Report

  • Download Report CSV

  1. Click one of these export links and the file is downloaded.

File History

File History provides a way to save historical files and download them more than once. File History is closed by default, but can be expanded by clicking +. Filters let you narrow down search options by State, Employer ID, Tax Year, or Tax Quarter. In this example, Massachusetts was chosen as the State filter.

[Image: screenshot]

You can download historical files as .txt or .csv file by clicking the hyperlinks. In this example, if you click the first link under Report, the report is displayed and you can print it, save as PDF, or download in .XLS format.

Rebuilding the Tax Journal

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Rebuild-Tax-Journal.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Rebuild-Tax-Journal.htm

Rebuilding the Tax Journal

When PrismHR posts a payroll, it collects voucher data and writes it to the TAX.JOURNAL file. The Mastertax PTS export file is built based on values stored in the TAX.JOURNAL file. The final step of these processes is archiving voucher data from the file, so that voucher data is not reported twice. It is possible that either of these files can become corrupted, so you need to rebuild this file using historical payroll data. The Rebuild Tax Journal file completes this process.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To rebuild the journal:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From Employer|Action, select Rebuild Tax Journal file.

  3. Complete these fields as required.

Field — Description

Clear Tax Journal prior to rebuild? — Select No so that the process does not delete existing values. Payroll vouchers that are selected in the next screen are added. Select Yes to delete all values in TAX.JOURNAL before rebuilding. Contact PrismHR Support before attempting this action.

Use Pay Date or Post Date — Determines the data to look at when adding voucher data back to the tax journal.

Pay Dates — Start/End Pay Date: Enter the starting and ending pay dates for this rebuild process.

Post Dates — Start/End Post Date: Enter the starting and ending posting dates for this rebuild process.

Employer ID — Select the employer ID for this process.

Client ID — Optional: Select the client ID for this process.

  1. Click Run. The system asks if you want to proceed.

  2. Click Yes. The system displays a rebuild progress window.

  3. Click Report to view or download the report. See Viewing the Job Control Status Report

Building the Reconciliation Tax Summary

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Recon-Tax-Summary.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Recon-Tax-Summary.htm

Building the Reconciliation Tax Summary

The MasterTax RTS (Reconciliation Tax Summary) file build process reviews the various tax registers and generates a file in a specific format for a third party vendor called MasterTax. Run this process quarterly and use it to reconcile the check amounts that were imported throughout the previous three months. Now, positive and or negative adjustments made in the grid in the FUTA Credit Adjustment Entry form displays on the MasterTax Reconciliation Tax Summary (RTS). The values entered in the grid adjust the state XX-17 total YTD value in the RTS. This will not require a register rebuild, instead when you run the RTS, any value in the grid will offset either the E or F code record based on the Employet and/or Client setup.

Adjustments to the xx-17 record will be saved and stored to the Futa Credit Adjustment Entry grid for each employee.

The 501 record is reduced in statistic four (which is the employee count) by any employee in which an adjustment reduces their FUTA taxable wages to 0 for the state, or increase the 501 record by any employee in which an adjustment adds fUTA taxable wages that were not originally to be reported.

There are multiple versions of this form as well as a NON SBEA and SBEA build that look to different tax registers when generating the values on the file. These build types are controlled by the MasterTax Interface parameter form.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To build the RTS file:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, click MasterTax Processing > File Exports > Mastertax RTS File Build.

  2. Complete these fields as required:

Field Description
Tax Year Tax year for this build.
Tax Quarter Tax quarter for this build.
Limit to Employer Filters so that the file generated only contains tax information for a specific employer.
Include client reportable taxes for PEO clients Client-reported taxes that are under the client’s FEIN or unemployment ID. This only displays when the Limit to Employer field has a set value.
Limit to Client Client ID that this build is limited to. This only applies to client SUTA reporting states.
Build FUTA Exempt Records This only applies when running an RTS build for the fourth quarter.
Exclude Pennsylvania local taxes when no tax has been withheld Enable to exclude PA local taxes if no tax has been withheld.
Include zero taxable wages for Ohio non-resident local tax Enable to include zero taxable wages for Ohio non-resident local tax.
Limit to ASO/ASA/PAY service types Enable to limit this build to ASO/ASA/PAY service types.
Build SBEA certified relationship file Enable to build an SBEA certified relationship file.
Use tax code 00-87 to determine SS credit within MasterTax? > Note: Note: This setting applies to 2021 COVID-19 tax reporting. If selected, the system performs the following calculation during the RTS build: (00-87 tax amount associated with line item) / (0.062). After computing this value, the system uses this value to fill in Statistic 1 of the 501 record for tax code 00-81, up to the value reported under 00-81 on the 500 record. If any amount remains after reaching the 00-81 reporting value, the system enters the remainder into Statistic 1 of the 501 record for tax code 00-80. For more details about these tax codes, see the COVID-19 Feature Guide.
Use COVID Credits as post March 31? > Note: Note: This setting applies to 2021 COVID-19 tax reporting. The federal government makes a distinction, for reporting purposes, between COVID-19 credits accrued before and after April 1 2021, since this is the date the American Rescue Plan Act (ARP or ARPA) took effect. Select this option to consider any COVID-19 credits accrued in Q2 2021 as “post-March 31” credits, which means they were accrued subject to the American Rescue Plan Act. These credits will be reported accordingly on the RTS file. On the file itself, this means: - On 501 records for 00-80 and 00-81, the full value under these tax codes populates under statistic 1. - On FE0000-116H and FE0000-117H records, statistic 1 is set to 0. For more details about reporting COVID-19 tax credits, see the COVID-19 Feature Guide.
  • On 501 records for 00-80 and 00-81, the full value under these tax codes populates under statistic 1.
  • On FE0000-116H and FE0000-117H records, statistic 1 is set to 0. | RTS File History | You can save and download historical files with the following information: - The date and time the process was started - The user who started the process - A hyperlink to download the file - SBEA Relationship file - RTS file summary report - RTS file detail report |
  • The date and time the process was started
  • The user who started the process
  • A hyperlink to download the file
  • SBEA Relationship file
  • RTS file summary report
  • RTS file detail report | Configuration Information | Displays the MasterTax version number. You cannot build an RTS file unless you are using MasterTax Version 39 or greater. |
  1. Click Build. A progress window displays. You can download an RTS file, or view an audit detail or summary report.

Note: Note: If an RTS build process is already running when you attempt to build the file, the system displays a message stating that the process is currently running for and was started at . You cannot build the file until the current process has finished.

Exporting Retirement Contributions

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Retirement-Exports/Retirement-Exports.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Retirement-Exports/Retirement-Exports.htm

Exporting Retirement Contributions

An export file contains data extracted from the system, often to provide to another party. The Retirement Exports form offers multiple retirement export types from a single page. These export types are shown in the Vendor/Template field. When you select an export type from the list, the fields relevant to that type display. Once the export file is generated, you can export it to your computer.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form. If client selection is left blank to run for all clients, only clients to which you have access are available.

To access the form, click Back Office. Under Operations|Action, click Retirement Exports.

To generate a retirement export:

  1. Select a Vendor/Template from the following options, and complete the fields as required:

  • 401(k) Extended Download

  • ADP

  • Anico

  • Boston Land

  • Fascorp

  • Generic (Non Third Party) Retirement Export

  • Great West

  • ING

  • John Hancock

  • Kentucky Retirement Systems

  • Lincoln Financial

  • Mass Mutual

  • Michigan Benefit Services

  • Pallet

  • Pinnacle

  • Ruby

  • Slavic

  • The Standard

  • Transamerica

  • Wells Fargo

  1. Click Generate File. A new job progress window opens and displays the processing status as the download is built. Fix any errors that are found and then rebuild the download.

Note: The system only allows one user at a time to build the file, which accommodates the fixed format in the output filename.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Close to close the job progress window.

  2. The Preview section shows a preview of the text file - up to 100 records show up on the Preview section. If there are more than 100 records a pop up window tells you the number of records ready for export. Click OK to close the pop up window. [Image: screenshot]

  3. Click Download File to download the .txt file.

  4. Click Clear to clear the screen.

Field — Description

End Pay Date — Enter the end date of the pay period to include in the export download.

Clients — This field is optional. Leave this field blank to run the export for all clients. If you want to run this export for selected clients, enter the Client IDs or click Client ID and select them from the Select Clients list.

Include 1099 Employees — By default, this field is disabled and 1099 employees are not included. Enable this field if you want to include 1099 employees in the export.

Field — Description

End Pay Date — Enter the end date of the pay period to include in the export download.

Clients — This field is optional. Leave this field blank to run the export for all clients. If you want to run this export for selected clients, enter the Client IDs or click Client ID and select them from the Select Clients list.

Include 1099 Employees — By default, this field is disabled and 1099 employees are not included. Enable this field if you want to include 1099 employees in the export.

Include Hours-paid for non-productive Pay Codes — Enter non-productive pay codes. The hours paid for these pay codes are included in the total hours that display in the export file.

Exclude Hours-worked for Productive Pay Codes — Enter productive pay codes. The hours for these pay codes are not included in the total hours that display in the export file.

Running Tax Register Reports

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Tax_Register_Report.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Tax_Register_Report.htm

Running Tax Register Reports

There are two different Tax Register Reports that display basic tax information (such as gross taxable earnings and tax amounts) for a given tax year and quarter. The two report types are:

  • Employer Summary – displays tax data by tax type (no employee data)

  • Employer Detail – displays tax data by employee

This report is useful for verifying changes to tax registers or to the MasterTax RTS file – for example, if a register rebuild is needed.

To run the Tax Register Report:

  1. In the Reports menu, select Payroll|Report > Tax Register Report Entry.

  2. For Report Type, select either Employer Detail or Employer Summary.

Note: If you set a user role’s security for the Show Unmasked SSN field to Enable on the Field Security Maintenance form and select Employer Detail in this step, the Show Unmasked SSN field displays. Selecting this field displays the employee’s full Social Security number in the report instead of only the last four digits.

  1. Enter the Tax Year and Quarter as appropriate. You can also run the report for All quarters.

  2. You can limit the report to specific Employers, Tax Authorities, and taxes (Tax IDs), if needed.

  3. Click Build Data. A Job Control form displays the progress of the data build. Click Close when the build finishes.

  4. If the build was successful, a new Run Report button displays. Click this button to download the report.

Report Outputs

This first example was run with the following parameters:

  • Employer Summary

  • All quarters

  • All tax authorities and IDs

  • one Employer ID

[Image: screenshot]

This second example was run with the following parameters:

  • All quarters

  • All tax authorities and IDs

  • one Employer ID
