Transferring Employees to New Clients

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/Transfer-EE.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/Transfer-EE.htm

Transferring Employees to New Clients

You can move employee records and accompanying check information to a different client using the Transfer Employee to New Client form.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To move records:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From Operations|Action, select Transfer Employee to New Client.

  3. Complete these fields as required:

Field Description
From Client/To Client From Client: Click the link and select the client ID for the client that the employee is transferring from. To Client: Click the link and select the client ID for the client that the employee is transferring to. > Note: Note: To ensure that an employee remains enrolled in a benefit plan after transfer. benefit plans must be set up in the To Client.
Employee/To Employee Employee: Click the link and select the ID of the employee whose information requires a transfer. To Employee: Displays the employee ID for the company where the employee is being transferred.
Employer/To Employer Employer: Displays the employer ID assigned to the current client. To Employer: Displays the employer ID assigned to the new client where the employee is being transferred. Observe the following behavior that occurs during these transfer scenarios: - If the new client and the current (old) client have different primary employer IDs and the same Service Type of Professional Employer (PEO), you can perform a valid transfer of employees between those clients by selecting the employee’s new employer ID, which the system updates in the employee record under the new client. In addition, if you select the non-primary employer ID in the above scenario, a transfer alert displays, “The primary employer for Client <new/to client ID> is <primary employer ID>. You will receive payroll calculation errors for this employee if Employer <selected Employer ID that is non-primary> is not set up as an alternate employer in this client.” - If the new client and the current client have different primary employer IDs and different Service Types, such as PEO and ASO, or they both have the same ASO Service Type, when you enter the full employee ID or paste the employee ID in the Employee field, you can only select a valid (primary) employer ID. Also, after you make the selection, the To Employee field displays “New Employee will be created.”
  • If the new client and the current (old) client have different primary employer IDs and the same Service Type of Professional Employer (PEO), you can perform a valid transfer of employees between those clients by selecting the employee’s new employer ID, which the system updates in the employee record under the new client.
  • If the new client and the current client have different primary employer IDs and different Service Types, such as PEO and ASO, or they both have the same ASO Service Type, when you enter the full employee ID or paste the employee ID in the Employee field, you can only select a valid (primary) employer ID. Also, after you make the selection, the To Employee field displays “New Employee will be created.” | Pay Group/To Pay Group | Pay Group: Displays the employee’s current pay group. To Pay Group: Select a pay group for the destination client. The search contains only valid pay groups for the destination client. | | Current Retire Plan/To Retire Plan | Current Retire Plan: Displays the currently enrolled retirement plan. To Retire Plan: Displays the retirement plan where the employee is being transferred. | | Current Position/To Position | Current Position: Displays the employee’s current position. To Position: Select or enter a valid position for the destination client. (If you select this field, the Select Position list that displays contains only valid positions for the destination client.) | | Last Hire Date | After selecting an employee associated with the From Client selection, the employee’s last hire date displays in this field. | | To Location | Select or enter a valid location for the destination client. (If you select this field, the Select Location Code list that displays contains only valid locations for the destination client.) | | To Benefit Group | Select or enter a valid benefit group for the destination client. (If you select this field, the Select Benefit Groups list that displays contains only valid benefit groups for the destination client.) | | To Client Hire Date | Enter or select the hire date to use for the company where the employee is being transferred. After entering or selecting a date in this field, a dialog containing that date displays. Select Yes to confirm that date should be used to update the Status, Type, Status Type History, Position History, and Pay History. If you select No, the system updates that information using the most recent date for that record in the From Client employee record after the transfer finishes. Note: If you re-enter a new date in this field after selecting an option in this dialog, the dialog displays again. After you select an option in the dialog, the following occurs: - Yes: A transfer alert message displays: “Employee Status, Type, Status Type History, Position History and Pay History dates will be <date from To client hire date field>.” - No: A transfer alert message displays: “Employee Status, Type, Status Type History, Position History and Pay History dates will be the most recent date from Client <ID of the From Client>.” |
  • Yes: A transfer alert message displays: “Employee Status, Type, Status Type History, Position History and Pay History dates will be <date from To client hire date field>.”
  • No: A transfer alert message displays: “Employee Status, Type, Status Type History, Position History and Pay History dates will be the most recent date from Client <ID of the From Client>.” | Transfer Y-T-D Check Stubs | Transfers the year-to-date check stub details to the company the employee is transferring to. | | Terminate Employee in Original Client | Select this option only if you want to terminate the employee and their benefits in the original client. When you select this option, a mandatory date field displays, so you can accept the current date (default) or enter or select which date the transferring employee will be terminated in their old client. > Note: Note the following: - The date field only displays if you select the Terminate Employee in Original Client field. - The date field is mandatory, so you must either accept the current (default) date or select a date, which can be a future or past date. Otherwise, when you complete the other fields but leave this field blank, an error message displays when you click Transfer, “All mandatory fields must be filled in.” - If you enter a future date, the status and status date information do not update in the employee record until the termination date occurs. However, the status type history record immediately reflects the future-dated information. - When you select the Terminate Employee in Original Client field, a transfer alert displays, “Terminating the employee in the original client can cause a change to the employee’s Benefits Thru Date in the original client.” |
  • The date field only displays if you select the Terminate Employee in Original Client field.
  • The date field is mandatory, so you must either accept the current (default) date or select a date, which can be a future or past date. Otherwise, when you complete the other fields but leave this field blank, an error message displays when you click Transfer, “All mandatory fields must be filled in.”
  • If you enter a future date, the status and status date information do not update in the employee record until the termination date occurs. However, the status type history record immediately reflects the future-dated information.
  • When you select the Terminate Employee in Original Client field, a transfer alert displays, “Terminating the employee in the original client can cause a change to the employee’s Benefits Thru Date in the original client.” | Term Reason Code | Select a valid termination reason code (only those codes with “Termination” included in their Valid Actions on the Employee Termination form display) for the original client when transferring and terminating an employee in one action. Running the W-2 Reconciliation Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Employer/W-2-Reconciliation-Report.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Employer/W-2-Reconciliation-Report.htm

Running the W-2 Reconciliation Report

Social Security’s Old-Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance (OASDI) program limits the amount of earnings subject to taxation for a given year. The W-2 Reconciliation Report compares OASDI with Medicare to determine whether the wage data processed by the SSA was less than the amount reported to the IRS. If the wage data is different, the SSA assumes that the processed earnings are incorrect.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To run the W-2 Reconciliation report:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, select Tax > W-2 Processing > W-2 Reporting > W-2 Reconciliation Report.

  2. Select an Employer ID from the selector that opens.

  3. Select a Tax Year from the drop-down.

  4. Click Run. If errors occur, fix them and run the report again.

  5. Click Close. The system displays the report. You can click the XLS link to download the report.

Assigning a Benefit Commission Code

When you create a commission based on the benefit commission type, the system bases the calculations on any plans that have that type defined in the special options.

To assign a benefit commission code to a benefit plan, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From Operations|Change, select Group Benefit Plans.

  3. Enter or select a benefit plan ID for the plan you want to edit.

  4. Scroll down to the Special Options panel.

  5. Enter a Commission Type Code. Make the code simple, such as DENT for Dental. You can create as many benefit commission codes as needed, but you can only assign one code to a specific benefit plan.

  6. Click Save.

  7. Repeat for each plan that requires this commission code.

  8. Enter that code in the Based On Item field of the commission plan. When the code entered on the commission plan matches the code on the group benefit plan, the commission calculation includes that benefit plan. [Image: screenshot]

Grouping Commissions

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Front_Matter/Commission_Groupings.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Front_Matter/Commission_Groupings.htm

Grouping Commissions

PrismHR’s commission plan grouping feature enables the system to compare the results of the commission calculations and, according to how you arrange the groups, apply only the commission structure with the lowest or highest result. The grouping feature also enables the system to choose between commission results that use the same basis for calculation.

When the system calculates commissions, it totals the commission amounts within the same numbered group and compares the results against the results of other groups. The group with the highest or lowest commission amount (depending on what is indicated in the Commission Group Highest or Lowest field) is the one added to the commissions of the salespeople assigned to the commission plan.

For example, this example shows that the salesperson’s commission is the total of the fourth commission line (benefit plans with the commission code MED) plus whichever group is the highest:

  • Gross wages or admin fees (Group 1)

  • Active lives (Group 2) [Image: screenshot]

User Roles, Users, and MFA Security

PrismHR uses role-based security to manage user accounts. The use of multi-factor authentication (MFA) further ensures security.

Administrative users control system access across multiple dimensions to ensure that company, client, user, and employee information is secure and protected. Access controls include:

  • Limiting user access to the system with user roles and user types

  • Configuring user access based on IP address

  • Configuring user printer access

  • Setting up strong login security, including multi-factor authentication, account locks, and password expiration

  • Limiting user access to clients with Client Access Groups

You might need to make an adjustment to a commission calculation if there was an error. You need to make an adjustment rather than altering the commission setup; if you alter the permanent data, you would create conflicting reports. To avoid this accounting problem, make an adjustment that displays in an adjustment column in reports and justifies the new total amounts.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter the Client ID for which you are going to adjust the commission balance.

  • To add an amount to the salesperson’s net commission, enter a positive amount.

  • To subtract an amount from the net commission, enter a negative amount.

The Net Commission and Grand Total display the new amounts.

  1. You can enter new lines, if needed. Be sure that this is what you want to do because once you save, you cannot remove the line. (You can only adjust it as described in step 3.)

To enter a new line, do the following:

Field Name — Description

Salesperson — Enter the user ID of the Salesperson, which must be a service provider user with the Sales Representative account management role.

Commission Adjustment — Enter the Commission Adjustment, as described above.

The Net Commission and Grand Total display the new amounts.

  1. Click Save to finalize the adjustments in the system.

Computing Commissions

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Compute_Commissions.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Compute_Commissions.htm

Computing Commissions

The Compute Commissions form calculates all salesperson commission assignments, based on the client invoices, and includes them in the Commission Report. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To calculate all salesperson commission assignments:

  1. From Operations|Action, select Compute Commissions.

  2. If required, enter the Begin Date and End Date. The system bases the computation on the date range that you enter, which coincides with client invoice dates. If you leave these fields blank, all outstanding commissions to the present date will be included in the computation and marked as computed.

When you enter the date range, be mindful of the way the commissions were set to calculate. For example, commissions are paid out once a month and your organization has a commission based on the number of active lives. If you run the report twice during the month instead of once, the salesperson would be set to receive twice the proper amount.

  1. If you are recalculating commissions, select Clear Comm to replace the previous commissions computations with the new information.

  2. Enter the numbers of the Flat Amt Group(s) to include in the calculation, if flat amount groups are specified in the plans. For example, entering 12 would include groups 1 and 2, and entering 135 would include groups 1, 3, and 5, and salespeople assigned to the specified flat amount group will receive the amount.

Note: For flat-rate commissions that are based on the Benefit Commission Type, the system applies the commission per billed enrollment (as opposed to per invoice).

  1. Enter each Company ID of the clients for which you need to calculate commissions.

  2. Click Start Computation.

  3. Click Yes in the message that prompts you to confirm that you want to start computing commissions.

The system displays a window to show that the computations are running. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. When the computation is complete, click Close.

The system displays a printable report. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. After computing the commissions and closing the on-screen report, the Download Pay File link displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click the Download Pay File link to download a .csv file that contains the following commission data that was just calculated:

  • Client ID

  • Employee ID

  • Salesperson Name

  • Commission Amount

Note: Note the following:

Working with the Custom Code Translation Table

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Custom_Code_Translation_Table.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Custom_Code_Translation_Table.htm

Working with the Custom Code Translation Table

Use the Custom Code Translation Table for PrismHR-assisted data conversions only. Custom Code Translation Tables are used to create and maintain mapping/translation tables to convert legacy software data into PrismHR.

Adding and Updating Translation Codes

  1. Select the Table ID. The Table ID is used to categorize different types of codes.

  2. Enter Legacy Code. Enter the code from the legacy platform. This must be a unique value.

  3. Enter the Prism Code. Enter the corresponding Prism Code related to the Legacy Code on the same row.

  4. Enter Additional Columns. Enter additional Prism Codes in the applicable columns for each table.

  5. Click Save.

Most data conversions use a standard set of translation (mapping) tables. The format and need for each type of table will vary based on your specific conversion. Use the various column headings as a guide on how to enter each translation table. For more information, see the section Translation Table Overview.

If there are a large quantity of codes you need to add to the table at once, Data Engineering can upload them for you. Prepare a spreadsheet per Table ID with a layout matching the headings of the Tabe ID and send to your Data Engineer.

Sorting Codes

Sort By — Use the drop-downs menus to sort the specific column by ascending or descending order.

Searching Codes

  1. Search—Use the drop-down to select either the Legacy Code or Prism Code column for a specific value.

  2. Search Value—Enter the specific value you want to search for. This value can be the entire code or a portion of the code. The search will look for that phrase found anywhere in the column specified above.

  3. Click Search.

  4. Clicking Search again will take you to the next value that meets your search criteria. To see all matching records, continue clicking Search until you receive a message that the last value has been found.

Exporting Translation Tables

  1. Select the Code Translation Table ID you want to export.

  2. Select Download Type. Either .xls or .csv from the drop-down menu.

  3. Click Export.

Code Translation Table Overview

Code Translation Tables uniquely identify legacy system codes and map them to PrismHR codes. All legacy system codes must be unique. You can map multiple legacy codes to the same PrismHR code if they are set up the same. You may have multiple legacy software databases that will be used as part of the legacy code.

For example, if you had two pay codes, “REGULAR” and “REGULAR1”, that have the same set up in the legacy system, you can map both pay codes to the same pay code in PrismHR (REG). Doing this allows you to consolidate similar codes during the conversion and minimize the amount of codes to set up in PrismHR.

Legacy Code Prism Code
REGULAR REG
REGULAR1 REG

Depending on the Code Translation Table, if a Legacy Code is set up differently for a specific client, you can make the code specific to that client by adding a “^” and the Legacy Client ID (refer to Legacy Code in the CM Code Translation Table).

Deduction Codes are the most common codes that are used differently by client in legacy software.

For example, you have a Legacy Deduction Code = DENTAL125. For the majority of clients this Legacy Deduction Code should be mapped in PrismHR to “DEN125”. But for Legacy Client ID = 01-123 it is set up differently than the majority and should be mapped to a different PrismHR Deduction Code = CDEN125 that will be specific to that client. You would enter one row that will map the majority of clients and an additional rows for mappings that are specific to individual clients.

Refer to the sample below for the proper mappings to accomplish this.

Legacy Code Prism Code
DENTAL125 DEN125
DENTAL125^01-123 CDEN125

Clients Import Translation Tables

The following Code Translation Table IDs are used to convert client-level information. Most conversions will need the all the Code Translation Table IDs noted as required below, but may vary based on your specific conversion.

CM - Client Mapping Table (Required)

CM Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Client ID to their new PrismHR Client ID. You can map multiple Legacy Client IDs to a single PrismHR Client ID if you are consolidating multiple Legacy Clients together as a part of the conversion. This Code Translation Table can also be used to set various client parameters that may differ for each individual Legacy Client ID (i.e. Billing Template, Bill Format, Retirement Plan, etc.). Refer to the column headings set up for your conversion for the various client parameters.

EM - Employer Mapping Table (Required)

EM Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Employer ID to their new PrismHR Employer ID. You will need to enter a mapping for each PEO and ASO Legacy Employer ID.

DM - Delivery Method Mapping Table (Required)

DM Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Delivery Method Code to their new PrismHR Delivery Method Code (System/Change/Delivery Methods).

USER - User Mapping Table (Required)

USER Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy User ID to their new PrismHR Service Provider User ID (System/Change/Users).

LC - Location Mapping Table (Optional)

LC Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Client Worksite Location Code to their new PrismHR Worksite Location Code (Client/Change/Worksite Locations). The Legacy Code should be a combination of the Legacy Client ID^Legacy Worksite Location Code (i.e. Legacy Worksite Location Code = Main for Legacy Client ID = 01-123 would be Legacy Code = 01-123^Main).

CK - Bank Account Mapping Table (Optional)

CK Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Bank Accounts to their new PrismHR Bank Account ID (System/Change/Bank Accounts).

WCP - W/C Policy Mapping Table (Optional)

WCP Code Translation Table is used to map Legacy Workers Compensation Plan Codes to their new PrismHR Workers Compensation Policy ID (System/Change/W/C Policies).

Employees Import Translation Tables

The following Code Translation Table IDs are used to be able to convert Employee information. Most conversions will need the all the Code Translation Table IDs noted as required below, but may vary based on your specific conversion.

CM—Client Mapping Table (Required) - Refer to Clients Import Translation Tables for Details.

EM—Employer Mapping Table (Required) - Refer to Clients Import Translation Tables for Details.

ES - Employee Status Mapping Table (Required)

ES Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Employee Status Codes to their new PrismHR Employee Status Codes (System/Change/Employee Statuses).

ET—Employee Type Mapping Table (Required)

ET Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Employee Type Codes to their new PrismHR Employee Type Codes (System/Change/Employee Types).

EC—Ethnicity Code Mapping Table (Required)

EC Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Ethnicity Codes to their new PrismHR EEO Ethnic Codes (System/Change/EEO Ethnic Codes).

ETR—Employee Term Reasons Mapping Table (Required)

ETR Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Employee Term Reason Codes to their new PrismHR Reason Codes (System/Change/Reasons).

FS—Tax Filing Status Mapping Table (Required)

FS Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Filing Status Codes to their new PrismHR Filing Status Codes (HR/Change/Employee Tax > Tax tab). Legacy Code is commonly the State combined with the Filing Status, however, Legacy Code may be entered with dashes between the State and FIling Status depending on your Legacy software.

Please see sample below for States without Alternate Calculations.

Legacy Code Prism Code
ALMAR M
ALSINGLE S

Certain States have Alternate Calculations as their Filing Status. Similar to the above sample, map the Legacy Filing Status Code to their new PrismHR Filing Status Code and/or the Alternate Calculation Code as applicable.

Please see sample below for States with Alternate Calculations.

Legacy Code Prism Code Alt. Calc Code
AZ1.3 9
NJMARA M 1

Employee Deduction Import Translation Tables

The following Code Translation Table IDs are used to be able to convert Employee Deduction information. Most conversions will need the all the Code Translation Table IDs noted as required below, but may vary based on your specific conversion.

D—Deduction Code Mapping Table (Required)

D Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Deduction Codes to their new PrismHR Deduction Codes (System / Change / Deduction Codes).

The following are records that are created from the Employee Deduction Import:

  • Recurring Deductions - (Payroll / Change / Recurring Deductions)

  • Retirement Plan Enrollments - (HR / Change / Retirement Plan Enrollment)

  • FSA/HSA Enrollment - (HR / Change / Employee Flexible Spending Accounts)

  • Employee Garnishments - (Payroll / Change / Employee Garnishments)

  • Employee Loans - (Payroll / Change / Employee Loans)

  • Retirement Loans - (HR / Change / Employee Retirement Loans)

  • Group Benefit Enrollment - (HR / Action / Employee Benefits Enrollment)

For all Legacy Deduction Codes enter the respective PrismHR Deduction Code.

For Legacy Deduction Codes that you desire to create Employee Benefit Enrollments, add the PrismHR Group Benefit Plan ID (System / Change / Group Benefit Plans) in the “Benefit Plan ID” column. Also, if the Legacy Deduction Code uniquely identifies the Benefit Plan Type, add the PrismHR Benefit Plan Type (System / Change / Group Benefit Plan Types) into the “Plan Type” column.

Note: Note: Note that the D table is used differently based on the “Deduction Type” of the PrismHR Deduction Code mapped. Only populate columns as instructed above or as directed by your Implementation Consultant or Data Engineer.

PAYEE—Payee Mapping Table (Required)

PAYEE Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Payee Codes to their new PrismHR Payee Codes (System/Change/Payees).

B—Benefit Plans Mapping Table (Required for conversions from Pay Plus)

B Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Benefit Plan Codes to their new PrismHR Group Benefit Plan Codes (System / Change / Group Benefit Plans).

BP - Benefit Plan Types Mapping Table (Required for conversions from Pay Plus)

BP Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Benefit Plan Type Codes to their new PrismHR Group Benefit Plan Type Codes (System / Change / Group Benefit Plan Types).

Employee YTD Import Translation Tables

The following Code Translation Table IDs are used to be able to convert Employee YTD Check History information. Most conversions will need the all the Code Translation Table IDs noted as required below, but may vary based on your specific conversion.

P - Pay Code Mapping Table (Required)

P Code Translation Table is used to map the Legacy Pay Codes to their new PrismHR Pay Codes (System / Change / Pay Codes). P Code Translation Table is used when importing the following types of records:

  • Scheduled Payments - (Payroll / Change / Scheduled Payments)

  • Check History - (Payroll / View / Employee Payroll Vouchers)

D—Deduction Code Mapping Table (Required) - Refer to Employee Deductions Import Translation Tables for Details.

EET—Employee Paid Tax Codes Mapping Table (Required)

EET Code Translation Table is used to map the legacy system Employee Paid Tax codes to their new PrismHR Employee Paid Tax Deduction Codes (System / Change / Tax Deductions). The Legacy Code is usually a combination of the Tax Authority and Tax Code columns in YTD Check History data files. The Prism Code should be mapped as a combination of the PrismHR Tax Authority and Tax Deduction concatenated by a dash.

Please see sample below:

Legacy Code Prism Code
ALSTATEINC 01-20
FEDINC 00-10

For Legacy Employee Paid Tax Codes that are Local School District Tax Codes, add the School District Tax ID with the School District Tax Code. Additionally, you will need to add the PrismHR (Vertex) School District Code in the respective column of the EET Table.

ERT—Employer Paid Tax and Employer Match Codes Mapping Table (Required)

ERT Code Translation Table is used to map Legacy Employer Paid Tax Codes and Employer Paid Benefit Match Codes in YTD Check History data files.

Employer Paid Tax Codes

The Legacy Code is usually a combination of the Tax Authority and Tax Code columns in the check history data files. The Prism Code should be mapped as a combination of the PrismHR Tax Authority and Tax Deduction concatenated by a dash.

Please see sample below:

Legacy Code Prism Code
FEDERALFUTA 00-17
ALSUTA 01-24

Employer Paid Benefit Match Codes

Use ERT Code Translation Table to map Legacy ER Benefit Match Codes to the respective Employer Match Code listed below. These categories are used to direct the applicable amounts to the correct sections of the converted Payroll Vouchers.

Employer Match Code Type = Prism Employer Match Code

  • Client Paid Retirement Match = MATCH

  • PEO Paid Retirement Match = PEOMATCH

  • Non-Elective Retirement Match = MATCHNE

  • Safe Harbor 1 Retirement Match = MATCHSH1

  • Safe Harbor 2 Retirement Match = MATCHSH2

  • HSA Match = HSA

  • FSA Match = FSA

  • Employer Paid Contributions/Premiums for W-2 reporting = W2BEN

  • No match/skip match amount (does not fall into categories above) = *

Note: Note: Not all legacy systems can provide the information needed to properly populate the information needed for Employer Matches that are Employer Paid Contributions/Premiums for W-2 reporting. You will be advised by your Implementation Consultant or Data Engineer if that import is possible.

Importing Client BE/OE Workflows

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Client%20BE%20and%20OE%20Workflow.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Client BE and OE Workflow.htm

Importing Client BE/OE Workflows

You can import BE/OE workflows into the Client Workflow Grid to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: Note: This import template is only available for service providers.

To upload and import BE/OE workflows for a client, do the following:

  1. You can navigate directly to the Data Import Tool form by clicking [Image: screenshot] (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

  2. From the Import Template drop-down menu, select Client BE/OE Workflows.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - Workflow Effective Date (Required): Date on which the workflow is available. - BE Workflow (Optional): The workflow to use for benefit enrollments. - BE Open Window Length (Optional): The number of days from the benefit enrollment effective date during which an employee can enroll in benefits. (Note: If you enter the BE Workflow, the BE Open Window Length is required.) - Enable Notifications (Optional): - If left blank, defaults to ALL ON (Value = Y) - ALL ON (Value = Y) - ALL OFF (Value = N) - BE ONLY (Value = B) - OE ONLY (Value = O) - AE ONLY (Value = A) - Min # of Overlap Days (Optional): Designates the limited amount of time an employee has to complete the open enrollment workflow when the workflow start date plus the Min # of Overlap Days extends beyond the open enrollment window. - AE Workflow (Optional): The workflow to use for automatic benefits enrollment. - OE Workflow (Optional): The workflow to use for benefits open enrollment. (Note: If you enter the OE Workflow, then the OE Start Date, OE End Date, and End Effective Date are required.) - OE Start Date (Optional): The date when benefits open enrollment start. - OE End Date (Optional): The date when benefits open enrollment ends. - End Effective Date (Optional): The date till which employee benefits apply.

  • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.

  • Workflow Effective Date (Required): Date on which the workflow is available.

  • BE Workflow (Optional): The workflow to use for benefit enrollments.

  • BE Open Window Length (Optional): The number of days from the benefit enrollment effective date during which an employee can enroll in benefits. (Note: If you enter the BE Workflow, the BE Open Window Length is required.)

  • Enable Notifications (Optional):

  • If left blank, defaults to ALL ON (Value = Y)

  • ALL ON (Value = Y)

  • ALL OFF (Value = N)

  • BE ONLY (Value = B)

  • OE ONLY (Value = O)

  • AE ONLY (Value = A)

  • Min # of Overlap Days (Optional): Designates the limited amount of time an employee has to complete the open enrollment workflow when the workflow start date plus the Min # of Overlap Days extends beyond the open enrollment window.

  • AE Workflow (Optional): The workflow to use for automatic benefits enrollment.

  • OE Workflow (Optional): The workflow to use for benefits open enrollment. (Note: If you enter the OE Workflow, then the OE Start Date, OE End Date, and End Effective Date are required.)

  • OE Start Date (Optional): The date when benefits open enrollment start.

  • OE End Date (Optional): The date when benefits open enrollment ends.

  • End Effective Date (Optional): The date till which employee benefits apply. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | When using the Client BE/OE Workflows import template, note the following:

  • If users do not have access to the company through client access groups, users cannot import data into a company.

  • If their user role is set to DENY for the Client Details form, but FULL for the Client Accounts form, users can view the Client BE/OE Workflows option on the Import Template menu and import data .

  • If their user role is set to DENY for the Client Workflow Grid form, users cannot view the Client BE/OE Workflows option on the Import Template menu.

  • If their user role is set to INQUIRY for the Client Workflow Grid form, users can view the Client BE/OE Workflows import template, but cannot import data.

  • If their user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool form, users can view Form and import templates, but cannot import data.

Using the Data Import Tool

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Database_File_Import.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Database_File_Import.htm

Using the Data Import Tool

The Data Import Tool lets you upload data and import it into the system. The Data Import Tool is available from the Operations|Import Processing menu in the Back Office menu. For example, the following form displays after you access the Data Import Tool and select the Department Codes import template option:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • The list of Import Template options display in alphabetical order.

  • You can also access the Data Import Tool by selecting its link on the Benefit Imports & Reporting landing page. (You must have either Full or Inquiry access set in your user role for the Data Import Tool (HRPY.WORK*DATABASE.IMPORT.ENTRY). Otherwise, this link does not display.)

Before you can upload and import data, your source file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. When you select the import template that you want on the Data Import Tool form, the required file layout displays. The layout must match the requirements for number and order of columns, category descriptions, and the required fields.

In addition, you can use the sample header file before importing, whose link resides on the Data Import Tool form, to avoid manually creating an import file that matches the import template type.

Note: Note the following when using a comma (,) in a description in your import file:

  • If you include a comma in a description field using the .csv file format, you must enclose the item in double quotes. For example, “Manager, Admin.”

  • If you include a comma in a description field using the .txt file format, no extra formatting is necessary.

Using the Sample Header File

Before starting the import process, you can first download a sample header file by clicking that link on the Data Import Tool form after selecting an import template option or from a local form that displays the Import icon (

[Image: screenshot]

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: The header file is in .csv format. You can save the file in .csv or .txt format.

After you click the Download Sample Header File link, the system downloads or prompts for download a sample header file that displays columns and headers that match each column and description for the import template option. Also, the file displays a title that matches the selected option.

Note: Note: The sample header file is only available to users who have access to the selected import template option.

To upload and import a database file in .txt format and import its data, do the following:

  1. From the Import Template drop-down menu in the Data Import Tool form, select the template type.

  2. At the bottom of the form, click Find File. The Upload a File dialog displays.

  3. Click Choose File and browse to the .txt file you want to upload.

  4. Click Open.

  5. Click Submit.

If the file uploads successfully, a confirmation message displays. If your file does not upload successfully, an error message displays. Click Close, then click Clear to try again or to upload a different file.

  1. Click Close to return to the Data Import Tool form, where the file name and the imported content display.

  2. Review the content, and then click Import to complete the process. A confirmation dialog displays to confirm that the file content was successfully imported.

If the import process encounters duplicates, a dialog displays stating the data already exists. Click OK. The Import Duplicates form displays.

To process the duplicate data, you can either click Skip or Replace with New. If you want to apply the action to all data, select the Apply to all option.

Troubleshooting

If errors occur during the import process, do the following:

  1. Click OK.

  2. Click the Messages tab and review the error messages.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Import to proceed. If the import is successful, a confirmation dialog displays.

  2. Click OK to proceed and view the report or click Close to restart the process.

[Image: screenshot]

Viewing the Report

To view the report on the data you uploaded and imported, do the following:

Click Report.

[Image: screenshot]

The data displays in a report format, which includes the Import Status results. The report (see example below) displays all imported records and includes any records that were skipped.

[Image: screenshot]

When you finish reviewing the report, close the report window and click Clear to upload another file.

Importing ACA Offered Employees

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_ACA_Offered_Employees.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_ACA_Offered_Employees.htm

Importing ACA Offered Employees

You can use this import template to import part-time employees who need to be reported as full-time employees for ACA purposes for the client to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: This import template is only available to service providers.

To upload and import ACA offered employees, do the following:

  1. Select Client.

  2. From the Client|Change menu, select ACA Offered Employees. The ACA Offered Employees form displays.

  3. On the ACA Offered Employees form, click Import [Image: screenshot] to launch the Data Import Tool form. (This button displays for all user roles except Deny.)

The ACA Offered Employees import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display when you access this template directly from the ACA Offered Employees form.

You can navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.

Importing Benefit Adjustments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Benefit_Adjustments.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Benefit_Adjustments.htm

Importing Benefit Adjustments

You can import multiple benefit adjustments for multiple employees at once to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: Note: This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors.

To upload and import benefit adjustments, do the following:

  1. Click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

  2. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Benefit Adjustments import template option.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - Employee ID (required): Unique identifier for the employee whose benefit billing record will receive an adjustment. - Plan ID (required): Unique identifier for the Benefit Plan that requires an adjustment. - Plan Period (required): The benefit plan period in the format YYYYMM. For example, 202310 for October 2023. - Bill Amount (required): The amount to bill to the client per pay cycle as a result of an adjustment. - Employee Contribution: The amount to deduct from the employee’s pay check per cycle. This amount is credited to the client to offset the billing amount. - Cycles (required): The number of future payroll cycles to apply an adjustment. - Start Date (required): The Start Date of the period when the deduction related to an adjustment goes into effect. - Insurance Cost: The premium cost associated with an adjustment. - Adjustment Amount: The B/R adjustment to apply to the benefits reconciliation process of an adjustment. - Retro Enroll: Whether an adjustment applies to a retroactive enrollment. Pre-tax contributions cannot fund any part of the premium for retroactive enrollments. Valid values are Yes or No. - Comments: Descriptive comments about an adjustment.
  • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.
  • Employee ID (required): Unique identifier for the employee whose benefit billing record will receive an adjustment.
  • Plan ID (required): Unique identifier for the Benefit Plan that requires an adjustment.
  • Plan Period (required): The benefit plan period in the format YYYYMM. For example, 202310 for October 2023.
  • Bill Amount (required): The amount to bill to the client per pay cycle as a result of an adjustment.
  • Employee Contribution: The amount to deduct from the employee’s pay check per cycle. This amount is credited to the client to offset the billing amount.
  • Cycles (required): The number of future payroll cycles to apply an adjustment.
  • Start Date (required): The Start Date of the period when the deduction related to an adjustment goes into effect.
  • Insurance Cost: The premium cost associated with an adjustment.
  • Adjustment Amount: The B/R adjustment to apply to the benefits reconciliation process of an adjustment.
  • Retro Enroll: Whether an adjustment applies to a retroactive enrollment. Pre-tax contributions cannot fund any part of the premium for retroactive enrollments. Valid values are Yes or No.
  • Comments: Descriptive comments about an adjustment. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | > Note: Note: Cycles Billed is not a required field anymore for importing Benefit Adjustments. It will automatically be set to 0 when importing Benefit Adjustments.

You can import changes to bill pending data to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: Note: This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors who have full access to the Bill Pending form enabled for their user role. Bill pending data imported through this process will be added to existing records. Updates to existing bill pending data must be made manually.

To upload and import bill pending data, do the following:

  1. Select Client.

  2. From the Client|Action menu, select Bill Pending.

  3. On the Bill Pending form, click Import [Image: screenshot] to launch the Data Import Tool form. (This button displays for all user roles except Inquiry Only.)

The Bill Pending import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display when you access this template directly from the Bill Pending form.

Note: Note: You can also navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Bill Pending import template option.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Bill Date (required): Date on which billing occurs; the system recognizes different formats as long as they are in the order month, day, and year (if no year is specified, the system uses the current year). - Bill Event Code (required): Billing event code. - Bill Rate (required): Billing rates for each billing unit. - Bill Unit (required): Number of billing units. - Client ID (required): ID of the client for this billing line item. - Employee ID (required): ID of the employee associated with the line item, if applicable (must be in the client in the row). (Optional when using Location.) - Location (required): Location code associated with the line item, if applicable. (Optional when using Employee ID.) - Division: Division code associated with the line item, if applicable. - Comment (max 40 characters): Comment for the line item, if appropriate. (Note: If there are more than 40 characters in a comment, an error displays.) - Department: Department code associated with the line item, if applicable. - Shift: Shift code associated with the line item, if applicable. - Project: Project code associated with the line item, if applicable. - Cost: Cost amount can be positive to charge against the line item, or negative to lower the total amount. - Pay Group: Pay group associated with the line item, if applicable (requires a Location for calculating taxes). Note that you cannot have both an employee ID and a pay group in the same file; the system will reject it if you do. - Payroll Type: Indicates the type of payroll, which can be Regularly Scheduled (R), Manual (M), or Special (S). - Repeat Thru Date: Indicates when the recurring event starts and stops. (Use the MM/DD/YYYY date format.) - Repeat Cycle (required if Repeat Thru Date is used): Indicates billing frequency, which can be one of the following: - W = Weekly - B = Biweekly - M = Monthly - Q = Quarterly - A = Annually
  • Bill Date (required): Date on which billing occurs; the system recognizes different formats as long as they are in the order month, day, and year (if no year is specified, the system uses the current year).
  • Bill Event Code (required): Billing event code.
  • Bill Rate (required): Billing rates for each billing unit.
  • Bill Unit (required): Number of billing units.
  • Client ID (required): ID of the client for this billing line item.
  • Employee ID (required): ID of the employee associated with the line item, if applicable (must be in the client in the row). (Optional when using Location.)
  • Location (required): Location code associated with the line item, if applicable. (Optional when using Employee ID.)
  • Division: Division code associated with the line item, if applicable.
  • Comment (max 40 characters): Comment for the line item, if appropriate. (Note: If there are more than 40 characters in a comment, an error displays.)
  • Department: Department code associated with the line item, if applicable.
  • Shift: Shift code associated with the line item, if applicable.
  • Project: Project code associated with the line item, if applicable.
  • Cost: Cost amount can be positive to charge against the line item, or negative to lower the total amount.
  • Pay Group: Pay group associated with the line item, if applicable (requires a Location for calculating taxes). Note that you cannot have both an employee ID and a pay group in the same file; the system will reject it if you do.
  • Payroll Type: Indicates the type of payroll, which can be Regularly Scheduled (R), Manual (M), or Special (S).
  • Repeat Thru Date: Indicates when the recurring event starts and stops. (Use the MM/DD/YYYY date format.)
  • Repeat Cycle (required if Repeat Thru Date is used): Indicates billing frequency, which can be one of the following:
  • W = Weekly
  • B = Biweekly
  • M = Monthly
  • Q = Quarterly
  • A = Annually | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | ========================================================================

Importing Client Account Assignments

You can import changes to client account assignments to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: Note: This import template is only available for service providers.

To upload and import employee client account assignments, do the following:

  1. You can navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking [Image: screenshot] (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

  2. From the Import Template drop-down menu, select Client Account Assignments.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

You can enable one of the following fields during imports:

  • Remove existing assignments (default): Removes existing assignments that are not included in the file.

  • Replace existing assignments: Replaces existing assignments with assignments included in the file but does not remove assignments that are not included in the file.

  • Keep Existing Assignments: Prioritizes keeping existing assignments and adds new assignments included in the file. (That is, if an assignment exists and is included in the file, the upload skips the value in the file and keeps the existing system values.)

The layout requirements are:

Field Description

Category Description - Company ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - Payroll (required): The payroll employee representative. - Human Resources (required): The human resources employee representative. - Benefits: The benefits employee representative. - Risk: The risk employee representative. - Sales: The sales employee representative. - Coordinator: The coordinator employee representative. - Broker: The broker employee representative. - I-9 Approver: The I-9 approver employee representative. - Print/Mail User: The Payroll Processor (Print/Mail) employee representative.

  • Company ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.

  • Payroll (required): The payroll employee representative.

  • Human Resources (required): The human resources employee representative.

  • Benefits: The benefits employee representative.

  • Risk: The risk employee representative.

  • Sales: The sales employee representative.

  • Coordinator: The coordinator employee representative.

  • Broker: The broker employee representative.

  • I-9 Approver: The I-9 approver employee representative.

  • Print/Mail User: The Payroll Processor (Print/Mail) employee representative. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | When using the Client Account Assignments import template, note the following:

  • If users do not have access to the company through client access groups, users cannot import data into a company.

  • If their user role is set to DENY for the Client Details form, but FULL for the Company Accounts form, users can view the Client Account Assignments option on the Import Template menu and import data .

  • If their user role is set to DENY for the Company Account form, users cannot view the Client Account Assignments option on the Import Template menu.

  • If their user role is set to INQUIRY for the Company Account form, users can view the Client Account Assignments import template, but cannot import data.

You can enable one of the following fields:

  • Keep existing data field (default): Retains existing data during the import and only adds or replaces data included in the file to the client.

  • Remove existing client commissions data for all client in the import file: Overwrites existing data in the Commission Maintenance form during the import. (The Commission Maintenance form is accessible by selecting Commissions on the Actions menu in the Client Details form.)

  • Keep existing data and update duplicates: Prior to creating new records, ensures the system looks for duplicates between the existing commissions data and the file upload to permit updates to those matching records for the Amount, Flat or Percent, and Target Amount fields, in addition to uploading new commissions configurations.

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - Salesperson (required): The user ID of an employee at your organization who is a sales representative associated with the client. - From Date (required): Date on which the commission level goes into effect. - To Date (required): Date on which the commission level expires. - Amount: Indicates the commission amount as a flat amount or a percentage. - Flat or Percent: Indicates if the commission amount is Flat or Percent. - Based On: Indicates what the commission is based on. If you include Based On in the import file, it must match one of these options: - Gross Wages - Admin Fees - Benefit Commission Type - Benefit Commission Percentage - Workers Comp - Workers Compensation Profit - Average Number Lives - Gross Profit - Tax Profit - Percent of Bill Code - Profits to Admin [Enter Bill Code in Based On] - Fixed Amount Group 1 - Fixed Amount Group 2 - Fixed Amount Group 3 - Fixed Amount Group 4 - Fixed Amount Group 5 - Fixed per Paid Employee - Percent of Target Amount - Based On Item: Additional based-on types to the commission rule at the client level, such as Percent of Bill Code, Profits to Admin, Workers Compensation Profit, Benefit Commission Type, and Benefit Commission Percentage. - Based On Plan: Indicates the ID of the commission plan that exists at the system level. (Cannot be used in conjunction with Amount, Flat or Percent, Based On, and Based on Item.) - Target Amount: Indicates the commission’s target amount, which is used in conjunction with the Percent of Target Amount Based On option. (You can enter up to two decimals in this field. The system truncates values with more than two decimals.) The Target Amount field value is an overall dollar figure the system multiplies by the Amount Percent value to calculate the salesperson’s commission payout amount. For example, a Target Amount set to 100,000 for a 30% of Target Amount Commission setup would pay out $30,000 as the Commission amount for the defined commission period.

  • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.

  • Salesperson (required): The user ID of an employee at your organization who is a sales representative associated with the client.

  • From Date (required): Date on which the commission level goes into effect.

  • To Date (required): Date on which the commission level expires.

  • Amount: Indicates the commission amount as a flat amount or a percentage.

  • Flat or Percent: Indicates if the commission amount is Flat or Percent.

  • Based On: Indicates what the commission is based on. If you include Based On in the import file, it must match one of these options:

  • Gross Wages

  • Admin Fees

  • Benefit Commission Type

  • Benefit Commission Percentage

  • Workers Comp

  • Workers Compensation Profit

  • Average Number Lives

  • Gross Profit

  • Tax Profit

  • Percent of Bill Code

  • Profits to Admin [Enter Bill Code in Based On]

  • Fixed Amount Group 1

  • Fixed Amount Group 2

  • Fixed Amount Group 3

  • Fixed Amount Group 4

  • Fixed Amount Group 5

  • Fixed per Paid Employee

  • Percent of Target Amount

  • Based On Item: Additional based-on types to the commission rule at the client level, such as Percent of Bill Code, Profits to Admin, Workers Compensation Profit, Benefit Commission Type, and Benefit Commission Percentage.

  • Based On Plan: Indicates the ID of the commission plan that exists at the system level. (Cannot be used in conjunction with Amount, Flat or Percent, Based On, and Based on Item.)

  • Target Amount: Indicates the commission’s target amount, which is used in conjunction with the Percent of Target Amount Based On option. (You can enter up to two decimals in this field. The system truncates values with more than two decimals.) | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | > Note: Note the following when using the Client Commissions import template:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Commission Maintenance form cannot import data using the Client Commissions import template. (You can access the Commission Maintenance form by selecting Commissions on the Action menu in the Client Details form.)

Importing Client Details Special Delivery Instructions

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Client_Details_Special_Delivery.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Client_Details_Special_Delivery.htm

Importing Client Details Special Delivery Instructions

You can import special delivery instructions for clients to reduce the amount of manual work required.

To upload and import client details special delivery instructions, do the following:

  1. You can navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking [Image: screenshot] (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

  2. From the Import Template drop-down menu, select Client Details (Special Delivery).

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

You can enable one of the following fields during imports:

  • Replace existing data: Replaces existing data with data included in the file but does not remove data that is not included in the file. For example:

  • If the system already has a delivery method for location 1 and location 1 is included in the file with changes, the system confirms the changes.

  • If the system already has a delivery method for location 2 and location 2 is not in the file, then the system keeps the location 2 delivery method data.

  • Remove existing data (default): Removes existing data that is not included in the file for that client. For example:

  • If the system already has a delivery method for location 1 and location 1 is included in the file with changes, the system confirms the changes.

  • If the system already has a delivery method for location 2 and location 2 is not in the file, then the system removes the location 2 delivery method data.

  • Keep existing data: Prioritizes keeping existing data and adds new data included in the file. (That is, if data exists and is included in the file, the upload skips the value in the file and keeps the existing system values.) For example:

  • If the system already has a delivery method for location 1 and location 1 is included in the file with changes, the system keeps the existing data, not the data included in the file.

  • If the system already has a delivery method for location 2 and location 2 is not in the file, then the location 2 delivery method data remains the same in the system.

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - All Locations: Indicates if special delivery method applies to all locations. - Location Code: Indicates location code for this special delivery. - Company Override Method: Indicates special delivery methods defined in your system. - Days In Transit: Indicates special delivery method’s number of days in transit. - Bill Event Codes: Indicates ID of billing event that the system uses to track this special delivery method. If there is no charge for the special delivery method, leave this field blank. - Special Bill Amt: Indicates override for the standard billing amount for this client. - Create Spec Sheet: Indicates that a special sheet will print during payroll processing. (Do not use this option if a special sheet is not necessary.) - Method Active: Indicates status of this special delivery method. - Method Until: Indicates date when the special delivery method should stop being used for the client. - Special Message: A special message that prints on the special delivery sheet. - Name: Indicates name that should appear on the special delivery sheet. - Address: Indicates address that should appear on the special delivery sheet. - Address 2: Indicates second address line that should appear on the special delivery sheet. - City, State, Zip Code: Indicates city, state, and zip code that should appear on the special delivery sheet. - Delivery Sheet Format: Indicates special delivery sheet format used to ensure that the address on the printed special delivery sheet displays in the window envelopes your organization uses.

  • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.

  • All Locations: Indicates if special delivery method applies to all locations.

  • Location Code: Indicates location code for this special delivery.

  • Company Override Method: Indicates special delivery methods defined in your system.

  • Days In Transit: Indicates special delivery method’s number of days in transit.

  • Bill Event Codes: Indicates ID of billing event that the system uses to track this special delivery method. If there is no charge for the special delivery method, leave this field blank.

  • Special Bill Amt: Indicates override for the standard billing amount for this client.

  • Create Spec Sheet: Indicates that a special sheet will print during payroll processing. (Do not use this option if a special sheet is not necessary.)

  • Method Active: Indicates status of this special delivery method.

  • Method Until: Indicates date when the special delivery method should stop being used for the client.

  • Special Message: A special message that prints on the special delivery sheet.

  • Name: Indicates name that should appear on the special delivery sheet.

  • Address: Indicates address that should appear on the special delivery sheet.

  • Address 2: Indicates second address line that should appear on the special delivery sheet.

  • City, State, Zip Code: Indicates city, state, and zip code that should appear on the special delivery sheet.

  • Delivery Sheet Format: Indicates special delivery sheet format used to ensure that the address on the printed special delivery sheet displays in the window envelopes your organization uses. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | When using the Client Details (Special Delivery) import template, note the following:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Client Details form cannot import data using the Client Details (Special Delivery) import template and subsequently, the Data Import Tool icon will not display on this form.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Client Details form can view the Client Details (Special Delivery) import template, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

  • Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Client_Tax.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Client_Tax.htm

Importing Client Taxes

You can use this import template to import taxes for the client into the state tax setup on the Client Details form to reduce the amount of manual work required.

To upload and import client tax details, do the following:

  1. Select Client.

  2. Click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu. The Data Import Tool form displays.

  3. Select Client Details (Tax).

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

You can enable one of the following fields during imports:

  • Keep existing data: Prioritizes keeping existing data and adds new data included in the file. (That is, if data exists and is included in the file, the upload skips the value in the file and keeps the existing system values.) Enabling this field only adds new State Tax data included in the file to the client.

  • Keep existing data and update duplicates: Prior to creating new records, ensures the system looks for duplicates between the client tax data and the file upload to permit updates to those matching records for the Client ID and State fields, in addition to uploading new tax configurations.

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - State: Indicates a two-character state code. States with or without suffixes will display in alphabetical order once any changes are saved. - State Unemployment Insurance ID: Indicates a state unemployment insurance ID for the selected state. - Secondary SUI ID: If this is a PEO company, indicates a secondary ID for reporting a client’s wages in states such as Kansas and Missouri that use the employer’s rate but report it separately using this ID. - State Tax ID: Indicates the state tax ID for the selected state. - Client Reporting Start Date: Indicates the Client Reporting Start Date for SUTA tax reporting. - Client Reporting End Date: Indicates the Client Reporting End Date for SUTA tax reporting. - Misc Tax ID: Indicates the miscellaneous tax ID for the selected state - Misc Tax Code: Indicates one or more miscellaneous comma-separated tax codes to apply to a single Misc. Tax ID. This is helpful for states that require a separate tax account ID such as Washington for WA Cares and WA PFML.
  • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.
  • State: Indicates a two-character state code. States with or without suffixes will display in alphabetical order once any changes are saved.
  • State Unemployment Insurance ID: Indicates a state unemployment insurance ID for the selected state.
  • Secondary SUI ID: If this is a PEO company, indicates a secondary ID for reporting a client’s wages in states such as Kansas and Missouri that use the employer’s rate but report it separately using this ID.
  • State Tax ID: Indicates the state tax ID for the selected state.
  • Client Reporting Start Date: Indicates the Client Reporting Start Date for SUTA tax reporting.
  • Client Reporting End Date: Indicates the Client Reporting End Date for SUTA tax reporting.
  • Misc Tax ID: Indicates the miscellaneous tax ID for the selected state
  • Misc Tax Code: Indicates one or more miscellaneous comma-separated tax codes to apply to a single Misc. Tax ID. This is helpful for states that require a separate tax account ID such as Washington for WA Cares and WA PFML. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | ========================================================================

You can import changes to department codes to reduce the amount of manual work required.

  1. Select Client.

Note: Note: You can also navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Department Codes import template option.

(Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Company ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - Department Code (required) : Abbreviation for the department. - Department Name (required): The full name of the department. - Per Diem Percent: Defines the percentage of pay that is allocated to non-taxable per diem when per diem is paid using the percentage method. - GL Segment 1: Code that defines the G/L account number segment instead of the department code. This replaces EEDP instead of the actual code. - GL Segment 2: Allows for more accounting options based on the department code. Rarely used, it ties to the EEDP2 mnemonic in the G/L interfaces. - Union Eligible Days: Number of days for Union eligibility.

Importing Eligible Benefits

You can import eligible Benefit Plans based on the Eligible Benefits Determinant field assigned to each client on the Client Details form.

A quick link to the Eligible Benefits import template, Import Eligible Benefits, is available in the Eligible Benefits panel on the following forms:

  • Benefit Groups

  • Worksite Locations

  • Departments

  • Divisions

Note: Note: The Import Eligible Benefits quick link only displays on the forms mentioned above if you have selected the Eligible Benefits Determinant field in the Benefits tab on the Client Details form. For example, if you want the Import Eligible Benefits quick link to display on the Departments form, then you must select the Departments Restrict Eligibility option in the Eligible Benefits Determinant field in the Benefits tab on the Client Details form.

Note: Note: This import template is only available to service providers.

To upload and import eligible benefits:

  1. Click the Import Eligible Benefits quick link from one of the forms mentioned above or navigate to the import template in the Data Import Tool by clicking [Image: screenshot] (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

The Eligible Benefits import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display when you access this template directly from the above-mentioned forms.

  1. Enter the Client ID or select Client ID to pre-populate the client data. If you select Client ID, the Select Clients list displays.
  1. — Select the clients by clicking the list of clients that you want to add. The added clients display in the Selected Clients section. Click Add All to add all the clients at once. Click Remove All to remove the clients from the Selected Clients section at once.
b. Click Done to add the selected clients. The added clients display in the Data Import Tool.
  1. Enable Include Obsolete/Expired valuesbased on your requirement. (The default is disabled.)

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Data File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

Note: Note: While uploading a .csv file to import its data, if there is any error with any of the benefit plans, then under the Messages section, the error message displays errors for all the benefit plans which helps you in correcting the import files.

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - Client Description: The eligible benefits description. - Eligible Benefits Determinant (required): Indicates the benefits available to an employee if the client makes different sets of benefits available to their employees based on department, division, location, or benefit group. - Benefit Groups: Indicates the benefit groups for each group of employees. - Locations: Indicates the details for the client’s worksite locations. - Departments: Indicates the details for the client’s departments. - Divisions: Indicates the details for the client’s divisions. - Clear Existing Data: Clears any existing data on the form. - Benefit Plan ID: Indicates the Benefit Plan ID where the employees are enrolled. > Note: Note: The valid values for different “Eligible Benefits Determinant” are: D - Departments B - Benefit Groups V - Divisions L - Locations

  • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.

  • Client Description: The eligible benefits description.

  • Eligible Benefits Determinant (required): Indicates the benefits available to an employee if the client makes different sets of benefits available to their employees based on department, division, location, or benefit group.

  • Benefit Groups: Indicates the benefit groups for each group of employees.

  • Locations: Indicates the details for the client’s worksite locations.

  • Departments: Indicates the details for the client’s departments.

  • Divisions: Indicates the details for the client’s divisions.

  • Clear Existing Data: Clears any existing data on the form.

  • Benefit Plan ID: Indicates the Benefit Plan ID where the employees are enrolled. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | > Note: Note the following when using the Eligible Benefits import template:
