Importing Employee Direct Deposit

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Employee_DD.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Employee_DD.htm

Importing Employee Direct Deposit Data

You can import changes to employee direct deposit data to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: Note the following:

  • This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors.

  • Access to this template (Full, Inquiry, or Deny) mirrors the access the user has to the Deposit tab on the Employee Details form.

  • This process imports direct deposit records when bringing on new employees. If you use this process for employees that already have direct deposit records, the current direct deposit record will be replaced with the contents of this file.

To upload and import employee direct deposit information, do the following:

  1. You can navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking [Image: screenshot] (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

  2. From the Import Template drop-down menu, select Employee Direct Deposit.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Company ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - Employee Identifier (required): Either the SSN, Employee ID, or the Employee Number of an employee who works for the client and belongs to a pay group included in the payroll batch (can be a terminated employee). If needed, you may enter more than one line for an individual employee. Note: Only the last four digits of the SSN display when you review the information on the File Content tab. - Deposit Status (required): Indicates the following: - For active (A) deposit status, the system generates an ACH entry for the voucher. - For inactive (I) deposit status, the system produces a paycheck during payroll processing for the net amount of the pay voucher. - Pay Types to Deposit (required): Indicates the deposit pay types that the system directly deposits, which include the following: - All (RVS): All voucher types - Regular (R): Only regular checks - Vacation (V): Only vacation checks - Supplemental (S): Only supplemental checks - Reg & Vac (RV): Regular and vacation checks - Reg & Sup (RS): Regular and supplemental checks - Sup & Vac (SV): Supplemental and vacation checks - Suppress Account Number Print: Prevents the system from printing the employee’s bank account number on the direct deposit advice. The allowed values are Y or N. - Type (required): The bank account type for the deposit transaction, which includes the following: - C: Checking - S: Savings - HE: Employee checking - HES: Employee savings - HC: Client checking - HSC: Client savings > Note: Note the following: - An employee or client cannot have more than one type of HSA deposit. (They can deposit to a checking or savings account, but not to both accounts.) - A type that begins with an “H” always designates an HSA deposit. - Transit Number (required): The nine-digit ABA Transit Number of the receiving bank or other financial institution. - Account Number (required): The account number associated with the transit number where the money is deposited. (This number is alphanumeric with a maximum of 0-9 characters.) - Pay Type (required): The deposit pay types for the data on the specific row. (You can select different pay types for different accounts.) The pay types include the following: - All (RVS): All voucher types - Regular (R): Only regular checks - Vacation (V): Only vacation checks - Supplemental (S): Only supplemental checks - Reg & Vac (RV): Regular and vacation checks - Reg & Sup (RS): Regular and supplemental checks - Sup & Vac (SV): Supplemental and vacation checks - Method (required): The method used to determine the deposit amount. The allowed values are F, P, or B. (Note: For service providers, additional values are FS and PN.) - Amount (required): The direct deposit amount that is either a percentage or fixed amount, depending on the calculation method defined for the deduction code. (Note: This field is required if the Method chosen is F, P, FS, or PN.) - Limit: The maximum deposit amount. - Status (required): The status of the direct deposit account. The allowed values are P, D, or I.(Note: Worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors are only allowed to import a status of P (processing errors display if they import a status of D or I).)
  • Company ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.

  • Deposit Status (required): Indicates the following:
  • For active (A) deposit status, the system generates an ACH entry for the voucher.
  • For inactive (I) deposit status, the system produces a paycheck during payroll processing for the net amount of the pay voucher.

Importing Employee Dependents

You can import multiple employee dependents for multiple employees at once to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: Note: This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors.

To upload and import employee dependents do the following:

  1. Click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processingmenu.

  2. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Employee Dependents import template option. When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.) The layout requirements are: | Field | Description | | | — | — | — | | Column Number | The corresponding column number for the imported data. | | | Category Description | - Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - Spouse: Whether the dependent is the employee’s spouse. A spouse must have a Relationship Type of Dependent. - First Name (required): The dependent’s first name. - Last Name (required): The dependent’s last name. - Middle Initial: The dependent’s middle initial. - Gender: The dependent’s birth gender. Please note the below validations for the Gender field: - If Gender Non Binary is flagged on the System Parameters form, then you must be able to import Non-binary as a Gender option. The Gender Non-binary field value is defined as X. - If Gender Decline To State is flagged on the System Parameters form, then you must be able to import Declined to state as a Gender option. The Gender Declined to state field value is defined as D. - Birth Date: The dependent’s birth date. - Dependent SSN: The dependent’s Social Security number. - Tobacco Use: Whether the dependent uses tobacco. - EE SSN, EE ID, or Clock No. (required): Used to identify employees using their SSN, Employee ID, or Clock Number. It ensures consistency across import types and provides more flexibility for managing dependent data. - Relationship: The dependent’s relationship to the employee. - Full Time Student: Whether the dependent is a full‑time student. - Address Line 1: The dependent’s address. - City: The dependent’s city of residence. - State: The dependent’s state of residence. - Zip Code: The dependent’s ZIP code and extension. - Phone: The dependent’s phone number. - Work Phone: The dependent’s work phone number. - Gender Designation: Indicates to define the gender designation of the dependents. - Preferred Pronoun: Indicates to define the preferred pronoun of the dependents. | | | | • | Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. | | | • | Spouse: Whether the dependent is the employee’s spouse. A spouse must have a Relationship Type of Dependent. | | | • | First Name (required): The dependent’s first name. | | | • | Last Name (required): The dependent’s last name. | | | • | Middle Initial: The dependent’s middle initial. | | | • | Gender: The dependent’s birth gender. Please note the below validations for the Gender field: | | | • | If Gender Non Binary is flagged on the System Parameters form, then you must be able to import Non-binary as a Gender option. The Gender Non-binary field value is defined as X. | | | • | If Gender Decline To State is flagged on the System Parameters form, then you must be able to import Declined to state as a Gender option. The Gender Declined to state field value is defined as D. | | | • | Birth Date: The dependent’s birth date. | | | • | Dependent SSN: The dependent’s Social Security number. | | | • | Tobacco Use: Whether the dependent uses tobacco. | | | • | EE SSN, EE ID, or Clock No. (required): Used to identify employees using their SSN, Employee ID, or Clock Number. It ensures consistency across import types and provides more flexibility for managing dependent data. | | | • | Relationship: The dependent’s relationship to the employee. | | | • | Full Time Student: Whether the dependent is a full‑time student. | | | • | Address Line 1: The dependent’s address. | | | • | City: The dependent’s city of residence. | | | • | State: The dependent’s state of residence. | | | • | Zip Code: The dependent’s ZIP code and extension. | | | • | Phone: The dependent’s phone number. | | | • | Work Phone: The dependent’s work phone number. | | | • | Gender Designation: Indicates to define the gender designation of the dependents. | | | • | Preferred Pronoun: Indicates to define the preferred pronoun of the dependents. | | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | |

  3. Optionally, click Clear existing dependents from employee records to replace existing employee dependent records with the information in the import file. Leave this option unchecked to add this information to existing employee dependent records, including duplicates.

  4. When this option is checked, the validation logic evaluates any previously identified dependent record not included in the current import file to determine if that dependent record has current coverage or prior coverage history.

  5. Additionally, an informational message stating, “Required fields may vary based on client setup for New Hire and Dependent Field Overrides” displays.

    • If a previously identified dependent record is found to have current coverage or prior coverage history: The record is skipped and the following error message displays:

  7. “Error: You may not delete the dependent ID [Dependent ID Number] for Employee ID [Employee ID] on line [import file line number] because there are existing benefit records associated with it.”

  8. A variation of this same message displays when multiple dependent records with current coverage or prior coverage history must be skipped for the same employee:

  9. “Error: You may not delete the dependent ID’s [Dependent ID Numbers separated by a comma] for Employee ID [Employee ID] on line [import file line number] because there are existing benefit records associated with them.”

    • If a previously identified dependent record is found to have no current coverage or prior coverage history associated with it: The record is deleted.

  11. This validation works similar to the validation logic used when you attempt to manually delete a dependent with coverage history from the system. In that instance, a message displays indicating that you cannot delete the record but you can mark it Inactive.

Required Fields Validation

When fields are configured as required fields on either the New Hire and Dependent Required Fields (Global) form or the New Hire and Dependent Field Overrides form, validations are in place to ensure correct data is passed and required fields are not missing or invalid during the File Upload process.

Valid Data Checks:

If the following fields are configured as required and the field values are found to be invalid during the File Upload process of the Employee Dependents Import, an error message displays on the Messages tab of the Data Import Tool for each invalid value.

  • Birth Date - Must have valid date format.
  • Gender - Must have valid value (i.e., M, F, X, or D).
  • Relation - Must have valid value. The system uses the Relation Codes specified here to validate against: Benefit Plan Maintenance > Group Benefit Plans (Global) > Relationships.

Missing Data Checks:

If the following fields are configured as required and the field values are missing, an error message displays on the Messages tab of the Data Import tool for each missing value.

  • Social Security Number
  • Birth Date
  • Gender
  • Relation
  • Address (Address Line 1, City, State, ZIP Code)

Importing Employee Loan Data

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Employee_Loan_Data.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Employee_Loan_Data.htm

Importing Employee Loan Data

You can import changes to employee loan data to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: Note: This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors who have full access to the Employee Loans form enabled for their user role. Employee loan data imported through this process will be added to existing records. Updates to existing employee loan data can be made using the Loan Number column, which is an optional field.

Note: Note the following:

  • When an import file includes a valid loan number that already exists, the system updates that record with the information on that row.

  • When an import file includes an invalid loan number, an error occurs during the update.

  • When an import file does not include a loan number, the system creates a new record.

To upload and import employee loan data, do the following:

  1. Select Client.

  2. From the Payroll|Change menu, select Employee Loans.

  3. On the Employee Loans form, click Import [Image: screenshot] to launch the Data Import Tool form. (This button displays for all user roles except Inquiry Only.)

The Employee Loans import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display when you access this template directly from the Employee Loans form.

Note: Note: You can also navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Employee Loans import template option.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Client ID (required): ID of the client for this loan item. - Employee Identifier (required): Either the SSN, Employee ID, or the Employee Number of an employee who works for the client. (Note: Only the last four digits of the SSN display when you review the information on the File Content tab.) - Loan Number: Number associated with the loan. - Loan Date: Date on which this loan was granted. - Loan Amount (required): Amount granted to the employee. (This value must be greater than zero.) - Loan Payment (required): Amount to deduct automatically from each paycheck to repay the loan. - Payment Frequency (required): How often the payroll deduction is made: - O: Once per month. - P: Once per payroll period. - A: All payroll types. - Payback Amount (required): Amount required to consider the loan paid in full, which is the amount of this loan plus interest (if any). (Note: This amount can be different from the loan amount.) - Deduction Code (required): Code used for the employee loan. (Note: The deduction type must equal the employee loan payment.) - Start Date: Date on which payroll deductions will begin to pay back the loan. - Stop Date: Date on which payroll deductions will cease. - Reason for Loan: Reason why loan was taken. - Amount Paid: Amount that the employee has paid back on this loan to date. - Payee: Payee associated with the employee loan. > Note: Note the following: - The payee must be an existing payee and have a Payee Type set to Loans on the Payees form. - You can only use payees whose Third Party Format for the Processor ID associated with the Payroll Check Account is set to Cachet or –Select– on the ACH Originators form.
  • Client ID (required): ID of the client for this loan item.
  • Employee Identifier (required): Either the SSN, Employee ID, or the Employee Number of an employee who works for the client. (Note: Only the last four digits of the SSN display when you review the information on the File Content tab.)
  • Loan Number: Number associated with the loan.
  • Loan Date: Date on which this loan was granted.
  • Loan Amount (required): Amount granted to the employee. (This value must be greater than zero.)
  • Loan Payment (required): Amount to deduct automatically from each paycheck to repay the loan.
  • Payment Frequency (required): How often the payroll deduction is made:
  • O: Once per month.
  • P: Once per payroll period.
  • A: All payroll types.
  • Payback Amount (required): Amount required to consider the loan paid in full, which is the amount of this loan plus interest (if any). (Note: This amount can be different from the loan amount.)
  • Deduction Code (required): Code used for the employee loan. (Note: The deduction type must equal the employee loan payment.)
  • Start Date: Date on which payroll deductions will begin to pay back the loan.
  • Stop Date: Date on which payroll deductions will cease.
  • Reason for Loan: Reason why loan was taken.
  • Amount Paid: Amount that the employee has paid back on this loan to date.

Importing Employee One-Time Deductions

You can import changes to employee one-time deductions to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: Note the following when using this import template:

  • This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors. (An error message displays, if the deduction does not meet this criteria.)

  • Import files accept multiple rows for the same employee with the same deduction code. In this situation, the codes import into the scheduled deduction record displaying one row, per row, in the import file.

To upload and import employee one-time deductions, do the following:

  1. Select Client.

  2. From Payroll|Change, select Scheduled Deductions.

If needed, you may enter more than one line for an individual employee. Note: For security purposes, the system only displays the last four digits of the SSN on the File Content tab when you use this number in Column 2 as the Employee Identifier. - Deduction Code (required): The deduction code for the client. - Amount (required): The deduction amount that is either a percentage or fixed amount, depending on the calculation method defined for the deduction code. - Stop Date: The date after which the system ceases taking the deduction. - Check Stub Description: The check stub description for the employee’s Scheduled Deduction. (If you do not use a description, the system populates this field with the deduction code’s description by default.)

Importing Employee Recurring Deductions

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Employee_Recurring_Deductions.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Employee_Recurring_Deductions.htm

Importing Employee Recurring Deductions

You can import changes to employee recurring deductions to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: Note: This import template is only available for service providers.

To upload and import employee recurring deductions, do the following:

  1. Select Client.

  2. From Payroll|Change, select Recurring Deductions.

  3. On the Recurring Deductions form, click Import [Image: screenshot] to launch the Data Import Tool form. This button displays for all user roles except Inquiry Only.

The Employee Recurring Deductions import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display when you access this template directly from the Recurring Deductions form.

Note: Note: You can also navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

Before you import employee recurring deductions, the system prompts you to clear all payroll deductions for this client’s employees before it loads the deduction file.

  • Select Yes to clear all of the voluntary deductions from the recurring deductions form for each employee in the client.

  • Select No to retain the existing voluntary deductions for the employees.

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Company (required): Unique ID for the client. - Employee Identifier (required): Either the SSN, Employee ID, or the Employee Number of an employee who works for the client. If needed, you may enter more than one line for an individual employee. Note: For security purposes, the system only displays the last four digits of the SSN on the File Content tab when you use this number in Column 2 as the Employee Identifier. - Deduction Code (required): The deduction code for the client. - Amount (required): The deduction amount that is either a percentage or fixed amount, depending on the calculation method defined for the deduction code. - Periods (required): The deduction periods that determine when this deduction is taken from the employee’s net earnings after payroll taxes. - Start Date: The date to begin taking the deduction. - Stop Date: The date after which the system stops taking the deduction. - Maximum Amount: The maximum amount the system can deduct on a monthly, quarterly, yearly, or lifetime basis, as set in the Maximum Amount Basis category. (Note: Any maximum set here overrides the maximums defined for the deduction code. If you do not enter a maximum here, then any maximums set for the deduction code apply.) Note: An error message displays if you try to import either the Maximum Amount or Maximum Amount Basis categories individually without both having a value (leaving them blank will update to NULL). However, you can import the file without completing these columns because they are not mandatory. - Maximum Amount Basis: The basis to which the maximum applies: Monthly, Quarterly, Annually, or Lifetime. The following valid codes are available: - Monthly (M) - Quarterly (Q) - Annually (A) - Lifetime (L)

  • Company (required): Unique ID for the client.

  • Employee Identifier (required): Either the SSN, Employee ID, or the Employee Number of an employee who works for the client. If needed, you may enter more than one line for an individual employee.

  • Deduction Code (required): The deduction code for the client.

  • Amount (required): The deduction amount that is either a percentage or fixed amount, depending on the calculation method defined for the deduction code.

  • Periods (required): The deduction periods that determine when this deduction is taken from the employee’s net earnings after payroll taxes.

  • Start Date: The date to begin taking the deduction.

  • Stop Date: The date after which the system stops taking the deduction.

  • Maximum Amount: The maximum amount the system can deduct on a monthly, quarterly, yearly, or lifetime basis, as set in the Maximum Amount Basis category. (Note: Any maximum set here overrides the maximums defined for the deduction code. If you do not enter a maximum here, then any maximums set for the deduction code apply.)

  • Maximum Amount Basis: The basis to which the maximum applies: Monthly, Quarterly, Annually, or Lifetime.

  • Monthly (M)

  • Quarterly (Q)

  • Annually (A)

  • Lifetime (L) | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | > Note: Note the following when importing Employee Recurring Deductions:

  • Imported deductions must have the Voluntary deduction type defined at the system level.

  • If there are client-specific voluntary deductions defined on the Control tab on the Client Details form, importing is restricted to only those voluntary deduction codes. (See the Recurring Deductions form’s in-product help for more information.)

  • Users must have access to a particular company as specified in the Client Access Groups form on the System|Change menu to import data into that company.

Importing Employee Resident Addresses

You can import changes to employee resident addresses to reduce the amount of manual work required.

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Client ID (required): Unique ID for the client. - Employee ID (required): Unique ID for the employee. - Resident Address - Line 1 (required): First resident address line for the employee. - Resident Address - Line 2: Second resident address line for the employee. - Zip Code (required): Zip code for the employee’s resident address. Note: The system automatically updates the following fields in the Employee Details form if the Zip Code or Geocode changes: - City - State - County - School District - Zip+4: Indicates the ZIP+4 extension for the residential address, if it was not populated by the system. - Geocode: Geocode for the employee’s resident address. - Unincorporated Area: Indicates if the employee’s city or town is not governed by its own local municipal services and is not subject to local resident taxes. - Portland Metro District: Indicates if the employee resides in, or receives pay from the Portland Metro district.   • State
  • County
  • School District

  • Portland Metro District: Indicates if the employee resides in, or receives pay from the Portland Metro district. This is for highly compensated employees who qualify for the Portland Metro SHS tax. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | ## Working with Imported Address Validation

If the import file includes an address that fails validation or USPS-accepted address status, the system displays a dialog during the import process, Database File Import dialog entry, so you can either replace the incorrect address with a validated version or skip (keep) the current address.

Note: A prompt displays in this instance, “Click Replace to use the suggested address or Skip to not import the employee’s address.”

When this prompt displays during the import process, do one of the following:

  • Click Replace with New to update the address in the import file. (Note: To apply the correct address information to all address information that displays in this prompt, select Apply to all, then click Replace with New.)

  • Click Skip to keep the current address.

After you make a selection, the dialog closes and a confirmation message displays, “File content successfully uploaded and ready to be imported.” Click OK. (Note: Any skipped addresses do not display and any replaced addresses display in the File Content tab in the Data Import Tool.)

After you click Import and the import finishes, a confirmation message displays, “File content successfully imported. View report for details.” (Note: Any skipped addresses display the “Skipped with a Comment” import status.)

Note: Note the following:

  • The Database File Import dialog entry does not display in the following instances:

  • When the address in the import file is a valid address with no address suggestions (this is equivalent to entering an address in the Employee Details form when no dialog displays suggestions to update the address).

  • When the fields in a row in the import data display an error (for example, characters instead of numbers in a zip code).

  • The Database File Import dialog entry does display when the address in the import file is a valid address and there is a suggested update (for example, address line 1 is 555 Elm and the suggested address is 555 Elm Drive).

Scheduled payments imported through this process will be added to existing records. Updates to existing scheduled payments must be made manually.

  • Only pay codes with a Fixed calculation method can be imported.

Note: Service providers can enable the ALLPAYCODESINT custom feature code on the System Parameters form to override the restriction listed above, so the system imports any pay codes, including the allowed pay codes that are defined in the Control tab on the Client Details form. (See Using Custom Feature Codes.)

To upload and import employee scheduled payments, do the following:

If needed, you may enter more than one line for an individual employee. (Note: Only the last four digits of the SSN display when you review the information on the File Content tab.) - Pay Code (required): The pay code for this scheduled payment. - Status (required): The status of the scheduled payment. - Amount (required): The scheduled payment that is either a percentage or fixed amount, depending on the calculation method defined for the payment. - Periods: The payment periods that determine when this scheduled payment is taken from the employee’s net earnings after payroll taxes. - Start Date: The date the system starts taking the payment. - Stop Date: The date after which the system stops taking the payment. - Move to T/S: Select Yes to move this expensed reimbursement or fringe pay code to the detail line on the payroll Voucher Earning Detail form once the payroll initializes.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Network_Zip_Codes.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Network_Zip_Codes.htm

Importing Network ZIP Codes

You can Import zip codes to benefit plans that have a network assigned with the Network ZIP Codes import template.

Note: Note: This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors.

To upload and import ZIP codes, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office, then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.
  2. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Network ZIP Codes import template option. When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it. The sample header file contains a single column header labeled “ZIP”.) The layout requirements are: | Field | Description | | — | — | | Column Number | The corresponding column number for the imported data. | | Category Description | ZIP (required): The ZIP code(s) you are importing. | | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. |
  3. Before you import, you must complete the following required fields. | Use this option | To define this | | — | — | | Plan ID | Benefit plan ID for zip code import. | | Network ID | Network ID for zip code import. |

Updating ZIP Codes

Importing ZIP codes adds them to the benefit plan record, but it does not update the ZIP code records at the system-level. You must enter All ZIP codes at the system-level to attach them to a benefit plan.

System-level zip code records always display City & State information in the table. If this information is not displayed, then the zip code record does not exist at the system-level. When zip code records are correctly entered at the system-level, you can attach them to the benefit plan.

The import form can save the imported record, but when you select the Network ID to view the benefit plan’s networks in the Benefit Network Locations form, the system displays the following error message for each ZIP code that cannot be validated:

Warning - Key [ZIP code] is not valid for ZIP codes

PrismHR recommends that you review all imported ZIP codes and update ZIP code records in the Zip Codes form before you import. For more information, see Setting Up Zip Codes.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Offer_Types.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Offer_Types.htm

Importing Offer Types

You can use this import template to import/update offer types for existing benefit plans. This will save time and effort to manually add/update the Offer Type field on the Group Benefit Plans form. (If you try to modify any other field using this process, you will receive an error.)

Note: Note the following:

  • This import template is only available to service providers.

  • Client Access Group Security is not enabled on this form.

To import and update offer types:

  1. To access this form, click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office). In the Operations|Import menu, click Data Import Tool.

  2. Select Offer Types in Import Template.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Data File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

The layout requirements are:

Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Plan ID (required): Unique identifier for the benefit plan. - Plan Description (required): Description of the benefit plan. - Insurance Class (required): Indicates the type of coverage this plan provides. - Offer Type (required): Indicates the offer type that classifies the benefit plan.
  • Plan ID (required): Unique identifier for the benefit plan.
  • Plan Description (required): Description of the benefit plan.
  • Insurance Class (required): Indicates the type of coverage this plan provides.
  • Offer Type (required): Indicates the offer type that classifies the benefit plan. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. |
  1. Click Download Data File to download the sample header file. The header file contains the four columns in the File Format tab. Fill in the necessary data for all the Benefit Plan IDs to update the Offer Type to build your Import file.

Note: If you want to update the Offer Type for all Benefit Plan IDs in bulk that do not have an associated offer type, select Prepopulate file (all plans with BLANK Offer Type). The system downloads a .csv file to your system that is pre-populated with data from the Group Benefit Plans for all plans with a BLANK offer type. (If you do not select this field, the system downloads the file with headers only.)

  1. Click Find File to open the File Upload dialog box.

  2. Click Add Files in the File Upload dialog box.

  3. Select the specified Import File from your system that you have created. Once selected, the Import File displays in the File Upload dialog box.

  4. Click Start Upload to upload the file.

  5. Click Close in the File Upload dialog box.

  6. The uploaded Import File name displays in the File Name field on the form. The content of the file displays in the File Content tab. Errors, if any, display in the Messages tab. Correct the errors and redo the process.

  7. Click Import to import the content into PrismHR.

  8. Click Report to display the Imported Offer Types Report. The Import Status column indicates whether the offer type for that plan ID was imported. If not, then the Messages tab states the reason why.

Once the import is successful, the system updates the Offer Type field on the Group Benefit Plans form with the plans contained in the Import File.

You can navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Company ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - Position Code (required) : Abbreviation for the position. - Position Name (required): Name that defines the position. - Position Classification (required): Identifies the job classification. - Position Description: Description for this position. - Supervisory: Indicates a supervisory position. - Tipped Position: Indicates that the position allows tips. - GL Segment 1: Code that defines the G/L account number segment instead of the department or division code. Rarely used, it ties to the EEDP2 mnemonic in the G/L interfaces. - GL Segment 3: Allows you to enter a third G/L code, if necessary. - Alaska Position Code: The code sent to MasterTax for quarterly tax reporting to the state of Alaska. - SOC Code: The Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Code, which only consists of numbers, no dashes. This information is included in the MasterTax RTS file and the Employer and Client LA quarterly files in place of the position’s description. If you do not define a SOC code for the position, the files include the description. - Indiana Seasonal Employee Code: A two-digit code if the position is seasonal and located in Indiana. This code is required for SUI electronic filing in Indiana. - Obsolete: Indicates the position is no longer used. - TTO Code: Indicates a valid Tipped Taxable Occupation Code that applies to an eligible tipped position, which complies with the tips requirements of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.

  • Company ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.

  • Alaska Position Code: The code sent to MasterTax for quarterly tax reporting to the state of Alaska.

  • SOC Code: The Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Code, which only consists of numbers, no dashes. This information is included in the MasterTax RTS file and the Employer and Client LA quarterly files in place of the position’s description. If you do not define a SOC code for the position, the files include the description.

  • Indiana Seasonal Employee Code: A two-digit code if the position is seasonal and located in Indiana. This code is required for SUI electronic filing in Indiana.

  • Obsolete: Indicates the position is no longer used.

  • TTO Code: Indicates a valid Tipped Taxable Occupation Code that applies to an eligible tipped position, which complies with the tips requirements of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | > Note: Note the following when using the Position Codes import template:

  • Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company.

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Positions form cannot import a file containing positions codes using this template and subsequently, Import [Image: screenshot] will not display on this form.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Positions form can view the Position Codes import template, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

Importing Certified Pay Rates for Projects

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Project_Certified_Pay_Rates.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Project_Certified_Pay_Rates.htm

Importing Certified Pay Rates for Projects

You can import certified pay rates (that is, position code, position title, base rate, fringe rate, and prevailing wage rate) for projects to reduce the amount of manual work required.

To upload and import certified pay rates for projects:

  1. You can navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking [Image: screenshot] (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

  2. From the Import Template drop-down menu, select Project (Certified Pay Rates).

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

You can enable one of the following fields during imports:

  • Keep existing data: Retains existing data during the import and only adds or replaces new certified pay rates included in the file for the project.

  • Replace existing data: Replaces existing data with data included in the file but does not remove data that is not included in the file (that is, leaves existing data, adds new data, and updates duplicates). For example, a duplicate would be a client ID, project code, and position code that is already listed on the Certified Pay Rates panel on the Projects form.

  • Remove existing data (default): Removes existing data in the Certified Pay Rates panel on the Projects form that is not included in the file for that client.

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - Project ID (required): Indicates the unique project code for projects subject to certified payroll regulations. - Position Code (required): Indicates the unique code that briefly describes the position. For example, OPER for vehicle operator. - Base Rate: Indicates the portion of the job rate used to calculate the overtime rate. - Fringe Rate: Indicates the fringe portion of the job rate.

  • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.

  • Project ID (required): Indicates the unique project code for projects subject to certified payroll regulations.

  • Position Code (required): Indicates the unique code that briefly describes the position. For example, OPER for vehicle operator.

  • Base Rate: Indicates the portion of the job rate used to calculate the overtime rate.

  • Fringe Rate: Indicates the fringe portion of the job rate. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | When using the Project (Certified Pay Rates) import template, note the following:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Projects form cannot import data using the Project (Certified Pay Rates) import template.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Projects form can view the Project (Certified Pay Rates) import template, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

  • Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company.

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Company ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - Project (required): The unique project code. - Description (required): The project description. - Certified Payroll: Indicates if this project is subject to certified payroll regulations. - G/L Segment 1: The code to use as an alternative to the Project Code. - G/L Segment 2: The G/L code that substitutes for EEPR2 in G/L code routines. - G/L Segment 3: A third G/L code, if needed. - Project Class: The class code for the project. - Obsolete: Indicates if this project is no longer used. - Union Project: Indicates if this project is associated with a union. - Union Code: Indicates the union code for the project. otherwise, the system uses the job rate defined here. - Subtract Benefit/Hour from Calculated Pay Rate: Indicates whether to subtract the employee’s cost of benefits per hour from the employee’s rate when determining the higher rate. - Filter Cert Pay on Jobs: Indicates whether to filter certified payroll on job codes. - Contractor or Subcontractor: Indicates whether a contractor or subcontractor is working on this project. - Name of Contractor: Indicates the contractor’s name as listed on the certified payroll form. - Address: Indicates the contractor’s address to print on the certified payroll report. - Project and Location: Indicates the project and location where the project work takes place. - Project or Contract No.: Indicates a project or contract number. - Signatory Name: Indicates the name that appears on the certified payroll form, which is the person responsible for this project. - Signatory Title: Indicates the title that appears on the certified payroll form. - Fringe Benefits Paid to Approved Plans: Indicates if fringe benefits are paid to approved plans, funds, or programs. - Fringe Benefits Paid in Cash: Indicates if fringe benefits are paid in cash. - Report Hours Paid Instead of Hours Worked: Indicates if you want to include pay codes in the report that are flagged as being included in the certified payroll report but do not represent hours worked, such as sick time. - CA License Type: Indicates the license type: Contractor State License Board, Professional License, or Other License. - CA License No: Indicates the license number that should be presented in the CA XML file. Importing Shift Codes

You can use this import template to import shift codes to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: Note: This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors.

To upload and import shift codes, do the following:

  1. Select Client.

  2. From the Client|Change menu, select Shifts.

The Shift Codes import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display when you access this template directly from the Shifts form.

You can navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - Shift Code (required): Code for the shift. - Description (required): Description for this shift. - Differential Method: Method to calculate shift differentials. - Differential Amount: Percentage or fixed amount, based on the differential method selected. - Include in Pay Rate: Adds this shift’s differential pay to the employee’s regular pay rate. Otherwise, it uses a separate pay code. - Regular Pay Code: Code to pay the shift differential associated with regular hours. - Overtime Pay Code: Code to pay the shift differential associated with overtime (premium) hours. - Overtime Pay Factor: Pay factor (usually 1.5) to multiply the overtime shift premium amount when using a separate pay code. - Per Diem Percent: Percent to allocate to non-taxable per diem when paid using the percentage method. - Calc O/T Differential on Straight Rate: Calculates the differential on overtime pay using the straight pay rate.

  • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.

  • Shift Code (required): Code for the shift.

  • Description (required): Description for this shift.

  • Differential Method: Method to calculate shift differentials.

  • Differential Amount: Percentage or fixed amount, based on the differential method selected.

  • Include in Pay Rate: Adds this shift’s differential pay to the employee’s regular pay rate. Otherwise, it uses a separate pay code.

  • Regular Pay Code: Code to pay the shift differential associated with regular hours.

  • Overtime Pay Code: Code to pay the shift differential associated with overtime (premium) hours.

  • Overtime Pay Factor: Pay factor (usually 1.5) to multiply the overtime shift premium amount when using a separate pay code.

  • Per Diem Percent: Percent to allocate to non-taxable per diem when paid using the percentage method.

  • Calc O/T Differential on Straight Rate: Calculates the differential on overtime pay using the straight pay rate. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | > Note: Note the following when using the Shift Codes import template:

Importing State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA)

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_State_Tax_Bill_Rates_SUTA.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_State_Tax_Bill_Rates_SUTA.htm

Importing State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA)

You can import changes to Client State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA) to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: Note: This import template is only available to service providers who have full access to the State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA) form enabled for their user role and for non-client reporting states.

To upload and import state tax bill rates:

  1. Select Client.

  2. From Client|Change, select State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA).

  3. On the State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA) form, click Import [Image: screenshot] to launch the Data Import Tool form. (This button displays for all user roles except Inquiry Only.)

The State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA) import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display when you access this template directly from the State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA) form.

You can also navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

Note: Note the following:

  • Importing only creates/adds new entries and does not edit or update existing state tax bill rate entries.

  • If you try to import a record with the exact same state code and effective date combination as an existing record the following message displays, “A record already exists for Client <Client ID> for <state code> with an effective date of <effective date>. Updates to existing records should be done on the State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA) form.”

  • You can import at the operations level for single clients or for multiple clients at once.

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - State Code (required): The two-character state code. - Effective Date (required): The date when the bill rate goes into effect. - SUTA Bill Rate (required): The SUTA Bill Rate for the state that applies to the client. - Officer SUTA Rate: The Officer SUTA Rate, if it is different for officers. - SDI Rate: The employer’s SDI Rate, if the employer pays disability insurance in this state. - Location Code: The location code where the billing rate applies. If the location is not valid for the client an error message displays, “Location Code is not valid for Client <XXX>.” - Lock Down Employer: Set Yes or No (upper, lower, or mixed case) to lock down the employees working in this state to one of the employer IDs. This lock goes into effect during payroll calculation and new hire/rehire. > Note: Note the following: - If you set the Location Code field to Yes, the Lock Down Employer field is not available. An error message displays, “The lock-down option is not available when rates are by location.” - If you do not use Yes, No, or Null in this field (that is, you enter another option), the following error message displays, “Lock Down Employer - Valid entry is required.” - Lock New Hire: Set Yes or No (upper, lower, or mixed case) to lock new or rehired personnel working in this state to the employer. > Note: Note the following: - You must set the Lock Down Employer field to Yes to use this field. If you do not provide a lock down employer an error message displays, “Lock Down Employer is required if Lock New Hire is set to Yes.” - If you set the Location Code field to Yes, the Lock Down Employer field is not available. An error message displays, “The lock-down option is not available when rates are by location.” - If you do not use Yes, No, or Null in this field (that is, you enter another option), the following error message displays, “Lock New Hire - Valid entry is required.” - If you set an option in this field, but not for the Employer ID field the following error message displays, “Corresponding employer ID required for Lock New Hire.” - Lock New Hire 2: Set Yes or No (upper, lower, or mixed case) to lock new or rehired personnel working in this state to the employer. > Note: Note the following: - You must set the Lock Down Employer field to Yes to use this field. If you do not provide a lock down employer an error message displays, “A Lock Down Employer is required.” - If you set multiple Lock New Hire fields to Yes an error message displays, “Only 1 Employer can be locked down at a time.” - If you set the Location Code field to Yes, the Lock Down Employer field is not available. An error message displays, “The lock-down option is not available when rates are by location.” - If you do not use Yes, No, or Null in this field (that is, you enter another option), the following error message displays, “Lock New Hire - Valid entry is required.” - If you set an option in this field, but not for the Employer ID 2 field the following error message displays, “Corresponding employer ID required for Lock New Hire.” - Lock New Hire 3: Set Yes or No (upper, lower, or mixed case) to lock new or rehired personnel working in this state to the employer. > Note: Note the following: - You must set the Lock Down Employer field to Yes to use this field. If you do not provide a lock down employer an error message displays, “A Lock Down Employer is required.” - If you set multiple Lock New Hire fields to Yes an error message displays, “Only 1 Employer can be locked down at a time.” - If you set the Location Code field to Yes, the Lock Down Employer field is not available. An error message displays, “The lock-down option is not available when rates are by location.” - If you do not use Yes, No, or Null in this field (that is, you enter another option), the following error message displays, “Lock New Hire - Valid entry is required.” - If you set an option in this field, but not for the Employer ID 3 field the following error message displays, “Corresponding employer ID required for Lock New Hire.” The following fields indicate the miscellaneous override rates for employer-paid taxes. (Note: If you leave any of State Misc fields blank, the system uses the default rate.) - State Misc1 Rate: The State Misc1 Rate (Tax ID 26). - State Misc2 Rate: The State Misc2 Rate (Tax ID 28). - State Misc3 Rate: The State Misc3 Rate to set employer tax rates for tax codes 22-41 (Massachusetts) and 48-41 (Washington). - State Misc4 Rate: The State Misc4 Rate to set employer tax rates for tax codes 24-54 (Minnesota). The rest of the fields are sometimes associated to include multi-value arrays, which are indicated by displaying a <number> at the end of the field name: - Employer ID, Employer ID 2, and Employer ID 3: The employer ID to which this SUTA bill rate applies. - Overbill Credit Amount, Overbill Credit Amount 2, and Overbill Credit Amount 3: The overbill credit amount back rate only if it is different from the SUTA bill rate. - Location Rate Obsolete Date: If this rate is for a specific location that is closing, and the code is no longer used in calculations, this date refers to the last active pay date. - Overbill CR Bill Code: The overbill CR bill code to use for credit backs for SUTA overlimit credits instead of the default. - Wage Base Override: The wage base override if you want to use a different amount than that specified in the Vertex guide. For example, Michigan has two tiers based on experience. - SUTA Bill Rate 2 and SUTA Bill Rate 3: The SUTA Bill Rate for the state that applies to the client.

  • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.

  • State Code (required): The two-character state code.

  • Effective Date (required): The date when the bill rate goes into effect.

  • SUTA Bill Rate (required): The SUTA Bill Rate for the state that applies to the client.

  • Officer SUTA Rate: The Officer SUTA Rate, if it is different for officers.

  • SDI Rate: The employer’s SDI Rate, if the employer pays disability insurance in this state.

  • Location Code: The location code where the billing rate applies. If the location is not valid for the client an error message displays, “Location Code is not valid for Client <XXX>.”

  • Lock Down Employer: Set Yes or No (upper, lower, or mixed case) to lock down the employees working in this state to one of the employer IDs. This lock goes into effect during payroll calculation and new hire/rehire.

  • If you set the Location Code field to Yes, the Lock Down Employer field is not available. An error message displays, “The lock-down option is not available when rates are by location.”

  • If you do not use Yes, No, or Null in this field (that is, you enter another option), the following error message displays, “Lock Down Employer - Valid entry is required.”

  • Lock New Hire: Set Yes or No (upper, lower, or mixed case) to lock new or rehired personnel working in this state to the employer.

  • You must set the Lock Down Employer field to Yes to use this field. If you do not provide a lock down employer an error message displays, “Lock Down Employer is required if Lock New Hire is set to Yes.”

  • If you set the Location Code field to Yes, the Lock Down Employer field is not available. An error message displays, “The lock-down option is not available when rates are by location.”

  • If you do not use Yes, No, or Null in this field (that is, you enter another option), the following error message displays, “Lock New Hire - Valid entry is required.”

  • If you set an option in this field, but not for the Employer ID field the following error message displays, “Corresponding employer ID required for Lock New Hire.”

  • Lock New Hire 2: Set Yes or No (upper, lower, or mixed case) to lock new or rehired personnel working in this state to the employer.

  • You must set the Lock Down Employer field to Yes to use this field. If you do not provide a lock down employer an error message displays, “A Lock Down Employer is required.”

  • If you set multiple Lock New Hire fields to Yes an error message displays, “Only 1 Employer can be locked down at a time.”

  • If you set the Location Code field to Yes, the Lock Down Employer field is not available. An error message displays, “The lock-down option is not available when rates are by location.”

  • If you do not use Yes, No, or Null in this field (that is, you enter another option), the following error message displays, “Lock New Hire - Valid entry is required.”

  • If you set an option in this field, but not for the Employer ID 2 field the following error message displays, “Corresponding employer ID required for Lock New Hire.”

  • Lock New Hire 3: Set Yes or No (upper, lower, or mixed case) to lock new or rehired personnel working in this state to the employer.

  • You must set the Lock Down Employer field to Yes to use this field. If you do not provide a lock down employer an error message displays, “A Lock Down Employer is required.”

  • If you set multiple Lock New Hire fields to Yes an error message displays, “Only 1 Employer can be locked down at a time.”

  • If you set the Location Code field to Yes, the Lock Down Employer field is not available. An error message displays, “The lock-down option is not available when rates are by location.”

  • If you do not use Yes, No, or Null in this field (that is, you enter another option), the following error message displays, “Lock New Hire - Valid entry is required.”

  • If you set an option in this field, but not for the Employer ID 3 field the following error message displays, “Corresponding employer ID required for Lock New Hire.”

  • State Misc1 Rate: The State Misc1 Rate (Tax ID 26).

  • State Misc2 Rate: The State Misc2 Rate (Tax ID 28).

  • State Misc3 Rate: The State Misc3 Rate to set employer tax rates for tax codes 22-41 (Massachusetts) and 48-41 (Washington).

  • State Misc4 Rate: The State Misc4 Rate to set employer tax rates for tax codes 24-54 (Minnesota).

  • Employer ID, Employer ID 2, and Employer ID 3: The employer ID to which this SUTA bill rate applies.

  • Overbill Credit Amount, Overbill Credit Amount 2, and Overbill Credit Amount 3: The overbill credit amount back rate only if it is different from the SUTA bill rate.

  • Location Rate Obsolete Date: If this rate is for a specific location that is closing, and the code is no longer used in calculations, this date refers to the last active pay date.

  • Overbill CR Bill Code: The overbill CR bill code to use for credit backs for SUTA overlimit credits instead of the default.

  • Wage Base Override: The wage base override if you want to use a different amount than that specified in the Vertex guide. For example, Michigan has two tiers based on experience.

  • SUTA Bill Rate 2 and SUTA Bill Rate 3: The SUTA Bill Rate for the state that applies to the client. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | > Note: Note the following when using the State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA) import template:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA) form cannot import data using the State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA) import template and subsequently, the Data Import Tool icon will not display on this form.

  • Users whose user role is set to FULL or INQUIRY for the State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA) form, but whose user role is also set to DENY for the Data Import Tool cannot view the Import icon on the State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA) form.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA) form can view the State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA) import template, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

  • Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company.

Importing State Tax Rates (SUTA)

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_State_Tax_Rates_SUTA.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_State_Tax_Rates_SUTA.htm

Importing State Tax Rates (SUTA)

You can import changes to Client State Tax Rates (SUTA) to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: Note: This import template is only available to service providers who have full access to the State Tax Rates (SUTA) form enabled for their user role and for non-client reporting states.

To upload and import state tax rates:

  1. Select Client.

  2. From Client|Change, select State Tax Rates (SUTA).

  3. On the State Tax Rates (SUTA) form, click Import [Image: screenshot] to launch the Data Import Tool form. (This button displays for all user roles except Inquiry Only.)

The State Tax Rates (SUTA) import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display when you access this template directly from the State Tax Rates (SUTA) form.

You can also navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

Note: You can import at the operations level for single clients or for multiple clients at once.

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - State Code (required): The two-character state code. - Effective Date (required): The date when the rate goes into effect. - SUTA Bill Rate: The SUTA Bill Rate for the state that applies to the client. - Officer SUTA Rate: The Officer SUTA Rate, if it is different for officers. - SDI Rate: The employer’s SDI Rate, if the employer pays disability insurance in this state. - Wage Base Override: The taxable Wage Base Override the system should use for SUTA billing calculations for the state. - State Misc 3 Employee Rate: The State Misc 3 Employee Rate to set employee tax rates for codes 22-40 (Massachusetts) or 48-40 (Washington) paid family medical leave. For example, you can decrease the tax rate paid by employees. The following fields indicate the miscellaneous override rates for employer-paid taxes. (Note: If you leave any of State Misc fields blank, the system uses the default rate.) - State Misc1 Rate: The State Misc1 Rate (Tax ID 26). - State Misc2 Rate: The State Misc2 Rate (Tax ID 28). - State Misc3 Rate: The State Misc3 Rate to set employer tax rates for tax codes 22-41 (Massachusetts) and 48-41 (Washington). - State Misc4 Rate: The State Misc4 Rate to set employer tax rates for tax codes 24-54 (Minnesota).

  • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.

  • State Code (required): The two-character state code.

  • Effective Date (required): The date when the rate goes into effect.

  • SUTA Bill Rate: The SUTA Bill Rate for the state that applies to the client.

  • Officer SUTA Rate: The Officer SUTA Rate, if it is different for officers.

  • SDI Rate: The employer’s SDI Rate, if the employer pays disability insurance in this state.

  • Wage Base Override: The taxable Wage Base Override the system should use for SUTA billing calculations for the state.

  • State Misc 3 Employee Rate: The State Misc 3 Employee Rate to set employee tax rates for codes 22-40 (Massachusetts) or 48-40 (Washington) paid family medical leave. For example, you can decrease the tax rate paid by employees.

  • State Misc1 Rate: The State Misc1 Rate (Tax ID 26).

  • State Misc2 Rate: The State Misc2 Rate (Tax ID 28).

  • State Misc3 Rate: The State Misc3 Rate to set employer tax rates for tax codes 22-41 (Massachusetts) and 48-41 (Washington).

  • State Misc4 Rate: The State Misc4 Rate to set employer tax rates for tax codes 24-54 (Minnesota). | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | > Note: Note the following when using the State Tax Rates (SUTA) import template:

  • If you select a state code based on settings on the State Rules form and on the Tax tab on the Client Details form a warning displays on the Messages tab in this import template before you select Import, which prevents you from adding an unnecessary record if the state is not set up as a client reporting state.

For example:

  • If the SUTA PEO/Client Based field is set to SUTA is PEO Based on the State Rules form the following message displays, “Warning: <state code> is not a client reporting state. There should not be a client reporting entry required for Client <Client ID>. Row <row number>.”

  • If there is no state code set on the Tax tab in the State Tax Setup panel on the Client Details form the following message displays, “Warning: The State Information for <Client ID>/<State Code> is not on Client Details State Tax Setup section. Row <row number>.”

  • If the SUTA PEO/Client Based field is set to SUTA is PEO Based on the State Rules form AND you select the Officer SUTA Client Based field the following message displays, “Warning: Client Reporting is required for Officers only in <state code> for Client <Client ID>. Row <row number>.”

Note: These warnings are informational only and when you select Import, the system imports the data unless there are other failure messages. In addition, the warning messages display in the Confirmation Report after the import finishes with the “Success” import status.

  • Two failure errors occur in conjunction with the Wage Base Override column:

  • If the amount is less than zero (0) the following error displays, “You can’t set an override wage base less than zero - Client <Client ID> Row <row number>.”

  • If the amount is equal to zero (0) the following error displays, “You can’t set an override wage base of zero - Client <Client ID> Row <row number>.”

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the State Tax Rates (SUTA) form cannot import data using the State Tax Rates (SUTA) import template and subsequently, the Data Import Tool icon will not display on this form.

  • Users whose user role is set to FULL or INQUIRY for the State Tax Rates (SUTA) form, but whose user role is also set to DENY for the Data Import Tool cannot view the Import icon on the State Tax Rates (SUTA) form.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the State Tax Rates (SUTA) form can view the State Tax Rates (SUTA) import template, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

  • Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company.

Importing Third Party Sick Pay Adjustments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Third_Party_Sick_Pay_Adjustment.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Third_Party_Sick_Pay_Adjustment.htm

Importing Third Party Sick Pay Adjustments

You can use this import template to import third-party sick pay adjustments to create adjustment vouchers and client bill pendings for each record to reduce the amount of manual work required.

To upload and import third-party sick pay adjustments, do the following:

  1. Click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

  2. In the Data Import Tool form, select the Third Party Sick Pay Adjustment import template option.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - Employee ID (required): Unique identifier for the employer. - Adjustment Date (required): Indicates the date the system uses to derive the tax year, quarter, and month to adjust. - Bill Date (optional): Indicates the date to use for any billing transaction. - Employer ID (required): Indicate the employer ID affected by this adjustment. Note: If you import an Employer ID in a row in the import file that is not assigned to or is an Alternate Employer for the Client ID in the same row an error message displays, “Must be a valid Employer ID for the client,” and the row does not import. - Federal Taxable Sick Pay (optional): Indicates the total amount paid to the employee by a third-party insurer to cover lost wages during an illness. - Federal Non-Taxable Sick Pay (optional): Indicates the amount of sick pay that was not taxable because it was attributed to employee contributions to insurance premiums. - Federal Income Tax Withheld (optional): Indicates the amount of federal income tax withheld by the third-party insurer. - FICA Taxable Sick Pay (optional): Indicates the amount of taxable sick pay paid to the employee by a third-party insurer to cover lost wages during an illness. - FICA Non-Taxable Sick Pay (optional): Indicates the sick pay that was not taxable because it was attributed to employee contributions to insurance premiums. - Social Security Tax Withheld (optional): Indicates the amount of Social Security tax withheld by the third-party insurer. - Medicare Tax Withheld (optional): Indicates the amount of Medicare tax withheld by the third-party insurer. - Adjust Client Tax Register? (optional): Indicates whether the system should update the client’s register for client-based taxes. - State Code (optional): Indicates the two-character postal code for the state that might have miscellaneous state taxes, such as Hawaii employee disability tax. Note: You can indicate a two-character state code (for example, CA, which can be uppercase or lowercase) or an authority ID (for example, 05). - Tax ID (optional): Indicates the tax ID for the state tax withheld from the employee by the third-party insurer. - Taxable Pay (optional): Indicates the taxable pay applicable to that state. Note: If you indicate an amount in the Taxable Pay or the Tax Withheld category, you must include a State Code and a Tax ID. - Tax Withheld (optional): Indicates the tax withheld by the third-party insurer for that state.

  • Client ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.

  • Employee ID (required): Unique identifier for the employer.

  • Adjustment Date (required): Indicates the date the system uses to derive the tax year, quarter, and month to adjust.

  • Bill Date (optional): Indicates the date to use for any billing transaction.

  • Employer ID (required): Indicate the employer ID affected by this adjustment.

  • Federal Taxable Sick Pay (optional): Indicates the total amount paid to the employee by a third-party insurer to cover lost wages during an illness.

  • Federal Non-Taxable Sick Pay (optional): Indicates the amount of sick pay that was not taxable because it was attributed to employee contributions to insurance premiums.

  • Federal Income Tax Withheld (optional): Indicates the amount of federal income tax withheld by the third-party insurer.

  • FICA Taxable Sick Pay (optional): Indicates the amount of taxable sick pay paid to the employee by a third-party insurer to cover lost wages during an illness.

  • FICA Non-Taxable Sick Pay (optional): Indicates the sick pay that was not taxable because it was attributed to employee contributions to insurance premiums.

  • Social Security Tax Withheld (optional): Indicates the amount of Social Security tax withheld by the third-party insurer.

  • Medicare Tax Withheld (optional): Indicates the amount of Medicare tax withheld by the third-party insurer.

  • Adjust Client Tax Register? (optional): Indicates whether the system should update the client’s register for client-based taxes.

  • State Code (optional): Indicates the two-character postal code for the state that might have miscellaneous state taxes, such as Hawaii employee disability tax.

  • Tax ID (optional): Indicates the tax ID for the state tax withheld from the employee by the third-party insurer.

  • Taxable Pay (optional): Indicates the taxable pay applicable to that state.

  • Tax Withheld (optional): Indicates the tax withheld by the third-party insurer for that state. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | > Note: Note the following when importing Third Party Sick Pay Adjustment data:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Third-Party Sick Pay Adjustment form cannot import data using the Third Party Sick Pay Adjustment import template.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Third-Party Sick Pay Adjustment form can view the Third Party Sick Pay Adjustment import template, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

  • Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company.

  • You can indicate a negative value in the following categories:

  • Federal Taxable Sick Pay

  • Federal Non-Taxable Sick Pay

  • Federal Income Tax Withheld

  • FICA Taxable Sick Pay

  • Social Security Tax Withheld

  • Medicare Tax Withheld

  • Taxable Pay

  • Tax Withheld
