Importing Tips and Overtime Data

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Tip_OT_Register.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_Tip_OT_Register.htm

Importing Tips and Overtime Data

You can use this import template to import employee tips and overtime data to reduce the amount of manual work required.

To upload and import tips and overtime data:

  1. Select Client.

  2. Click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu. The Data Import Tool form displays.

  3. Select Tip OT Register.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

Note: Before you begin the import, you can select to Overwrite Existing Data, which performs as follows in these conditions:

  • TTO Code and Tip Amount resides in the import file: Overwrites the existing data with the data in the import file when the Employer ID, Client ID, Employee ID, Year, and TTO Code information resides in the import file. (If you do not enable this field and that information exists in the import file, the data does not import and an error message displays, “A Tip amount already exists.”)

  • Overtime Amount resides in the import file: Overwrites the Overtime Amount with the data in the import file when the Employer ID, Client ID, Employee ID, and Year information resides in the import file. (If you do not enable this field and that information exists in the import file, the system does not overwrite the existing Overtime Amount and an error message displays, “An Overtime amount already exists.”)

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Employer ID (required): Unique identifier for the employer. - Company ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - Employee ID (required): Unique identifier for the employee. - YEAR (required): indicates the tax year. - TTO Code: The Tipped Taxable Occupation Code (TTO). - Tip Amount: The calculated total of the TTO tip amount. - Overtime Amount: The approximate portion of overtime.

  • Employer ID (required): Unique identifier for the employer.

  • Company ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.

  • Employee ID (required): Unique identifier for the employee.

  • YEAR (required): indicates the tax year.

  • TTO Code: The Tipped Taxable Occupation Code (TTO).

  • Tip Amount: The calculated total of the TTO tip amount.

  • Overtime Amount: The approximate portion of overtime. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | > Note: Note the following when using the Tip OT Register import template:

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY or DENY for the Qualified Tips and Overtime form cannot import data using the Tip OT Register import template.

  • The import file must contain a Tip Amount, Overtime Amount, or both amounts. Otherwise, an error message displays, “A Tip or OT Amount must be imported.”

Importing Workers’ Compensation Billing Modifiers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_WC_Billing_Modifiers.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Data_Import_Tool/Import_WC_Billing_Modifiers.htm

Importing Workers’ Compensation Billing Modifiers

You can import changes to workers’ compensation policy information to reduce the amount of manual work required. At the Operations level, service providers can import this information for multiple clients.

Note: Note: This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors.

To upload and import workers’ compensation billing modifiers:

  1. Select Client.

  2. From Client|Change, select W/C Billing Modifiers.

  3. On the W/C Billing Modifiers form, click Import [Image: screenshot] to launch the Data Import Tool form. (This button displays for all user roles except Inquiry Only.)

The W/C Billing Modifiers import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display when you access this template directly from the Positions form.

You can also navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Company ID (required): Unique identifier for the client. - State Code (required): State code for the client’s address. - Effective Date (required): A new effective date. - Location: If the rate applies to a specific location for this client, this is the location or existing location billing modifier record. - Use Override Rates? (required): Calculates the billing amount using the override rates. - Discount/Debit: The employer’s discount/debit rate. - Modifier: The employer’s modifier rate. - W/C Class Code: The workers’ compensation classification code. - Billing Override Rate: The rate per hundred dollars in wages or per hour worked (depending on the state) used to calculate the bill amount to the client for this workers’ compensation classification. - Bill on Wages or Hours: Determines whether to bill on wages or hours. The standard is to bill on wages unless the state specifies that the rate is based on hours. Note: You must use either W to represent wages or H to represent hours. - Accrual Override Rate: The rate per hundred dollars in wages or per hour worked (depending on the state) used to calculate the accrual override amount to the client for this workers’ compensation classification.

  • Company ID (required): Unique identifier for the client.

  • State Code (required): State code for the client’s address.

  • Effective Date (required): A new effective date.

  • Location: If the rate applies to a specific location for this client, this is the location or existing location billing modifier record.

  • Use Override Rates? (required): Calculates the billing amount using the override rates.

  • Discount/Debit: The employer’s discount/debit rate.

  • Modifier: The employer’s modifier rate.

  • W/C Class Code: The workers’ compensation classification code.

  • Billing Override Rate: The rate per hundred dollars in wages or per hour worked (depending on the state) used to calculate the bill amount to the client for this workers’ compensation classification.

  • Bill on Wages or Hours: Determines whether to bill on wages or hours. The standard is to bill on wages unless the state specifies that the rate is based on hours.

  • Accrual Override Rate: The rate per hundred dollars in wages or per hour worked (depending on the state) used to calculate the accrual override amount to the client for this workers’ compensation classification. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. | > Note: Note the following when importing W/C Billing Modifiers:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the W/C Billing Modifiers form cannot import data using this template and subsequently, Import [Image: screenshot] will not display on this form. Also, this option does not display as an Import Template option for those users on the Data Import Tool form.

  • Users must have access to a particular company as specified in the Client Access Groups form on the System|Change menu to import data into that company.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

Importing Worksite Locations

You can import changes to worksite locations to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: Note: This import template is available to service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors.

To upload and import worksite locations:

  1. Select Client.

  2. From Client|Change, select Worksite Locations.

  3. On the Worksite Locations form, click Import [Image: screenshot] to launch the Data Import Tool form. (This button displays for all user roles except Inquiry Only.)

The Worksite Locations import template option and its tabs/fields automatically display when you access this template directly from the Positions form.

You can also navigate directly to the Data Import Tool by clicking

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office), then select Data Import Tool on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

When you select the import template that you want, the required file layout displays in the form. Before you can upload and import data, your file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. (Note: You can click Download Sample Header File to download a sample Excel data file in .csv format, which can be saved in either .csv or .txt format before importing it.)

You can enable the Keep existing data for fields not in the import file field, so optional fields in the Worksite Locations import template will keep their existing data during imports. (If you do not enable this field, the system overwrites optional fields with no data during imports.)

Important! When you enable Keep existing data for fields not in the import file in the Worksite Locations import template, the Address entry validation dialog and the File Content tab display blank information for fields not included in the import file, but the import keeps the original information entered on the Worksite Locations form.

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - Company (required): Unique ID for the client. - Location Code (required): Abbreviation for the location. - Location Name (required): Name that defines the worksite location. - Address One (required): First address line for the client. (Note: See “Working with Imported Address Validation,” below.) - Address Two: Second address line for the client. - Zip Code (required) : Zip code for the client’s address. - Geocode: Geocode for the client’s address. - City: City for the client’s address. - County: County for the client’s address. - State: State for the client’s address. - Lat: Latitude for the client’s address. - Long: Longitude for the client’s address. - W/C State (required): State where the client’s location is covered by workers’ compensation insurance. - G/L Seg 1: The first general ledger account number segment code. - G/L Seg 2: The second general ledger account number segment code. - G/L Seg 3: The third general ledger account number segment code. - Min Wage Rate Date: The effective date for the minimum wage rate. - Min Wage: The hourly wage for this location. - Min Cash Wage: The minimum cash wage for this location. - Min Wage Minor: The minimum hourly wage for minors, if it is different than the wage for adults. - Min Cash Wage Minor: The minimum cash wage for minors, if it is different than the wage for adults. - Adult Age: The age that this location classifies individuals as adults. Anyone under this age is considered a minor. - Obsolete Date: The obsolete date for this worksite location. (Note: If you provide an obsolete date but do not provide an obsolete status, the system records the date but leaves the obsolete location unchanged.) - Obsolete Loc?: The obsolete status for this worksite location. (Note: An error displays if you try to import an obsolete location that has active employees.) > Note: Note the following: - If you select Yes but do not include an obsolete date, the system automatically defaults to the date when the import was performed. - If you select No for a location that was previously set to Yes, the system updates the record so it is no longer obsolete (clears the value on the form). - W/C Policy: Defines the W/C policy for this location. - Add Date: The date this location was added. - Default Department: The default department for this location. - Default Division: The default division for this location. - Default Project: The default project for this location. - Default Pay Group: The default pay group for this location. - Remote Location: Defines whether the worksite geocode will be ignored and taxes will be based on the employee’s resident geocode. (Workers Compensation will also follow the resident geocode when enabled on the Benefit tab in the Client Details form.) - EEO Unit Number: The seven-character EEO Unit Number assigned to this location by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission for reporting purposes. - EEO Override Location: The EEO Override Location if employees should appear under a different location on the alternate EEO download. - EEO Federal Contractor: Indicates if this worksite location of the client is a federal contractor and differs from the client or other worksite locations of the client. - EEO Unique Entity ID: Identifies the 12-character (no special characters) Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number issued by the System for Award Management (SAM) to identify businesses and other entities that do business with the federal government. (This field is only necessary if the worksite location differs from other locations.) Note: Only applies if the worksite location of the client is an EEO Federal Contractor. - Override Work Geocode: The Onboarding module looks to this field and automatically populates the work address with the resident address. (This supports work-from-home employees.) Indicates the Override Work GeoCode setting as appropriate. The system only applies the override if there are no overrides set at the system, client, or employee level. Typically, this is used to create “worksite locations” for remote employees. - Use Worksite Location GeoCode (no value): No override; the system uses the worksite location for the GeoCode. This is the default behavior. - Override with Resident GeoCode (R): The system uses the employee’s resident GeoCode, defined in the Employee Details Address tab (either GeoCode or Override GeoCode) instead of the worksite location’s GeoCode. Typically, you can select this when employees assigned to this location work from home. For example, you can use it for a worksite location defined as “Ohio-Based Works From Home” or “Indiana-Based Works From Home.” - Override with Home Location GeoCode (H): The system uses the employee’s “home” location assignment to supply the GeoCode for the location-based portion of taxes. This selection is not routinely used. - Override T/S GeoCode with Resident GeoCode (T): The system uses the employee’s resident GeoCode from the Employee Details Address tab in place of the worksite location’s GeoCode in the timesheet. Note: If none of the options described above are indicated an error displays, “Invalid Override Work Geocode.” - Worksite Federal EIN: Indicates the Worksite Federal EIN if it is different from the client’s employer identification number. - Worksite ID: If required by the state (such as MN), indicates a Worksite ID. This is the Reporting Unit Number used in 601 record on Mastertax RTS file and for AK-Geo Code. - Federal Entity ID: Indicates the Federal Entity ID only if the location is a different federal entity than the client for SBEA reporting purposes. - Exclude this location from E-Verification: Indicates whether to suppress the Submit for E-Verification field from displaying in the following locations: - New Hire form for this worksite location - Personal tab on the Employee Details form when the worksite location is set to Excluded - Enable Remote Verification for this location: Indicates whether to allow I-9 Approvers to remotely examine supporting documents for a new hire’s Form I-9 using an alternative procedure authorized by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

If the import file includes an address that fails validation or USPS-accepted address status, the system displays a dialog during the import process, Database File Import dialog entry, so you can either replace the incorrect address with a validated version or skip (keep) the current address.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The address information consists of the street, city, zip code, geocode, county, state, latitude, and longitude.

When this prompt displays during the import process, do one of the following:

  • Click Replace with New to update the address in the import file.

Note: Note the following:

  • To apply the correct address information to all address information that displays in this prompt, select Apply to all, then click Replace with New.)

  • Clicking Replace with New updates all data with the contents of the data file and removes existing data for that worksite location if there are any blank fields in the import file.

  • Click Skip to keep the current address.

Note: Note the following that happens if you click Skip:

  • The system does not apply the latitude and longitude to the address, which is required for the onboarding process.

  • The system does not import any data in the import file.

After you make a selection, the dialog closes and a confirmation message displays, “File content successfully uploaded and ready to be imported.” Click OK. (Note: Any skipped locations do not display and any replaced locations display in the File Content tab in the Data Import Tool.)

After you click Import and the import finishes, a confirmation message displays, “File content successfully imported. View report for details.” (Note: Any skipped locations display the “Skipped with a Comment” import status.)

Employees who have never had an initialized voucher or have not received a check or arrearage voucher for any client can be deleted using the Delete Unused Employee form.

To delete an unused employee:

  2. From Operations|Utility Processing, select Delete Unused Employee.

  3. Fill in these fields as required.

Fields/Panels Description
Client Enter or select the client (required) associated with the unused employee.
Employee Enter or select the employee (required) you want to delete. The employee’s information displays in the Employment panel.
Employment This field displays the following employee information: - Employment Status: Employee’s position status (for example, ACTIVE) - Employer: Employee’s listed employer - Status Date: Employer’s date of inception - Employer Start Date: Date employee began working for employer - Employment Type: Employee’s type of employment (for example, FULL TIME) - Last Hire Date: Most-recent date of hire - Type Date: Date associated with the Employment Type - Original Hire Date: Date when employee was first hired - Position: Employee’s position - Termination Reason: Reason why employee was terminated
  • Employment Status: Employee’s position status (for example, ACTIVE)
  • Employer: Employee’s listed employer
  • Status Date: Employer’s date of inception
  • Employer Start Date: Date employee began working for employer
  • Employment Type: Employee’s type of employment (for example, FULL TIME)
  • Last Hire Date: Most-recent date of hire
  • Type Date: Date associated with the Employment Type
  • Original Hire Date: Date when employee was first hired
  • Position: Employee’s position
  • Termination Reason: Reason why employee was terminated | Errors | Errors that occurred during this process. | | Warnings | Warnings that occurred during this process. |
  1. Click Delete Employee. A dialog displays asking you to confirm this deletion.

Note: If the employee is currently listed in a payroll batch, an error message displays in the Errors panel and the employee cannot be deleted.

Exporting the ExpertPay File

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Exporting-Expert-Pay.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Exporting-Expert-Pay.htm

Exporting the ExpertPay File

Use the ExpertPay Export form to generate a CSV file that is transmitted to a third-party vendor (ExpertPay). The data is then transmitted by ExpertPay to various garnishment authorities.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, click

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office) > Operations|Action > ExpertPay Export

To build the export file:

  1. Enter Starting Pay Date which is a mandatory date field. It is the starting date for the pay date range for this file.

  2. Enter Ending Pay Date which is a mandatory date field. It is the starting date for the pay date range for this file.

  3. Enter Profile Name for Header — This information is shown in Column B of the ExpertPay CSV file.

  4. Click the Client ID link to limit the report to a selected client or leave blank to include all clients.

  5. Click Build to generate the export file.

  6. Click Close when the process is complete.

After the file is downloaded, the system generates the export file and an error report.

Posting External Third Party Checks Journal

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/External%20Third%20Party%20Checks%20Journal%20Post.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/External Third Party Checks Journal Post.htm

Posting External Third Party Checks Journal

Use the External Third Party Checks Journal Post form to download an export file that can be used to import third party check information to an external G/L system.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To access the form, click Back Office. Under Operations|Action, click External Third Party Checks Journal Post.

To post the External Third Party Checks Journal:

  1. Select a Days Back option to display only the journal data pertaining to that selection, such as 1 Month (default), 2 Months, 3 Months, or 1 Year, or select Show All to display all data.

  2. If you want to select:

  • All transaction dates, select the Select All checkbox in the header row.

  • Specific transaction dates, select the individual checkboxes beside each of the transaction dates.

  1. Click Process Batch. A message displays asking you to confirm posting all selected entries. Do the following:

  • Click Yes if you want to post all the selected entries. A job progress window appears building the external journal posting file. Click Close to close the job progress window once the process is complete. The COMBINED.JOURNAL.POST_xxxxxxxxx zip file is downloaded to your system.

  • Click No if you are not sure. Redo the process.

Note: Note: Click Cancel to undo all the transaction date selections.

Locking the Payroll Processing Through Date

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Lockout%20Payroll%20Processing%20Control%20Date.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Lockout Payroll Processing Control Date.htm

Locking the Payroll Processing Through Date

Use the Lockout Payroll Processing Control Date form to set up a through date at the global level for all clients to prevent payroll calculation and finalization from occurring after that date.

Important! This process impacts everyclient in the system, not just clients who use Pre-ACH. Once it is set up, the system does not allow calculation and posting, even for clients with an ACH Status not equal to ACH.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To set the payroll processing through date:

  1. Click Back Office. On the Operations|Action menu, select Lockout Payroll Processing Control Date.

  2. Complete the following:

Field Name Description
Payroll Processing Through Date Enter or select the date up to which you want to process payroll globally. Important! Note the following: - Setting a date in this field impacts payroll processing globally for allclients. - Use this option if you are a Pre-ACH client who wants to release posting daily after ACH notifications are received. - If you are any other user, then leave this field blank or set up a date far in the future. - If a payroll processing through date is set and you are trying to process payroll on a date beyond that, you cannot proceed. Instead, when you try to process payroll on the Process Payroll form past that date the following error displays: Payroll processing through date is set to . You cannot calculate or finalize a payroll until this date is advanced on the Lockout Payroll Processing Control Date screen. However, if the Suppress Payroll Warnings panel is set to Payroll Processing Through Date - Calculation/Finalization on the Users form, then the system does not display any warnings and you can process payrolls.
  • Setting a date in this field impacts payroll processing globally for allclients.
  • Use this option if you are a Pre-ACH client who wants to release posting daily after ACH notifications are received.
  • If you are any other user, then leave this field blank or set up a date far in the future.
  • If a payroll processing through date is set and you are trying to process payroll on a date beyond that, you cannot proceed. Instead, when you try to process payroll on the Process Payroll form past that date the following error displays:
  1. Click Save to save the payroll processing through date.

Select one of the following:

  • Yes: Saves the payroll processing through date. A confirmation message displays, The payroll processing though date has been set to .

  • No: Returns to the form and displays the existing payroll processing through date. (You can change this date before saving again.)

  1. To delete the existing the payroll processing through date, click Delete.

Select one of the following:

  • Yes: Deletes the existing payroll processing through date on the form and database, and removes any lockout of payroll calculation and payroll finalization.

  • No: Returns to the form and displays the existing payroll processing through date.

Using the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Mass_Employee_Transfer_Import.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Mass_Employee_Transfer_Import.htm

Using the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool

You can use the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool to quickly import a list of employees to transfer to new clients.

Note: Note the following:

  • This tool is only available for service providers who have FULL access to the Mass Employee Transfer Import form.

  • Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Mass Employee Transfer Import form displays the form in read-only format.

  • Users who do not have access to a particular client as configured in Client Access Groups cannot transfer employees into or out of the client using the Mass Employee Transfer Import form.

  • This process accomplishes the same results as executing the standard employee transfer process using the Transfer Employee to New Client form. (See Transferring Employees to New Clients.)

The Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool is available from the Operations|Import Processing menu in the Back Office

[Image: screenshot]

. For example, the following form displays after you access the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool:

[Image: screenshot]

Before you can upload and import data, your source file must be saved in either comma-separated values (.csv) tabular format or text tab delimited (.txt) format with no spaces or special characters in the file name. When you open the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool form, the required file layout displays. The layout must match the requirements for number and order of columns, category descriptions, and the required fields.

In addition, you can use the sample header file before importing to avoid manually creating an import file that matches the import template type.

Note: Note the following when using a comma (,) in a description in your import file:

  • If you include a comma in a description field using the .csv file format, you must enclose the item in double quotes. For example, “Manager, Admin.”

  • If you include a comma in a description field using the .txt file format, no extra formatting is necessary.

Using the Sample Header File

Before starting the import process, you can first download a sample header file by clicking that link on the Mass Employee Transfer Import Tool form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: The header file is in .csv format. You can save the file in .csv or .txt format.

After you click the Download Sample Header File link, the system downloads or prompts for download a sample header file that displays columns and headers that match each column and description for the import template option. Also, the file displays a title that matches the selected option.

To perform a mass employee transfer import:

  1. Select Back Office [Image: screenshot] .

  2. From the Operations|Import Processing menu, select Mass Employee Transfer Import.

The layout requirements are:

Field Description
Column Number The corresponding column number for the imported data.
Category Description - From Client (required): The client ID for the client that the employee is transferring from. - Employee ID (required): The ID of the employee whose information requires a transfer. - To Client (required): The client ID for the client where the employee is transferring. - To Employer (required): The employer ID assigned to the new client where the employee is being transferred. - To Pay Group (required): The pay group for the destination client. - To Retire Plan (optional): The retirement plan where the employee is being transferred. - To Position (required): A valid position for the destination client. - To Location (required): A valid location for the destination client. - To Client Hire Date (required): The hire date to use for the company where the employee is being transferred. Note: After entering or selecting a date, a message containing that date displays. Select Yes to confirm that date should be used to update the Status, Type, Status Type History, Position History, and Pay History. If you select No, the system updates that information using the most recent date for that record in the From Client employee record after the transfer finishes. - Update historical dates? (required): Indicates whether to keep status, type, status type history, position history, and pay history dates. - Transfer YTD Check Stubs (required): The year-to-date check stub details to the company where the employee is transferring. - Terminate Employee in Original Client (required): Indicate whether to terminate the employee and their benefits in the original client. - Termination Date (optional): The date when the transferring employee will be terminated in their old client. - Termination Reason (optional): A valid termination reason code. - Terminate Benefit Coverage Today (required): The terminated group benefits for the employee ends coverage today.
  • From Client (required): The client ID for the client that the employee is transferring from.
  • Employee ID (required): The ID of the employee whose information requires a transfer.
  • To Client (required): The client ID for the client where the employee is transferring.
  • To Employer (required): The employer ID assigned to the new client where the employee is being transferred.
  • To Pay Group (required): The pay group for the destination client.
  • To Retire Plan (optional): The retirement plan where the employee is being transferred.
  • To Position (required): A valid position for the destination client.
  • To Location (required): A valid location for the destination client.
  • To Client Hire Date (required): The hire date to use for the company where the employee is being transferred.
  • Update historical dates? (required): Indicates whether to keep status, type, status type history, position history, and pay history dates.
  • Transfer YTD Check Stubs (required): The year-to-date check stub details to the company where the employee is transferring.
  • Terminate Employee in Original Client (required): Indicate whether to terminate the employee and their benefits in the original client.
  • Termination Date (optional): The date when the transferring employee will be terminated in their old client.
  • Termination Reason (optional): A valid termination reason code.
  • Terminate Benefit Coverage Today (required): The terminated group benefits for the employee ends coverage today. | Required? | Indicates if the field is required. |

  1. Click Find File to open the File Upload dialog box.

  2. Click Add Files in the File Upload dialog box.

  3. Select the specified Import File from your system that you have created. Once selected, the Import File will display in the File Upload dialog box.

  4. Click Start Upload to upload the file.

  5. Click Close on the File Upload dialog box.

  6. The uploaded Import File name will display under the File Name field on the form. The content of the file will display under File Content tab. Errors, if any, will display in the Messages tab. Correct the errors and redo the process.

While processing the uploaded file, the following validation occurs:

  • If any mandatory field is missing from the file, the system displays an error message, “<field name> is a required field.”

  • If the system does not associate the Employee ID with the From Client field, it displays an error message, “Employee <Employee ID> not located in client <From Client>.”

  • If the values in the Pay Group, To Retire Plan, To Position, and To Location fields are not valid for the To Client record, then the system displays an error message, “Record <To Client>.<field value> is not on file in <field’s filename>.”

  • In the Termination Reason field, the system identifies a valid value only if the REASON.CODES contain “Termination.” If you provide any other value, the system displays an error message, “<Termination Reason> is not a valid Term Reason Code.”

  1. Click Import to import the content into PrismHR. After the import finishes, the following occurs:

  • If Transfer YTD Check Stubs is enabled, the program transfers the YTD check stubs.

  • If Terminate Employee in Original Client is enabled, the program terminates the employee on the original client using the corresponding Termination Date and Termination Reason from the upload file.

  • If Terminate Employee in Original Client is disabled, the program does not terminate the employee on the original client.

  • If Terminate Benefit Coverage Today is enabled, the program terminates the employee’s benefit coverage.

  • If the uploaded file contains a mix of employees who are successfully validated and employees that fail the validations, those employees that are successfully validated are transferred appropriately and the employees that fail validation are documented in the error log and are not transferred or terminated.

  1. Click Report to view the transaction report. This report contains the following information:

  • Successfully transferred employees display “Success” in the Import Status column.

  • Employees that failed validation and could not be transferred display “Skipped” in the Import Status column. The “Comments” column for the failed transfer employees displays the error message for whichever failed validation event prevented the transfer.

Calculate Taxes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/New%20Check%20Import/Calculate%20Taxes.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/New Check Import/Calculate Taxes.htm

Calculate Taxes

This is the fifth screen of the check import wizard. Use this form to calculate taxable earnings on pay checks and create payroll vouchers.

Note: Note the following:

  • The Calculate Taxes option on the steps indicator at the top is highlighted to indicate that you are on this screen.

  • You can only access this screen from the Review & Fix Data screen.

  • You cannot find this screen using the normal search function.

  • You cannot save this screen to your Favorites.

  • Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

After calculating taxes, you should compare the totals to the reports from the original system to make sure that the checks and totals match.

You must calculate taxable earnings and create payroll vouchers successfully before finalizing the import. The Finalize & Post button will remain grayed out till you calculate taxable earnings and create payroll vouchers successfully for this check import batch. If you try to run Finalize & Post before calculating taxable earnings and payroll vouchers are created for this check import batch, you will get a prompt stating “Taxes have not been calculated for this batch. You must run the Calculate Taxable Earnings & Create Vouchers process.”

To calculate taxable earnings and create payroll vouchers, complete the following:

  1. Click Calculate Taxable Earnings & Create Vouchers. A job progress window appears showing the processing. The system first calculates taxable earnings and then creates payroll vouchers.

  1. — If payroll vouchers have already been created for this check import batch a pop-up message displays, Payroll vouchers have already been created for this batch. Do you want to delete them and create new payroll vouchers?

  2. — Click OK if you want to delete the existing payroll vouchers of this check import batch and create new ones.

  1. — Click Cancel if you do not want to delete the existing payroll vouchers of this check import batch.

  1. — If the system finds any errors on either process, it will show up on the job progress window.

  2. — Click Close to close the job progress window. A pop-up message confirms that The Create Payroll Vouchers process completed with errors. Click OK to proceed.

  1. — Click Error Report to view the Error Report for Create Payroll Vouchers Process for this check import batch on screen. Click the XLS link to download this error report to your system to review and make the necessary adjustments.

Note: Note: The Error Report button only displays if errors are found while running these processes.

  1. Click Previous to go back to the Review & Fix Data screen to make the adjustments.

  2. Once all errors are fixed for this check import batch, you will see the following sections on the screen:

a. Summary section, which displays the total:

  • Number of Payroll Vouchers for this check import batch

  • Gross Earnings for this check import batch

  • Federal Taxable Pay for this check import batch

  • Deductions for this check import batch

  • Federal Tax for this check import batch (tax code 00-10)

  • FICA Tax for this check import batch (OASDI 00-12 + Medicare 00-11)

  • State Tax for this check import batch (Income and Disability)

  • Other Taxes for this check import batch

  • Expenses for this check import batch

  • Net Pay for this check import batch

The Voucher Summary Report button is available on the top-right in the Summary section only after you have calculated taxable earnings and created vouchers in the Calculate Taxes screen in the Check History Import form. Click this button to download the report in a .csv format. This report runs off the generated vouchers, that is, all vouchers in the current/selected batch and grand totals. Checks not imported are not included in this report. The report is sorted first by the employee’s last name and then by the voucher number. The report has the following columns:

Batch ID, Batch Name, Client ID, Client Name, Employer ID, Employer Name, Voucher Number, Employee Name (in Lastname, Firstname format), Employee ID, Pay Date (in MM/DD/YYYY format), Hours/Units, Federal Taxable Pay, Gross Earnings, Deductions, Federal Tax, FICA Tax, State Tax, Other Tax, Expenses, Net Pay

The TOTALS row provides totals for the following columns:

Hours/Units, Federal Taxable Pay, Gross Earnings, Expenses, Deductions, Federal Tax, FICA Tax

Note: All numbers are formatted up to two decimal places; for example, 1,234,567.89.

  1. — Total Taxes section, which displays the totals of all the different Employer and Employee paid taxes contained in this check import batch.

  2. — The Employee Tax table displays the total value of each of the tax descriptions for this check import batch including the tax code, the taxable amount and the withheld amount.

  1. — The Employer Tax table displays the total value of each of the tax descriptions for this check import batch including the tax code, the taxable amount and the tax amount.

The Total Taxes Report button is available on the top-right in the Total Taxes section only after you have calculated taxable earnings and created vouchers in the Calculate Taxes screen in the Check History Import form. Click this button to download the report in a .csv format. This report runs off the generated vouchers - all imported vouchers in the current/selected batch and grand totals. Checks not imported are not included in this report. The report has the following sections:

  • First Section contains:

  • Batch ID - This is the batch number.

  • Batch Name - The name of the batch.

  • Client - In format “ - ”, for example “102 - Arrow Technologies”.

  • Employer - In format “ - ”, for example “102 - Arrow Technologies”.

  • Total Gross Earnings - For this batch.

  • Total Net Pay - For this batch.

  • Expenses - For this batch.

  • Second Section contains Employee Deductions/Taxes, Employee Contributions/Taxes sections for the batch and their TOTALS broken up into columns.

  • EMPLOYEE TAX section contains the following columns:

  • Tax - Employee paid tax description; for example, Federal Income Tax and Medicare for the batch. Employee paid taxes typically include Federal Income Tax, Earned Income Credit (EIC), OASDI (Social Security Tax), Medicare, State Taxes as applicable etc.

  • Prism Code - Corresponding Prism Codes for the batch; for example, 00-10 and 00-11.

  • Imported Code - Corresponding Imported Code for the batch.

  • Taxable - Corresponding taxable amount for each of the employee paid taxes noted above for the batch; for example, 10,000.00 and 10,000.00t.

  • Withheld - Corresponding amount withheld for each of the employee paid taxes noted above for the batch; for example, 1,000.00 and 145.00.

  • TOTALS - Total amount of employee paid tax withheld for the batch; for example, 1,145.00.

  • EMPLOYER TAX section contains the following columns:

  • Tax - Employer paid tax description; for example, FUTA and Medicare for the batch. Employer paid taxes typically include FUTA, OASDIER (Social Security Tax - employer contribution), MedicareER (Medicare - employer contribution), Employer contribution to State Taxes as applicable, and so on.

  • Prism Code - Corresponding Prism Codes for the batch; for example, 00-17 and 00-15.

  • Imported Code - Corresponding Imported Code for the batch.

  • Taxable - Corresponding taxable amount for each of the employer paid taxes noted above for the batch; for example, 10,000.00 and 10,000.00.

  • Withheld - Corresponding amount withheld for each of the employer paid taxes noted above for the batch; for example, 600.00 and 145.00.

  • TOTALS - Total amount of employee paid tax withheld for the batch; for example, 745.00.

c. Vouchers section, which displays the following:

Voucher Details Report button is available on the top-right in the Vouchers section only after you have calculated taxable earnings and created vouchers in the Calculate Taxes screen in the Check History Report form. Click this button to download the report in a .csv format. This report runs off the generated vouchers - all vouchers in the current/selected batch and grand totals. Checks not imported are not included in this report. The report is sorted first by the employee’s last name and then by the voucher number. The report has the following sections:

  • First Section contains:

  • Employee Name (all caps, as header for the voucher)

  • Batch ID & Voucher Number

  • Company - In format “ - ”, for example “102 - Arrow Technologies” & Pay Date in MM/DD/YY format

  • Employer - In format “ - ”, for example “102 - Arrow Technologies” & Period Begin Date in MM/DD/YY format

  • Employee ID & & Period End Date in MM/DD/YY format

  • Employee Name - In format “Last Name, First Name” & Work State (two letter State Code)

  • Gross Pay & Weeks Worked

  • Non-Cash Pay & 1099 Check? (Y/N)

  • Non-Taxable Pay & School District

  • Gross Receipts

  • Net Pay

  • Second Section contains Earnings, Employee Deductions/Taxes, Employee Contributions/Taxes sections for each voucher and their TOTALS broken up into columns.

  • EARNINGS section contains the following columns:

  • Description - Pay Code description; for exampl,e Regular Pay and Tips.

  • Prism Pay Code - Corresponding Prism Pay Code for the Description above; for example, REG and TIPS.

  • Imported Pay Code - Corresponding imported pay code for the prism pay codes, for example, Regular and Tips.

  • Hours/Units - Corresponding Hours or Units worked for each pay code noted above; for example, 40 and 1.

  • Amount - Corresponding earnings for each pay code noted above; for example, 1,750.00 and 250.00.

  • TOTALS - Totals for earnings noted above; for example, 2,000.00 (1,750.00+250.00)

  • EMPLOYEE DEDUCTION/TAXES section contains the following columns:

  • Description - Employee Deduction or Tax description; for example, Federal Income Tax and Medicare. Employee Deductions/Taxes typically include as applicable State Taxes, Federal Income Tax, Medicare, Social Security and other deductions; for example, Christmas Club, and so on.

  • Prism Code - Corresponding Prism Code; for example, 00-10 and 00-11.

  • Imported Pay Code - Corresponding Imported Code.

  • Amount - Corresponding Amount of deduction or tax; for example, 100 and 62.

  • TOTALS - Total amount of deduction and taxes for the employee; for example, 162.

  • EMPLOYEE CONTRIBUTION/TAXES section contain the following columns:

  • Description - Employer Deduction/Contribution or Tax description; for example, FUTA and Medicare. Employer Contribution/Taxes typically include as applicable State SUTA, FUTA, Medicare, Social Security, Safe Harbor Type 1, HSA Match etc.

  • Prism Code - Corresponding Prism Code; for example, 00-17 and 00-15.

  • Imported Pay Code - Corresponding Imported Code.

  • Amount - Corresponding Amount of deduction/contribution or by employer tax; for example, 98 and 59.

  • TOTALS - Total amount of deduction and taxes for the employee; for example, 157.

An Inline Grid displays the first twenty voucher numbers on the screen. If there are more than twenty vouchers in the check import batch, click the arrows in the bottom-right of your screen to navigate and view them. The vouchers are sorted by employee last name and then employee first name in an ascending order.

  • Voucher Number - shows the Payroll Voucher number. Click the voucher number to view the employee payroll voucher in a modal. You cannot edit any values on this Payroll Voucher screen. You can navigate to the various tabs on the Payroll Voucher form for further details on this employee payroll voucher. Click Cancel or Close to exit the modal.

  • Name - shows the Employee Name for each of the corresponding payroll vouchers for this check import batch. The employee name is shown in Lastname, Firstname format.

  • Employee ID - shows the Employee ID for each of the corresponding payroll vouchers for this check import batch.

  • Hrs/Units - shows the hours/units worked by the employee for the corresponding payroll vouchers for this check import batch.

  • Gross Earnings - shows the gross earnings for each of the corresponding payroll vouchers for this check import batch.

  • Federal Tax Pay - shows the federal taxable pay for each of the corresponding payroll vouchers for this check import batch.

  • Deductions - shows the total deductions for each of the corresponding payroll vouchers for this check import batch.

  • Taxes - shows the total taxes for each of the corresponding payroll vouchers for this check import batch.

  • Net Pay - shows the net pay for the employee for the corresponding payroll vouchers for this check import batch.

  1. Click Close to go back to the Managing Batches for Check Import Process screen. Payroll vouchers are created but are not posted. You can always come to this screen later and post them or delete the created payroll vouchers and create new payroll vouchers and post them.

  2. Click Finalize & Post. A prompt displays, which asks, Do you want to update MasterTax? If you select Yes, the system will create tax journal entries for the imported vouchers and vouchers will be reported via the MasterTax PTS file.

  • Click Yes if you want to update the MasterTax PTS file.

  • Click No if you do not want to update the MasterTax PTS file.

  1. A job progress window opens showing the processing of the finalizing and posting of payroll vouchers for this check import batch.

  2. Click Close once the register update process is complete. A prompt tells you The Finalize and Post process completed successfully. Click OK.

  3. The Import Complete screen opens.

Check History Entry

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/New%20Check%20Import/Check%20History%20Entry.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/New Check Import/Check History Entry.htm

Check History Entry

This is an extension of the third screen of the check import wizard. Use this screen to manually enter a check. (Skip this step if you do not need to enter checks manually.)

Note: Note the following:

  • The Enter Check History option on the steps indicator at the top is highlighted to indicate that you are on this screen. All the other options on the steps indicator are grayed out.

  • You can access this screen when you click the Add Check button on the Enter Check History screen or from the Review & Fix Data screen to edit a check to fix errors or warnings.

  • You cannot find this screen using the normal search function.

  • You cannot save this screen to your Favorites.

  • Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

To manually enter a check:

  1. Complete the following fields:
Field Description
Document ID By default, this will show NEW. When you manually enter a new check, the document ID will be the last document ID number plus one. If you want to edit an existing check, click the Document ID link, and select it from the list of existing document IDs from the selected batch from the dialog box.
Client ID Enter the Client ID or click the Client ID link and select one from the Select Client dialog box.
Employer ID Enter the employer ID or click the Employer ID link to select the employer from the Select Employer dialog box.
Employee ID Enter the employee ID or click the Employee ID link to select the employee from the Select Employee dialog box.
SSN This field is auto-populated with the social security number of the employee once you fill in the above field.
Check Number Enter the check number.
Pay Date Enter the pay date for this check. The following validations apply: Pay Date must be a valid date. Valid date formats are MM/DD/YYYY, MM/DD/YY, MM-DD-YYYY, MM-DD-YY, MM.DD.YYYY, and MM.DD.YY.
Period Start Date Enter the start date of the pay period of this check. This field is optional. The following validations apply: i. — Period Start Date must be a valid date. Valid date formats are MM/DD/YYYY, MM/DD/YY, MM-DD-YYYY, MM-DD-YY, MM.DD.YYYY, and MM.DD.YY. \ ii. \ Period Start Date must be before Period End Date. \ \ — \ — \ \ iii. \ Period Start Date cannot be more than 1 year earlier than the Pay Date. \ \ — \ — \
i. Period Start Date must be a valid date. Valid date formats are MM/DD/YYYY, MM/DD/YY, MM-DD-YYYY, MM-DD-YY, MM.DD.YYYY, and MM.DD.YY.
ii. Period Start Date must be before Period End Date.
iii. Period Start Date cannot be more than 1 year earlier than the Pay Date.
Period End Date Enter the end date of the pay period of this check. This field is optional. The following validations apply: i. — Period End Date must be a valid date. Valid date formats are MM/DD/YYYY, MM/DD/YY, MM-DD-YYYY, MM-DD-YY, MM.DD.YYYY, and MM.DD.YY. \ ii. \ Period End Date must be later than the Period Start Date entered above. \ \ — \ — \ \ iii. \ Period End Date cannot be more than 1 year earlier than the Pay Date. \ \ — \ — \
i. Period End Date must be a valid date. Valid date formats are MM/DD/YYYY, MM/DD/YY, MM-DD-YYYY, MM-DD-YY, MM.DD.YYYY, and MM.DD.YY.
ii. Period End Date must be later than the Period Start Date entered above.
iii. Period End Date cannot be more than 1 year earlier than the Pay Date.
Work State Enter the work state code. This will be used to accrue SUI and W/C liability for the state entered.
Weeks Worked Enter the number of weeks worked.
1099 Check? This field is optional. Select one of the following options: - Yes - If this check is for a self-employed or an independent contractor. - No - If this check is for a W-2 employee.

  1. Click the Edit Code Mapping link to edit code mappings if you are getting errors on the check related to code mapping.
a. The Edit Code Mapping screen opens in a modal.

  1. — The current values for the batch are displayed on the fields. Edit the values as necessary.

  2. — Click Save to save the code mapping changes. The check you were working on is automatically sent through the system validation process. You now return to the check that you were working on in the Enter Check History screen.

  1. Click Save to save this check.
a. If there are no errors:

  1. — If you were entering a NEW pay check, a Document ID will be generated and associated with this pay check and you will return to the Enter Check History screen.

  2. — This check will now be listed in the Enter Check History screen.

  3. — If you were editing an existing check from the Review & Fix Data screen, you will return to the Review & Fix Data screen.

b. If there are errors:
i. You will not be able to save the check.
— —
ii. All the fields that have errors will be highlighted in red.
— —

  1. — A top section shows the number of errors and warnings and lists them along with the field name which has the error.

  2. — Only the first five errors/warnings are listed. If there are more errors/warnings, scroll down to see them.

v. Error/Warning icons will also appear beside the field that needs correction.

  1. — Click on an error/warning icon beside the field to see the error/warning details. This will help you to resolve the error.

  2. — Once you resolve an error, it will not be listed anymore on the top section. The corresponding field will no longer be highlighted in red. The error/warning icon beside the field will also be gone.

  3. — If you generate another error in the process of solving an error, it will also be listed at the top section. The new field which now has an error will be highlighted in red and the error/warning icon will show beside the field name.

ix. Resolve all errors/warnings before you can save the check.

  1. To manually add another check, redo the process.

  2. Click Delete to delete the check.

  3. Click Cancel to refresh the screen at any time.

  4. Click Close to close this window and you will return to Enter Check History screen.

Managing Batches for Check Import Process

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/New%20Check%20Import/Check%20History%20Import.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/New Check Import/Check History Import.htm

Managing Batches for Check Import Process

Use the Check History Import form for batch management for the check import process. All processes required for check imports can be only accessed from this form using a wizard which takes you step by step through the check import process.

Note: Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, click the Back Office menu. Under Operations|Import Processing, click Check History Import.

Important! If you have employees listed in several clients and employers, you might need to complete a successor wage import before processing a check history import. Note the following instances when you should perform this action:

  • An employee is listed in the same employer for multiple companies as an active employee: Since this makes a difference for taxes, it affects how the limits are honored. The employee is listed within the same employer, so the system pushes the taxes that were previously processed at the first company to the taxes on this import, so they are over the limit and not including any charges.

  • An employee is listed in two different employers: The voucher honors the limit for each, so the system does not display any of the taxes over the limit but instead collects those taxes as well.

Note: This is typically correct, but if a client only collects the taxes under one employer and the employee is listed in two employers and you do not want to account for taxes under both employers, you can use successor wages to account for those wages. With successor wages in place, the system will not collect taxes under both employers.

Batch Management Dashboard

This Dashboard has the following sections:

  • Imports in Progress

  • Past Imports

  • Tools

Imports in Progress

Note: Note: If you want to copy a batch, you must first set up a new batch.

  • If you want to copy to a new batch, click New Import to create a new check import batch and then click Copy Existing Import.

  • If you want to copy to an existing batch, click the Batch ID link and navigate to the Import Setup window and then click Copy Existing Import.

Import Setup

This is the first screen of the check import wizard. Use this form to set up a batch for the check import process or update an existing check import batch.

  • The Import Setup option on the steps indicator at the top is highlighted to indicate that you are on this screen.

  • You can only access this screen from the Managing Batches for Check Import Process screen.

  • You cannot find this screen using the normal search function.

  • You cannot save this screen to your Favorites.

Note: Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

To create or edit a check import batch, complete the following:

  1. Under the Import Batch Setup section, you can either create a new check import batch or Copy Existing Import batch which would copy all the Code Mapping as well as the FICA & FUTA conditions of that batch on to this screen.
  1. — To copy from an existing check import batch, click Copy Existing Import. Select the Batch ID you want to copy from in the Select Import Batch dialog box. Click OK to close the dialog box.
b. Batch ID - This field is read only:

  1. — This field will by default show NEW if you come to this screen by clicking New Import on the Managing Batches for Check Import Process screen. When you proceed to the State & Code Setup screen in this case, a new Batch ID will be generated.

  2. — To edit an existing check import batch in progress, click the Batch ID link on the Managing Batches for Check Import Process screen. The Batch ID will show here. You cannot edit the Batch ID. When you proceed to the State & Code Setup screen in this case, the Batch ID will remain the same.

  3. — You can click Previous on the State & Code Setup screen to come back to this screen to edit an existing check import batch. The Batch ID will show here. You cannot edit the Batch ID. After editing the check import batch when you proceed to the State & Code Setup screen, the Batch ID will remain the same.

c. Batch Name - The name for this batch:
i. If you are creating a new check import batch, then enter the name for this batch here.
— —
  1. — If you are editing an existing check import batch, then edit the name of the check import batch here.
d. Client ID - The client ID for whom checks will be imported in this batch:

  1. — If you are creating a new check import batch, then enter the Client ID here, or click the Client ID link and select the Client from the Select Client dialog box.

  2. — If you are editing an existing check import batch, then edit the Client ID here, or click the Client ID link and select the correct Client from the Select Client dialog box.

  3. — If you enter or select more than one Client ID a warning displays, “Clients with different taxation rules should have their own check history import batch.” Click OK to continue.

  1. Under the FICA & FUTA section, complete the following fields:
a. If Medicare tax amounts are zero, select one of the following:

  1. — Include Medicare taxable amounts on vouchers - This is the default option where Employer paid Medicare taxable amounts are included on all vouchers in this check import batch.

  2. — Do not include - Select this option if you do not want to include Employer paid Medicare taxable amounts included on all vouchers in this check import batch.

b. If OASDI tax amounts are zero, select one of the following:

  1. — Include OASDI taxable amounts on the vouchers - This is the default option where Employer paid OASDI taxable amounts are included on all vouchers in this check import batch.

  2. — Do not include - Select this option if you do not want to include Employer paid OASDI taxable amounts included on all vouchers in this check import batch.

c. Employer FUTA (Tax Code 00-17), select one the of the following:

  1. — Include - By default, calculation of employer FUTA tax is included on all vouchers in this batch.

  2. — Suppress - Select this option if you want to suppress the calculation of the employer FUTA tax on all vouchers in this batch.

  1. Under the Upload File section complete the following if you want to upload the checks from a file. Skip this section if you only want to enter check history manually.

  1. — Click Upload File to upload a check import batch file in a .txt or .csv format. A dialog box opens.

  2. — Click Choose File to select the check import batch file from your system in a .txt or .csv format.

Note: Note: When importing a .csv file, you do not need to remove the headers.

c. Click Submit to close the dialog box. The file uploaded now shows on the screen.

  1. Click Close to go back to the Managing Batches for Check Import Process screen. All changes made are lost.

  2. Click Next to save all changes made to this screen and go to the State & Code Setup screen.

  • If no file has been uploaded, then the State & Code Setup screen appears.

  • If you have already uploaded a file to import from, then a job progress window opens. The system starts to load the State Tax Rules from the default for the states included in the import file and the imported code setup from the imported spreadsheet.

  • Click Close once the process is complete to go to the State & Code Setup screen.

Warning - Uploading a replacement Check History Import file

You may need to upload a replacement check history import file if you have imported a wrong check history import file or the check history import file is badly formatted and so on. If you try to upload a new check history import file when a check history import file has already been uploaded using the import utility, and to prevent unexpected data loss, you will receive the following pop-up message:

Checks have already been imported from a file.

If you proceed, the previous imported checks will be cleared and you will lose any corrections you have made. Manually entered checks will be retained.

Do you want to clear the existing imported checks and start over?

  • Click Yes to upload a new check history import file. The file upload pop-up appears.

  • Existing checks uploaded earlier using the import utility are not cleared until you select the replacement check history import file and click Next.

  • Checks that were entered manually will be retained.

File Audit

From this Import Batch Setup screen, you can click the Actions menu and select the Audit option to show the Audit Log Display. You can view the logs for all the changes made for this Batch ID.

Review & Fix Data

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/New%20Check%20Import/Review%20&%20Fix%20Data.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/New Check Import/Review & Fix Data.htm

Review & Fix Data

This is the fourth screen of the check import wizard. Use this screen to review the check history and make corrections. Both imported or manually created checks are listed on this screen.

  • The Review & Fix Data option on the steps indicator at the top is highlighted to indicate that you are on this screen.

  • You can access this screen from the Enter Check History screen or from the Calculate Taxes screen.

  • You cannot find this screen using the normal search function.

  • You cannot save this screen to your Favorites.

Note: Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

This screen has the following sections:

  1. The first section gives a summary count of this check import batch. It shows the following:

  • The total number of checks in this import batch.

  • The total number of errors that need to be fixed before you can complete this check import batch. As you fix the number of errors, this count will reduce unless the fix has not generated further errors.

  • The total number of warnings that need to be fixed before you can complete this check import batch. As you fix the number of warnings, this count will reduce unless the fix has not generated further warnings.

  • As you fix the errors/warnings, it shows the number of errors/warnings fixed for this check import batch.

  • The total number of checks in this check import batch that will not be imported.

  1. The second section gives the totals for this check import batch for the following parameters:

  • Total Hours

  • Total Gross Pay

  • Total Deductions

  • Total Taxes

  • Total Net Pay

  1. Import Corrections - The third section provides the following options:
  1. — Show - Lists the following views for the inline grid that displays below. (The count of checks for the selected view displays in that field.)
i. All Checks - Lists all the checks in this check import batch.
  1. — Only errors and warnings - Lists only those checks that have errors or warnings in this check import batch.
iii. Not importing - Lists only those checks that are not imported in this check import batch.

  1. — Client ID - You can filter the list of clients to display All clients or a specific client.

  2. — Refresh data - If you have made adjustments to the State Tax Rules or the Code Translation Tables, click this button to send all records through the system validation routine.

  3. — State Tax Rules - You have the ability to edit the state tax rules from this screen to fix errors relating to state tax rules. However, it will open as a modal in Batch view. You will not be able to edit the Batch ID and the Client Name as you are working on that batch. You can edit all the other fields or Copy All from Default. Click Save to close the form, run all records automatically through the system validation routine and return to this screen.

  4. — An inline grid shows all the individual checks for this check import batch. Use this table to review the check history and make corrections where necessary.

  • Each line represents one unique check number.

  • Checks imported using an import file as well as checks imported manually are all listed here.

  • The number of checks displayed on the screen depends on the view selected using the Show drop-down. For example, if you have set the Show to Only errors and warnings, you will not be able to see the checks that do not have any errors and the checks which are not imported.

  • A maximum of fourteen checks are displayed on the screen. If there are more than fourteen checks for the selected Show, use the arrows at the bottom right of your screen to navigate to the next checks.

  • Each line will be prefixed with an icon to denote the check status.

  • A check with a green circle with a check mark inside denotes a check with no errors that is imported.

  • A check with a red circle with an exclamation mark inside denotes a check with errors that is imported. If you click the icon a dialog box opens showing the employee name and check number and lists the error messages for each error on that check.

  • A check with an amber triangle with an exclamation mark inside denotes a check with a warning that is imported. If you click the icon a dialog box opens showing the employee name and check number and lists the warning messages for each warning on that check.

  • A check with a purple circle with a backslash inside denotes a check that is not imported.

  • The check that has errors or warnings will have the respective fields highlighted also on the inline grid to indicate which fields have errors or warnings and need to be fixed.

  • The inline grid has the following columns:

i. Name
ii. SSN
— —
iii. Client ID
— —
iv. Employer ID
— —
v. Check Number
— —
vi. Pay Date
— —
vii. Weeks Worked
— —
viii. Work State
— —
ix. Total Hours
— —
x. Gross Pay
— —
xi. Total Deductions
— —
xii. Total Taxes
— —
xiii. Net Pay
— —

To review and fix data:

  1. Click the check you want to edit and the Check History Entry screen opens up. You can click anywhere on the row to open the check for the employee that you want to edit.

  2. Make the necessary changes. No field should be highlighted in red which indicate an error that needs to be fixed.

  3. Click Save to save the changes and return to the inline grid.

  4. Click Refresh Data so that the changes reflect on the inline grid.

Note: Note: If the Show drop-down is set to Only errors and warnings, once you Refresh Data after editing a check, it will not be listed anymore if it does not contain any error or warning.

  1. Click Previous to go to the Enter Check History screen if you want to upload a different import file or want to import more checks manually.

  2. Click Next after you fix all errors and warnings. All records for this check import batch go through the system validation routine. If there are no errors, the Calculate Taxes screen opens.

  3. Click Close to close this window to return to the Managing Batches for Check Import Process screen.

State & Code Setup

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/New%20Check%20Import/State%20&%20Code%20Setup.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/New Check Import/State & Code Setup.htm

State & Code Setup

This is the second screen of the check import wizard. Use this form to set up the State Tax Rules for the selected check import batch and Code Translation Tables for Earnings, Deductions and Taxes for the check import batch selected in the Import Setup screen.

Note: Note the following:

  • The State & Code Setup option on the steps indicator at the top is highlighted to indicate that you are on this screen.

  • You can only access this screen when you click Next on the Import Setup screen.

  • You cannot find this screen using the normal search function.

  • You cannot save this screen to your Favorites.

Note: Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

This form has the following two sections:

  • State Tax Rules

  • Code Mapping

Setting Up State Tax Rules

You will need to have state tax rules setup for each state that appears in your imported data either using the check import utility or manual check entry. You can set up the state tax rules for each state from the State Tax Processing Rules link under Tools section in the Check History Import form. If the rules are not set correctly for any of the states that appear in your imported data, you will see errors/discrepacies later in the workflow.

To set up the State Tax Rules for the selected check import batch:

  1. If you are importing checks from an import file, then the system will automatically load the default State Tax Rules for all the states contained in the imported spreadsheet. This will ensure that you can set up all the required state tax codes correctly to prevent future errors. The following fields appear in an inline grid along with the values imported for each field:

  • State - all the states codes contained in the original import file are listed here.

  • State Income Tax Shelter Flag

  • SUTA Shelter Flag

  • SUTA Taxable Limit

  • SUTA Tax Rate (%)

  • Employee SDI Shelter Flag

  • Employee SDI Taxable Limit

  • Employer SDI Taxable Limit

  • Employer SDI Tax Rate (%)

  • Misc Employer State Taxes

  1. You can click a state link above to open the State Tax Rules form for the state in a modal.

  • The Rule Type section will not be visible.

  • The Rule Type will be set to Batch as you are accessing this form while processing this check import batch.

  • The Batch ID will be pre-populated which you cannot change.

  • The corresponding Batch Name will be displayed.

  • The Batch Status will display State & Code Setup which is the screen from where you are accessing the State Tax Rules form.

  • You can edit all the fields on this State Tax Rules form including the State Code. You cannot save this form unless a State Code is selected.

  • Click Save to save the changes and you will return to the State Tax Rules Section. The changed values will reflect on the inline grid.

  • Click Delete to delete the state tax rules for the selected state.

  • Click Cancel to close the form. All changes will be lost.

  • Click Close to close the form. Changes are saved and reflect in the inline grid.

  1. Click Copy All from Default to copy the default state tax rules to the state tax rules form for the batch. The changed values will reflect on the inline grid. You can use this option to

  2. Click Copy State to Default to copy the state tax rules for this batch to the default state tax rules.

Setting Up Code Mapping

For each code that appears in the import spreadsheet, choose the corresponding code in your PrismHR system. Make sure to choose codes with the same tax- settings, or the totals will not match.

If you are importing from a file, then the system will load the codes for Earnings, Deductions and Taxes from the imported spreadsheet. If the imported codes are already contained in your PrismHR code translation tables, they will also reflect in the appropriate table. If not then you will need to manually provide the PrismHR code so that the system can calculate the Earnings, Deductions, and Taxes appropriately. As you already get to see the number of foreign codes that you need to translate (if any), the chances of getting errors is reduced and you can complete the process faster.

Earnings

To map the Imported Pay Codes, complete the following:

a. Enter the corresponding Prism Pay Code for the Imported Pay Code OR
b. Click the Map to Prism Pay Code link and search from the Select Pay Code dialog box.
— —

  1. — Check the Pay Code Description to confirm that you have selected the correct Prism Pay Code for the corresponding Imported Pay Code.

  2. — In case of any errors, redo the process to select the correct corresponding Prism Pay Code for the Imported Pay Code from the Select Pay Code dialog box.

Deductions

To map the Imported Deduction Codes, complete the following:

a. Enter the corresponding Prism Deduction Code for the Imported Deduction Code OR

  1. — Click the Map to Prism Deduction Code link and search from the Select Deduction Code dialog box.

  2. — Check the Deduction Code Description and the Deduction Type to confirm that you have selected the correct Prism Deduction Code for the corresponding Imported Deduction Code.

  3. — In case of any errors, redo the process to select the correct corresponding Prism Deduction Code for the Imported Deduction Code from the Select Deduction Code dialog box.

Taxes

To map the Imported Tax Codes, complete the following:

a. Enter the corresponding Prism Tax Code for the Imported Deduction Code OR

  1. — Click the Map to Prism Deduction Code link and search from the Select Deduction Code dialog box. You can use the Paid By filter to narrow down your search for the correct Prism Tax Code.

  2. — Check the Tax Code Description to confirm that it is the correct Prism Tax Code for the corresponding Imported Tax Code.

  3. — In case of any errors, redo the process to select the correct corresponding Prism Tax Code for the Imported Tax Code from the Select Tax Deduction Code dialog box.

  4. — You have the option to select if the Prism Tax Code selected is Sheltered or not from the drop-down under the Sheltered? column.

  1. Click Previous to go to the Import Setup screen. All changes made will be lost.

  2. Click Next to save all the changes and proceed to the Enter Check History screen.

  3. Click Close to exit the wizard. All changes made will be lost.

Use this form to generate the download for New York Form MTA-305 Metro Commuter Transport Mobility Tax Report for an employer for a quarter.

Field Name Description
Employer ID Enter the employer ID here for whom you want to run this report or click the Employer ID link and select it from the Select Employer dialog box.
Tax Year Select the year from the drop-down for which you want to run this report. The default is the current year. The drop-down has a 10 year look back starting from the current year.

Promptax/Overpayment This field is optional. Enter the total of any Promptax payments made during the quarter and the amount of any MCTNT overpayment from the previous quarter.
Refund/Credit This field displays only if an entry is made in the Promptax/Overpayment field above. If an overpayment is claimed, select from the following options: - Credit - Refund

  • Amended - Column 162 will reflect the letter A.
