Creating a New Client Company

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/New_Company.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/New_Company.htm

Creating a New Client Company

Create a new client company with the New Client form.

To create a client company:

  1. Click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office).

  2. Select New Client from the Operations|Action menu.

  3. Fill out these fields as required.

Field Description
Client ID The system generates the Client ID when you save the new record. This field defaults to NEWwhen you open the form.
Legal Name Enter the Legal Name of the new client company.
Client D/B/A Enter the legal doing business as client name in the Client D/B/A field.
Address Enter the client’s main mailing address in the Address fields. After saving the new client record, you can enter other addresses (if required).
ZIP Code Enter the ZIP Code and press Tab. The system automatically displays the GeoCode, City, and State. If multiple GeoCodes are associated with the ZIP Code, the system prompts you to select the correct one.
GeoCode, City, and State After entering the client’s address and ZIP Code, the GeoCode, city, and state display.
Telephone Enter the client’s main Telephone number.
Ext Enter the telephone Ext (optional).
Fax Enter the client’s Fax number.
Website Enter the URL of the client’s Website.
Service Type Select the Service Type provided to this client. You must select the appropriate Service Type to ensure accurate billing. - Administrative Services Only (ASO): When you save the new client record, the system automatically creates both a new client record and a new employer record with the same information as the new client. The system immediately links the new employer record to the client. The system assumes cost equals billed for taxes and workers’ compensation. - Corporate: Indicates that the new record is a corporate client, typically used for tracking the service provider’s internal employees. No billing occurs for a corporate client. If the new client needs to be billed, select a different service type. - Professional Employer (PEO): Indicates that the service provider manages human resources, employee benefits, payroll, workers’ compensation, accounts receivable, and COBRA administration for the new client. Cost is considered the PEO cost for taxes and workers’ compensation rates, which are entered at the system/employer levels. Billed rates can be higher (for profit centers) or lower than cost, if appropriate, and rates are specified at the client level. - HR Services Only: The service provider only manages human resources for the client’s employees, which includes hiring, termination, performance, compensation, training, policy, and OSHA-related services. (There is no payroll.) - Payroll Services Only: The service provider only provides payroll and payroll tax services for the client. (The employer does not provide human resources services.) - Admin. Service/Alt. Billing: This is similar to an ASO in that the system creates an employer record automatically. The system treats the new client as it would a PEO client for billing purposes. The service provider can open profit centers on taxes and workers’ compensation. The system does not assume cost equals billed.
  • Administrative Services Only (ASO): When you save the new client record, the system automatically creates both a new client record and a new employer record with the same information as the new client. The system immediately links the new employer record to the client. The system assumes cost equals billed for taxes and workers’ compensation.
  • Corporate: Indicates that the new record is a corporate client, typically used for tracking the service provider’s internal employees. No billing occurs for a corporate client. If the new client needs to be billed, select a different service type.

The service provider can open profit centers on taxes and workers’ compensation. Clearing the Lock on Pay On-Demand Processing Features

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Pay_OnDemand_Clear_Lock.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Pay_OnDemand_Clear_Lock.htm

Clearing the Lock on Pay On-Demand Processing Features

Do not clear the lock on Pay On-Demand processing features until you have verified that no one at your organization is engaged in processing any Pay On-Demand files. If they are, do not use the Pay On-Demand Clear Lock feature.

To clear the lock:

  1. After ensuring that no users are actively working in any Pay On-Demand forms, click Clear Lock.

  2. Click Yes to confirm that you want to clear the lock.

  3. Click OK.

Listing Pending Payments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Payments_Pending.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Payments_Pending.htm

Listing Pending Payments

The Payments Pending form lists any payments required to proceed with a payroll. This is for clients where your organization requires an ACH or wire transfer before finalizing the payroll. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To list pending payments:

  • After selecting the filter settings and then selecting Find Payments, the form displays payments that are Payment Pending or Wire Pending, Created or Pending, or both, according to the selected filter settings. You can also filter your view to the Wire Transfer, Reverse Wire, or Real Time Payment type only, or filter to view records for a specific client, multi-entity group, or cost center.

Note: Multi-entity groups do not display for a client if the service provider does not have access to that client. Also, the name of the multi-entity group created in the Multi-Entity Groups form displays. (If there is more than one multi-entity group, they display as listed in the Client Details form, which are truncated if necessary.)

  • Once you receive the payment, select the payroll line item and then click Mark Received. A message displays, “Are you sure you want to mark these payments as received?” Click Yes to continue. (This updates the batch Status so the payroll processor can continue to process the payroll batch.)

  • To view the detailed invoice, select the Payroll line item or click the checkbox next to the Payroll column to select all payments. The invoice displays, where you can click the following buttons to access more information:

  • Client Accounting: Displays the Invoice Client Accounting form.

  • Accounting: Displays the Invoice Accounting form.

  • Display PDF: Displays the invoice in PDF format.

PEO Client Accounting G/L Detail Report

Use this form to generate a report of PEO client accounting over a pay date range for all or selected clients.

To generate the PEO Client Accounting G/L Detail Report:

  2. Select PEO Client Accounting G/L Detail Report under Operations|Report.

  3. Complete the following information as appropriate:

Field — Description

Starting Pay Date — Enter the starting pay date from which you want to run this report.

Ending Pay Date — Enter the ending pay date up to which you want to run this report.

Run Legal Width Report — Select this field to adjust the column width to accommodate account codes up to 68 characters.

Client ID — This field is optional. Leave this field blank to run this report for all clients. If you want to restrict this report to a few selected clients, enter the Client IDs here or click the Client ID link and select them from the Select Client dialog box. The Client Name auto populates.

  1. Click Run to generate the report. The report displays.

This report displays the following columns:

Importing New Hires from Employee Portal

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Portal_New_Hire_Import.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Portal_New_Hire_Import.htm

Importing New Hires from Employee Portal

You can use the Portal New Hire Import form to import new hires all at once from several clients who were registered in Employee Portal (EP). After uploading a file for import, you can view any errors that occurred during the import or view successfully imported rows. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Important! This process applies as follows:

  • This form does not take the place of the New Employee Import process.

  • The imported employees will only display on the New Hire Dashboard in Employee Portal (EP). (See the Employee Portal (EP) online help and the Enabling the New Hire Dashboard article in the Customer Resource Center for more information.)

To perform an import using the Portal New Hire Import form, simply upload a file for import and then view any errors that occurred during the import or view successfully imported rows.

Note: Note the following:

  • This form is only available for service providers.

  • Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Portal New Hire Import form displays the form in read-only format.

  • Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

To import new hires from Employee Portal:

  1. Select Download Spreadsheet Template to download a .csv file to your computer that contains the new hires import headings in row 1. A separate window displays the downloaded file link.

Important! The first row of the import file must contain all the columns in the downloaded spreadsheet template in the same order. (Optional fields with no data can be included, but must be left blank.)

  1. Click Open File. The spreadsheet template displays, where you can enter the new hires information.

The spreadsheet template contains the following columns:

Column Description
Employer ID Employer ID associated with the new hire (required). Note: If the Employer ID or Client ID is not valid, the system does not validate the remaining data in that row. In addition, this Employer ID must be associated with the Client ID.
Client ID Client ID associated with the new hire (required). Note: You must set Electronic On-Boarding to Prompt or Always in the client-level settings on the Control tab in the Client Details form. Otherwise, the entire import will fail and an error message displays, “Client does not use Electronic On-Boarding. New Hires cannot be imported.”
First Name First name of new hire (required).
Last Name Last name of new hire (required).
Middle Name Middle name of new hire (optional).
Employment Status Current employment status associated with the new hire (required). Note: If there are restrictions on the Control tab in the Client Details form, only those employee statuses listed in the form can be used.
Employee Type Employment type associated with the new hire (required). Note: If there are restrictions on the Control tab in the Client Details form, only those employee types listed in the form can be used.
Work Location Work location associated with the new hire (required).
Position Position of new hire (required).
Start Date Date when new hire began employment (required).
Pay Method Pay method associated with the new hire (required): - S = Salary - V = Variable Salary - H = Hourly - D = Driver - C = Commission Note: The Variable Salary option only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form. You can use the Variable Salary option to accurately track the hours that salary-exempt employees actually work. For example, non-profit companies could use this option to track the work hours of their employees who are paid a standard salaried amount, so they can use these hours and their allocations for grant purposes.
  • S = Salary
  • V = Variable Salary
  • H = Hourly
  • D = Driver
  • C = Commission | Pay Rate | Pay rate that corresponds with the selected Pay Rate Basis for the new hire (required). | | Pay Rate Basis | Determines the new hire’s pay period (required): - H = Hourly - W = Weekly - B = Bi-monthly - S = Semi-monthly - M = Monthly - Y = Yearly |
  • H = Hourly
  • W = Weekly
  • B = Bi-monthly
  • S = Semi-monthly
  • M = Monthly
  • Y = Yearly | Standard Hours | Standard hours worked by the new hire during the pay period (required). | | Benefit Group | Benefit group of new hire that can be used to establish eligibility, coverage, and contribution rules for benefit plans (required). | | Pay Group | Pay Group to which new hire belongs (required). | | Employee Number | Employee number associated with the new hire (optional). | | Work Shift | Work shift associated with the new hire (optional). | | Department Code | Department code associated with the new hire (optional). | | Personal Email Address | Personal email address associated with the new hire (optional). | | Send Email | Email address system uses to send emails to new hire (optional): - Yes - No - Blank Note: If this column contains Yes, Null, or is not included in the import and the Personal Email Address contains an entry, the system sends a welcome email to the new hire. |
  • Yes
  • No
  • Blank | Division Code | Division where new hire works (optional). | | Project | Project associated with the new hire (optional). | | Work Group | Work group associated with the new hire (optional). | | Union | Union to which new hire belongs (optional). | | PTO Approver | Person who approves new hire’s PTO requests (optional). | | Manager | Person that new hire reports to upon employment (optional). | | Mobile Phone | Mobile phone number associated with the new hire (optional). | | Nickname | Alternative name associated with the new hire (optional). | | Seniority Date | Benefit start date associated with the new hire (optional). | | Preferred Language | Preferred language associated with the new hire (optional): - ENG = English - SPA = Spanish Note: Leaving this entry blank defaults to English. |
  • ENG = English
  • SPA = Spanish

  1. Select Upload File. Click Add Files and select the file to upload, then click Start Upload.

  2. Click Close. The uploaded filename displays.

  3. Select Preview Data. (If you select Preview Data before uploading the file, no information displays.) Information displays on the following tabs:

  • Errors: Any errors from the import process display on this tab. (Error messages specify the line number where the error occurred.) Click Error Report to view the new hires errors. (A browser window opens where you can download the .csv file that contains the errors.)

  • File Content: Any successful rows from the import process display on this tab. The following fields from the import display as a header:

  • Client ID

  • First Name

  • Last Name

  • Position

  • Start Date

  • Pay Rate

  • Benefit Group

Note: If no successful rows display in the file and you select File Content a message displays, “No New Hires to import.”

  1. Click Import Data to import new hires that display on the File Content tab. The “File content successfully imported” message displays. Click OK. The imported new hires display on the New Hire Dashboard in Employee Portal (EP) where the system generates a welcome code, so these new hires can obtain that code in the New Hire Dashboard.

Note: Any additional errors that occur during the import display in the existing errors list on the Errors tab.

  1. Click Confirmation Report to download a .csv report that contains the successfully imported new hires information.

Note: Columns that are blank indicate an unsuccessful data import.

Create Positive Pay Files

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Positive_Pay_Files_Create.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Positive_Pay_Files_Create.htm

Create Positive Pay Files

Use the Create Positive Pay Files form to create the file that you will send to the financial institution.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Before you begin, disable the pop‑up blocker on your browser.

  2. You can generate a positive pay file for one checking account, or for multiple accounts:

  • To generate a positive pay file for only one bank account, enter the Checking Account ID; this is the number that represents an account in PrismHR and might not match the actual bank account number. The account name displays.

  • To generate positive pay files for all bank accounts, leave the Checking Account ID field blank.

  1. If you are creating one positive pay file for multiple accounts, enter the File Stub ID for the accounts that you want to include in the file.

The file stub is specified in Positive Pay Setup, accessed through the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

of the Bank Accounts form.

  1. Typically, you would enter the Starting Check Date and Ending Check Date to create the positive pay file for a specific range of dates. If you do not enter dates, the positive pay file will include all available data.

  2. Select Include Voided Checks to include voids in the positive pay file.

  3. Click Create Positive Pay Files.

  4. Click Yes in the confirmation message.

The Starting CREATE Positive Pay Files form displays the processing steps.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. When the creation process is complete, click the Close button.

The system prepares to download the file (or the first of multiple files) to your computer. This process depends on the browser you are using and its settings.

  1. Some browsers open a blank window when they process the download file. Close this window when the download is complete; in the case where you have created multiple positive pay files, that window would prevent the additional files from downloading.

  2. If your browser is set to prompt you for the location to save the file, use your computer’s Save As window to navigate to the location where you want to save the file. Otherwise, the system saves it to your default file location. Make a note of the directory and file name.

  3. Go to the location where you saved the file and open it in a text editor such as Notepad. Check the file format; if it is not correct, open Positive Pay Setup for the account and make corrections.

  4. Send the positive pay file to the financial institution.

Removing Inactive Customer Data

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Purge_Clients.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Purge_Clients.htm

Removing Inactive Customer Data

Use the Inactive Data Deletion form to remove or deidentify customer data for clients or employees that are inactive for a certain number of years. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: To preserve data integrity, the system deidentifies employee data and removes any Personally Identifiable Information (PII). (The tool tip (

[Image: screenshot]

) displays this information.)

The Inactive Data Deletion form consists of two panels:

  • Select Inactive Data to Delete: Displays inactive data for clients or employees, so you can easily delete or deidentify this customer data.

  • History: Search for data deletions or deidentifications using a date range. The system populates this panel based on data from the Batch Control Record. (This panel is collapsed by default.)

Note: Note the following:

  • The Inactive Data Deletion form is only available for service providers.

  • You can access the Inactive Data Deletion form by clicking [Image: screenshot] (Back Office), then select Inactive Data Deletion from the System|Utility Processing menu.

  • Clients must be inactive for at least four years before they can be deleted. The system determines inactivity by the duration of a client’s terminated status or the years since their most recent pay voucher, whichever occurs first.

  • Employees must be inactive for at least seven years before they can be deidentified.

  • You can search for a particular client (either by Client Name or Legal Name) or employee (either by employee ID or the employee’s first or last name) in the table results using the Search box.

  • You can only select a maximum of 20 clients to delete at a time. If more than 20 clients display after setting the Years of Inactivity a message displays, “Please select a maximum of 20 clients per run.” Click OK to continue.

  • You can only select a maximum of 1000 employees to deidentify at a time.

  • The Delete Client Data and Deidentify Employee Data buttons are disabled until you select clients or employees.

  • If there are no vouchers, the Last Voucher Date and Years Since Voucher columns will be blank.

To delete files for an inactive client:

  1. Select Clients in the Data Type field.

  2. In the Years of Inactivity field, select the minimum number of years a client must be inactive to display. The clients matching this criteria display. In addition, a message displays, “Please select a maximum of 20 clients per run.”

  3. Select the clients to be deleted in the Clients table.

  4. Select Rebuild Employer Registers to remove employee voucher data from the company tax registers. (Disable this field to prevent the system from removing employee voucher data.)

  5. Once all settings have been verified, click Delete Client Data. A warning displays, “Permanently delete all data for the <number> selected clients?” Confirm the action to remove data for the displayed clients by clicking Yes. (Clicking No returns to the form.)

Note: Note: This action cannot be undone.

  1. Once a deletion is complete, click a link in the Clients column in the History panel to download a report of all clients removed from the system.

To deidentify files for an inactive employee:

  1. Select Employees in the Data Type field.

  2. In the Years Terminated field, select the minimum number of years an employee must be inactive to display. The employees matching this criteria display. In addition, a message displays, “Employee Inactive Data Deletion limited to 1000 employees per run.”

Note: Note the following:

  • Only employees who have been terminated for at least seven years can have their PII deidentified from active and inactive clients. (The tool tip ( [Image: screenshot] ) displays this information.)

  • Employees display in the Inactive Data Deletion list when their last termination status date is more than the selected number of Years Terminated from the current date.

  1. To narrow the search, enter or select the employee’s Client ID. After entering or selecting an ID and moving your cursor off the field, the search immediately displays all inactive employee data for that ID.

Note: To narrow down the list of employees that displays, enter the employee ID or the employee’s first or last name in the Search box. After clicking the magnifying glass icon (

[Image: screenshot]

) or pressing Enter, the employee list redisplays that criteria. (Searches can return up to 1,000 employees at a time since only 1,000 employees can be deidentified at a time.)

  1. Select the employees to deidentify in the Employees table. (Click Employee ID to select all employees that display.)

  2. After verifying the settings, click Deidentify Employee Data. A confirmation message displays, “Deidentify all data for the <number> selected employees?” Confirm the action to remove data for the displayed employees. (The system replaces the attribute values in Column F.)

Note: This action deidentifies employee data (that is, it removes the data instead of deleting it) and cannot be undone.

  1. Once the deidentify process is complete, click a link in the Employees column in the History panel to download a report of all employees removed from the system.

Note: This downloadable report lists the company ID and the employee ID for all employees who were deidentified. However, no PII is shared.

To search for data deletions within a date range:

  1. Open the History panel by clicking the plus sign ( [Image: screenshot] ).

  2. Enter or select the From and To date range. The system adjusts the display of data deletions or deidentifications to match the criteria.

  3. The following columns display:

Column Description
Date Completed Timestamps when the deletion finished, displaying the date, hours, minutes, seconds, and the CST time zone.
Data Type Displays the type of data that was deleted: - Client: Displays if both client and employee data was deleted. - Employee: Displays if only employee data was deleted.
  • Client: Displays if both client and employee data was deleted.
  • Employee: Displays if only employee data was deleted. | Clients | Displays total number of clients deleted. Note: Displays a dash (-) if only employee data was deleted. | | Employees | Displays total number of employees deleted. Note: Displays a dash (-) if only client data was deleted. | | Processed by User | Displays the user ID of the person who performed the deletion. | | Clients | Displays a link to the client deletion file that can be downloaded as a ZIP file. | | Employees | Displays a link to the employee deidentification file that can be downloaded as a ZIP file. | Note: Searches can only return up to 1,000 employees at a time since only 1,000 employees at a time can be deidentified.

Summary of Employee Data Deidentification Mapping

This information outlines the specific actions taken to deidentify sensitive employee data across various system files. Each file listed contains attributes that are either:

  • Replaced with deidentified data to anonymize sensitive information.

  • Replaced with null values to entirely remove sensitive content.

  • Deleted in full when the record that contains data is completely removed.

Note: The goal in presenting this information ensures compliance with data privacy standards by systematically removing or anonymizing personally identifiable information (PII) across all relevant datasets.

Recalculating COVID-19 Tax Credits & Client Rebates

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Recalculate%20COVID-19%20Tax%20Credits%20&%20Client%20Rebates.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Recalculate COVID-19 Tax Credits & Client Rebates.htm

Recalculating COVID-19 Tax Credits & Client Rebates

Use this form to cycle through a client’s payroll batches starting with any payroll batch that contains the selected Starting Pay Date and recalculate the appropriate sick hours, credit accruals and tax credits for each such selected payroll batch. This process will add or remove tax codes from employee payroll vouchers.

Warning! We recommend familiarizing yourself with this functionality first before running on live client data.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access this form, click Back Office. Under Operations|Utility click Recalculate COVID-19 Tax Credits & Client Rebates.

To Recalculate COVID-19 Tax Credits & Client Rebates:

  1. Complete the following fields:

Field Name — Description

Client ID — Enter the client ID for whom you want to recalculate COVID-19 Tax Credits & Client rebates or click the Client ID link and select it from the Select Client dialog box.

Start Date — Enter the starting pay date of the date range.

End Date — The end date will auto-populate appropriately.

Include in recalculation:

Billing (Rebates) — Check this box if you want to recalculate all COVID related billing events. However, if you select this option, a warning displays.

CARES Retention — Check this box if you want to recalculate tax codes associated with the CARES Act tax credit.

Sick & Family Leave — Check this box if you want to recalculate tax codes associated with COVID-19 sick and family leave credits.

Families First — Check this box if you want to recalculate tax codes associated with COVID-19 Families First credits.

Medicare — Check this box if you want to recalculate tax codes associated with COVID-19 Emergency Medicare Tax credits.

  1. Click Run to Recalculate COVID-19 Tax Credits & Client Rebates. A job progress window appears showing the processing. A pop-up box indicates that recalculation is complete

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Reset%20Federal%20Withholding%20Blocked%20Override.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Reset Federal Withholding Blocked Override.htm

Resetting Blocked Filing Status

This process resets the employee tax filing status of blocked to single with zero exemptions. The filing year for the Form W-4 must be prior to or equal to the applicable tax year.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To reset the employee tax filing status:

  1. On the [Image: screenshot] (Back Office) menu, select Operations|Action > Reset Federal Withholding Blocked Override.

  2. In Year, enter the tax year applicable to the most current federal Form W-4 on file for this employee.

  3. Click Process.

  4. Click Yes when prompted to continue. A progress window opens and notifies you when the Federal Withholding Blocked Initialization has completed along with the number of employees updated. The Close and Report buttons remain disabled number of employees while the report is being generated.

  5. Click Close to close the window.

  6. Click Report to display the Job Control Status Report window.

  7. In the Job Control Status Report window, click the XLS link to download the report.

Performing Slavic 401K Imports

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Slavic_401K_Import.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Slavic_401K_Import.htm

Performing Slavic 401K Imports

You can upload a retirement plan’s database file and import its contents using the Slavic 401K Import form. After a successful import, the process updates employee deferral changes.

Using the Slavic 401K Import Form

Use the Slavic 401K Import form to import data from an uploaded database file.

[Image: screenshot]

This form consists of the following fields:

Fields Description
Plan ID Select the Plan ID. After selecting the ID, the system displays the following message: If no Match eligibility rules are found, the Import defaults the “Eligible For Match” field to Y and uses the effective date for the “Match Starts On Date”. If it finds a “Match Starts On Date” less than the effective date, it will set the “Eligible For Match” field to Y and it will use the effective date.
Loan Payment Cycle Select one of the following loan payment cycles: - Per Pay Period (default): Loan payment cycle will be paid per pay period. - Monthly: Loan payment cycle will be paid in monthly increments. (This payment cycle can only be selected for new enrollments.) > Note: Note: If you select the Monthly loan payment cycle option, observe the following: - The loan payment cycle option automatically reverts to the Per Pay Period option when the employee has an existing retirement enrollment record. - If you are creating a new retirement enrollment, then the record reflects Monthly as the loan payment cycle option; therefore, the loan period entered from the import is honored. - If this is an existing record, it retains the original loan payment cycle value. If the original value was set to Monthly and the import runs with that option set to Per Pay Period, the original value remains set to Monthly.
  • Per Pay Period (default): Loan payment cycle will be paid per pay period.
  • Monthly: Loan payment cycle will be paid in monthly increments. (This payment cycle can only be selected for new enrollments.)
  • The loan payment cycle option automatically reverts to the Per Pay Period option when the employee has an existing retirement enrollment record.
  • If you are creating a new retirement enrollment, then the record reflects Monthly as the loan payment cycle option; therefore, the loan period entered from the import is honored.
  • If this is an existing record, it retains the original loan payment cycle value. If the original value was set to Monthly and the import runs with that option set to Per Pay Period, the original value remains set to Monthly. | Carry Forward Existing Amounts if NOT in the Import? | Deselecting this field prevents the system from carrying forward existing amounts during the import process. (Note: This field is selected by default.) | | Data Filename | File you uploaded for import, which must be in .csv format, displays in this field. (The filename displays after completing Step 1 in the Import process.) | | Error Count | Total number of errors after the file imports. Any errors encountered during the process display in the window below this field. | | Imported Records | Number of records imported. | | Error Message | Displays the error occurred during import process. > Note: Note: While performing the Slavic 401K import process, the following validations has been added with regard to the prohibit deductions on the Retirement Plans form: - On the Retirement Plans form, if the Prohibit Deductions is checked for the Employee Deferral Deduction Code or the Employee Catch-up Deduction Code for the indicated retirement plan and the employee election reflects type D in column D of the import file on the Slavic 401K Import form, then during the import process, an error message, “Deferral type prohibited by plan setup, cannot import row .” displays and the import process fails. - On the Retirement Plans form, if the Prohibit Deductions is checked for the Roth Post-tax Deduction Code or the Roth Catch-up Deduction Code for the indicated retirement plan and the employee election reflects type R in column D of the import file on the Slavic 401K Import form, then during the import process, an error message, “Deferral type prohibited by plan setup, cannot import row .” displays and the import process fails. |
  • On the Retirement Plans form, if the Prohibit Deductions is checked for the Employee Deferral Deduction Code or the Employee Catch-up Deduction Code for the indicated retirement plan and the employee election reflects type D in column D of the import file on the Slavic 401K Import form, then during the import process, an error message, “Deferral type prohibited by plan setup, cannot import row .” displays and the import process fails.
  • On the Retirement Plans form, if the Prohibit Deductions is checked for the Roth Post-tax Deduction Code or the Roth Catch-up Deduction Code for the indicated retirement plan and the employee election reflects type R in column D of the import file on the Slavic 401K Import form, then during the import process, an error message, “Deferral type prohibited by plan setup, cannot import row .” displays and the import process fails. ## Uploading/Importing a Retirement Plan

Clicking Start Import in the Slavic 401K Import panel uploads a retirement plan’s database file and import its contents.

Before You Begin

Before you start this process, ensure your database file is set up as follows:

  1. Set up an Excel spreadsheet with the following columns:

  • Column A: Company ID

  • Column B: Social Security Number formatted as a text field without dashes; for example, 111223333

  • Column C: Effective Date in MM/DD/YYYY format

  • Column D: Deferral Type specifying D as “Pre-Tax” or R as “After Tax”

  • Column E: Contribution Type specifying 1 as “Flat Amount” or 2 as “Percent”

  • Column F: Amount specifying Populate if Contribution Type = “1” (no commas)

  • Column G: Percent specifying Populate if Contribution Type = “2”

  1. Do not include a header row.

  2. Save the file in .csv format.

Also, ensure the employee is employed by the client and enrolled in the retirement plan you want to import.

Uploading/Importing a Database File

To upload a database file in .csv format and import its data, do the following in the Slavic 401K Import panel:

  1. Click Plan ID and select the appropriate ID. A dialog displays as described in the table above. Click OK to close the dialog.

  2. Click the Loan Payment Cycle option.

  3. Click Start Import to upload a database file, then click Choose File and browse to the file. Click submit.

  4. The data file imports and a confirmation dialog displays. Click Close.

  5. The imported data filename displays in the window, along with any errors encountered.

  6. Click Clear to remove information from the window and repeat the process for another retirement plan, or click Close to close the form.

The import process accepts Post-Tax Elections (P) in the import file as well.

Please note the following while importing new retirement plan elections on this form:

  • You can now import elections for Post Tax deferral types when Post Tax elections are not prohibited by the Retirement Plan setup.
  • You can now import elections for standard pre-tax deferrals when Employee Catch-up Deduction Code is flagged as prohibited. Please note that no Catch-up amount for pre-tax elections are recorded.
  • You can now import elections for Roth deferrals when Roth Catch-up Deduction Code is flagged as prohibited. Please note that Catch-up amount for Roth elections are recorded.
  • However, you cannot import elections for Post Tax deferral types when Post Tax elections are prohibited by the Retirement Plan setup.

Updating Existing Standard Employee Data

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Standard%20Employee%20Import.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Standard Employee Import.htm

Updating Existing Standard Employee Data

Use the Standard Employee Import form to update existing employee data via the standard employee import file format only.

WARNING! This process needs to be used with utmost caution as you may lose existing employee data. If your import file has incorrect or missing data (blank cells) for existing employees, it will replace existing employee data. If you want to import new hire records, use the New Employee Import menu. The PrismHR Menu Path is Back Office > Operations|Action > New Employee Import.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access this form, click the Back Office menu. Under Operations|Action, click Standard Employee Import. You cannot find this form using the normal search option.

To update existing employee data using the Standard Employee Import form:

  1. Enter the Code Set to be used for processing this import or click the Code Set link to select one from the Select Translation Table Code Set.

  2. Click Upload File to select the appropriate import file.

  3. Click Import Employees. A job progress window opens showing the progress. In case of any errors, correct them and redo the process.

  4. Click Close to close the job progress window. The employees are imported into a temporary IMPORT.EMPLOYEES file.

  5. Under the Convert Employees section choose the following:

  • Build Department Codes? By default this checkbox is unchecked. Check it if you want to build department codes.

  • Re-Use Employee IDs Generated Previously? By default this checkbox is unchecked. Check it if you want to reuse employee IDs generated previously.

  • Populate employee new-hire report dates? By default this checkbox is unchecked. Check it if you want to populate employee new-hire report dates.

  • Convert Employee Name, Address & Emer. Contact Name to Uppercase? By default this checkbox is unchecked. Check it if you want to convert employee name, address & emergency contact Name to uppercase.

  1. Click Convert Employees. This will move valid employee from the temporary IMPORT.EMPLOYEES file and overwrite the existing employee data in the permanent employee master file.

Managing Transactions On Hold

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Third-Party_Check_Hold_Review.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Third-Party_Check_Hold_Review.htm

Managing Transactions On Hold

Use the Third Party Check Hold and Review form to manage transactions on hold. From there, you can put transactions on hold, remove a hold, or delete transactions.

Note: Note: When you open this form, the system locks third party check processing until you close it.

To review third party transactions, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office [Image: screenshot] , then select Third Party Check Hold and Review from the Operations|Change menu. The Third Party Check Hold & Review form displays.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: You can also access this form from the Third Party Check Process form by clicking Hold Review. (See Creating a Third Party Check Processing Batch.)

  1. Select the Current On-Hold Status to view: All, On Hold, or NOT On Hold.

  2. Using the other four fields, you can limit the list to review only the third party transactions related to a specific employer, company (client), employee, or payee.

  3. Click Run. The Third Party Check Hold Maintenance & Review form opens, displaying all third party transactions that meet the criteria you specified.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: If you make a change on this form without saving it and then click Close, a message displays, “Any unsaved changes you entered will not be kept. Are you sure you want to exit?” Click Yes to close the form without saving your changes and return to the Third Party Check Hold & Review form.

  1. You can change the on-hold status of the transactions one at a time or all at once:

  • To change the on-hold status of one transaction, click the link in the On Hold? column. You can toggle the status between Y (on hold) and N (not on hold).

  • To put all transactions in the list on hold, click All On Hold. This applies to all pages.

  • To remove holds from all in the list transactions, click All Off Hold. This applies to all pages.

  1. You can mark transactions for deletion:

  • Click the N link in the Delete? column.

  • Click Yes in the confirmation message.

The link in the column changes to Y. It will not be deleted until you click the Save button. If you do not want to delete the transaction, click the Y link to set it back to N.

  1. Click Save to save all your changes. This includes the hold statuses for transactions and deletions.

  2. Click Close to exit the form without saving your changes. The system prompts you to confirm that you want to close the form without changing any on-hold statuses or deleting any transactions:

  • Click Yes to confirm and close without saving your changes.

  • Click No to stay in the Third Party Check Hold Maintenance & Review form.

Note: The system prompt that displays when you close the form always displays as a reminder and if you save the changes, these saved selections remain saved.

Setting Up Third Party Check Printing Mode

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Third-Party_Check_Printing_Mode.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Third-Party_Check_Printing_Mode.htm

Setting Up Third Party Check Printing Mode

In order to support third party check printing, your organization must set up the Third Party Check Printing Mode in the System Parameters form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To set the print mode for third party checks, do the following:

  1. Open the System Parameters form. (Click Back Office. Select System Parameters under System|Change.)

  2. Select one of the two options for the Third Party Check Printing Mode to support the way your organization wants to work:

  • Batch Mode: Consolidates liabilities and prints third party checks in batch mode

  • Real Time: Prints third party checks when payroll batch posts (with other payroll reports)

Important! If you do not select an option in the Third Party Check Printing Mode field (that is, this field selection remains “–Select–”), the system processes as though it was in Batch Mode. However, to access third party check processing, you must set this field to Batch Mode.

Note: Note: In the backend system, you can manage Third Party Check Printing Mode in mvQuery Third Party Checks Maintenance along with the third party check format, logo, and signature. The setting is always the same setting in both forms.

  1. Click Save.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Third-Party_Check_Process_Create.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Third-Party_Check_Process_Create.htm

Creating a Third Party Check Processing Batch

Use the Third Party Check Process form to select an employer and create a batch of third party checks to process. For example, you can select the employer in this form as part of the third party check processing batch process:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: When you open this form, the system locks third party check processing until you close it. Also, if you set the Third Party Check Printing Mode to Real Time on the System Parameters form, a message displays, “This account is set up to print Third Party Checks during payroll processing. If Third Party Checks should be processed in ‘Batch Mode,’ change the Third Party Check Printing mode at System Parameters.” Click OK.

The Third Party Check Process form serves as the main “hub” for some third party check processing transactions. In addition to creating a third party check processing batch, you can also do the following in this form:

  • View posted batches by clicking Posted Batches (see Viewing Posted Third Party Check Batches)

  • Manage transactions on hold by clicking Hold Review (see Managing Transactions On Hold)

  • View third party check processing batches that are ready to post to the system and then post batches by clicking Batches Available to Post (see Posting a Third Party Check Processing Batch)

Important! Before you begin this process, you must set the Third Party Check Print Mode field to Batch Mode on the System Parameters form.

To select an employer and create a batch of third party checks to process, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office [Image: screenshot] , then select Third Party Check Process from the Operations|Change menu. The Third Party Check Process form displays.

  2. If necessary, enter the pay date in the Pay Date on or before field to limit the list to payroll batches that were processed for that date or earlier. (The default is the Friday of the current week.)

  3. To begin creating a batch of third party checks, click the Employer Name or Employer ID. This opens the Third Party Check Batch Control form, where you can create a batch. To apply filters, select the + sign next to Batch Creation Filters to expand the form.

Note: If the net payee amount was less than or equal to zero, the following message displays when the Third Party Check Batch Control form opens, “Some items were skipped because the net payee amount was less than or equal to zero.”

  1. Complete the appropriate information:
Field Description
Check Date Enter or select the Check Date.
Checking Account Enter or select the Checking Account. (Note: You can set up a separate checking account only for third party check processing, but this is not a requirement.)
Batch Name Enter the Batch Name.
Batch Creation Filters Use the filters, if you need to limit the items in the third party check processing batch: - Enter or select the Pay Date on or before date. - Select the Check Type. - Select the Filter, then select the Payee ID, Client ID, or Employee ID. Note: If you select a Filter option, such as Payee, add some payees, but then decide not to use them and switch to the Client or Employee options and then select Payee again, the system remembers and displays the payees you originally added. (This behavior also applies to the Pay Date on or before date and the Check Type filter.) Note: Select Clear Filters to remove any filters you selected.
  • Enter or select the Pay Date on or before date.
  • Select the Check Type.
  • Select the Filter, then select the Payee ID, Client ID, or Employee ID. The following example displays third party (voluntary deductions) check transactions (labeled “Third” in the Check Type column) for a particular client:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Garnishment transactions are labeled “Garn” in the Check Type column.

  1. To view the details of a line item, click the [Image: screenshot] icon next to the Payee ID. When you are finished, click Close Detail View.

  2. When the list displays only the third party check transactions that you want to include, click Create Batch.

The system displays a message with the ID of the batch that you created.

  1. Click OK to return to the main Third Party Check Process form.

Posting a Third Party Check Processing Batch

Use the Third Party Check Batches Available to Post form to select a batch of third party checks to post.

Note: When you open this form, the system continues to lock third party check processing until you close the main Third Party Check Process form.

To view batches available to post and select a batch for posting, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office [Image: screenshot] , then select Third Party Check Process from the Operations|Change menu. The Third Party Check Process form displays.

The Third Party Check Batches Available to Post form displays the number of employers, journals, and total amount ready to be processed as of the specified effective date. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. To begin posting a batch of third party checks, click the Batch Name or Batch ID. This opens the Third Party Check Batch Processing form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

In addition, you can delete a batch on this form by clicking Delete Batch. A confirmation message displays where you can click Yes to proceed with deleting the batch. (Click No to return to the form without deleting the batch.)

Note: After deleting a batch, the transactions in that batch are once again available to process in a new batch using third party check processing.

  1. If necessary, enter or select a different Check Date and Checking Account. (This updated information will display on the posted batch and checks.) Note: After making these changes, if you close the form without posting the batch the information reverts back to its original state when you reopen that batch.

  1. To view the details of a line item, click the Payee Type-ID. When you finish, click Close Detail View.

The system displays a message that the batch is posting. After that, it displays the Printing Third Party Checks job progress form to display the print process. Click Close when it finishes. (Note: The PDF of the check print file automatically loads to display on the screen.)

The system returns you to the Third Party Check Batch Processing form.

  1. Click Close.

The system returns you to the Third Party Check Batches Available to Post form with the list of open batches.

Performing Third Party Check Processing

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Third-Party_Check_Processing.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Third-Party_Check_Processing.htm

Performing Third Party Check Processing

Third party check processing connects employee garnishments and voluntary deductions with designated payees. PrismHR deducts the designated pay amounts from the employee and allows a service provider to create a check made payable to the designated payee by using the Third Party Check Process.

Important! Before you begin this process, you must set the Third Party Check Print Mode field to Batch Mode on the System Parameters form.

The Third Party Check Process form lists all third party check payments that are being processed in payroll batches that meet the selection criteria.

From this form, you can maintain third party check batches by doing the following:

  • Create a batch (see Creating a Third Party Check Processing Batch)

  • View batches available to post and post a batch (see Posting a Third Party Check Processing Batch)

  • Hold/release third party check transactions (see Managing Transactions On Hold)

  • View posted batches, then select a batch to reprint or void checks, view the accounting or check information, and run reports (see Viewing Posted Third Party Check Batches)

Voiding Third Party Checks

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Third-Party_Check_Void.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Third-Party_Check_Void.htm

Voiding Third Party Checks

Use the Third Party Check Void form to void a check included in the batch.

Note: Note: You can only void checks that have been printed. Also, when you open this form, the system locks third party check processing until you close it.

To void a check included in the batch, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office [Image: screenshot] , then select Third Party Check Void from the Operations|Action menu. The Third Party Check Void form opens.

  2. Enter or select the Checking Account and the Check Number. The Payable To, Check Date, and Check Amount display. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Review the check information to confirm that it is accurate.

  2. Enter the Reason for Void.

  3. Click Void Check. A confirmation message displays where you can click Yes to proceed with voiding the check. (Click No to return to the form without voiding the check.)

  4. Click Close to release the third party check processing lock.

Note: After a check is voided, it is once again available to process in a new batch using third party check processing.

Related Topics

Viewing Posted Third Party Check Batches

Performing Third Party Check Processing

Transfer Accounting Downloads File to PC

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Transfer%20Accounting%20Downloads%20File%20to%20PC.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Transfer Accounting Downloads File to PC.htm

Transfer Accounting Downloads File to PC

Use this form to transfer PrismHR accounting files from the server’s download directory to the user’s system.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

Note: Note: When you give access to this form on the User Role menu, you will receive the following warning message:

This form does not have any client access group security built into this menu. It is possible for users to gain access to information that they should be restricted from by downloading files from this menu.

Note: Note: A warning message displays on the User Role screen if a user,

  • who has access to the Transfer Accounting Downloads File to PC menu is switched to a new User Role, BUT

  • is also restricted from clients via client access group security.

The message states:

The user role has access to the Transfer Accounting Downloads File to PC menu. This form does not utilize client access group security so it is possible that maybe be able to download accounting files that contain data they should not be allowed to access. Do you wish to continue?

  • If Yes is selected, then the user record is saved, and the screen is cleared.

  • If No is selected, then the user record is not saved, and the data is left as is on the screen.

To access the form, click the Back Office menu > Operations|Action > Transfer Downloads File to PC.

To transfer an accounting download file to a user’s system:

  1. In the Filename field, enter the accounting journal file name that you want to download or click the Filename link to select one. A separate Select Field window opens.

  2. Scroll and select the accounting journal file that you want to download from the list. Refine the search using Filename Description and Date. The list displays 100 options. If there are more than 100 options, scroll down and click the More… link to view the next list of options. Continue till you find the accounting file that you want to download.

  3. Once you select the Filename, the File View shows the first 15 lines of the selected accounting downloads file.

  4. Click Download to download the selected accounting downloads file to your PC .

Transfer Downloads File to PC

Transfer Downloads File to PC

Use this form to download files to a user’s system, from the server’s download directory generated by the PrismHR system.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

Note: Note: A warning message displays on the User Role form if a user,

  • who has access to the Transfer Downloads File to PC menu is switched to a new User Role, BUT

  • is also restricted from clients via client access group security.

The message states:

The user role has access to the Transfer Downloads File to PC menu. This form does not utilize client access group security so it is possible that maybe be able to download files that contain data they should not be allowed to access. Do you wish to continue?

  • If Yes is selected, then the user record is saved, and the screen is cleared.

  • If No is selected, then the user record is not saved, and the data is left as is on the screen.

To access the form, click the Back Office menu > Operations|Action > Transfer Downloads File to PC.

To transfer a Download File to a user’s PC:

  1. Click the Filename link. A separate Select File window opens.

Transfer Tax Basis from Successor Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/Transfer%20Tax%20Basis%20from%20Successor%20Report.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/Transfer Tax Basis from Successor Report.htm

Transfer Tax Basis from Successor Report

Use this form to generate a report to show successor tax data in the system. Successor tax data is entered into the system using the Successor Wage Tax Import process. These values are written to the various tax registers during the import so the employees do not accrue specific taxes any longer. This report sorts the information either by the employee name or tax code.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access this form, clickReports menu. Under Operations|Report, click Transfer Tax Basis from Successor Report.

To generate the transfer tax basis from successor report:

  1. Complete the following fields:
Field Description
Sort Option Select one of the following options from the drop-down: - Employee Name (Default) - Select this option if you want to sort the report by employee name. - Tax Code - Select this option is you want to sort this report by tax code.
  • Employee Name (Default) - Select this option if you want to sort the report by employee name.
  • Tax Code - Select this option is you want to sort this report by tax code. | Client ID | This field is optional. - Leave it blank to select all clients. - If you want to restrict this report to run for a specific client, enter the Client ID or click the Client ID Link to select one from the Select Client dialog box. > Note: Note: If this report needs to run for all clients then it will take longer to complete. |
  • Leave it blank to select all clients.
  • If you want to restrict this report to run for a specific client, enter the Client ID or click the Client ID Link to select one from the Select Client dialog box. | Year | Select the year from the drop-down for which you want to run this report. |
  1. Click Generate to generate the report. The report contains the following columns:

  • Client ID

  • Client Name

  • Employee Name

  • Employee ID

  • Tax Entity Type

  • Tax Entity ID

  • Tax Entity Name

  • Tax Code

  • Tax Description

  • Successor Taxable Amount

  • Successor Tax Amount

  1. Click XLS to download the report.

Changing a W/C Policy

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/Operations/WC_Policy_Update.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/Operations/WC_Policy_Update.htm

Changing a W/C Policy

You can use the W/C Policy Update form to update a W/C policy that is listed on the Benefits tab in the Client Details record. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: This feature is only available for service providers.

To update a W/C policy:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From Operations|Utility Processing, select W/C Policy Update.

  3. Enter or select one or multiple Policy IDs you want to update. The Description displays in a read-only field.

  4. Select Find Clients. The system populates the table with the clients associated with the selected policies.

  5. Select the clients for updating. (Select the checkbox directly under Select Clients to select all clients.)

  6. Enter or select the existing Policy you want to change, which can consist of the workers’ compensation policy that covers the employees for the client.

  7. Enter or select the Policy Effective Date for the client’s coverage.

  8. Click Process Policy Changes. A message displays, “Are you sure you want to change the selected clients to Policy <policy ID>?” Select Yes to continue.

Note: Note the following:

  • After making a policy change, the Audit Log Display on the Client Details form displays the change and the user who made it.

  • An error message displays if you enter a W/C policy that doesn’t match a policy already in place, “Record <policy ID> is not on file WC.POLICIES.”

Specifying Direct Deposit Terms and Conditions

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/2019/Direct_Deposit_Acceptance_Text.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/2019/Direct_Deposit_Acceptance_Text.htm

Specifying Direct Deposit Terms and Conditions

Enter your organization’s Direct Deposit Terms and Conditions text to display it before accepting direct deposit account information when entered via any web application.

To access this form:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change, select System Parameters.

  3. From the Actions menu, select Direct Deposit Acceptance Text.

To create a Direct Deposit Terms and Conditions text:

  1. Enter the effective date when you want the text to display.

You can submit multiple effective dates for different texts. For example, enter text for 07/01/2019, then enter differently worded text effective on 07/03/2019, then a different text for 02/01/2019.

  1. Enter the text in the box below the Effective Date field.

You can also do the following:

  • To edit existing text, enter or select the date in the Effective Date field and the text for that date displays in an editable format.

  • To delete an existing text, enter or select the date in the Effective Date field and click Delete.

  1. Click Save.

Maintaining Document Security

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/2019/Document_Security_Maintenance.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/2019/Document_Security_Maintenance.htm

Maintaining Document Security

Control document category permissions (upload, delete, move, rename, and other updates) for service providers, worksite trusted advisors, and worksite managers on a per‑role basis with the Document Security Maintenance form.

To open the Document Security Maintenance form:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change, select User Roles. The User Roles form opens.

  3. In Role ID, enter a role ID, or click the Role ID link and select a role ID from the list.

  4. From the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] , select Document Security. The Document Security Maintenance form opens.

To add document categories and permissions to a user role:

  1. Click Add. The Document Security Selection form opens.

  2. Select the document category to add or check Select All to add all categories to the user role.

  3. Click Accept.

  4. Click Save.

To change document category permissions for a user role:

  1. Select Change Permissions next to the Document Category you want to update. The Document Category Permissions panel displays.

  2. Select the category permissions for the user role.

  3. Click Accept.

  4. Click Save.

Maintaining Global mvQuery Image Path

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/2019/Global_mvQuery_Image_Path_Maintenance.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/2019/Global_mvQuery_Image_Path_Maintenance.htm

Maintaining Global mvQuery Image Path

Control the logos that appear on checks and reports printed using mvQuery with this form. Each field controls a different image that you can print on your organization’s checks. Fill in the fields as needed.

  • On-Premise customers: Indicates the location of these logos on your organization’s servers.

  • PrismHR cloud customers: Indicates the location of the images on PrismHR’s servers. Contact support for assistance with setting up this form.

Note: Note: You can override some of these settings at the client level.

Field Name Field Description
Blank Image File Path This image takes up the same space as a logo, but is blank. Enter the location of this image on the mvQuery print server.
mvQuery Report Logo Filepath This logo prints on all reports. Enter the location of this image on the mvQuery print server. Set a client-level report logo by entering the file path in the Print Service Report Logo Filepath field, located on Client\ Change\ Client Details >Actions menu [Image: screenshot] > Report Print Options.
mvQuery Check Logo Filepath This logo prints on all checks. Enter the location of this image on the mvQuery print server. Set a client-level check logo by entering the file path in the Check Print Service Logo Filepath field, located on Client\ Change\ Client Details >Actions menu [Image: screenshot] > Print Service Options.
Show Logos On Garnishment Checks? You can select: - No Logo - Yes - Always Use Global Logo (use the global logo, established in the mvQuery Check Logo Filepath field) - Yes - Use Client Logo If Entered (use a client-level logo, if one exists). Set a client-level check logo by entering the file path in the Check Print Service Logo Filepath field, located on Client\ Change\ Client Details >Actions menu [Image: screenshot] > Print Service Options.
  • No Logo
  • Yes - Always Use Global Logo (use the global logo, established in the mvQuery Check Logo Filepath field)
  • Yes - Use Client Logo If Entered (use a client-level logo, if one exists). | NON-NEGOTIABLE Image File Path | This image prints “NON-NEGOTIABLE” on the check. Enter the location of this image on the mvQuery print server. | ========================================================================

Managing Cash Types

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/2020/Cash_Types.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/2020/Cash_Types.htm

Managing Cash Types

You can manage cash types using the Cash Types form.

[Image: screenshot]

Using this form, you can edit existing cash type codes or enter new ones.

Editing Existing Cash Type Codes

The first time you access this form, it loads any cash type codes that were previously set in the “global” record.

To edit an existing cash type code, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change, select Cash Types. The Cash Types form displays.

  3. Make changes in the following fields:

Field — Description

Cash Type Codes — Edit the cash type code.

Cash Type Descriptions — Edit the cash type code’s description.

Obsolete — Edit the Obsolete option to determine if the cash type code should be obsolete. (Selecting Yes keeps a code and its description from displaying in input fields, so it cannot be re-entered.)

  1. Click Save.

Entering New Cash Type Codes

To enter a new cash type code, do the following:

  1. Click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office).

  2. From System|Change, select Cash Types. The Cash Types form displays.

  3. Click + in the header row. A new line displays in the list.

  4. Complete the following fields:

Field — Description

Cash Type Codes — Enter the cash type code.

Cash Type Descriptions — Enter the cash type code’s description.

Obsolete — Select whether or not the cash type code should be obsolete. (Selecting Yes keeps a code and its description from displaying in input fields, so it cannot be re-entered.)

  1. Click Save.

Converting Global Pay Rate Changes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/2020/Converting-Global-Pay-Rate-Changes.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/2020/Converting-Global-Pay-Rate-Changes.htm

Converting Global Pay Rate Changes

Change pay rates globally with the Global Pay Rate Change form. This process is typically used for minimum wage rate adjustments.

To change a pay rate globally:

  1. Click Back Office.
  2. From System|Action, select Global Pay Rate Change.
  3. Set the date this change becomes effective.
  4. Select a reason for this change. For example, Promo indicates a promotion.
  5. Optional: Select a state for this pay change. If a state is selected, only employees in that state are processed. Leave this field blank to apply this rate change for all employees.
  6. Enter the current hourly rate and the new hourly rate.
  7. Click Preview Changes to review the desired rate change and all employees whose rates are impacted. The screen displays up to the first 100 changes. [Image: screenshot]
  8. Click Download Report to generate a copy of the report.
  9. Click Close; the system downloads the report to your local drive. This will contain all changes made, not just the first 100 employees.
  10. Click Apply Changes if rate changes are set correctly. This button remains disabled until Preview Changes is pressed.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/2020/Default-Network-IDs-Benefit-Plan.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/2020/Default-Network-IDs-Benefit-Plan.htm

Defaulting Network IDs by Benefit Plan

The Default Network by Benefit Plan utility assigns all employees who are covered by the specified benefit plan, but who do not have an assigned network, to the selected network

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group security.

To assign a network for enrollees of a benefit plan who do not have an assigned network:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From Operations|Action, select Default Network by Benefit Plan. The Default Network by Benefit Plan form opens.

  3. Fill in the form.

Option Description
Benefit Plan Click the link and select the benefit plan to which the members belong.
Network ID Enter the Network ID to assign to the unassigned members of the selected benefit plan.

  1. Click Process. A progress box displays the status.

  2. When the progress box shows that the process is complete, click Close to return to the Default Network by Benefit Plan page or Report to open the Job Control Status Report. See Viewing the Job Control Status Report

Deleting Group Benefit Enrollments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/2020/Deleting-Group-Benefit-Enrollments.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/2020/Deleting-Group-Benefit-Enrollments.htm

Deleting Group Benefit Enrollments

Use this utility to delete benefit enrollments from all employees regardless of the status of the benefit plan. The benefit plan is not deleted by the utility at either the client or system level.

WARNING: Important: Only use this utility if an Auto-Enrollment process occurred in error. Running this process deletes all employee enrollments for a given plan.

To perform a group benefit enrollment deletion:

  1. Click Work Centers.

  2. From Work Centers|Onboarding & Benefits, select Benefit Plan Maintenance.

  3. From Group Benefit Plans (Global), select Delete Unused Group Benefit Enrollments.

  4. Enter or select a Benefit Plan ID from the Select Benefit Plan list.

  5. Click Process, then click Yes to delete enrollments. A success or fail message then displays.

  6. Click Cancel to clear the form.

Maintaining the HSA PEO Match

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/2020/HSA-PEO-Match.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/2020/HSA-PEO-Match.htm

Maintaining the HSA PEO Match

The HSA PEO Match form establishes the HSA match amounts paid by the PEO for each medical plan type offered in a specified year. Use this form when the PEO (and not the client) provides an HSA match. The system prorates annual amounts if someone is enrolled mid-year.

To do this, you must add the custom feature code of HSAPEOMATCH to the custom feature codes list. Also, the client needs to check HSA G/L Accounts and add the credit/debit accounts for the HSA PEO Match.

The amount of the PEO match can be overridden on the flexible spending accounts record.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group security.

To maintain the HSA PEO match:

  1. Click Back Office menu > System|Change > HSA PEO Match.

  2. Enter the 4-digit calendar year for the match amount.

  3. Select the Plan and Plan Type. See Selecting Data

  4. In Match Amt, enter the match amount paid by the PEO for the specified plan and year.

  5. If necessary, add another Plan, Plan Type, and Match Amt.

  6. Click Save.

  3. Select an existing DataBridge Code, or enter a new code.

  4. Set up to four codes.

  5. Click Save.

Retiring Vertex GeoCodes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/2020/Retire-Vertex-Geocodes.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/2020/Retire-Vertex-Geocodes.htm

Retiring Vertex GeoCodes

Periodically, in some Monthly Update packages, Vertex announces the retirement of GeoCodes. This procedure walks you through the steps for retiring and replacing Vertex® GeoCodes and rebuilding Tax Registers once the GeoCodes have been retired. Do not run this process until all users are logged off the system.

Note: Note: This form does not use Client Access Group Security.

To retire and replace GeoCodes:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Action, select Retire GeoCodes.

  3. Click the Retired GeoCode link and select the GeoCode you want to retire.

  4. Click the Replacement GeoCode link and select the GeoCode to replace the retired one.

  5. Click Run.

  6. Rebuild the tax registers.

Defining Payday Notifications Daily Start Time

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/2021/Notification_Control_Panel_for_Payday_Notify.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/2021/Notification_Control_Panel_for_Payday_Notify.htm

Defining Payday Notifications Daily Start Time

You can specify the daily start time for payday notifications using the Payday Notify panel on the Notification Control Panel form, which is accessible from the Operations|Action menu. In addition, you can view the last date/time they were run.

To specify the daily start time for payday notifications, do the following:

  1. Click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office).

  2. From Operations|Action, select Notification Control Panel.

  3. In the Payday Notify panel, enter the daily start time in the Daily Payday Notification Start Time field (this field defaults to 05:00:00). Valid entries for this field are times between 12:01AM and 12:00PM (essentially, between midnight and noon), in military time. For example, to start payday notifications at 1:00AM, enter 01:00:00.

Note: Note: If you enter a time outside the 12:01AM and 12:00PM time-frame, an error message displays, “Payday Notification time must be between 12:01 AM and 12:00 PM.”

  1. Click Save.

To the right of the Daily Payday Notification Start Time field a display-only process status displays, which matches the same control number that displays in the BE Notify panel. (See Using the Notification Control Panel (Benefits Enrollment).)

In addition, the display-only Last Run Date/Time field displays the last date and time the process ran.
