Reviewing WSM/WTA Setup and Data Security Access

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/2021/Worksite_User_Data_Security_Download_Report.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/2021/Worksite_User_Data_Security_Download_Report.htm

Reviewing WSM/WTA Setup and Data Security Access

Use the Worksite User Data Security Download form to review your worksite manager/worksite trusted advisor user setup, data security access information, and last login information in a downloaded report in .csv format.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: This report is only available for service providers and only displays data for worksite manager/worksite trusted advisor users, not service providers or worksite employees information.

After processing this report, you can verify that user data security access is setup correctly. Also, after viewing this report you can ensure that the users have access to the appropriate information and then make updates based on these results, so they cannot access sensitive company and employee data.

Generating the Report

To generate this report, do the following:

  1. In PrismHR, click Reports.

  2. From System|Report, select Worksite User Data Security Download. The report opens.

  3. Enter the Selection Criteria to determine what displays on the report:

  • Select the users’ Status (defaults to All).

  • Select the Sort Criteria (defaults to User ID).

  • Select the Filter. A filter table option displays depending on the filter you select. Select the Client ID or User ID link to search for and select clients or users from the multi-value selector that displays. (As you select from the list, that selection moves to the Selected Clients list or the Selected Users list. Click Done when finished.)

Note: A client ID or user ID is not required, so you can leave the filter table option blank.

  1. Click Generate File. A new window opens that displays the reporting process.

  2. When the process is complete, click Report. The Job Control Status Report displays, which indicates the process is complete. Close the report.

  3. Close the process window, then click the downloaded report link that displays at the bottom of the window to open the report in .csv format. Save the report in the appropriate folder.

Reviewing the Report

Note: Note the following when reviewing the downloaded report:

  • The data exactly matches the user’s full record as recorded in the Users form, including Data Security and entities.

  • The report name displays in the first column, Report Title, similar to data that displays in the User Report (XLS version).

  • The sort selection details display in the second column, Selection Criteria, similar to data that displays in the User Report (XLS version).

Listed are samples of the report columns, based on the criteria in the form:

Column — Description

Report Title — The name of the report.

Selection Criteria — The user status, which includes all users, active users, or inactive users.

User ID — The user’s ID.

User Name — The user’s name.

Status — The user’s usage status.

Last Password Change — The last date a change was made to the user password.

Email Address — The email address associated with the user ID.

Mobile Phone — The mobile phone number associated with the user ID.

Employee ID — The employee’s ID.

Employee Name — The employee’s name.

Last Login Date — Last successful login date.

Last Login Time — Last successful login time.

Client ID — The client’s ID.

Access — Indicates if the client is granted, denied, or thru XX/XX/XXXX.

Data Security Location ID — Indicates the location ID that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Member column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form).

Data Security Location Description — Indicates the location description that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Member Name column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form).

Data Security Location Access — Indicates the location access that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Access column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form).

Data Security Division ID — Indicates the division ID that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Member column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form).

Data Security Division Description — Indicates the division description that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Member Name column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form).

Data Security Division Access — Indicates the division access that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Access column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form).

Data Security Department ID — Indicates the department ID that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Member column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form).

Data Security Department Description — Indicates the department description that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Member Name column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form). (Note: This column only displays if the Data Security Entity field is set to Department on the Client Security form.)

Data Security Department Access — Indicates the department access that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Access column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form).

Data Security Shift ID — Indicates the shift ID that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Member column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form).

Data Security Shift Description — Indicates the shift description that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Member Name column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form). (Note: This column only displays if the Data Security Entity field is set to Shift on the Client Security form.)

Data Security Shift Access — Indicates the shift access that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Access column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form).

Data Security Work Group ID — Indicates the work group ID that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Member column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form). (Note: This column only displays if the Data Security Entity field is set to Work Group on the Client Security form.)

Data Security Work Group Description — Indicates the work group description that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Member Name column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form).

Data Security Work Group Access — Indicates the work group access that matches the client ID, which is the same value that displays in the Access column in the Data Security form (accessed from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] on the Users form).

User Role — Indicates each user role as assigned to the user in the Users form on the System|Change menu, where each role displays in a separate column. For example, if two user roles are assigned to a user ID in the Users form: [Image: screenshot] Then those user roles display in separate columns in the report: [Image: screenshot]

H/R Role — Indicates each H/R role as assigned to the user in the Users form on the System|Change menu, where each role displays in a separate column. Note: This column displays information in the same manner as the User Role column.

For more information about managing the client’s data security, see the Client Administration Guide.

Using ACH Originators

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/ACH_Originators.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/ACH_Originators.htm

Using ACH Originators

An ACH originator is a financial institution to which a client sends ACH files. The financial institution becomes the “originating DFI” by submitting the transactions to the ACH network. If you process ACH transactions for clients, each client can have a different financial institution. Use the ACH Originators form to maintain records for each institution.

Maintaining Financial Institution Information

Use the ACH Originators panel to maintain the financial institution information.

To maintain financial institution information, do the following:

  1. Go to the ACH Originators form on the System|Change menu.

  2. Complete the following fields in the ACH Originators panel:

Field — Description

Processor ID — Enter a Processor ID for the financial institution. The PrismHR Customer Support Team recommends that you use easy-to-remember abbreviations for the processor IDs.

Processing Bank ID — Enter the Processing Bank ID, which is the bank-assigned number that identifies your service bank as the destination of the ACH input files. In line 101, it occupies 10 characters, beginning at position 4.

Processing Bank Name — Enter the Processing Bank Name that processes the ACH file on behalf of your organization. This is the originating depository financial institution (ODFI).

Processing Company ID — Enter the Processing Company ID of the originating company that sends ACH files to the bank. Typically, this is the taxpayer ID of the entity sending the files to the bank.

Processing Company Name — Enter the Processing Company Name of the organization that sends ACH files to the originating bank. Typically, this is the employer’s name.

Customer Data Sender ID — Enter the Customer Data Sender ID.

Reference Code — Enter an optional Reference Code that describes the input file for internal accounting purposes. The system uses this in positions 87 through 94 of the file header record. Note: If the Trace Number Prefix field is left blank, PrismHR uses the first eight (8) digits of the originating bank’s ID.

Trace Number Prefix — Enter the Trace Number Prefix, which is the first eight characters of the trace number that the system will enter in positions 80 through 94 in the entry detail record. (If you leave this field blank, the system uses the first eight digits of the originating bank ID.)

Header Trace Number — Enter the eight-character custom number to automatically include it in positions 80-87 of both the Company/Batch Header and Company/Batch Control records within the NACHA file. (This number meets the specific formatting requirements of certain financial institutions, such as credit unions.)

ACH File Options — Select the ACH File Options to use.

Insert End-of-Transmission Character — Select Insert End-of-Transmission Character to include the end-of-transmission character at the end of the ACH deposit file.

End-of-Transmission ASCII Character — If you have chosen to insert an end-of-transmission character, select the End-of-Transmission ASCII Character to use.

Note: Note: The Local Download Path Name and PC File Name fields are used only by the legacy ACH process. You do not need to complete those fields when you use the PrismHR ACH features. When users process consolidated ACH files, they will name the file and choose the location on their system where they want to save it.

  1. If your organization uses non-consolidated ACH processing, enter the full path to the directory in the Local Download Path Name field, including the forward slash (/) character at the end. The system downloads ACH files built for this checking account to this location on your local machine.

  2. Your organization can use a bank script to transfer ACH files to the financial institution that requires the use of a certain file name. Enter the NACHA Directory Override File Name to use instead of the standard file name when writing ACH files to the NACHA directory on a Windows 2000 operating system.

If you enter an override file name here, the system always uses that file name when writing to the NACHA directory. Users will overwrite files with the same name.

  1. To override the ACH naming convention enter the base name of the files transferred to your PC in the PC File Name field, where the first character must be alpha. (The date and “.txt” extension are included in the downloaded filename.) For example, using PHOTO1 as the base name could display the downloaded filename as PHOTO120200101.txt.

  2. If your organization uses non-consolidated ACH processing, enter the PC File Name, which is the base name of files transferred to your hard drive. The system appends the date and .txt extension to the file name in this field. The first character must be a letter of the alphabet.

  3. Indicate the format used for the Child Support EFT Addenda Format. The default is Fixed and you can choose to set it to Variable.

  4. Enter the number of business Days Into Future for ACH Selection. The system selects ACH transactions to submit to the ACH originator. This overrides the global setting in System Parameters; if you enter a negative number, the system holds the ACH until after its expected due date, which you can use to hold garnishments.

  5. Select Separate Child Support Batches by Company to separate child support batches by client.

  6. Select Separate ACH Batches For Debits/Credits to create separate payroll ACH batches within the file for credit and debit transactions. This applies only when you are separating child support batches by company.

  7. If you use Cachet or Wells Fargo, or want to process a Reverse Wire Transfer for ACH processing, select the appropriate Third Party Format.

Note: Note the following:

  • If you select Cachet or Wells Fargo, a panel displays at the bottom of the form (see the following sections for the relevant information).

  • If you select Reverse Wire Transfer, the following warning displays:

[Image: screenshot]

Click OK to continue, then perform the tasks listed in the warning (see the “Setting Up Reverse Wire Transfer Format” section, below).

Setting Up Multiple Email Addresses

When processing multiple ACH files, you must configure the email addresses in the Email addresses for multiple ACH processing section. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

After processing the files, the system distributes two emails:

  • User who ran the ACH process: This email confirms that the process successfully finished (includes all the batches in one email).

  • Users configured on the ACH Originators form: This email is distributed once each batch finishes and includes the file name, total credits, total debits, and total number of entries.

Note: If you do not configure any email addresses, the system does not send an email.

Entering the File Header/Footer

If required, enter the header and footer records unique to the ACH originator, if required. The system appends these to the start and end of each file, respectively.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter the ACH File Header Record for each line in the file header.

  2. Enter the ACH File Footer Record for each line in the file footer.

Setting Up Cachet Third Party Format

If you selected Cachet for the Third Party Format, complete the fields in the Cachet panel.

[Image: screenshot]

Complete the following information:

  1. Select Generate Cachet ACH File Format to generate a separate direct deposit funding transaction for Cachet.

Note: Note: Cachet prefers the net collection method, so typically you would select this option. If needed, contact the PrismHR Customer Support Team to verify.

  1. Select Generate Cachet Net Collection Funding to use the net collection funding method.

  2. Enter the Net Collection Bank Account to which to post net fund debits. The offset account on this bank account should be the one to which to credit funds.

  3. Enter the number of days prior to any pay date that a funding transaction should take place in the Cachet Funding Transaction Days Prior to Pay Date field.

  4. Select Suppress Child Support EFT from Funding Debit Amount if your organization does not use Cachet to process child support transactions.

  5. Enter the Cachet File Name Prefix for the transaction file sent to Cachet.

  6. To override the days prior to pay date for one or more clients:

  1. — Enter the client ID that makes the ACH transaction in the Cachet Client ID field. The client’s doing-business-as name displays.
b. Enter the number of days for the client in the Override Days Prior Pay Date field.

Setting Up Wells Fargo Third Party Format

If you selected Wells Fargo for the Third Party Format, complete the fields in the Wells Fargo panel.

[Image: screenshot]

Complete the following information:

  1. Enter the Wells Fargo Control No assigned by Wells Fargo Bank.

  2. Enter the CEO Company ID assigned by Wells Fargo Bank.

Setting Up Reverse Wire Transfer Format

Performing a reverse wire transfer allows clients to determine the payment amount prior to posting payrolls, so the system places those funds into a file that is sent before payroll is completed/posted. (This ensures that the client has the funds before payroll is posted.)

Important! The reverse wire process does not work for internal processing. (System validation on the Reverse Wire Account field on the Account tab in the Client Details form will not allow users to make an entry in this field if the active client is set up for internal ACH processing on the System Parameters form.)

Note: You cannot make changes to a reverse wire payroll whose payment has been marked as received because the funds were already sent. (These payrolls display with green checkmarks, marking them as lockedPayment Received payrolls when viewing them in the SuperBatch and Process Payroll forms.)

The following diagram displays the reverse wire transfer process:

[Image: screenshot]

To set up a reverse wire transfer:

  1. Set up an ACH originator to use Reverse Wire Transfer by selecting the desired format in the Third Party Format panel on the ACH Originators form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Important! You must test the ISO file format with your banking institutions before processing a live file. Not all banks may accept this format, so you must complete testing before payroll runs using the ISO format.

  1. Enter the number of Days Before Invoice Date, which is the offset days used to calculate the effective date for a transaction. For example, if you enter -1 and then the effective date, the system sets the offset days to one day before the invoice date.

Note: Note the following:

  • If you select Wells Fargo in the Bank Name field, enter the sender’s name and address in the fields that display.

  • Once an originator is defined as reverse wire, it cannot be used for employee direct deposits because the ACH output file format is different.

  1. Associate a bank Account ID in the Bank Accounts form with the ACH originator from the previous steps. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Do not use a checking account the system uses to process employee direct deposits.

  1. Set up the client for reverse wire by setting the ACH status to Wire Transfer Client on the Billing tab in the Client Details form. (You must include the client bank account information.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Selecting the Transfer Type helps easily identify which funding is set up for the client. (This step is not required to produce a successful file.)

  1. On the client, associate the bank Account ID from the previous step with the Reverse Wire Account field on the Account tab in the Client Details form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Maintaining Bank Accounts

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Bank_Accounts.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Bank_Accounts.htm

Maintaining Bank Accounts

Use the Bank Accounts form to maintain the information for the accounts at financial institutions used in PrismHR.

Entering Bank Account Information

Enter the basic information about the account in the Bank Accounts panel. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: The 00 Checking Account is a special purpose account, the master account for all transactions. Each file header shows the 00 Checking Account as the main file header, with the funds being transferred into the account from whatever checking account the individual ACH shows it is processed. This adds a level of abstraction to the process, but allows a single account to process all the ACH clearing with only summary transactions from each of the actual checking accounts.

To maintain account information:

  1. Enter or select the bank Account ID for this account. You can enter numeric or alphanumeric characters in this field, or a combination of both.

Note: If a bank Account ID has already been used to process a transaction, you cannot delete it when one or more of the following conditions exist:

  • The system created an ACH file with the bank Account ID.

  • The system processed cash receipts using the bank Account ID.

  1. Enter a Reference for the name of the financial institution where this account is maintained, as well as any other information. For example, Payroll Cash Account at Fleet Bank.

  2. Enter the Bank Name.

  3. Enter the Bank Address, which is the street or mailing address.

  4. Enter the City, State & ZIP Code.

  5. Enter the Transit Number assigned to this financial institution. This number prints on checks drawn on this bank unless you enter a different number in Transit Number (Chks) below.

  6. Enter the client’s Account Number at this financial institution. This account is debited when an offsetting settlement entry is created.

  7. Enter the Fractional Transit number that appears on checks. This number is the same for all checks drawn on a unique checking account, typically in the format NN/NNN.

  8. Enter the Check Title.

  9. Enter the Transit Number (Chks) that print on checks drawn on this bank. If this field is left blank, PrismHR uses the Transit Number value.

  10. Select Use Positive Pay if this account uses Positive Pay Files. You must also define the layout using the Positive Pay Setup form (see Positive Pay Setup).

  11. Enter the Acct Sys ChkID Number. This is the code your accounting software associates with this account and PrismHR uses for reconciliations or receipts.

  12. Select One Garn/Pay Chk Cntr to use the same check number sequence for payroll, third party, and garnishment checks. Otherwise, the system uses separate counters for each type.

  13. The Next Check Number and Next Garnishment Number display. You cannot modify those values on this form, but the number can be modified using the Managing Next Number Control form.

  14. Enter or select the Offset Account ID for the offset settlement checking account. (Use the same ACH originator as this bank account.)

  15. Enter or select the Rebate Bill Code if this account belongs to the client. The system uses this code to credit the client for net checks that have been drafted.

  16. Enter the MICR Account Number that prints on the MICR line of checks.

  17. Enter or select the Employer ID who is the owner of the checking account, from a general ledger point of view.

  18. Select Inactive Account if this account is no longer used.

  19. Select the ACH Options for this account, if appropriate.

  20. Select Use for Garnishments Only to indicate that the account is used only for garnishment payments. This ensures that the account does not stop processing due to XMit Day/Time rules.

  21. In the Minimum ACH Window (Days) field, enter the minimum number of days prior to the pay date that your organization must process a batch in order for employees to receive direct deposits. This value overrides the global parameter.

  22. Enter the minimum number of days it takes to obtain ACH credit in the Min ACH Receipt Days field.

This value adjusts the G/L receipt date to correspond with your bank’s practices. It also ensures that if you use a negative ACH adjust date for cash receipts, this date is never earlier than the selection made here. If the cash receipt is earlier than the time indicated, the G/L effect adjusts to be this date. This does not change the actual ACH file. For example, enter 0 if you get credit for the same date you send, and enter 1 if you always get credit on the next day.

  1. Select Show in Cash Receipts if this account should be available for cash receipts.

  2. If applicable, enter the Max Void ACH Days, which is the number of banking days this account allows to pass from the Pay Date to Void Date. After that number of days, PrismHR displays warnings.

  3. Enter Post Cutoff Time for posting to begin on a payroll batch that uses this checking account.

  4. Enable Same Day Processing if the bank account is used for same day processing. (If you enable this field, the system translates this information to the ACH file.)

Note: Note the following:

  • If you enable Same Day Processing, the Cutoff Time field displays. Select 1300 (default) or 1700 as the cutoff time.

  • If you attempt to finalize a same-day payroll after the defined time/pay date, the following payroll finalization error message displays when the SAMEDAYSTOP custom feature code is enabled at the global level, “Payroll posting after the Same Day Processing cutoff is prohibited. Correct the pay date to continue.” (This feature is only available for service providers.)

  1. Categorize the bank Account Type ownership by selecting PEO Master, Client Owned, or Demo.

Setting Up Print Parameters

The Print Parameters panel controls how the check print number and signature printed on the check.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Select the Check Number Print Mask that determines the format of the check number on checks.

  2. Select mvQuery Check Printing to enable mvQuery PSE Check Printing.

  3. Enter the complete mvQuery Signature Filepath, for example, m:\signature.png. This is the location of the check signature file on the mvQuery Print Server.

  4. Enter the Bank Account Name, Bank Account Address, and City, State & ZIP Code for this account.

Setting Up ACH Processing Parameters

Use the fields in the ACH Setup panel if this bank account is used for ACH processing. The panel controls the setup of the Batch Header form. The fields that are available depend on whether your organization is using consolidated ACH file processing or standard file processing. Refer to the instructions that match the setup in your system.

Basic Consolidated Processing

When Consolidated ACH File Processing Used in System Parameters is set to Yes, the ACH Setup panel displays as shown below.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter or select the ACH Processor ID. See Using ACH Originators to learn about creating ACH processors.

  2. Enter the Company Name (Batch Header), which is the name of the client who owns this checking account. This name appears in positions 5–20 of the Company Batch Header Record.

  3. Enter the Company Identification# (Batch Header), which is the client identification number used only on the batch header. Typically, this consists of a 1 followed by the 9-digit EIN.

  4. Enter the Company Identification# (CCD Batch Header), which is an optional client identification number used on the CCD batch header. Typically, you enter a value only when advised to do so by your financial institution.

  5. Enter the Company Identification# (PPD Batch Header), which is an optional client identification number used on the PPD batch header. Typically, you enter a value only when advised to do so by your financial institution.

  6. Enter the Company Identification# (Offset), which is an identification number used on the offset detail form when this account is specified as an offset account.

  7. If the service bank requires you to provide a different account number for offset transactions, enter the Immediate Destination Identification # (Offset).

  8. Enter the Originating DFI Identification # assigned by the service bank. It is 8 characters and appears on the lines that begin with 52 and 82 in positions 80–87.

  9. Enter the PC File Name, which is an optional field used as the base name of files transferred to your computer. The system also appends the date and .txt extension to the end of the name you indicate in this field.

  10. Select Use Suspense Accounting if this bank account should use suspense accounting. When selected, ACH transactions are tracked in a “suspense” account and do not move to the cash account until the ACH batch file is created. That allows users to easily reconcile account balances based on transactions processed by the bank. See Suspense Accounts.

  11. Do not select Process As Wire (only for special File Formats) unless directed to do so by a PrismHR Customer Support Team representative. It is only for custom-designed file formats.

Other Processing

The Company setting uses ACH originators and generates consolidated ACH files sorted by company.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter or select the ACH Processor ID. See Using ACH Originators to learn about creating ACH processors.

  2. Enter the Immediate Destination Identification # that identifies the service bank as the destination of ACH input files.

  3. If the service bank requires you to provide a different account number for offset transactions, enter the Immediate Destination Identification # (Offset).

  4. Enter the Immediate Origin Identification # assigned by the service bank. In the 101 record, this occupies the 10 characters beginning at position 14. If you use headers, this is typically the account number, and could be longer than 10 characters.

  5. Enter the Company Identification# (Batch Header), which is the client identification number used only on the batch header. Typically, this consists of a 1 followed by the 9-digit EIN.

  6. Enter the Company Identification# (CCD Batch Header), which is an optional client identification number used on the CCD batch header. Typically, you enter a value only when advised to do so by your financial institution.

  7. Enter the Company Identification# (PPD Batch Header), which is an optional client identification number used on the PPD batch header. Typically, you enter a value only when advised to do so by your financial institution.

  8. Enter the Company Identification# (Offset), which is an identification number used on the offset detail form when this account is specified as an offset account.

  9. Enter the Company Name. This can be up to 16 alphanumeric characters, and appears in the 101 record starting at position 64.

  10. Enter the Company Name (Batch Header), which is the name of the client who owns this checking account. This name appears in positions 5–20 of the Company Batch Header Record.

  11. The Reference Code is optional; use it to refer to your input file for internal accounting purposes.

  12. Enter the Trace Number Prefix, which is the first 8 digits of the Trace Number entered in positions 80–94 of the Entry Detail Record. If this field is blank, PrismHR populates it with zeroes.

  13. Enter the Company Name (Batch Header), which is the name of the client who owns this checking account. This name appears in positions 5–20 of the Company Batch Header Record.

  14. If required, enter the ACH File Header Record(s), which is unique to the financial institution. This information is placed at the beginning of the ASCII file.

  15. Enter the full DOS File Path Name (Unix Host Only) to which to download the ACH files built for the checking account. Include the  (backslash) at the end of the path name.

  16. Enter the PC File Name, which is an optional field used as the base name of files transferred to your computer. The system also appends the date and .txt extension to the end of the name you indicate in this field.

  17. Enter the NACHA Directory Override File Name (NT Host Only), which is the file name used instead of a standard file name when PrismHR writes to the NACHA directory.

If your organization uses a bank script to transfer your ACH file to a financial institution that requires the use of a certain file name. If you enter an override file name in this field, the system will always use that file name when writing to the NACHA directory.

This process assumes that there will not already be a file by the same name in the directory when writing to the directory. If it finds an existing file, the system displays a message that gives the user the choice of whether to overwrite the existing file.

  1. Enter the destination ACH Bank Name used in the header record of the ACH file. If left blank, the system uses the Bank Name.

  2. Select Suppress EOT Character to suppress appending the end-of-transmission character (Char(26)) at the end of the ACH deposit file.

  3. Enter the Slash Replacement Character that PrismHR replaces with a slash when it builds the ACH file. For example, ^.

  4. Select Use Suspense Accounting if this bank account should use suspense accounting. When selected, ACH transactions are tracked in a “suspense” account and do not move to the cash account until the ACH batch file is created. That allows users to easily reconcile account balances based on transactions processed by the bank. See Suspense Accounts.

Suspense Accounts

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Bank_Accounts_Suspense.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Bank_Accounts_Suspense.htm

Suspense Accounts

Rather than have ACH data update immediately against a cash account before it is transmitted to the bank, which can cause confusion when users attempt to reconcile the account, your organization might want to create a “suspense” account for any bank account that processes ACH transactions. Each voucher is posted in detail against the suspense account.

During ACH file creation, the total of the vouchers transmitted in a batch comes out of the suspense account and hits the cash account. This allows for easier reconciliation, as the ACH suspense account should be zero each day or reconcilable. It is easier to balance the bank’s daily reports because the totals in the cash account should match the amounts directly.

Bank Account Setup

Set up the bank account in PrismHR.

  1. Either create a new bank account or edit an existing one; see Maintaining Bank Accounts.

  2. Select the Use Suspense Accounting option in the ACH Setup panel.

G/L Template Setup

Enter the suspense G/L accounts for the account in the appropriate G/L template.

  1. Open G/L Setup Maintenance (found in the Back Office menu under System|Change).

  2. Enter the G/L Template.

  3. From the G/L Type drop-down, select Checking Accounts. The form lists each Checking Account and Description in the system.

  4. For the accounts that indicate they use a suspense account, enter the Suspense GL Account.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Save.

Voucher Examples

The suspense G/L account displays in the Accounting tab of each ACH Employee Voucher.

Bank Routing

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Bank_Routing.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Bank_Routing.htm

Bank Routing

Use the Bank Routing form to establish bank routing and contact information, as well as how to support debit card transactions.

  1. Enter the Routing Code for the financial institution.

  2. Enter the Bank Name.

  3. Enter the Bank City, State, and ZIP Code.

  4. Enter the Bank Phone Number.

  5. If your organization has enabled the pay card custom feature for any client, then the PayCard (Automove) option displays. Use this to indicate that the account is for pay cards that can be replaced automatically by a checking account. See Setting Up Pay Cards and Direct Deposit for details on this feature.

  6. Select Debit Card Update if this routing code supports debit cards and requires an update to the issuer for use of a new card.

  7. If you track debit card updates, the Debit Card Track option displays. Select this option if this financial institution tracks a debit card ID. The system then requests the debit card ID at ACH entry.

  8. Click Save.

Setting Benefit Network Locations

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Benefit_Network_Locations.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Benefit_Network_Locations.htm

Setting Benefit Network Locations

Use the Network Zip Codes form, accessed by selecting Network ZIP Codes in the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

, to enter locations by ZIP code for benefit plans that have a network assigned. This form only displays in the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

when the Collect Network Information option in the Other Processing Parameters panel is selected.

You can also import multiple locations using the Import Network ZIP Codes import template. To quickly access this import template, select Import Network ZIP Codes. For more information, see Importing Network ZIP Codes.

To set benefit network locations:

  1. On the Actions menu, click Network Zip Codes.

Use this option — To define this

Benefit Plan ID — This field is read only. This field auto populated with the benefit plan ID that was entered on the Group Benefit Plans form.

Network ID — The ID of the network to which the plan is assigned. This is required. > Note: Note: When a benefit plan is set up to use networks (for billing, premium or both) and a network is marked as Inactive, the inactive network now displays in the Network ID dropdown with ‘(Inactive)’ next to it. All inactive networks filter to the bottom of the list in the order that they appear on the networks grid. You cannot modify or add new rates for Inactive networks. However, you can view existing rates for Inactive networks. When an inactive network is selected, the table is disabled. The Save and Delete buttons are also disabled. A warning message displays stating The selected network is inactive. No modifications can be made. Click the OK button to acknowledge the message.

ZIP Codes — The five-digit ZIP code where this benefit plan is offered. The City & State display if the ZIP code exists in the system. You can enter multiple ZIP Codes as needed by clicking + to add additional rows. You can also click the Zip Code hyperlink and select the ZIP Codes from the Select ZIP Codes selector that displays. On this selector, you can filter the ZIP Codes according to State by using the State drop-down filter.

  1. Click Save.

Updating ZIP Codes

All ZIP codes must first be entered at the system-level to be attached to a benefit plan. ZIP code records that are in the system always display City & State information in the table. If city and state information does not display, the ZIP code record does not exist at the system-level.

It is recommended that you review and update all ZIP code records in the Zip Codes form. When a ZIP code record is in the system, you can attach it to a benefit plan. For more information, see Setting Up Zip Codes.

Using Billing Codes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Billing_Codes.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Billing_Codes.htm

Using Billing Codes

Use the Billing Codes form to define billing entry and accounting information.

There are certain bill codes that PrismHR requires, and rules for others. Here is a list of codes used as system defaults and their usage:

  • 000: Gross Wages

  • 001: FICA/OASDI

  • 002: FICA/Medicare

  • 003: FUTA

  • 004: SUTA

  • 004O: Other State Tax (when needed)

  • 005: Workers’ Compensation

  • 005D: Workers’ Compensation Discount

  • 006: Administrative Fee

  • 006D: Administrative Fee Special Discount

  • 006M: Adminstrative Fee Adjust to Min/Max

All other codes are added to the end of the list at bill time, such as benefits and deductions.

Sales tax codes are formatted TAX{xx}, where xx is the two-character state code, for example, TAXOH for Ohio state tax.

TB{BenefitPlanID} is the first bill code checked during the termination of an employee’s benefits. For example, a benefit plan MEDABC would look for the bill code TBMEDABC. If present, the system uses that, otherwise the system looks for a code TEBA (terminated employee benefit acceleration). This method gives the ability to create accounting detail where it is warranted while lumping smaller plans into one TEBA bucket.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Open the Billing Codes form and complete the following fields:
Field Description
Bill Code Enter or select the Bill Code that describes a billing entry. If you select this field, a selector form displays where you can search for a specific bill code or its description or select a code from the list that displays. When this form opens, the bill code, description, and obsolete date display. To filter the search to display only Obsolete codes, select Yes in the Obsolete field (the default is No). (Note: Codes with an obsolete date earlier than the current date do not display in the selector form.) To refresh the list, select Reset Search and Filters.
Bill Description Enter a Bill Description of this Bill Code. The description displays on invoices if the bill format does not normally include this bill code. It does not display on normal invoices if the billing code is included in the usual invoice format.
Profitability Rpt Column Select the Profitability Rpt Column of the report in which to include this billing code.
Annualized on Profit Select Annualized on Profit to annualize the bill code for the profitability report.
Invoice Sales Rpt Column Select the Invoice Sales Rpt Column of the Invoice Sales report in which to include this billing code.
Invoice Revenue Analysis Rpt Select the Invoice Revenue Analysis Rpt column of the Invoice Revenue Analysis report in which to include this billing code.
TX Franchise Rpt Accumulator Select the TX Franchise Rpt Accumulator to print on the Texas Franchise Report. The system adds any amount billed to this code to that accumulator.
Obsolete Date Enter the Obsolete Date when this billing code becomes obsolete, if ever.
Memo Client Acct Only Select Memo Client Acct Only if this bill code should not display in the actual invoice, but remain part of the client accounting system. Note: The Memo Client Acct Only field setting is only available for retirement 401(k) match reporting through PEO accounting. Selecting this option causes the client accounting record to be out of balance by the amount of the memo entries unless the client accounting records include a memo offset line. To do this, your organization must have a memo offset set up in PEO Client Accounting as an other bill code. The breakdown of these non-billed entries can be helpful on a retirement plan with a match that your organization does not collect.
Sales Tax Enter each Sales Tax state code where taxes apply to this billing code. If this is a state-based sales tax billing code, do not enter any states in the table.
Bill Redirect Code/Bill Redirect Clent To redirect billing: \ a. \ Enter the Bill Redirect Code to redirect this billing code based on a Redirection Plan. \ \ — \ — \ \ b. \ Enter the Bill Redirect Client against which this plan should redirect this billing code. \ \ — \ — \
a. Enter the Bill Redirect Code to redirect this billing code based on a Redirection Plan.
b. Enter the Bill Redirect Client against which this plan should redirect this billing code.
  1. Click Save.

Establishing Billing Events

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Billing_Events.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Billing_Events.htm

Establishing Billing Events

You can use the Billing Events form to establish events to bill, or override prices for various items.

There are certain events that PrismHR requires, and rules for others. Here is a list of codes used as system defaults and their usage:

  • 000: Payroll Generated; you cannot edit the bill code for this event. Those codes are predefined.

  • NESxx: New Employee Setup, where xx is the employment type. If the system does not find an NES code with the appropriate employment type, it uses the standard NES code.

  • TEPxx: Terminated Employee Processing, where xx is the employment type. If the system does not find a TEP code with the appropriate employment type, it uses the standard TEP code.

  • RHSFEE: Rehire Setup Fee. Auto-bills for employees of any type when there is no specific FT/PT designation.

  • RHSFEEF: Rehire Setup Fee Full Time Employees. Auto-bills for employees of any type when there is no specific FT/PT designation.

  • RHSFEEP: Rehire Setup Fee Part Time Employees. Auto-bills for employees of any type when there is no specific FT/PT designation.

Note: Note: You can override billing event rates for specific clients using the Billing tab on the Client Details form.

Creating a Billing Event

You can use the Billing Events panel to establish an event to bill.

[Image: screenshot]

To create a billing event, do the following:

  1. Enter or select a Bill Event Code that represents the reason for a billing item. If you select this field, a selector form displays where you can search for a specific bill event code or its description or select a code from the list that displays. When this form opens, the bill event code, description, and obsolete date display.

To filter the search to display only Obsolete codes, select Yes in the Obsolete field (the default is No). (Note: Codes with an obsolete date earlier than the current date do not display in the selector form.)

To refresh the list, select Reset Search and Filters.

  1. Enter a Description of the billing event.

  2. Enter the Bill Code related to this billing event.

  3. Select Show Detailed if you want to display the details of this billing event on an invoice.

  4. If you selected Show Detailed in the previous step, the Display Duplicate Detail Lines on Invoices field now displays.

If your organization does not use the INVDUPEDETAIL feature code, you can select this option to only display duplicate detail line items associated with this billing event. Please note that this is a system-level setting and will take effect for any client in your system that is billed under this billing event code.

Note: Note: Your profits are the difference between the Standard Price billed to your client and the Standard Cost to your organization.

  1. Enter the Standard Price if the event has a standard amount to bill for this billing event.

  2. Enter the Bill Pend Std Cost if there is a standard cost associated with this billing event. For example, 2nd Day Air could have a standard cost of $9.00.

  3. Enter the Obsolete Date when this billing event is no longer valid.

  4. Enter the desired template combination in the Comment Template text box. This text box is available only for the following Third Party Sick Bill Event Codes:

  • TPS-FUTA
  • TPS-MED
  • TPS-OASDI
  • TPS-TAX

Establishing Price Overrides

You can use the Price Overrides panel to establish prices that override the standard price of this billing event.

[Image: screenshot]

To establish override prices, do the following:

  1. For each cost center that requires a different standard price from the default:
a. Enter the Cost Center ID.
b. Enter the Override Rate to use for the cost center.
— —
  1. — Enter the Bill Pend Cost to charged against this override. A negative number represents a decrease in costs.
  1. Click Save.

Establishing Billing Formats

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Billing_Formats.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Billing_Formats.htm

Establishing Billing Formats

The Billing Formats form establishes bill formats/invoices that you can use for one or more clients.

Note: Note: If a user creates a new billing code, you must define a bill format that links to that code, or else it displays as an “other” line on the invoice.

To set up a billing format:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change, select Billing Formats.

  3. Complete these fields as required:

Field Description
Format Specifies the Billing Format ID.
Format Description A description that indicates how this billing format is used. If the format is specific to one client, indicate that in the description.
Invoice Print Format Format for printing invoices. For example, STACK Print 3Col by Break Stacked Version (WCSort on Template!). > Note: Note the following: - The STACK Print 3Col by Break Stacked Version (WCSort on Template!) option is only valid in PrismHR Core and will not display in Employee Portal (EP). - The STDNOBANK Standard Invoice with suppressed banking info option hides ACH/banking account information (that is, the system removes the bank account and all ACH Payment record data from the on-screen invoice display and the invoice’s PDF output) when the client is using any of the Electronic Billing options on the Billing tab in the Client Details form. Note: This format is only valid in PrismHR Core and will not display in Employee Portal (EP).
  • The STACK Print 3Col by Break Stacked Version (WCSort on Template!) option is only valid in PrismHR Core and will not display in Employee Portal (EP).
  • The STDNOBANK Standard Invoice with suppressed banking info option hides ACH/banking account information (that is, the system removes the bank account and all ACH Payment record data from the on-screen invoice display and the invoice’s PDF output) when the client is using any of the Electronic Billing options on the Billing tab in the Client Details form. | Format Orientation (Portrait or Landscape) | Specifies the orientation for invoices. If you select landscape, specify whether you want invoices to display a client logo or return address. For landscape, this formats the first page of the report so that address information displays in double-window 9” x 12” envelopes. | | Message ID | Enter text or select an invoice message for any special message format. (These formats are defined in System Parameters.) If you select this field, the Select Invoice Message list displays where you can select an invoice message. | | Show Past Due | Displays open/past due amounts on the invoice. | | Past Due In Invoice Total | Displays open and past due invoices in the invoice total. Otherwise, there is only a statement listing at the end. | | Show on Remit | Displays open/past due invoice listings on the remittance form. | | Billing Code Multi-Value Grid Fields: | | | Line Description | Description that appears on the invoice in the position indicated, depending on the value of the Print if 0 field. > Note: Note: Position indicated means the order of these line items determines the order of the billing lines when printed. In other words, the first description in this column is the first line printed on the bill, the second description is the second line printed, and so forth. | | Company Account | Account number used to show clients what journal effect to post on their records. This is for special client accounting. | | Print if zero | Select Yes from the drop-down to print the line on the invoice even when the value is zero. If you select No, the invoice does not include the line if its value is zero for that invoice. | | View Code | Click [Image: screenshot] to see the list of bill codes included in the line. [Image: Bill Code and description] | | Add/Edit Code | Click [Image: pen and paper] to add or edit billing codes. > Note: Note: When entering codes for a new line item, the search link no longer adds extra lines before the first bill code in a multi-value grid. |
  1. Click Save in the Billing Formats form.

Note: Note: You can copy data by selecting the Copy option from the Actions menu; however, do not use spaces in the Copy To field (an error message will display).

Adding Billing Codes to a New Line Item

This section describes how to add billing codes to new line items on a billing format.

To add billing codes to a new line item:

  1. Select an existing bill format. The form is populated with the billing format settings and existing line items for this format.

  2. Click + to add a new line item. A new row appears at the bottom of the multi-value grid (MVG). [Image: line items, along with company account and the view and edit icons]

  3. Enter a Line Description. When you click outside that field, the View and Edit icons appear.

  4. Click the Edit icon [Image: screenshot] . The Bill Codes selector appears.

  5. Select a code from the list. The view switches to the Bill Codes for MVG with that code displayed in the first row.

Note: Note: You can enter additional rows either by entering codes manually or by using the search link in the Bill Code header. The form should not insert any blank rows.

  1. Click Save to save that code to the line item. The system returns to Billing Formats.

  2. Click View for the new line item to confirm that the billing code was added. For example, Auto401k for NEW. [Image: Bill Code and Description]

  3. Click Save on the main Billing Formats form to commit these changes to your billing format.

Rate Groups

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Billing_Rate_Groups.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Billing_Rate_Groups.htm

Rate Groups

Use the Rate Groups form to maintain rate group codes. The system uses these codes to manage billing for benefit plans.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: Rate Group Codes can contain any alphanumeric characters except 0. They also cannot contain a period (.).

To set up a rate group:

  1. Enter the Rate Group code.

  2. Enter a description of the rate group in the Group Name field.

  3. Select Inactive if this rate group is not currently used in PrismHR.

  4. Select Premium Rate Group to use this rate group for premiums instead of billing.

  5. Click Save.

When you select an existing Rate Group and save the form, the system checks for the following validations for the Premium Rate Group checkbox:

  • If the Premium Rate Group field is checked, then on clicking Save, the system verifies that there are no Billing Rate records associated with the selected Rate Group.

  • If the Premium Rate Group field in unchecked, then on clicking Save, the system verifies that there are no Premium Rate records associated with the selected Rate Group.

Note: Note: If any Billing Rate or Premium Rate is found in any of the above mentioned validation, an error message stating, Rates are currently associated with this Rate Group. Changes to the ‘Premium Rate Group’ are not allowed. is displayed.

Defining Methods for Billing Clients

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Billing_Templates.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Billing_Templates.htm

Defining Methods for Billing Clients

Use the Billing Templates form to define methods for billing clients.

Establishing Parameters Required to Bill Clients

The Billing Templates panel establishes the parameters required to bill a client for services.

Example of the Billing Templates form (PEO type)

[Image: screenshot]

Example of the Billing Templates form (ASO type)

[Image: screenshot]

To configure billing templates:

  1. Enter the Template ID used to access this billing template.

  2. From the Template Type list, select whether this template applies to PEOs or ASOs. Selecting one of these options does the following:

  • PEO: Allows users to enable check boxes in the Limit and Discount Shelter columns as default items.

  • ASO: Automatically defaults to honoring Limit and Discount Shelter column items.

  1. Enter a Template Description.

  2. Select Bundled if this is a bundled billing template. The client is billed at a fixed rate and the Admin fee is a squeezed computation.

Note: You cannot select the Default Rates check box unless you also select the Bundled check box.

  1. Select Default Rates to use the standard default rate.

  2. Select the Based On method, which determines whether to base the Admin fee on Units or Wages. If you select Units, you must also complete the Bundled Unit Based Maintenance panel.

  3. Select Workers’ Comp Sort if the invoice should sort and break on Workers’ Compensation codes. The system applies this sort after other sorts for the stack invoice only.

Other sorts are set at the client level (by department, division, location, and so on). The stack invoice formats the invoice differently, presenting hours, wages, and extensions—usually for bundled billing.

  1. Select the service types and matching G/L templates:

  • Enter each Service Type for which this billing template can be used.

  • Enter the G/L Template that is appropriate for this billing template and Service Type.

  1. Enter the billing template expiration date in the Expires On field, if any. After this date, PrismHR will not allow your organization to process payrolls using this template until it is updated.

  2. Select the Replaced By template, which is the template that replaces this one after the expiration date in the Expired On field.

  3. Select the check boxes as appropriate. (Fewer check boxes are available for ASO templates than for PEO templates.)

  • Select Add to indicate that each bill item is an add-on to the compensation rates for unbundled amounts.

For Workers’ Comp (if Hourly), this determines whether to add hourly based workers’ compensation to each billing item.

  • For PEO templates, select Limit to indicate that each bill item must stop at the prescribed high limit for billing purposes. For bundled amounts, the bundled rates are decreased. On bundled companies, the rate decreases when the limit is met for items that are limited. It decreases by the amount of the client’s bill rate for the item.

  • For PEO templates, select Discount Shelter to indicate that clients with this template should receive a benefit of any sheltered amounts (Section 125, 401(k), and so on) for each bill item.

  • Workers Comp High Comp indicates whether compensation is limited on employees determined as highly compensated, or whether to compute it on all compensation-eligible wages. An employee is high comp if they are over the high compensation limit (either the state-mandated or officer).

  • Workers Comp Overtime indicates whether the Workers’ Compensation should use two-thirds (2/3) of overtime for premium computations.

Note: Note: Use the Special FUTA Rate only as an override; do not use it for all clients. If the federal government changed FUTA to be 0.85% and you used this field to set the FUTA rate for each client, you would have to change it for every client.

  1. If appropriate, enter the Special FUTA Rate as a percentage.

  2. Select Skip Employee Fees for New Clients if you will not charge the client for new hires and terminated employees during the first 30 days of service.

  3. Complete the additional sections below, as needed. When finished, click Save.

Maintaining Bill Rates and Administration Fees

If this is a bundled billing template that uses default rates, use the Bundled Rate Maintenance panel to maintain the bill rates and administrative fees.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: If the Default Rate is greater than zero, the system uses it for any Workers’ Compensation code not listed in the table. If there is a value in this field and no value in the W/C Code field, there may be billing errors; use the Default Rate with care. If you leave the Default Rate blank, users entering data for clients with this billing template see messages that the listed Workers’ Compensation code does not have a billing amount. The system continues to display this message until you update the bill template for the code or enter a default amount.

Field Name Description
Default Rate Enter the Default Rate to use for all clients’ Workers’ Compensation rates not defined in the table. This value is useful for “one-price-fits-all” clients.
W/C Code Grid For each Workers’ Compensation code that requires a different rate: - Enter the W/C Code. The Class Description displays. - Enter the Min Admin Fee amount to use. This overrides any amount entered on the client record, except for special rates. The system discounts the minimum fee by the special discount rate. - Enter the WC Def Bill Rate, which is the default billing rate for the W/C Code.
  • Enter the W/C Code. The Class Description displays.
  • Enter the Min Admin Fee amount to use. This overrides any amount entered on the client record, except for special rates. The system discounts the minimum fee by the special discount rate.
  • Enter the WC Def Bill Rate, which is the default billing rate for the W/C Code. ## Selecting Pay Codes That Control Unit-based Administration Fees

If this is a bundled billing template with rates based on units, use the Bundled Unit Based Maintenance panel to select the pay codes that control the unit-based Admin fee.

Enter all Pay Codes to include in the Admin fee computation.

[Image: screenshot]

Defining Benefits Included in Administration Fees

Use the Benefits Included panel to define the benefits included in the Admin fee.

[Image: screenshot]

For each benefit:

  1. Enter any Included Benefits for this billing template’s Admin fees.

  2. Indicate whether the benefit plan is Included on Arrears:

  • Yes: The system charges the fee even if employees do not receive pay. The system creates a zero billing, charging the value of the benefits against the Admin fee, and resulting in negative Admin fees.

  • No: The client pays the benefit for employees when they do not receive pay. The system bills clients for each employee (who is not on leave) receiving an arrearage voucher. It returns the value of these charges upon the employee’s return, with the assumption that billing covers all fees up to that time. If the employee never receives another payment, the system continues the charge.

  1. Select Retirement Match Included to include the match amounts in the billing template amount.

Including Other Taxes

Use the Other Tax Code Billing Options panel to include other taxes in the billing template.

[Image: screenshot]

To include other taxes:

  1. Enter each Tax Code to include.

  2. Indicate whether to Add the tax code to the Comp rates.

  • Yes: The system adds the tax code to the Comp rates listed above. Typically, you select Yes for unbundled billing rates.

  • No: Select No if the tax code is included in the Comp Rate above. Typically, you select this for bundled amounts.

Note: Note: On bundled billing, the rate decreases when the limit is met for items that are limited. It decreases by the amount of the client’s bill rate of the item.

  1. Indicate whether to stop at high Limit if this tax code stops at prescribed limits.

Note: You cannot set the Limit or Discount Shelter for an ASO billing Template Type to Yes. (An error message displays when you click Save.)

  1. Indicate whether the billing template includes Discount Shelter limits.

  2. Enter the Override Wage Base if there is a wage base override for this tax code. Leave this field blank if the standard wage base applies.

Entering Overrides by State

Use the SUI Billing Wage Base Overrides panel to enter overrides by state.

[Image: screenshot]

To enter overrides by state:

  1. Enter each State Code. The State Name populates.

  2. Enter the taxable Wage Base Override the system should use for SUTA billing calculations for the state.

  3. Enter the overriding FUTA Bill Rate for the state. This overrides the Special FUTA Rate, if any.

Classifying Expense Reimbursement Pay Codes

Use the Taxable Expense panel to classify any expense reimbursement pay codes as taxable pay codes for the purposes of tax billing.

Select each Taxable Expense Reimbursement Pay Code. The Description populates.

Changing Benefit Groups for Multiple Employees

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Bulk-Change-Benefit-Group.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Bulk-Change-Benefit-Group.htm

Changing Benefit Groups for Multiple Employees

To change the benefit group for multiple employees at one time, use the Bulk Change Benefit Group form.

Note: Note: You must create benefit groups at the client level before you can move employees to another benefit group.

To change benefit groups for multiple employees:

  1. On the CLIENT menu, select Client|Action > Bulk Change Benefit Group. The Bulk Change Benefit Group form opens.

  2. To improve the response time for loading results, you can filter the results by benefit group. Click Continue.

To load all results without filtering, do not select a benefit group and click Continue. The load time is longer than normal.

Column — Description

Client ID — The unique identifier for the client.

Employee ID — The unique identifier for the employee.

Employee Name — The name of the employee.

Benefit Group — The benefit group the employee is assigned.

Enrollment Status — A unique code describing the enrollment status. For example, A for active. This value is defined on the Employee Statuses form.

Enrollment Type — A unique code describing the enrollment type. For example, FT for full-time. This value is defined on the Employee Types form.

Position — A unique code describing the position. For example, OPER for operator. This value is defined on the Positions form.

Location — A unique code describing the worksite location. For example, MA for Massachusetts. This value is defined on the Worksite Locations form.

Division — A unique code describing the division. For example, 1 for the First Division. This value is defined on the Divisions form.

Department — A unique code describing the department. For example, 300 for Accounting. This value is defined on the Departments form.

  1. Using the checkmarks, hold the CTRL key and select multiple employees from the list. The employees must be in the same benefit group.

  2. Click Change Benefit Group. The Change Benefit Group dialog box displays.

  3. In Select benefit group, select the benefit group to move the selected employees. The shown benefit groups are existing benefit groups for the client.

  4. In Effective Date, select the date for the change to take effect.

  5. Click Continue. To view a report of the changes, click View Report. You can view and download the report at the time you make changes. You cannot access the report after viewing it the first time. To confirm and close the dialog box, click Done.

Clearing Backup Account Assignments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Clear_All_Backup_Account_Assignments.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Clear_All_Backup_Account_Assignments.htm

Clearing Backup Account Assignments

Use the Clear All Backup Account Assignments form to clear all backup account assignments regardless of which clients are listed in the import file.

Important! This process cannot be reverted.

Note: This form is only available for service providers.

To clear all backup account assignments:

  1. Click Back Office and select System Parameters under System|Change.

  2. Click Process. A message displays, “This will clear all Backup Account Assignments for ALL Clients. Do you wish to continue?” Click Yes to continue.

  3. The clearing process runs. A message displays indicating that all backup account assignments for all clients have been cleared. Click OK.

Note: Note: The backup account assignments no longer display when you select Backup Assignments on the Account tab in the Client Details form. Use the Data Import Tool to import new backup account assignments.

Attaching Files to Client Records

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Client-Documents.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Client-Documents.htm

Attaching Files to Client Records

Use the Client Documents form to attach files to the client record and open any files attached to it. To access the form, open the Actions menu in Client Details select Documents.

To upload a document:

  1. Click Load a Document.

  2. In the Upload a File window, click Choose File.

  3. Navigate to the file that you want to upload, and click Open.

  4. In the Upload a File window, click Submit.

  5. In the successful upload message, click Close.

  6. On the Confirm Document form, Document Name populates with the file name.

  7. To enter any document notes, use the Document Notes option.

  8. Click Accept. The Client Documents form displays.

For a document in the list:

  • Click the Document Name to download the document.

  • Click the [Image: screenshot] next to a document to remove it from the company record.

  • If you uploaded an employee document, use the ESS check box to indicate whether the document is visible in Employee Portal (EP).

Defining Client Access Groups

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Client_Access_Groups.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Client_Access_Groups.htm

Defining Client Access Groups

Client access groups define the clients, cost centers, and sub cost centers a user can access. Use the Client Access Groups form to manage user access to clients, cost centers, and sub cost centers. Access this form in the Back Office menu under System|Change.

Assign a client access group to any service provider in the system. After entering initial setup information (name and ID), you can restrict clients in one of several ways.

Permit and restrict user access to these entities using the panels on this form. Different panels display for different Assignment Method values. Use the Assignment Method panels and procedure that most closely matches your organization’s requirements. For example, if Grant Access to all Clients with exceptions is selected, Restricted Clients, Restricted Cost Centers, and Restricted Sub Cost Centers are visible.

Note: Note: The system includes a feature for grouping clients into cost centers and sub cost centers. For example, you can have one cost center and sub cost center for clients in the Northeast and another for clients in the South. Use these groupings to control client access at a high level.

To do this Perform these steps
Set up a client access group You must define basic information about the group before you can add clients, cost centers, and sub cost centers to a client access group. When you set up PrismHR for the first time, you need to specify a value in the Assignment Method field. After users and client companies are created, return to this screen to set up further restrictions. 1. Enter a Group ID. 2. Enter a descriptive Group Name. 3. Select the Assignment Method to define the group. Different panels display based on the Assignment Method that is selected.
  1. Enter a Group ID.
  2. Enter a descriptive Group Name.
  3. Select the Assignment Method to define the group. Different panels display based on the Assignment Method that is selected. | Grant access to all clients, cost centers, and sub cost centers You can create a client access group with no restrictions, though there is no specific Assignment Method for this option. | - Select Grant access to all Clients with exceptions in the Assignment Method field. Do not assign any clients, cost centers, or sub cost centers. | | Restrict access to clients and cost centers | Use the Restricted Clients and Restricted Cost Centers panels to specify clients that a user cannot access. To restrict access to specified clients and cost centers: 1. Select Grant access to all Clients with exceptions in the Assignment Method field. 2. Enter each Client ID in the Restricted Clients panel. The Client Name displays. 3. Enter each Cost Center ID in the Restricted Cost Centers panel. The Cost Center Name displays. |
  4. Select Grant access to all Clients with exceptions in the Assignment Method field.
  5. Enter each Client ID in the Restricted Clients panel. The Client Name displays.
  6. Enter each Cost Center ID in the Restricted Cost Centers panel. The Cost Center Name displays. | Grant access to specified clients Use the Authorized Clients panel to specify clients that a user can access. The system automatically restricts access to all other clients. | To grant access to specified clients: 1. Select Grant access to specified Clients in the Assignment Method field. 2. Enter each Client ID in the Authorized Clients panel. The Client Name displays. |
  7. Select Grant access to specified Clients in the Assignment Method field.
  8. Enter each Client ID in the Authorized Clients panel. The Client Name displays. | Grant access to specified cost centers and sub cost centers Use the Authorized Cost Center panel to specify cost centers and sub cost centers that a user can access. The system automatically restricts access to all other cost centers and sub cost centers. | To grant access to specified cost centers and sub cost centers: 1. Select Grant access to specified Cost Centers in the Assignment Method field. 2. Enter each Cost Center and Sub Cost Center in the Authorized Cost Center panel. The Cost Center Name and Sub Cost Center Name displays. |
  9. Select Grant access to specified Cost Centers in the Assignment Method field.
  10. Enter each Cost Center and Sub Cost Center in the Authorized Cost Center panel. The Cost Center Name and Sub Cost Center Name displays. | Grant Security Access by Client Assignments Administrators can assign security access to Client Access Groups according to the client assignments made on the Company Account Form. | Select Grant Security Access by Client Assignments in the Assignment Method field to grant the users specified in the Account Assignments fields on the Company Accounts form. | | View and edit existing groups You can view and edit existing client access group data at the same time. | To view an existing client access group: - Enter the Group ID and tab into the next field. The group data populates on the form. If you don’t know the ID, click Group ID to view a complete list. | | Assign a client access group to a user | - Once you create one or more client access groups, you must assign one to every new user. Assign client access groups on the Users form with the Client Access Group field. This is a required step during new user creation. You can also use this field to assign a new client access group to a user. | ========================================================================

Creating Client Categories

Group and sort companies with Client Category Codes.

Creating or deleting a Client Status

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Client_Status_Codes.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Client_Status_Codes.htm

Creating or deleting a Client Status

Use this form to create or delete a client status.

To create or delete a client status:

  1. Click Back Office. Under System|Change, click Client Statuses.

  2. Status Code - Enter an alphabet from one of the following options or click the Status Code link and select an existing status code from the Select Client Status dialog box. To create a new status code, enter the appropriate option.

  • P=Pending

  • I= Inactive

  • C=Client Cancelling (Pre-Termination)

  • T=Terminated

  • A=Active

  1. Status - The status description auto-populates for existing status codes or enter the appropriate one from above while creating a new status code.

  2. Status Class - The status class auto-populates for existing status codes or select the appropriate one from the following drop-down while creating a new status code:

  • Pending - This is the initial status when setting up a client. The client can still be deleted. You cannot process payroll for such a client.

  • Active - Client cannot be deleted if there is payroll history. You can process payroll for such a client.

  • Inactive - Client cannot be deleted. You cannot process payroll for such a client. Once a client is set to Inactive, then the client is removed from superbatch.

  • Terminated - If the client status class is Terminated, enter the number of days to process manual batches in the Term Allow Manual Days field. This field only appears if the status code is set to T. A terminated client cannot be activated.

  • Client Cancelling (Pre-Termination) - Same as Inactive.

  1. Click Save to save the changes.

  2. Click Delete to delete an existing status code.

  3. Click Cancel to clear the form at any time.

Establishing Reason Codes for Client Terminations

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Client_Term_Reasons.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Client_Term_Reasons.htm

Establishing Reason Codes for Client Terminations

You can establish a reason code when terminating a client using the Client Term Reasons form.

To establish a reason code when terminating a client:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. Select Client Term Reasons under System|Change.

  3. Enter or select a Reason Code for terminating a client. If you are creating a new code, enter something brief but meaningful.

  4. Enter a Reason Description for terminating a client. This is the full description.

  5. Select a Valid Status Uses option for terminated clients, inactivated clients, or both.

  6. Enter the Obsolete Date when this code is no longer used.

  7. Click Save.
