Administering PTG Commission Types

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Commission_Period_Lookback.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Commission_Period_Lookback.htm

Administering PTG Commission Types

Use the Commission Period Look-back form to administer Percent Target Amount (PTG) commission types. This form streamlines the process of identifying active clients who had payrolls processed during a specified look-back period but have no corresponding invoice data in a target period and automatically generates the invoice records needed to accurately apply PTG commissions. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To administer PTG commission types and generate invoice records:

  1. Enter or select a mandatory Begin Date and an End Date in the Look Back Period panel.

Note: You cannot enter Look Back Period dates or Target Period dates that contain a gap greater than one year.

  1. Enter or select a mandatory Begin Date and an End Date in the Target Period panel.

  2. Enable Active Clients (only) to limit the assessment to active clients only.

  3. Click Run Process. (The system only enables the Run Process button after completing all date fields.) A message displays, “Are you sure you wish to start the Look-back process at this time?” Click Yes to continue.

  4. A progress report displays on-screen. Click Report to view the report details or Close to return to the Commission Period Look-back form.

  5. The system displays a printable/downloadable report titled Commission Period Look-back Report, which lists all invoices created during this process. (Otherwise, a message displays, “No invoices were Created.”) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following when using the Commission Period Look-back form:

  • Users whose user role is set to FULL for the Commission Period Look-back form can view the form, enter or select dates and use the buttons.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Commission Period Look-back form can view the form, but cannot enter data or use the buttons.

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Commission Period Look-back form cannot access this form.

  • Click Cancel to clear all data on the form.

Creating Commission Structures

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Commission_Plans.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Commission_Plans.htm

Creating Commission Structures

Create complex commission structures that your organization can assign to salespeople at the client level with the Commission Plan Maintenance form.

You can use a commission plan as a template. Organizations that use commissions often have a standard commission program for either all or a subset of its salespeople. Assigning a commission plan code to a salesperson rather than entering individual commission structures saves effort.

Note: After creating a commission plan at the client level, if you make updates to that plan and click Save, the system cannot apply those updates. For example, if you create commission plan A and apply it to client 123, then update commission plan A and save the updates the system displays an error message, “This plan is assigned to a client and changes cannot be made. Either unassign from all clients to make changes or create a new plan.” Click OK to continue.

In addition, existing commission plans already in use at the client level cannot be deleted. For example, if you click the Delete button for a client-level plan and then select Yes an error message displays, “This plan is in use and cannot be deleted.” Click OK to continue.

To create a commission structure, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From Operations|Change, select Commission Plan Maintenance.

  3. Complete these fields as required.

Field Name Description
Commission Plan ID Select a plan ID that represents the commission plan.
Commission Plan Name Enter a name that describes the plan.
Commission Plan Active Select if this commission plan is in use. If you deselect this option, it does not affect currently assigned plans, but it warns users when they review commissions.
Based On Select a value on which to base the commission line. - Gross Wages: Total gross wages of the client payroll invoice. - Admin Fees: Total amount of administrative fees on the client payroll invoice. - Benefit Commission Type: Benefits-based commission for a specific benefit type. You must enter the benefit type code in the Based On Item field. - Benefit Commission Percentage: Percentage based on the benefit list. You must enter the specific group benefit plan ID in the Based On Item field. - Workers Compensation: Total amount of workers’ compensation billed to the client for the payroll period. - Workers Compensation Profit: Checks bill code 005 and computes the profit, and also checks for information entered on losses. - Average Number Lives: Average number of active employees during the commission cycle. - Gross Profit: Sales items minus the direct cost items. The value is shown on the Profitability Report in the backend system. - Tax Profit (001/002/003/004): Sales of tax-based items (FUTA, SUTA, and FICA, as associated with the listed tax bill classes) minus the cost for those tax items. Tax profit is rarely used for commissions because when not passing shelter credits it can often show a loss for the month. - Percent of Bill Code: Fixed percentage for the amount charged on a specific bill code. Enter that in the Based On Item field. - Profits to Admin [Enter Bill Code in Based On]: The system uses the specified Bill Code and then subtracts the cost associated with that Bill Code. That amount (profit or loss) is used in the percent computation. For example, if you choose Bill Code 004 (SUTA) and specify 5% of profits, and there was $1000 in sales and $960 in costs, the payout would be $2.00 ($40.00 x 0.05). - Fixed Per Paid EE [PayFrequency in Based On if needed]: Fixed amount per paid employee. Specify a pay frequency if appropriate (see Based On Item description).
  • Gross Wages: Total gross wages of the client payroll invoice.
  • Admin Fees: Total amount of administrative fees on the client payroll invoice.
  • Benefit Commission Type: Benefits-based commission for a specific benefit type. You must enter the benefit type code in the Based On Item field.
  • Benefit Commission Percentage: Percentage based on the benefit list. You must enter the specific group benefit plan ID in the Based On Item field.
  • Workers Compensation: Total amount of workers’ compensation billed to the client for the payroll period.
  • Workers Compensation Profit: Checks bill code 005 and computes the profit, and also checks for information entered on losses.
  • Average Number Lives: Average number of active employees during the commission cycle.
  • Gross Profit: Sales items minus the direct cost items. The value is shown on the Profitability Report in the backend system.
  • Tax Profit (001/002/003/004): Sales of tax-based items (FUTA, SUTA, and FICA, as associated with the listed tax bill classes) minus the cost for those tax items. Tax profit is rarely used for commissions because when not passing shelter credits it can often show a loss for the month.
  • Percent of Bill Code: Fixed percentage for the amount charged on a specific bill code. Enter that in the Based On Item field.
  • Profits to Admin [Enter Bill Code in Based On]: The system uses the specified Bill Code and then subtracts the cost associated with that Bill Code. That amount (profit or loss) is used in the percent computation. For example, if you choose Bill Code 004 (SUTA) and specify 5% of profits, and there was $1000 in sales and $960 in costs, the payout would be $2.00 ($40.00 x 0.05).
  • Fixed Per Paid EE [PayFrequency in Based On if needed]: Fixed amount per paid employee. Specify a pay frequency if appropriate (see Based On Item description). | Based On Item | Enter the Based On Item that works in conjunction with the Based On value to calculate the commission. If the line is based on benefit type, enter the specific benefit code associated with the plan(s). The system uses benefit plans with this code in the calculation for this commission. (See Assigning a Benefit Commission Code.) If the line is based on gross wages or admin fees, you can also do computations based on the workers’ compensation code on the payroll vouchers. For example: - TX.8810 would specify that the system compute a rate based on TX.8810 wages (for gross wages) or administrative fees (for admin fees). - .8810 would be for all states using 8810 as a code. - .* would be for all workers’ compensation codes. - If all three were entered in that order, then the system would put all Texas 8810 in the first bucket, all 8810 except Texas in the second bucket, and all codes except 8810 in the third bucket. > Note: Note: The order must be correct. If . is the first code, then there would be no other data to allocate to other buckets because all WorkersCode would match this bucket and be assigned. For Fixed Per Paid EE, this field can be a pay frequency (W, B, S, or M) to allow different rates for different pay frequencies since this payment is per regular invoice. |
  • TX.8810 would specify that the system compute a rate based on TX.8810 wages (for gross wages) or administrative fees (for admin fees).
  • *.8810 would be for all states using 8810 as a code.
  • . would be for all workers’ compensation codes.
  • If all three were entered in that order, then the system would put all Texas 8810 in the first bucket, all 8810 except Texas in the second bucket, and all codes except 8810 in the third bucket. | Employee count - low/Employee count - high | Enter the Employee count - low and Employee count - high end values used to calculate this type of commission/rate. For example, if these fields define a range of 0–100 employees and the client has 125 employees, the system does not calculate this commission. The employee count fields are particularly important if the commission is based on the average number of active employees, since the count is used in the calculation itself. | | Flat Or Percent | Indicate whether the commission calculation is a Flat or Percent rate. This works in conjunction with the Commission Rate field. | | Commission Rate | Enter the Commission Rate, which relates to the Flat or Percent field value. If you enter 15.00 in this field, for example, the commission rate is $15.00 for a flat calculation rate or 15% for a percent calculation rate. | | Commission Group | Enter the Commission Group to group the commission line with other commission computations with the same number. Number the groups sequentially (1, 2, 3, and so on). Groups allow the system to test among groups to select either the highest or lowest amount, based on the Commission Group Highest or Lowest field. | | Commission Group Highest Or Lowest | If this is a grouped plan, indicate the amount to use: - Select Highest to use the highest result of the grouped commission computation lines. - Select Lowest to use the lowest result of the grouped commission computation lines. See Grouping Commissions for information on how the system uses commission groups. |
  • Select Highest to use the highest result of the grouped commission computation lines.
  • Select Lowest to use the lowest result of the grouped commission computation lines.
  1. Click Save.

Using Corporate/Staffing Accounting

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Corporate_Accounting.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Corporate_Accounting.htm

Using Corporate/Staffing Accounting

Use the Corporate/Staffing Accounting form to select the accounts to use. For example, the following fields display when you select the accounts to use for Deduction Codes. (The fields that display in this form depend upon the particular account you need to maintain.)

Note: Note: This only applies if your organization is set to use PrismHR as a corporate/staffing product.

To select the accounts to use, complete the fields that display in this form. For example, the following fields must be completed for Deduction Codes:

  1. In the Credit Account field, enter the account to credit with the amount of the deduction. This is usually an accrued liability account.

An amount deducted from an employee’s pay is usually payable to a third party. For example, if deducted as part of a payroll savings plan, the employer is responsible for depositing the deduction to each employee’s savings account. The payroll is a liability on the part of the employer. The account here is credited with any amount deducted from any employee’s pay using the deduction code.

  1. In the Debit Arrears field, enter the G/L account to debit (receivable account for arrearage) with any deduction amount due from an employee that goes into arrears.

  2. In the Credit Arrears field, enter the G/L account to credit when the employee pays the amount held in arrears.

Managing Cost Centers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Cost_Center.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Cost_Center.htm

Managing Cost Centers

Manage cost centers and sub-cost centers with the Cost Centers form. Your organization can use cost centers and sub-cost centers to track different things. For example, some organizations use these to track sales offices, and assign each of their clients to their associated office. Sub-cost centers are not linked to a specific cost center, allowing your organization more flexibility in using this feature.

To access this form:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change, select Cost Centers.

  3. Complete these fields as required:

Field — Description

Cost Center ID — Enter an ID or click this field to search for existing cost centers. - For new cost centers, enter text that is brief but descriptive, such as NE for Northeast. - When searching for an existing cost center, in the Search Cost Centers dialog, select a cost center from the list or enter the Cost Center ID or Cost Center Name in the Refine Search section, then click Refine.

Cost Center Name — Name for the cost center.

Sub-Cost Center — Select if this is a sub-cost center. Note: You can add an Invoice Logo override to a sub-cost center using the Report Print Options form. (See Configuring an Invoice Logo Override for Sub-Cost Centers.)

  1. Click Save.

Using Custom Feature Codes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Custom_Feature_Codes.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Custom_Feature_Codes.htm

Using Custom Feature Codes

Your organization can specify custom feature codes in PrismHR at the system level to customize its behavior for all clients. These are some of the most common feature codes available for you to use; do not implement other custom feature codes unless instructed to do so by the PrismHR Customer Support Team.

Custom Feature Code Type Category Short Description
2019STATUSES Controls when access to 2019 W-4 filing statuses is removed/displayed since users might delay converting to the new form and need to continue accessing these older records. If you activate the 2019STATUSES custom feature code, the following options display in the Federal Tax Filing field on the HR\ Change\ Employee Tax form: - Single or Married, but withhold at higher Single rate - Married If you remove this custom feature code, these options no longer display. However, any employees with one of these settings already configured remains in this status.
- Single or Married, but withhold at higher Single rate
- Married
A/RMASTDBA Global Accounting Updates A/R Master using the Client DBA, not Legal Name.
A/RMASTUPD Global Accounting Updates A/R Master on save of matching Client Master.
ACADATABUILD Global ACA Enables improved performance for building ACA data. See Activating the ACA Data Build for more information.
ACHBREAKONPRBATCH Global ACH Segregates ACH files into separate accounts.
ACHCONSOLMIXED Global ACH Consolidates mixed transactions (DB/CR) even when single type file built.
ACHHARDENFORCE Global ACH When a payroll batch is dated such that ACH cannot be processed, the system stops the posting process rather than displaying a warning and converting ACH payments to checks. ACH causes POST to halt, if batch date fails ACH tests.
ACHNAMEPARSE Global ACH Uses space delimiter between last name and first name. Use this feature code if your bank does not accept child support files that include commas. In the ACH journal for child support, when the last name is shorter than seven characters, the first name will be appended with a space separating it from the last name. (The default behavior is to separate the names with a comma.) The name displays in the ABBREV.NAME field in the ACH journal and comprises exactly ten characters. If the last name includes seven or more characters, there is never a separator. The names are concatenated with neither a space nor a comma.
ACHNOCONSOLIDATE Global ACH Does not ‘Net’ ACH journal transactions for the same employee.
ACHPROCESSLOCK Global ACH During ACH build, checks for pending batches and provides options for dealing with them.
ACHTOMORROW Global ACH Sets ACH Effective Date to tomorrow’s date. This is specifically if your bank does not allow for same-day dated pre-notes, etc. If the field under System Parameters has an N, it uses today’s date but if you add the feature code it overrides that date with tomorrow’s date.
ALLOW-LOCN-BASED-SUI Global Tax Allows location-based SUI accruals. Displays the Location Based SUI panel in Worksite Locations and the Location field in Tax Adjustment Entry. Allows your organization to track SUTA information for your clients by worksite locations.
ALLOW999SSNS Global System Params Allows entry of SSN as 999.
ALLOWALLTAXADJTTO Global Tax Adjustments Allows All Tax Adjustments on Terminated Take on Employees.
ALLOWDUPDEDNS Global Deductions Allows duplicate deduction codes for employees.
ALLOWONESIDEDFICA Global Tax Adjustments Allows one sided FICA tax adjustments for codes 00-11,00-12,00-15,00-16.
ALLOWTANDEMCROSSHIRE Global Onboarding Allows registering employees in the tandem environment.
ALLOWWCLOCCALC Global Workers Comp Allows choice of W/C Work Loc Based option at Company/Job level.
ALLOWWMNEWHIREALTEMP Global Onboarding Allows New Hire Alternate Employers for WS managers. Allows all users of the New Hire form to select one of the alternate employers defined in Client Details instead of the client’s primary employer. This applies to worksite managers and trusted advisors of all clients in the system.
ALLOWWMNEWHIREALTEMP.C Client Onboarding Allows New Hire Alternate Employees for WS managers.
ALLOWWSMWTABDLR Global Time Off Allows processing of backdated Lave Request processing for worksite managers and trusted advisors.
ALLOWZEROSSNS Global System Params Allows SSNs to be 000-00-0000.
ALLPAYCODESINT Global System Params Allows Internal Payroll Users to select from ALL pay codes and deduction codes. By default, users do not see any pay or deduction codes except those specified in the Client Details Control tab. If service providers need to see all codes, then your organization must enable this custom feature code. When you enable this feature code, the following happens: - Service Providers: Hyperlink returns all fixed amount pay codes or deduction codes. If you enter a pay code or deduction code that is not listed in the Client Details Control tab, you can continue. (Note: No error message or warning displays.) - Worksite Managers: Hyperlink returns only fixed amount pay codes or deduction codes listed in the Client Details Control tab. If you enter a pay code or deduction code that is not listed in the Client Details Control tab, the system displays an error message and you cannot continue. When you do not enable this feature code, the following happens: - Service Providers: Hyperlink returns only fixed amount pay codes or deduction codes listed in the Client Details Control tab. If you enter a pay code or deduction code that is not listed in the Client Details Control tab, the system displays a warning and you can continue. (Note: No error message displays.) - Worksite Managers: Hyperlink only returns fixed amount pay codes or deduction codes listed in the Client Details Control tab. If you enter a pay code or deduction code that is not listed in the Client Details Control tab, the system displays an error message and you cannot continue.
- Service Providers: Hyperlink returns all fixed amount pay codes or deduction codes. If you enter a pay code or deduction code that is not listed in the Client Details Control tab, you can continue. (Note: No error message or warning displays.)
- Worksite Managers: Hyperlink returns only fixed amount pay codes or deduction codes listed in the Client Details Control tab. If you enter a pay code or deduction code that is not listed in the Client Details Control tab, the system displays an error message and you cannot continue.
- Service Providers: Hyperlink returns only fixed amount pay codes or deduction codes listed in the Client Details Control tab. If you enter a pay code or deduction code that is not listed in the Client Details Control tab, the system displays a warning and you can continue. (Note: No error message displays.)
- Worksite Managers: Hyperlink only returns fixed amount pay codes or deduction codes listed in the Client Details Control tab. If you enter a pay code or deduction code that is not listed in the Client Details Control tab, the system displays an error message and you cannot continue.

- After entering the account number in the Direct Deposit Information panel, a window opens over the form covering the account number you just entered.

Creating Custom HR Approval Roles

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Custom_HR_Approval_Roles.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Custom_HR_Approval_Roles.htm

Creating Custom HR Approval Roles

Create custom HR approval roles for Account Management (Service Providers) or HR Role (Worksite Managers/Trusted Advisors) with the Custom HR Approval Roles form.

To create a custom approval role:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. Select Custom HR Approval Roles under System|Change.

  3. Create a Role ID and enter a Description.

Custom approval roles are available on the Approval Policies form and the Global Approval Policies form, where you can add the custom A/M Role or HR Role to the appropriate Approval Type. Once you create a new custom HR approval role, you must assign it to a user.

  1. Click Save.

Dashboard

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Dashboard.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Dashboard.htm

Using the Dashboard

The Dashboard provides quick access to company information and relevant features.

[Image: screenshot]

Panels

The Dashboard is organized into the following panels.

Panel Description
Favorites tab Provides links to the pages you have flagged as favorites.
Work Centers tab Categorizes functional areas in your organization and provides links to landing pages where you access the forms for completing a process. See Using Work Centers for details.
Perspective Provides a list where you can view the following graphs of the selected company’s employees. - Employees by Status (the default) - Employees by Location - Employees by Department - Employees by Shift - If you are using Onboarding, you can view the onboarding dashboard by selecting Onboarding Tasks by Status. - If you are using Benefit Enrollments , you can view the Benefits Enrollment dashboard by selecting Benefit Enrollments by Status.
  • Employees by Status (the default)
  • Employees by Location
  • Employees by Department
  • Employees by Shift
  • If you are using Onboarding, you can view the onboarding dashboard by selecting Onboarding Tasks by Status.
  • If you are using Benefit Enrollments , you can view the Benefits Enrollment dashboard by selecting Benefit Enrollments by Status. | Employees | Lists the employees of the selected client or company (shown in the header area). If you have access to multiple companies, click the Client or Company in the header area to search for a different client company. If the entire list of employees does not fit within the panel, you can click View All to display a scroll bar for navigating through the list. If you click the link to an employee, the Employee Details page opens. > Note: Note the following when navigating through this list: - If your client has 1000 or less employee records, after you click View All in the Employees list, a scroll bar displays so you can easily scroll up or down to the employee you want to review. - If your client has more than 1001 or more employee records, after you click View All in the Employees list, pagination controls display so you can easily paginate to the next or previous page. Note: These pagination controls continue to display for an employee status of 1000 or less, if you first page through using these controls for 1001 or more employees. However, if you don’t use the pagination controls, a scroll bar displays for an employee status of 1000 or less instead of pagination controls. |

  • PrismHR launches the PrismHR website.

  • Privacy opens the PrismHR Privacy statement.

  • Version <number> provides access to current and past release notes, PDF, and Excel files, sorted by release/year.

Note: Note: Video help is available on many of these features. Click the video help icon at the top right of the form to watch the video.

Controlling Dashboard Views

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Dashboard_Access.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Dashboard_Access.htm

Controlling Dashboard Views

Use the Dashboard Access form to control which dashboard views are available for clients when they view the At a Glance Dashboard part of the Enhanced Dashboard.

Important! This is a global form whose access can be customized at a global level or at a client level using overrides, and is accessible only for service providers.

To access this form, select Dashboard Access on the Global Configuration form. For example:

[Image: Selecting the Dashboard Access link on the Global Configuration form opens the Dashboard Access form]

Note: By default, the At a Glance view for employees will always display for all users and therefore, it cannot be controlled by this form.

Selected settings on this form control which At a Glance Dashboard views are available for clients on the Enhanced Dashboard on a global level, with the option to override these views at the client level.

Note: Note the following regarding user access to the Dashboard Access form:

  • If the user’s access is set to Inquiry, the link displays on the Global Configuration form but is dimmed (unavailable).

  • If the user’s access is set to Deny, the link does not display on the Global Configuration form.

To set up At a Glance dashboard views for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors:

  1. On the System|Change menu, select Global Configuration.

  2. As a service provider for worksite managers or worksite trusted advisors, select Dashboard Access.

  3. The following panels display where you can control the client’s At a Glance Dashboard views:

Panel Action
Global Access Settings Make selections in this panel based on the options you want to display on a global level when a worksite manager or a worksite trusted advisor views the At a Glance Dashboard. For example, if you only select the Onboarding Tasks and Recent Payrolls options in this panel, only the Employees, Onboarding Tasks, and Recent Payrolls options display in the Employees menu on the At a Glance Dashboard view. (Note: The Employees menu is always enabled for all clients and is therefore not included as a controllable view.) Selecting the Support Contacts option and adding clients in the Support Contacts column displays the Support tab on the Enhanced Dashboard for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors. However, note that the client-level custom feature code HIDE-SUPPORT-TEAM continues to hide the Support tab when you apply it to a client even when the Global Access Setting is enabled. In addition, note the following: - By default, only the Support Contacts option is checked, so if you do not make a selection in this panel or the Client Access Overrides panel, only the Employees menu and the Support Contacts option displays for worksite managers or worksite trusted advisors. - If you make a selection in the Global Access Settings panel but you do not set any overrides in the Client Access Overrides panel, only the Employees menu and the views for the global access settings you select on the Global Configuration form would display for worksite managers or worksite trusted advisors.
  • By default, only the Support Contacts option is checked, so if you do not make a selection in this panel or the Client Access Overrides panel, only the Employees menu and the Support Contacts option displays for worksite managers or worksite trusted advisors.
  • If you make a selection in the Global Access Settings panel but you do not set any overrides in the Client Access Overrides panel, only the Employees menu and the views for the global access settings you select on the Global Configuration form would display for worksite managers or worksite trusted advisors. | Client Access Overrides | Make selections in this panel to override the settings in the Global Access Settings panel. Select Client ID to make a selection from the Select Clients list, then click Done. (By default, all checkboxes are unselected.) Any selections you make for this client provides them with the selected dashboard view and supersedes the settings in the Global Access Settings panel. For example, if you select Onboarding Tasks and Benefit Enrollment Workflows, those options display in the Employees menu on the At a Glance Dashboard view. Adding clients in the Support Contacts column displays the Support tab on the Enhanced Dashboard for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors for those clients. However, note that the client-level custom feature code HIDE-SUPPORT-TEAM continues to hide the Support tab when you apply it to a client even when the Client Access Override Settings are enabled. In addition, note the following: - If you select global access settings and client access overrides, only the Employees menu and the selected views for the client, such as Onboarding Tasks, will display on the At a Glance Dashboard for the logged-in worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor for a client listed in the Client Access Overrides panel. - If you remove settings in the Client Access Overrides panel, the available views revert to the selected global access settings. - Making a change in the Global Access Settings panel does not affect the access settings for clients listed in the Client Access Overrides panel. - When more than 10 data rows display in Client Access Overrides panel, scroll bars display to help you navigate the clients listed in this panel. |
  • If you select global access settings and client access overrides, only the Employees menu and the selected views for the client, such as Onboarding Tasks, will display on the At a Glance Dashboard for the logged-in worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor for a client listed in the Client Access Overrides panel.
  • If you remove settings in the Client Access Overrides panel, the available views revert to the selected global access settings.
  • Making a change in the Global Access Settings panel does not affect the access settings for clients listed in the Client Access Overrides panel.
  • When more than 10 data rows display in Client Access Overrides panel, scroll bars display to help you navigate the clients listed in this panel.
  1. Click Save.

Creating Translation Tables for Deduction Codes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Deduction%20Import%20Translation%20Table.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Deduction Import Translation Table.htm

Creating Translation Tables for Deduction Codes

Use this form to create translation tables for deduction codes that are not set up in PrismHR (Foreign Code) and map them to the codes that are set up in the PrismHR system.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, click Back Office, then select Deduction Import Translation Table from the System|Change menu.

To create a deduction import translation table:

  1. Click the Client ID link and select the client for the translation table.

  2. In Foreign Code, enter a code that is not recognized in PrismHR and the click the Deduction Code link and select the code to which it should be mapped.

  3. To create a blank row for adding another Foreign Code, click +. You can delete a row by clicking x.

  4. When the table is complete, click Save.

Maintaining Global Deduction Codes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Deduction_Codes.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Deduction_Codes.htm

Maintaining Global Deduction Codes

Use the Deduction Codes form to maintain global deduction codes. There are four main panels on this form (five if the deduction is marked Voluntary):

  • Deduction Codes: Set basic information about the code, such as a description, its calculation method, and whether it prints on employee pay stubs

  • Voluntary Classifications: This panel only displays if the deduction is set to Voluntary. Select the type of voluntary deduction on this panel.

  • Maximums: Set the maximum amount to be deducted from an employee’s check during a specified period.

  • Limits: Set payroll batch limits for this deduction code.

  • Other Processing Parameters: Miscellaneous settings specific to different circumstances. See the table for information about each field.

Viewing and Editing Existing Deduction Codes

You can view or edit deduction code information on the Deduction Codes form. Enter or select the Deduction Code you want to view. The form populates with the relevant information.

Note: Note: When making edits to an existing deduction code, be aware that you can cause issues with any existing records that use the deduction code.

Creating a New Deduction Code

Setting Up Basic Deduction Code Information

Select the parameters that define the new code in the Deduction Codes panel.

To set up basic deduction code information, do the following:

  1. Enter or select the code in the Deduction Code field. (When creating a deduction code, use something brief but descriptive, such as LIFE for life insurance.) If you select this field, a selector form displays where you can search for a specific deduction code or its description or select a code from the list that displays. When this form opens, the description, deduction type, and obsolete date display.

To filter the search further:

  • Select a Deduction Type (the default is All, see below).

  • To display only obsolete codes, select Yes in the Obsolete field (the default is No). (Note: Codes with an obsolete date earlier than the current date do not display in the selector form.)

To refresh the list, select Reset Search and Filters.

  1. Enter a more detailed Description of the deduction code.

  2. Select the Deduction Type.

Important! Some deduction types and calculation methods are not compatible with each other. If you make an incompatible selection, the system displays a validation message. For example, if you first select a deduction type and then make a calculation method selection that is incompatible with the deduction type, the following message displays, “That method is invalid for this Deduction Type.” (The reverse applies if you first select a calculation method.) The message includes a warning that changing an existing deduction type or a calculation method may adversely affect any employee records that have already been setup. (If you are unsure whether or not to continue, check with your local system administrator or contact PrismHR Customer Support.)

Deduction Type — Description

Voluntary — Select for an employee-authorized deduction that does not fall under a more specific deduction type. Note: the Voluntary Classifications panel displays.

Section 125 Plan — Select for fixed-amount deductions associated with an employer’s Section 125, or cafeteria, benefit plan. (These plans allow employees to use pretax contributions for eligible benefits.)

Post Tax Benefit — Select for fixed-amount deductions associated with benefits that are handled as post-tax deductions.

Flexible Spending Account — Select for fixed-amount deductions for employee FSA contributions. (FSAs can be used for eligible expenses, such as medical, dental, vision, or dependent care expenses.)

Wage Garnishment — Select for deductions that withhold part of an employee’s earnings to satisfy a garnishment order.

Employee Loan Payment — Select for fixed-amount payroll deductions used to repay an employee loan.

Pre-Tax Retirement Contribution — Select for retirement plan deduction codes that reduce taxable earnings before payroll taxes are calculated.

Catch-Up Retirement Contribution — Select for retirement plan deduction codes that record an employee’s catch-up contribution.

Post-Tax Retirement Contribution — Select for retirement plan deduction codes that record an employee’s post-tax contribution.

Retirement Plan Loan Payment — Select for retirement plan deduction codes that record employee repayments for a retirement plan loan.

Roth 401(k) Contribution — Select for retirement plan deduction codes that record employee Roth 401(k) contributions made post-tax.

Roth 401(k) Catch-Up Contribution — Select for retirement plan deduction codes that record employee Roth catch-up contributions.

For proper reporting on W2 forms, do not set up Roth retirement contributions using the Post-Tax Retirement Contribution deduction type.

Note: A warning displays if you try to update the Deduction Type for an existing Deduction Code, which results in the following after clicking OK and saving the record:

  • You cannot delete or update a Deduction Type after the system processes an updated Deduction Code through a complete payroll process.

  • A tool tip displays next to the Deduction Type field, “This deduction has already been applied to a payroll voucher. The type can no longer be adjusted and the code can no longer be deleted.”

  • The Deduction Type field and Delete button are disabled.

  1. Select the Calculation Method used to calculate the payroll deduction amount for this deduction code. For example, you can use the % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes option to associate a non-qualified deferred compensation (NQDC) plan that the client set up with another company, where a percentage of the commissions is deferred, reducing taxable earnings. (This deduction code functions similar to a pre-tax deduction.)

Deduction Type — Description

Fixed Amount — Select for deduction codes that deduct a specific amount from an employee’s pay.

Rate X Hours Worked — Select for deduction codes that calculate the deduction amount by multiplying a rate by the employee’s hours worked.

Garnishment — Select for deduction codes that calculate and withhold employee earnings for a garnishment order.

Retirement Plan — Select for deduction codes that calculate retirement-related deductions, including retirement contributions and retirement plan loan payments.

% of Gross Pay — Select for deduction codes that calculate the deduction as a percentage of the employee’s gross pay.

% of Gross Earnings — Select for deduction codes that calculate the deduction as a percentage of the employee’s gross earnings.

% of Straight Pay — Select for deduction codes that calculate the deduction as a percentage of straight-time pay.

% of Pay Rate — Select for deduction codes that calculate the deduction using a percentage of the employee’s hourly pay rate.

% of Pay Rate (Rounded to nearest dollar) — Select for deduction codes that calculate a percentage of the employee’s hourly pay rate and round the result to the nearest dollar.

% of Prior Month Pay Rate (Rounded to nearest dollar) — Select for deduction codes that calculate a percentage using the employee’s prior-month pay rate from payroll history and round the result to the nearest dollar.

% of Retirement Earnings — Select for deduction codes that calculate a retirement-related deduction as a percentage of the employee’s retirement-eligible earnings.

% of Gross Earnings (less Deductions) — Select for deduction codes that calculate a percentage of gross earnings after subtracting selected deductions.

% of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types) — Select for deduction codes that calculate a percentage of gross earnings after subtracting deductions from selected deduction types.

% of Earnings — Select for deduction codes that calculate the deduction as a percentage of selected employee earnings.

% of Earnings with Included Pay Codes — Select for deduction codes that calculate a percentage of earnings from selected pay codes.

Rate X Certified Job Hours Worked — Select for deduction codes that calculate the deduction by multiplying a rate by the employee’s hours worked on a certified job.

Rate X Hours Paid — Select for deduction codes that calculate deductions based on hours paid for selected pay codes.

% of Certified Job Earnings — Select for deduction codes that calculate a percentage of earnings associated with certified job work.

Union Dues Table — Select for deduction codes that calculate union dues using the rules defined for the employee’s labor union.

Ohio JEDD Tax — Select when a deduction code must calculate Ohio local tax for wages associated with a Joint Economic Development District.

Ohio SERS — Select for deduction codes that calculate employee retirement contributions for the Ohio School Employees Retirement System.

Rate by Union Job Hours — Select for deduction codes that calculate an amount from a rate and the employee’s union job hours.

Rate by Union Project Hours — Select for deduction codes that calculate an amount from a rate and the employee’s union project hours.

Sum of Union Fringe — Select for deduction codes that calculate the deduction from the total of applicable union fringe benefit amounts.

In/Out Deduction — Select or deduction codes that calculate the deduction using the associated in/out pay code setup.

Rate X Hours Paid (Selected Pay Codes) — Select for deduction codes that calculate deductions from hours paid for selected pay codes.

Rate Table Lookup — Select for deduction codes that calculate benefit plan deductions using a defined rate table.

Per Ten-Thousand Gross Pay — Select or deduction codes that calculate an amount for each $10,000 of an employee’s gross pay.

Per Ten-Thousand Gross Earnings — Select for deduction codes that calculate an amount for each $10,000 of an employee’s gross earnings.

Per Ten-Thousand Gross Straight Pay — Select for deduction codes that calculate an amount for each $10,000 of an employee’s straight pay.

Per Ten-Thousand Gross Retirement Pay — Select for deduction codes that calculate an amount for each $10,000 of an employee’s retirement pay.

Note: Note the following when using % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes:

  • You must set the Deduction Type to either Voluntary or Pre-Tax Retirement Contribution. (If you select another option, an error message displays.)

  • The Pay Codes panel displays when you select % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes. You must enter or select at least one pay code or an error message displays when you click Save.

  • Setting a deduction code with a calculation method of % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes and enabling the Voluntary deduction type deducts the amount applied to the pay code and treats the deduction as pre-tax when you enable 409(a) Retirement in the Voluntary Classifications panel.

  • Setting a deduction code with a calculation method of % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes and enabling the Voluntary deduction type deducts the amount applied to the pay code and treats the deduction as post-tax when you do not enable when you enable 409(a) Retirement in the Voluntary Classifications panel.

  • The onlyVoluntary Classifications you can enable with the % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes option is 409(a) Retirement. (If you select another option, an error message displays.)

  1. Enter the Pay Stub Name, which is a brief description that prints on pay stubs and certain reports.

Optional Settings

If necessary, you can also set up other basic deduction settings in this panel:

Field — Description

Mandatory — Select this option if this deduction code is for goods and services that are a mandatory part of employment.

Print on Paystub — Select whether or not you want this code to display on employee pay stubs.

Third Party Required — Voluntary deductions only. Select this option if this deduction must have a Third Party Payee associated with it. You can set this at the client level. See Maintaining Third Party Payees Vendor Information for more information.

To Arrears — Voluntary deductions only. Select this option if the deduction can go into arrears when the employee does not have enough pay to cover it.

Obsolete Date — The date after which this deduction code is no longer in effect.

Rate X Hours Paid (Selected Pay Codes)

If the Calculation Method is set to Rate X Hours Paid (Selected Pay Codes), use the RPS Pay Codes panel to select the pay codes. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Enter each applicable Pay Code in the table.

% of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types)

If the Calculation Method is set to % of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types), use the Exclude Ded. Type Code panel to exclude pre-tax benefit deduction types for plans that require contributions to be calculated as a percentage of gross earnings, such as COPERA. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following when using % of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types):

  • You can select one or more deduction type codes to exclude. However, you must select at least one deduction type code.

  • You must set the Deduction Type field to Voluntary or Pre-Tax Retirement Contribution.

  • You can enable the 403(b) Retirement option and select multiple voluntary classifications in the Voluntary Classifications panel. However, observe the following when making these selections:

  • You cannot enable more than one “retirement” voluntary classification.

  • You cannot enable bothSection 125 and Section 132.

  • If there are no matching Deduction Types, the system calculates the deduction on full gross earnings.

  • Selecting a deduction code with % of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types) and for all excluded Deduction Types ensures payroll processing subtracts the sum of all matching deduction amounts from gross earnings before calculating the deduction.

  • A deduction code set to % of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types) and a Deduction Type set to Voluntary excludes the deduction amount and treats the deduction code amount as pre-tax when you enableVoluntary Classification 409(a).

  • A deduction code set to % of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types) and a Deduction Type set to Voluntary excludes the deduction amount and treats the deduction code amount as post-tax when you do not enable Voluntary Classification 409(a).

Selecting Voluntary Classifications

The Voluntary Classifications panel only displays if the Deduction Type is Voluntary. Select any options that correspond to the type of voluntary deduction.

Note: Note: Selecting both of the Section 125 and Health Savings Account fields causes a double-shelter of the deduction amount. Only select one of these fields since each performs the same function.

  • Section 125: This deduction is part of client-sponsored Section 125 plans.

  • 401(k) Retirement: This deduction is for client-sponsored 401(k) retirement plans.

  • 457 Retirement: This deduction is for contributions to a supplemental retirement plan.

  • FSA Dependent Care: This deduction is for flexible spending dependent care plans.

  • 401(k) Catch-Up: This deduction is for 401(k) catch-up contributions.

  • 409(a) Retirement: This is for deducting contributions to a 409(a) deferred compensation plan.

  • Health Savings Account: This deduction is for client-sponsored Health Savings Accounts.

  • 414h Retirement: This deduction is for contributions to a 414h tax-deferred government retirement plan.

  • Group Medical: This deduction is for client-sponsored medical plans.

  • Section 132: This deduction is for client-sponsored transportation plans.

  • 403(b) Retirement:This deduction is to support a 403(b) tax-sheltered annuity plan. The deduction amount will be exempt from Federal Withholding and resident State Withholding.

Configuring Maximums and Limits

If necessary, use the Maximums and Limits panels to establish the maximum deduction amounts and the deduction limits for this deduction code.

Setting up Maximums

You can define monthly, quarterly, and annual maximums. Payroll automatically tracks the amount deducted from an employee’s pay during the period and stops making the payroll deductions once the maximum is reached. Enter maximums only when the maximum amounts apply to most employees.

To set up deduction maximums, do the following:

  1. Set the time period in the Basis field.

  2. Enter the Maximum amount that the system will deduct during the selected Basis. You can define maximum amounts for a specific employee on the employee’s Payroll Deduction form, which overrides the amount in this field.

Setting up Limits

You can define limits for the deduction. Since PrismHR only checks limits during batch payroll processing (as opposed to when you enter an online pay check), you can specify only pay periods supported during batch payroll processing. Enter limits only when the limit amounts apply to most employees.

Note: Note: The payroll period used as the basis for defining a limit displays in the Cd and Period fields.

To set up deduction limits, do the following:

  1. Enter the deduction’s Limit amount for the payroll period.

The value in the Limit field defines the maximum amount that PrismHR can deduct for this code during a payroll period. You can also define limits for a specific employee on the employee’s Payroll Deduction form, which overrides the value of this field.

Configuring Other Specific Deduction Options

The Other Processing Parameters panel establishes additional deduction code parameters. When you finish, click Save.

Field Description
Default Amount This value varies depending on the Calculation Method. It can be an amount, a percentage, or an hourly rate. The value entered here displays when you set up the employee’s deduction form. For any employee, you can override the value on that form. If you leave this field blank, you must set it at the employee level.
Default Periods Enter the Default Periods when the system should make this deduction; this displays when you set up each employee’s deduction form. You can override the default period on the employee form. Define up to five deduction periods, each one represented by a single digit corresponding to the deduction period. - To process the deduction in the second period, enter 2. - For multiple period deductions, enter multiple digits with no spaces; to process the deduction in periods two and four, type 24. - For deductions that should be made on every pay check, enter 12345. The frequency with which you pay your employees determines the length of these deduction periods. For employees paid on a weekly basis, the PrismHR Customer Support Team recommends that you make each week of the month a separate deduction period (deduction period one corresponds to week 1, deduction period two to week 2, and so on).
  • To process the deduction in the second period, enter 2.
  • For multiple period deductions, enter multiple digits with no spaces; to process the deduction in periods two and four, type 24.
  • For deductions that should be made on every pay check, enter 12345. | Union Related | Display this deduction as a default on Union Codes. | | Certified Description | Enter a description to display on a Certified Payroll Report. The report summarizes all deduction codes with the same description. | | Time Sheet Heading | This appears on the Fax Back time sheet. | | Allow Desc Override | Select to allow users to override this deduction description at the company level. Use this field to prevent codes from being misused, allowing specific variable codes. | | KPERS Contribution | Select if this deduction is for contributions to the Kansas Public Employees Retirement System | | MTRB Contribution | Select if this deduction is for contributions to the Massachusetts Teachers Retirement Board | | “In” Pay Code | Enter the “In Pay Code” to display on reports for vacation, holiday, and union dues. | | Match Percent | If there is a match for this deduction, enter the percentage here. | | Match Description | If there is a match for this deduction, enter the description. If you do not enter a description, the system uses the deduction code. | | Form W2 Box | Select the box in which this deduction prints. | | Form W2 Code | Select the code that should precede the amount in Box 12 of Form W-2. | | Other | If you selected Allow Other Codes from the Form W-2 Code drop-down, enter the code here. | | Job Rate Bill Code | Enter the Job Rate Bill Code deduction code. The system uses Job Rate Bill Code only if this deduction code is billed on a Job Rate client. If you leave this field blank, no bill reduction occurs for the deduction. | | Rebate Bill Code | Enter the Rebate Bill Code this deduction uses to reduce a company’s bill amounts, if applicable. Deductions from employee checks can reduce the amount that the company owes for a check run. Your organization would typically use client rebate bill codes on items such as client loan repayments or client-sponsored benefit plans. Leave this field blank if the deduction is for a PEO-paid benefit or tax. | ========================================================================

Defining the Worksite Manager/Trusted Advisor Proxy Role for Service Providers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Defining_Worksite_Manager_Proxy_Users.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Defining_Worksite_Manager_Proxy_Users.htm

Defining the Worksite Manager/Trusted Advisor Proxy Role for Service Providers

You can enable the Worksite Manager/Trusted Advisor Proxy account manager role for service providers, so they can proxy into the system as a worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor. (This role allows them to validate and troubleshoot user access).

Important! Do not enable the Activate User Administration Security field on the Global Configuration form unless you have already assigned the Service Provider User Administrator and Worksite User Administrator roles. This setting restricts user account access to service providers with user administrator roles. If you enable this field before assigning any roles, all users will be prevented from assigning the roles to user accounts.

To enable the Worksite Manager/Trusted Advisor Proxy account manager role:

  1. Select Users on the System|Change menu.

  2. Enter or select the User ID.

  3. Select Worksite Manager/Trusted Advisor Proxy in the Account Management Roles panel.

  4. Click Save.

After you enable the Worksite Manager/Trusted Advisor Proxy role, the Worksite Manager Proxy option displays on the Actions menu for worksite managers or worksite trusted advisors user records. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following when using the Worksite Manager/Trusted Advisor Proxy role:

  • The Service Provider User Administrator account manager role grants access to service provider user types on the Users form.

  • The Worksite User Administrator account manager role grants access to worksite manager/worksite trusted advisor user types on the Users form. Therefore, if the service provider has both roles, they will be the same as if the Activate User Administration Security field is not enabled. If the service provider only has the Service Provider User Administrator account manager role, they can only access service provider user records. If the service provider only has the Worksite User Administrator account manager role, they can only access worksite manager/worksite trusted advisor/worksite employee user records.

  • The system automatically uses hex color #82E910 as the background color for the Worksite Manager/Trusted Advisor Proxy role. However, you can override this color at the global level by entering a color name or Hex color code in the Custom Background Color (Worksite Manager Proxy Session) field in the Global Configuration form.

Defining Delivery Methods

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Delivery_Methods.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Delivery_Methods.htm

Defining Delivery Methods

Use the Delivery Methods form to define methods that users can select for shipping clients’ payrolls. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To define delivery method for shipping:

  1. Enter the Code for the delivery method. If you are creating a new code, use something brief but descriptive, for example, USPS or FEDX.

  2. Enter the Method description, which is usually the name for the service (for example, US Postal Service or FedEx).

  3. Enter the Days In Transit, which is the delivery method’s number of days in transit.

  4. Enter the Bill Event Code, which is the ID of the billing event that the system uses to track this delivery method. If there is no charge for the delivery method, leave this field blank.

  5. Select Create Spec Sheet to indicate that a special sheet will print during payroll processing. Do not select this option if a special sheet is not necessary.

  6. If a special sheet will print:

a. Enter the Special Message that prints on the sheet.
b. Enter the Name that should appear on the sheet.
— —
c. Enter the Address to print on the sheet.
— —
d. Enter the City, State, Zip Code to print on the sheet.
— —
  1. Select the Delivery Sheet Format, which ensures that the address on the printed delivery sheet displays in the window envelopes your organization uses. You can select one of the following:

  • The Standard and Expanded options display no line or indent adjustment fields when selected, and the delivery sheet prints the entered data in a fixed position.

  • The Large Window, Large Window (Expanded), Large Window - 1 Page, and Large Window - 1 Page (Expanded) options display adjustment fields for Delivery Sheet Address Line and Deliver Sheet Address Indent. The delivery sheet prints the entered data using these specified adjustments.

  • The 2 Window, 2 Window (Expanded), 2 Window - 1 Page, and 2 Window - 1 Page (Expanded) options display adjustment fields for Delivery Sheet Address Line, Deliver Sheet Address Indent, Client Information Line, and Client Information Indent. The delivery sheet prints the entered data using the specified adjustments.

  • The 2 Window (Shipping on Page 2) and 2 Window (Expanded) (Shipping on Page 2) options, in addition to the adjustment fields described above, print the address on the first piece of paper and the Special Message on the second sheet. The purpose is that the person who is preparing the envelopes can insert the address into the envelope and then read the instructions on the second page (what type of envelope to use, which mail bin to place the envelope in, and so on).

Note: If you select one of the 2 Window formats, you must enter the full address.

  1. Click Save.

After changing these settings, you can rerun the delivery sheet report from the Payroll Summary form, if needed.

Configuring Direct Pay Entries

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Direct_Pay_Entry_Configuration.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Direct_Pay_Entry_Configuration.htm

Configuring Direct Pay Entries

Use the Direct Pay Entry Configuration form to configure the payroll data file’s specifics into a .csv file that you can later import using the Direct Pay Entry form, which the system applies to the specified payroll.

Note: The Direct Pay Entry Configuration form is only available for service providers.

To configure the payroll data file:

  1. Select Direct Pay Entry Configuration on the System|Change menu.

  2. Complete the following information:

Field — Description

Payroll Cutoff Time — Enter the time when the payroll for the current period must be entered.

Manual Payroll Pay Date Logic — Select the appropriate option if the time needs to be added to a manual payroll. (The system uses this date to determine if a manual payroll is needed.)

Pay Period Lookback — Enter the Pay Period Lookback to include up to 10 pay periods before the current pay date (the default is 3 pay periods).

  1. Define the rules to apply a Payroll Option Template to the manual payroll:

  • Client ID: Enter or select the client’s ID. The Client Name automatically displays.

  • Position Code: Enter or select the position code for the client.

  • Garnishments: Select an option to include garnishments.

  • Benefits: Select an option to include benefits.

  • Hrs/Units Less Than: The system compares the number of hours being imported against the number entered in this field. If the hours are less than or equal to that number, the system applies the template.

  • Template ID: Enter or select the ID of the template.

  1. Click Save.

Note: To import the payroll data file, see Processing Direct Pay Entries.

Maintaining Employee Statuses

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Employee_Status.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Employee_Status.htm

Maintaining Employee Statuses

You can maintain employee status codes and define how the employee’s status affects various pay functions using the Employee Status form. Statuses indicate whether an employee is active, on leave, or terminated.

To maintain employee status information, do the following:

  1. Click the Back Office menu and select Employee Statuses from the System|Change menu.

  2. Complete the following fields:

Field — Description

Employee Status Code — Enter the one- or two-character Employee Status Code, for example, A for active or L for on leave.

Full Description — Enter a Full Description of this employee status code, for example, Active or Leave of Absence.

Abbreviated Description — Enter an Abbreviated Description of this employee status code, for example, Act or Leave.

Status Classification — Select the Status Classification for this employee status code.

Allowed Action Codes — For the Allowed Action Codes, select each of the Allowed HR Actions. When users perform those associated human resource actions, this status is available. For example, if you want to allow terminated employees to be rehired, select Rehire for a Terminated employee status. Users can enter terminated employees in the Rehire form. If you do not select Rehire for Active or On Leave employee statuses, then only terminated employees can be rehired.

Suppress Auto Pay — Select Suppress Auto Pay to suppress the automatic creation of time sheets or other payments for employees with this employment status.

Suppress Time Sheets — Using the Suppress Time Sheets drop-down, indicate whether to suppress the selection of time sheets for payment for employees with this employment status, or to display a warning before allowing users to proceed.

Suppress Other Pay — Select Suppress Other Pay to suppress the other payments to employees with this employment status.

Obsolete — Select Obsolete if this employee status code is no longer used. If you do not want this status to be available in HR action forms, you must also remove the Allowed Action Codes.

Selectable By Service Provider Only — Select Selectable By Service Provider Only to hide the Employee Status Code from Worksite Managers.

Skip EE Eligibility Test — For the Skip EE Eligibility Test option, when the benefit rule calculates eligibility based on the status date and an employee changes eligibility statuses, the Skip EE Eligibility Test option calculates eligibility based on their original status date. For employees with leave of absence statuses due to COVID‑19, this option calculates the correct open enrollment Benefit Effective Date.

  1. Click Save.

Establishing Employee Types

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Employee_Types.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Employee_Types.htm

Establishing Employee Types

You can establish employee types in PrismHR that are used to define employee employment type, such as full time or part time, using the Employee Type form.

To establish employee type information, do the following:

  1. Click the Back Office menu and select Employee Types from the System|Change menu.

  2. Complete the following fields:

Field Description
Employee Type Enter or select the one- or two-character Employee Type that represents the employee type; for example, F for full-time or P for part-time.
Full Description Enter a Full Description of the employee type, for example, Full-Time Employee or Part-Time Seasonal.
Abbreviated Description Enter an Abbreviated Description of the employee type, for example, Full or Season.
Type Classification Select the employee Type Classification.
Tax Exemption This field is optional. You can enable a specified form of income tax suppression for the selected Employee Type instead of setting income tax suppression at an employee level. You can select one of the following options: - –Select One– - No income tax suppression happens for the selected Employee Type. - Suppress All But Federal Income Tax - All income tax except Federal Income Tax is suppressed for the selected Employee Type. - Suppress All But State Income Tax - All income tax except State Income Tax is suppressed for the selected Employee Type. > Note: Note: This Tax Exemption field has field level security. It is set to DENY by default. You can add this field to a user role and set it to Enable, Disable or Hidden. - Enable - This field setting allows you to make changes. - Disable - This field setting allows you to see the data in the field but not change the data. - Hidden - This field setting will not display this Tax Exemption field on the Employee Types form for you.
  • –Select One– - No income tax suppression happens for the selected Employee Type.
  • Suppress All But Federal Income Tax - All income tax except Federal Income Tax is suppressed for the selected Employee Type.
  • Suppress All But State Income Tax - All income tax except State Income Tax is suppressed for the selected Employee Type.
  • Enable - This field setting allows you to make changes.
  • Disable - This field setting allows you to see the data in the field but not change the data.
  • Hidden - This field setting will not display this Tax Exemption field on the Employee Types form for you. | Allowed Action Codes | For the Allowed Action Codes, select the Allowed H/R Actions, which are the human resource actions that users can take when an employee has this status. For example, you might not want to allow users to enter an extended leave of absence for part-time seasonal employees. | | Seasonal | Select Seasonal if this is a seasonal employee type. Some states use this information for quarterly tax reporting. Note: If you select Statutory Employee, there will be a check mark in the Statutory Employee checkbox on Form W-2. | | Statutory Employee | Select Statutory Employee if this employee type is for statutory employees as defined by the IRS. | | Eligible For On-line Benefit Enrollment | Select Eligible For On-line Benefit Enrollment if this employee type can use Benefits Enrollment. | | Auto Term Ineligible Benefits | Select Auto Term Ineligible Benefits if the system should cancel ineligible benefits when employees of this type are terminated. | | Auto Enroll Eligible Benefits | Select Auto Enroll Eligible Benefits to automatically enroll employees of this type in eligible benefit plans and in time off. | | Obsolete | Select Obsolete if this employee type code is no longer used. | | Selectable By Service Provider Only | Select Selectable By Service Provider Only if you want to hide the Employee Type field from users with the Worksite Manager or Worksite Trusted Advisor user role in any form that requires an employee type. |

  1. Click Save to save the changes made on this form.

  2. Click Delete to delete an employee type.

  3. Click Cancel to clear this form at any time. Any unsaved changes will be lost.

Using the Enhanced Dashboard

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Enhanced_Dashboard.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Enhanced_Dashboard.htm

Using the Enhanced Dashboard

The Enhanced Dashboard provides quick access to company information, favorite forms, and work centers from a central location.

The Enhanced Dashboard includes the following helpful features:

  • The employee filters are consolidated for easier use and have additional filters by Status to produce a targeted list of employees.

  • The Benefit Plans view displays plans offered at the client level, along with an Employee Benefit Enrollment dashboard to help you manage enrollments.

  • Service providers and worksite managers can use the Recent Payrolls option to view a list of recent payrolls, along with the files and reports associated with each payroll.

To access the Enhanced Dashboard, click Client, select Client|Dashboard, and then select Enhanced Dashboard.

[Image: Enhanced Dashboard form, showing the Favorites and Work Centers sidebar and the ‘At a Glance’ data visualization panel.]

Note: Before you use the Enhanced Dashboard, you must enable the dashboard using the Global Configuration form (see Setting Global Configuration). In addition, the User Role assigned to the user must be granted access to the Enhanced Dashboard using the User Roles form (see Defining User Roles).

Working in the Dashboard

The Enhanced Dashboard is organized into the following tabs, panel, and data table.

Attribute Description
Favorites tab Links to forms that have been added to the user’s favorites display in this tab (see Designating Favorites).
Work Centers tab Links to various Work Center forms display in this tab (see Work Centers).
At a Glance panel This panel is used to review information about employees, benefits, payrolls, and onboardings. Select an option in the first drop-down to display information about the selection in the graph and/or data table. Some options allow for additional selections to be made using additional drop-downs or a search bar, which can be used to further customize the type of information that displays. The following options are available in the first drop-down: - Benefit Enrollment Workflows: This option is used to view information about active benefit enrollment workflows, such as the status of each workflow and a list of employees who have an active workflow (see Benefit Enrollment Workflows). - Benefit Plans: This option is used to view information about benefit plans, such as the insurance carrier associated with each plan and the number of employees enrolled in each plan (see Viewing Benefit Plans). - Employee Benefit Enrollments: This option is used to view a list of employees along with their benefits information and the benefit plans in which employees are enrolled (see Viewing Employee Benefit Enrollments). - Employees: This option is used to view a list of employees along with basic employment information, such as their position and hire date (see Viewing Employees). - Onboarding Tasks:This option is used to view information about active onboarding workflows, such as the status of each workflow and which forms in the workflow remain outstanding (see Onboarding Tasks). - Recent Payrolls: This option is used to view a list of recent payrolls as well as the files and reports associated with each payroll (see Viewing Recent Payrolls). > Note: Note: If the user navigates to another form, the last selection that was made in the first drop-down is retained when the Enhanced Dashboard is next accessed.
  • Benefit Enrollment Workflows: This option is used to view information about active benefit enrollment workflows, such as the status of each workflow and a list of employees who have an active workflow (see Benefit Enrollment Workflows).
  • Benefit Plans: This option is used to view information about benefit plans, such as the insurance carrier associated with each plan and the number of employees enrolled in each plan (see Viewing Benefit Plans).
  • Employee Benefit Enrollments: This option is used to view a list of employees along with their benefits information and the benefit plans in which employees are enrolled (see Viewing Employee Benefit Enrollments).
  • Employees: This option is used to view a list of employees along with basic employment information, such as their position and hire date (see Viewing Employees).
  • Onboarding Tasks:This option is used to view information about active onboarding workflows, such as the status of each workflow and which forms in the workflow remain outstanding (see Onboarding Tasks).
  • Recent Payrolls: This option is used to view a list of recent payrolls as well as the files and reports associated with each payroll (see Viewing Recent Payrolls). ## Menu Bar

The menu bar near the top of the page provides access to menus and other features.

Feature — Description
