Viewing Benefit Plans

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Enhanced_Dashboard_BenefitPlans.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Enhanced_Dashboard_BenefitPlans.htm

Viewing Benefit Plans

When you select Benefit Plans in the primary drop-down menu of the At a Glance panel, you can select:

  • All Offer Types in the secondary drop-down menu to display a chart that indicates the number of plans by offer type, and a list of data containing all plans. See All Offer Types for more information.

  • A single offer type in the secondary drop-down menu to display a chart that indicates the annual contributions for each plan for the selected offer type, and a list of data containing only the plans for the selected offer type. When selecting a single offer type, the system lists the Medical (MED), Dental (DEN), and Vision (VIS) offer types first in the secondary drop-down, and then lists all other offer types in alphabetical order. See Specific Offer Types for more information.

Benefit Plans - All Offer Types

When you select All Offer Types, the system displays a chart and a search bar above the plans data list. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Chart for Benefit Plans - All Offer Types

The chart illustrates the number of plans by offer type for all of the offer types for the indicated client. For example, you can quickly review the chart to determine how many plans exist for the Dental offer type and compare that number to the total number of plans in the Medical offer type. The chart illustrates the number of plans on the Y-axis by the offer types on the X-axis for the selected company. Each bar in the chart corresponds to an offer type and the number of plans for that offer type. The system color codes each bar in the chart. The color codes for each type correspond to the color codes in the data list.

Using the Plan Search Option

Use the search option to search the list of all plans. Enter a keyword to find one or more plans.

[Image: At a Glance search box to search for a plan ID or description.]

After entering part of a plan ID or plan description and pressing Enter, the data list re-displays all plans that match that criteria.

The system sorts the search results in the data list alphabetically.

Data List for Benefit Plans All Offer Types

The Benefit Plans All Offer Types At a Glance panel displays a list of data that contains information associated with each plan. The following table outlines the data that displays in the list.

Column — Description

(Color Codes) — This column indicates a colored dot that the system uses to color code the offer type. The color of each dot corresponds to the color of a bar in the chart.

Plan ID — This column indicates the Plan identifier.

Plan Description — This column indicates the plan description.

Plan ID and Plan Description include a hyperlink. Click the hyperlink to display the Benefit Plan Setup form in a modal window so that you can view or edit the plan. When finished with the Benefit Plan Setup form close the modal window to return to the At a Glance dashboard. When you click on a link, the actions menu is not available on the Benefit Plan Setup form. If you need to access the actions menu, you can set up the plan. See Setting Up a Benefit Plan > Note: Note: If a user has Inquiry access they can only view the Benefit Plan Setup form. If the user has Deny access they can not access the form.

Carrier — This column indicates the name of the insurance carrier.

Enrollments — This column indicates a count of employee enrollments in a plan with an active status. A hyperlink is available to the count of employees enrolled in is greater than 0. Click this hyperlink to open the Employees Assigned To modal form. > Note: Note: The hyperlink in this column is unavailable for users who do not have access to the Benefit Plan Setup form.

Start Date — This column indicates the plan start date for the indicated plan.

Stop Date — This column indicates the plan stop date for the indicates plan (if applicable).

Renew Date — This column indicates the date by which the subscriber must renew the plan.

Offer Type — This column indicates the benefit offer type associated with the plan.

Status — This column indicates the status of the plan.

Benefit Plans - Specific Offer Type

When you select a specific offer type, the system displays a chart and a search bar above the plans data list. For Example:

[Image: At a Glance panel, showing a split bar graph of employer/employee contributions to vision plan offer types.]

Chart for Benefit Plans - Specific Offer Type

The chart illustrates the total number of annual contributions by benefit plan for the selected offer type. For example, you can quickly review the chart to determine the total number annual contributions for a plan and how that breaks down between employee contributions versus employer contributions. The chart displays the total annual contributions on the Y-axis by the plans on the X-axis for the selected offer type. Each bar in the chart corresponds to the total employee (EE) and total employer (ER) contributions for each plan. For each bar in the chart, the system color codes the employee portion of the contribution in dark blue and the employer contribution in light blue. Hovering the pointer over the column will indicate the plan description, employee or employer contribution amount, and the total premium amount for the plan.

Using the Plan Search Option

Use the search option to search the list of plans for a specific offer type. Enter a keyword to find one or more plans.

[Image: At a Glance search box to search for plan IDs or descriptions.]

After entering part of a plan ID or plan description and pressing Enter, the data list re-displays all plans that match that criteria.

The system sorts the search results in the data list alphabetically.

You can select a plan id or description from the search results list to display the Benefit Plan Setup form.

Data List for Benefit Plans Specific Offer Types

The Benefit Plans Specific Offer Type At a Glance panel displays a list of data that contains information associated with each plan for the selected offer type. The following table outlines the data that displays in the list.

Column — Description

Plan ID — This column indicates the Plan identifier.

Plan Description — This column indicates the plan name.

Plan ID and Plan Description include a hyperlink. Click the hyperlink to display the Benefit Plan Setup form in a modal window so that you can view or edit the plan. When finished with the Benefit Plan Setup form close the modal window to return to the At a Glance dashboard. When you click on a link, the actions menu is not available on the Benefit Plan Setup form. If you need to access the actions menu, you can set up the plan. See Setting Up a Benefit Plan > Note: Note: If a user has Inquiry access they can only view the Benefit Plan Setup form. If the user has Deny access they can not access the form.

EE Contributions — This column indicates the annual employee contribution amount for the plan.

ER Contributions — This column indicates the annual employer contribution amount for the plan.

Enrollments — This column indicates a count of employee enrollments in a plan with an active status.

Start Date — This column indicates the plan start date for the indicated plan.

Stop Date — This column indicates the plan stop date for the indicated plan (if applicable).

Renew Date — This column indicates the date by which the subscriber must renew the plan.

Status — This column indicates the status of the plan.

Actions — Actions (a drop-down that contains a list of actions available to perform for the indicated offer type) > Note: Note: Currently there are no actions available for this At a Glance view on the Enhanced Dashboard.

Benefit Enrollment Workflows

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Enhanced_Dashboard_BenEnrollWrkFlw.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Enhanced_Dashboard_BenEnrollWrkFlw.htm

Benefit Enrollment Workflows

The Benefit Enrollment Workflows option on the Enhanced Dashboard is used to view information about active benefits enrollment workflows.

When this option is selected in the first drop-down, a color-coded pie chart displays to indicate the number of workflows in each status and the percentage of total active workflows made up by each status. In addition, a list of employees who have an active workflow displays in the data table, and a second drop-down displays to allow the user to filter the chart and table based on enrollment type.

Note: Note: The data table only displays employees to which the user has been granted access using the Users form (See Editing a User).

Viewing Employee Details

In the data table, click an employee’s name in the Employee Name column or click an employee’s ID number in the Employee ID column display the Employee Details form, where information about the employee can be reviewed or modified (See Maintaining Employee Details).

Note: Note: Reviewing employee information using these links requires inquiry access to the Employee Details form, and modifying employee information using these links requires full access to the Employee Details form. Access to this form can be granted to the User Role assigned to the user using the User Roles form (See Editing a User Role).

Actions

Click the Actions link for an employee to display a list of additional functions that can be performed for the employee.

The following options display:

Option — Description

Archive — This option is used to archive the employee’s benefit enrollment workflow. When this option is selected, a message displays to indicate that archiving the workflow will prevent the employee from being able to complete the enrollment and that the workflow’s end date will be unable to be extended. Click Yes to archive the workflow, or click No to close the message window without archiving the workflow. > Note: Note: This option is available if the User Role assigned to the user has been granted full access to Web Enrollment Configuration using the User Roles form. Otherwise, the option displays when the Actions link is clicked but cannot be selected.

Extend — This option is used to extend the end date of the employee’s benefit enrollment workflow. When this option is selected, a dialog displays to allow the user to enter a new end date for the enrollment. Enter the date and click Extend to apply the new end date. A message window displays to indicate the update was successful. > Note: Note: This option is available if the User Role assigned to the user has been granted full access to Web Enrollment Configuration using the User Roles form. Otherwise, the option displays when the Actions link is clicked but cannot be selected.

Proxy — This option is used to access the Proxy Login form, where the user can complete the workflow on behalf of the employee (See Logging in as an Employee). > Note: Note: This option is available if the User Role assigned to the user has been granted full access to Proxy Login using the User Roles form and the Enrollment Proxy role or the Onboarding Proxy role has also been assigned to the user using the Human Resource Roles panel on the Users form. Otherwise, the option displays when the Actions link is clicked but cannot be selected.

View Web Enrollment — This option is used to access the Web Enrollment Configuration form, where the user can review information about the employee’s enrollment period (See Changing an Enrollment Period). When the Web Enrollment Configuration form is accessed using this link, enrollment period information for the employee cannot be modified.

========================================================================

Viewing Employee Benefit Enrollments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Enhanced_Dashboard_EmployeeBenEnroll.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Enhanced_Dashboard_EmployeeBenEnroll.htm

Viewing Employee Benefit Enrollments

When you select Employee Benefit Enrollments in the primary drop-down menu of the At a Glance panel, you can select:

  • Employees in the secondary drop-down menu to display a list of data containing all employees. See Employees for more information.

  • Employees in the secondary drop-down menu and then click the hyperlink for an employee to display a chart and list of data for a specific employee. See Specific Employee for more information.

  • Active Plans in the secondary drop-down menu and All in the tertiary drop-down menu to display a chart and data for all active plans. See All Active Plans for more information.

  • Active Plans in the secondary drop-down menu and a specific plan in the tertiary drop-down menu to display a chart and data (a list of employees and their status for the selected plan). See Specific Active Plans for more information.

Employee Benefit Enrollments - Employees

When you select Employee Benefit Enrollments in the primary drop-down menu of the At a Glance panel and you select Employees in the secondary drop-down menu, the employees for the selected client display. For example:

[Image: At a Glance Employee list, showing employees associated with benefit enrollments.]

Using the Employee Search Option

Use the search option to search for one or more employees. Enter a keyword to find one or more employees.

[Image: At a Glance search box to search for employee names or IDs]

After entering part of an employee name or employee ID and pressing Enter, the data list re-displays all employees that match that criteria.

The system sorts the search results in the list alphabetically. You can select an employee name or employee id from the search results list to display the Employee Benefit Enrollments - Employees - specific employee At a Glance panel.

Data List for Employee Benefit Enrollments > Employees

This At a Glance panel displays a list of data that contains information associated with each employee.

When viewing the Employee Benefit Enrollments > Employees At A Glance Enhanced Dashboard and there are more than 500 employees, the system displays only a portion of the employees. You can click the View All Employees link in the lower right corner of the page to load all of the employees. The system paginates the list of employees. You can use the pagination tool in the lower right corner of the page to navigate to the next page or previous page, or you can enter a page number to jump to a specific page.

Tip: When the list contains a large list of values, use the search option to perform a keyword search and limit the number of values that displays in the list.

The list includes the following information:

Column Description
Employee Name This column indicates the employee’s name.
Employee ID This column indicates the employee’s ID.
You can navigate from the Employee Benefit Enrollments > Employees > All At a Glance View to the specific employee panel by clicking the link on the Employee Name or Employee ID in the list of all users.
Hire Date This column indicates the date of hire for the employee.
Benefit Group This column indicates the employee’s benefit group.
EE Type This column indicates the employee employment type, such as full time or part time.
Status This column indicates the employment status for the employee.
Actions Actions (a drop-down that contains a list of actions available to perform for the indicated employee) - Create a Life Event - Select this action to display the Life Event form. - Employee Details - Select this action to display a modal window to the Employee Details form. After saving any changes to the Employee Details form, click the close button for the window and the system returns you to the Enhanced Dashboard. - Update Dependent Info - Select this action to display the Employee Dependents form.
  • Create a Life Event - Select this action to display the Life Event form.
  • Employee Details - Select this action to display a modal window to the Employee Details form. After saving any changes to the Employee Details form, click the close button for the window and the system returns you to the Enhanced Dashboard.
  • Update Dependent Info - Select this action to display the Employee Dependents form. ## Employee Benefit Enrollments > Employees > (specific employee)

When you select the link associated with an employee name or employee ID on the Employee Benefit Enrollments > EmployeesAt a Glance panel, the employee benefit enrollments for that specific employee display in the At a Glance panel. For example:

[Image: At a Glance bar graph of employee benefit enrollments for a specific employee]

When viewing the Employee Benefit Enrollments > Employees > (specific employee) At A Glance Enhanced Dashboard, you can:

  • Select the Change Employee link to open the Select Employee modal window that allows you to navigate from the current employee to a different employee. You can enter a keyword in the Employee ID or Name field to search for an employee.

  • Select the View All Employees link to navigate from the specific employee back to the list of all employees.

Chart for Employee Benefit Enrollments - Specific Employee

The chart illustrates the number of plans by status for the selected employee. For example, you can quickly review the chart to determine how many plans the selected employee is eligible for. The chart displays the number of plans on the Y-axis by the status on the X-Axis. Each bar in the chart corresponds to a status and the number of plans in that status for the employee. The system color codes each bar in the chart. The color codes for each status correspond to the color codes in the data list.

Using the Plan Search Option

Use the search option to search the list of the employee’s plans. Enter a keyword to find one or more plans.

[Image: screenshot]

After entering part of a plan ID or plan description and pressing Enter, the data list re-displays all plans that match that criteria.

The system sorts the search results in the data list alphabetically.

You can select a plan id or description from the search results list to display the Benefit Plan Setup form.

Data List for Employee Benefit Enrollments - Specific Employee

The following table outlines the values that display in the data list for the Employee Benefit Enrollments > Employees > At a Glance panel. The Plans data list displays a list of insurance plans and details for those plans.

If the user has Deny access they can not access the form.

Use this enhanced dashboard to view all active plans associated with a client, and the number of employee enrollments in each active plan.

When you select Employee Benefit Enrollments in the primary drop-down menu of the At a Glance panel and you select Active Plans in the secondary drop-down menu, you can select All in the tertiary drop-down to display a chart and a list of data that illustrate information for all active plans for the selected client. For example:

[Image: At a Glance panel showing a bar graph of active benefit plans]

Chart for Employee Benefit Enrollments - All Active Plans

The chart illustrates the number of employees enrolled in active plans. The chart displays the number of enrolled employees on the Y-axis and the active plans on the X-axis. Each bar in the chart corresponds to an active plan and the number of employees enrolled in that plan. The system color codes each bar in the chart. The color codes for each plan correspond to the color codes in the data list. Hovering the pointer over the column will indicate the plan ID and the total number of employees enrolled in that plan.

Using the Plan Search Option

Use the search option to search the list of all active plans. Enter a keyword to find one or more plans.

[Image: screenshot]

After entering part of a plan ID or plan description and pressing Enter, the data list re-displays all plans that match that criteria.

The system sorts the search results in the data list alphabetically.

You can select a plan id or description from the search results list to display the Benefit Plan Setup form.

Data List for Employee Benefit Enrollments - All Active Plans

The system displays a list that contains data associated with each plan. Tip: Use the search bar to filter the number of entries that display in this list of data. The following table outlines the values that display in the data list.

Column — Description

Plan ID — This column indicates the Plan identifier. The system only displays plans with a status of Active.

Plan Description — This column indicates the plan name.

Plan ID and Plan Description include a hyperlink. Click the hyperlink to display the Benefit Plan Setup form in a modal window so that you can view or edit the plan. When finished with the Benefit Plan Setup form close the modal window to return to the At a Glance dashboard. When you click on a link, the actions menu is not available on the Benefit Plan Setup form. If you need to access the actions menu, you can set up the plan. See Setting Up a Benefit Plan > Note: Note: If a user has Inquiry access they can only view the Benefit Plan Setup form. If the user has Deny access they can not access the form.

Enrollments — This column indicates a count of employee enrollments in a plan with an active status.

Start Date — This column indicates the plan start date for the indicated plan.

Stop Date — This column indicates the plan stop date for the indicated plan (if applicable).

Renew Date — This column indicates the renewal month and day for the plan.

Employee Benefit Enrollments - Active Plans - Specific Plan

Use this enhanced dashboard to view an active plan and a list of all of the employees enrolled in the selected plan

When you select Employee Benefit Enrollments in the primary drop-down menu of the At a Glance panel and you select Active Plans in the secondary drop-down menu, you can select a specific plan in the tertiary drop-down to display a chart and a list of data that illustrate status and employee information for the indicated plan of the selected client. For example:

[Image: At a Glance panel showing a bar graph of eligibility by status for a single benefit plan]

Note: Note: Any plans with a Stop Date in the past do not appear in the chart or the tertiary drop-down. Also, the system sorts plans in the tertiary drop-down alphabetically with capitalized plans sorting before lower case (for example, the system sorts GNRL-Life before General-Life).

Chart for Employee Benefit Enrollments - Specific Plan

The chart illustrates the number of employees by status for the selected plan. For example, you can quickly review the chart to determine how many employees are eligible for the selected plan. The chart displays the number of employees on the Y-axis by the status on the X-Axis. Each bar in the chart corresponds to a status and the number of employees in that status for the plan. The system color codes each bar in the chart. The color codes for each status correspond to the color codes in the data list. Hovering the pointer over a column will indicate the status of the plan and the number of employees enrolled in the plan.

Using the Employee Search Option

Use the search option to search for one or more employees. Enter a keyword to find one or more employees.

[Image: screenshot]

After entering part of an employee name or employee ID and pressing Enter, the data list re-displays all employees that match that criteria.

The system sorts the search results in the list alphabetically. You can select an employee name or employee id from the search results list to display the Employee Details form.

Data List for Employee Benefit Enrollments > Active Plans > Specific Plan

The following table outlines the values that display in the data list for the Employee Benefit Enrollments > Active Plans> At a Glance panel.

Column — Description

You can select an employee name or employee ID to display the Employee Details form. You can edit employee information associated with the employee.

Coverage End — This column indicates the coverage end date for the plan (if applicable).

Coverage Level — This column indicates the coverage level for the plan.

EE Contribution — This column indicates the employee contribution toward the plan. This column is blank if an employee has a plan status of Eligible, Terminated, or Waived.

ER Contribution — This column indicates the employer contribution toward the plan. This column is blank if an employee has a plan status of Eligible, Terminated, or Waived.

Status — This column indicates the enrollment status of the plan.

Viewing Employees

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Enhanced_Dashboard_Employees.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Enhanced_Dashboard_Employees.htm

Viewing Employees

You can filter both the charts and the data tables by using the drop-down menus in the At a Glance panel, or by selecting the series bars in the chart. For example, to filter out an attribute in the chart, such as a particular location when the Location option is selected in the secondary drop-down menu, select that item in the legend.

Filtering Using Menu Selections

When you select Employees in the primary drop-down menu, the following options display in the secondary drop-down menu:

[Image: At a Glance panel with an employee filter dropdown selected, showing options for Status Classification, Location, Department, Shift, and Contact Info.]

Select one of the following options from the secondary drop-down menu to further filter the results:

Option — Description

Status Classification (previously displayed as Status) — Displays a chart and data table for employees by a status within a status classification that you can filter by clicking on a series bar in the chart. When you select the Status Classification option, a third menu automatically displays the Active (default), On Leave, and Terminated options to further filter the information. Selecting a third status classification refreshes the chart and table to display employees with the statuses within that class.

Location — Displays a chart and data table for employees by location. When you select Location, Department, or Shift, a third menu automatically displays a list of available options to filter the list further (default is All). Selecting a third option filters the data that already displays in the table. Note: Only employees that are in an Active status classification are included in the chart and table data for the Location, Department, and Shift options. In addition, any prior Status Classification selection (using the third drop-down menu) or filtering (using the chart) does not affect the data for Location, Department, and Shift.

Department — Displays a chart and data table for employees by department.

Shift — Displays a chart and data table for employees by shift.

Contact Info — Displays a data table that lists employee contact information, including their name, position, work phone, extension, cell phone, and work email address. This table includes the employee’s functional cell phone and work email links. For example, if you click the employee’s work email address, a separate window displays where you can launch the appropriate application to email that employee.

Note: Each time you make a selection in the secondary drop-down menu, the chart refreshes and a header pertaining to that selection displays above the chart, which lists the number of employees that apply to the selection. For example, if you select Status Classification and Active and the employees that meet that criteria numbers 48, the header displays “Employees by Status (48).”

Click the Client or Company in the header area to search for a different client company.

If the entire list of employees does not fit within the panel, you can click View all employees to display a scroll bar for navigating through the list. If you click the link to an employee, the Employee Details page opens.

When navigating through this list:

  • If your client has 1000 or less employee records, after you click View all employees in the Employees list, a scroll bar displays so you can easily scroll up or down to the employee you want to review.

  • If your client has more than 1001 or more employee records, after you click View all employees in the Employees list, pagination controls display so you can easily paginate to the next or previous page.

Note: These pagination controls continue to display for an employee status of 1000 or less, if you first page through using these controls for 1001 or more employees. However, if you don’t use the pagination controls, a scroll bar displays for an employee status of 1000 or less instead of pagination controls.

Using the Employee Search Box

You can use the Employee search box to search for an employee using any part of the employee name. For example, a search for “smith” might display “Franklin-Smith, Diane.”

[Image: Employee search box for At a Glance panel]

After entering part of an employee name and pressing Enter, the data table re-displays all employees who match that criteria.

Note: If you clear the search term and press Enter, the table results revert to displaying all employees, which is the default.

Performing Other Functions

In addition, you can perform the following functions in the Employees data table:

  • Select an employee’s name to display that employee’s information in the Employee Details form. You can update details for the selected employee in this form. (Note: If your access to the Employee Details form is set to Deny, this feature is not available.)

  • Use the options on the Actions menu to do the following:

Option Description
Employee Termination Select the Employee Termination option to access the Employee Termination form. The system pre-fills the employee’s ID in the form, so you can terminate that employee. After making the update, click Save to return to the Enhanced Dashboard. (Clicking Clear removes the selected employee’s information, so you can terminate a different employee.) > Note: Note the following when using this option: - If you make the employee termination effective as of the current or past effective date, the system refreshes the dashboard data with that update in the Status column after you click Save and the Employee Termination form closes. (If the effective date is in the future, no change displays.) - If you select an employee whose status is “Terminated” an error message displays, “<Employee Name> (<Employee ID>) is already terminated.” Click OK to return to the Enhanced Dashboard. (The Employee Termination form does not display.) - If your access to the Employee Termination form is set to Deny, the Employee Termination option does not display on the Actions menu.
  • If you make the employee termination effective as of the current or past effective date, the system refreshes the dashboard data with that update in the Status column after you click Save and the Employee Termination form closes. (If the effective date is in the future, no change displays.)
  • If you select an employee whose status is “Terminated” an error message displays, “<Employee Name> (<Employee ID>) is already terminated.” Click OK to return to the Enhanced Dashboard. (The Employee Termination form does not display.)
  • If your access to the Employee Termination form is set to Deny, the Employee Termination option does not display on the Actions menu. | Pay Rate Change | Select the Pay Rate Change option to access the Pay Rate Change form. The system pre-fills the employee’s ID in the form, so you can set a new pay rate for that employee. (Note: If your access to the Pay Rate Change form is set to Deny and you select the Actions menu, the system displays the following message, “No actions available. Contact your administrator.”) | | Position Change | Select the Position Change option to access the Position Change form. The system pre-fills the employee’s ID in the form, so you can change the position for that employee. After making the update, click Save to return to the Enhanced Dashboard. (Clicking Cancel removes the selected employee’s information, so you can change the position for a different employee.) > Note: Note the following when using this option: - If you make a position change effective as of the current or past effective date, the system refreshes the dashboard data with that update in the Position column after the Position Change form closes. (If the effective date is in the future, no change displays.) - If your access to the Position Change form is set to Deny, the Position Change option does not display on the Actions menu. |
  • If you make a position change effective as of the current or past effective date, the system refreshes the dashboard data with that update in the Position column after the Position Change form closes. (If the effective date is in the future, no change displays.)
  • If your access to the Position Change form is set to Deny, the Position Change option does not display on the Actions menu. | Status Type Change | Select the Status Type Change option to access the Status Type Change form. The system pre-fills the employee’s ID in the form, so you can change the status type for that employee. After making the update, click Save to return to the Enhanced Dashboard. (Clicking Cancel removes the selected employee’s information, so you can change the position for a different employee.) > Note: Note the following when using this option: - If you make a status type change effective as of the current or past effective date, the system refreshes the dashboard data with that update in the Type column after the Status Type Change form closes. (If the effective date is in the future, no change displays.) - If your access to the Status Type Change form is set to Deny, the Status Type Change option does not display on the Actions menu. |
  • If you make a status type change effective as of the current or past effective date, the system refreshes the dashboard data with that update in the Type column after the Status Type Change form closes. (If the effective date is in the future, no change displays.)

  • If your access to the Status Type Change form is set to Deny, the Status Type Change option does not display on the Actions menu.

Onboarding Tasks

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Enhanced_Dashboard_OnboardingTasks.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Enhanced_Dashboard_OnboardingTasks.htm

Onboarding Tasks

The Onboarding Tasks option on the Enhanced Dashboard is used to view information about active onboarding workflows.

When this option is selected in the first drop-down, a color-coded pie chart displays to indicate the number of workflows in each status and the percentage of total active workflows made up by each status. In addition, a list of employees who have an active workflow displays in the data table, and additional drop-downs display to allow the user to filter the chart and table based on which forms remain outstanding and time period.

Note: Note: The data table only displays employees to which the user has been granted access using the Users form (See Editing a User).

Viewing the New Hire Task List

In the data table, click an employee’s name in the New Hire column to display the New Hire Task List, where a list of the forms included in the employee’s workflow can be reviewed.

[Image: screenshot]

Field Description
Tasks performed by The new hire completing the tasks.
Workflow Status The status of the new hire workflow. - Not Started: Forms in the workflow have not been started - In Progress: At least one form has been started - Complete: All forms, Including the I‑9 Section 2, are complete
  • Not Started: Forms in the workflow have not been started
  • In Progress: At least one form has been started
  • Complete: All forms, Including the I‑9 Section 2, are complete | Form | The name of the form in the new hire workflow. | | Version | The version of the form. | | Form Status | The status of the form (Not Started, In Progress, Submitted, Completed). | | Due Date | The date the form is due. | | Due Date Status | The status of the form in relation to the due date (Not Due, Due Today, Past Due). | | Submit Date | The date the form was submitted. | | Approval | Type of approval (I‑9 Section 2, Pay Card Account). | | Version | The version of the approval. | | Approval Status | The status of the approval (Not Started, In Progress, Completed). | | Due Date | The date the approval is due. | | Submit Date | The date the approval was submitted. | | Approver | The approver . | ## Actions

Click the Actions link for an employee to display a list of additional functions that can be performed for the employee.

The following options display:

Option — Description

Send Reminder — This option is used to send a message to the employee to remind them to complete their onboarding workflow. The template for this message can be customized using the Message Templates form (See Maintaining Message Templates (Onboarding)).

Viewing Recent Payrolls

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Enhanced_Dashboard_Recent_Payrolls.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Enhanced_Dashboard_Recent_Payrolls.htm

Viewing Recent Payrolls

When you select Recent Payrolls in the primary drop-down menu of the At a Glance panel, the recent payrolls for the selected client display. For example:

[Image: At a Glance panel with the ‘Recent Payrolls’ option selected, listing scheduled payroll batches]

You can perform the following functions using this feature:

  • Search for payrolls using the Payroll search box. The search term can be any data that matches a value in the table, including the payroll number, description, type, and pay date. For example, if you search for “Weekly2” the results in the table should display all values that contain “Weekly2,” even if it’s preceded by the pay date in the description. (The search begins when you press Enter, tab out of the field, or click the search icon ( [Image: Magnifying glass] ) after entering the number.)

Note: If you clear the search term and press Enter, tab out of the field, or click the search icon (

[Image: Magnifying glass]

), the table results revert to displaying all payrolls, which is the default.

  • Sort the columns that display by selecting a header in the table output. For example, sort on the Payroll Number column to search for a particular payroll in ascending or descending order.

Note: The sorting function is disabled when five hundred or more records display and pagination is enabled.

  • View a list of files and reports included in a payroll by selecting the payroll number. The Payroll Reports form opens, where you can select the Open File icon in the Job column to open a specific file or report. For example:

[Image: Payroll Reports panel, listing date, time, user and title of reports that were run, with output status and options to download.]

Selecting Default Menus with ESS Menu Builder

Select default menus for Employee Portal (EP) with ESS Menu Builder. These menus are used for clients that haven’t defined their own menus.

[Image: screenshot]

Adding Menu Headers and Menu Items

Menu headers are the top-level menus seen by EP users.

To do this Perform these steps
Add a new header 1. Click New Menu Header. The Add a New Menu Structure window displays. [Image: screenshot] 2. Enter a menu header label in the Text field. This displays in EP on the menu tile. 3. In the Tool-Tip Text field, enter the text that appears when hovering the mouse over the menu header. 4. Enter the main page web URL for a menu in the Link field. 5. Display a menu icon by entering the Image URL, which is the file path for the image. For example, img/flatimages/svg/tiles/myself.svg. See ESS Menu Tile Images for a list of available images and the associated file path. 6. Click Save. You return to the ESS Menu Builder form, which displays the new header. 7. Repeat steps 1 through 6 to create a new menu, or click Save.

Maintaining ESS Menus

Maintain ESS Menu items with the ESS Menu Definition form.

To access this form:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change, select ESS Menu Definitions.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: Select an existing menu item to make changes. A red asterisk indicates a required field.

  1. Complete these fields as required.

Menu Item — Description

Menu Title — Name that displays in EP.

Menu Tooltip — Text that displays when hovering the mouse over the menu header.

Menu Code — Enter a unique code.

Is this Menu for a Single Sign On — Enable for menu items that connect to different products using single-sign on. Additional fields display when this option is enabled. Options include: - Select a Single Sign On - Product that launches when an ESS user selects this menu item. - SSO Service Name, SSO Description, SSO Base URL - Remaining fields that display when SSO is turned on.

Internal Component or External Site — Menu item links to an Internal Component or an External Site. Enter the Internal Component or External URL address.

Menu Image — Displays a menu icon. Supply the file path to the image (for example, img/flatimages/svg/tiles/myself.svg).

Additional Params — Optional parameters that you can add to the menu.

  1. Click Save.

Favorites

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Favorites.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Favorites.htm

Designating Favorites

You can select forms in PrismHR as Favorites that you access frequently. Favorites are listed on the Dashboard when you first log in to the system. You can also access them from the Favorites menu.

To add a form to Favorites, click the form’s Action menu and select Add to Favorites.

When a form is in your Favorites, the Action menu displays Remove from Favorites. Select this option to remove the form from your list of Favorites.

========================================================================

Importing Favorites

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Favorites_Template_Import.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Favorites_Template_Import.htm

Importing Favorites

You can use the Favorites Template Import form to pre-populate user favorites by importing the forms identified in the Template Process IDs panel, with the flexibility to add or remove those favorites templates in the future.

There are two sections in this form: Favorites Template and Import User Favorites. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • This feature is only available for service providers who have FULL access to the Favorites Template Import form.

  • Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Favorites Template Import form displays the form in read-only format.

  • Users whose role is set to DENY for any forms listed in the Process field will not display in their favorites list after the import finishes.

  • This form does not use Client Access Group security.

  • This form does not produce an Audit log.

To create and import a favorites template:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. On the System|Change menu, select Favorites Template Import to access the favorites import utility. The Favorites Template Import form displays.

  3. Expand the Favorites Template panel.

  4. Enter a new Template ID, or enter or select an existing template. Do the following:

  1. — For a new template ID, enter the Template Description (must be one word and only contain alpha-characters).
b. For an existing template ID, the Template Description and Template Process IDs display.

Note: You can update the Template Description, but not the Template ID.

  1. Enter or select the process IDs for the forms to associate with the template in the Process field. (You must select at least one process ID.) If you select the process IDs from the Select User Process list, click Done to add them. The Name displays.

Note: The Select User Process list displays the available Process IDs and their Process Description. (The system only displays process IDs that can be added to a user role in the User Role Maintenance list in the User Roles form.)

  1. Click Save. A message displays, “Saving an existing Favorites Template will not update Users Favorites. Do you wish to continue?” Click Yes to continue.

  2. To use the sample import file template, select Download Sample Header File and download the template.

  3. Select Upload File in the Import User Favorites panel to upload a new or existing template.

  4. Select Add Files, select the template, then select Start Upload. Click Close. The uploaded template name displays.

  5. Click Import. After the import finishes, the system adds the identified forms to the user’s existing favorites list.

  6. Click View Transaction Report to download the import details. (This report lists whether the update was successful for each User ID and the Template ID.)

Note: If both the User ID and the Template ID in a row are invalid, the report lists the error on a separate line in the report.

Note: To delete an existing favorites template, simply enter or select the template and click Delete in the Favorites Template panel. A message displays, “This will delete the Favorites Template. Do you wish to continue?” Click Yes.

FLSA Ruleset

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/FLSA_Ruleset.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/FLSA_Ruleset.htm

FLSA Ruleset

Use the FLSA Ruleset form to establish parameters for the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA).

FLSA Ruleset

The FLSA Ruleset panel describes the FLSA Ruleset and how to report overtime.

  1. Enter the FLSA Ruleset ID, something brief but descriptive.

  2. Enter a description of the FLSA ruleset in the Reference field.

  3. Select the Reporting Method for overtime:

  • Overtime Hours Reported Separately

  • Straight Hours Reported on One Pay Code

Overtime Hours Reported Separately

Use the Overtime Reporting Method panel to enter the pay code used only to track overtime pay.

  1. Enter the Premium Pay Code. This should be a pay code defined with the appropriate factor, for example, 0.5.

  2. Click Save.

Straight Hours Reported on One Pay Code

Use the Straight Reporting Method and Daily Overtime Rules panels to define how to calculate overtime. The number of hours you enter triggers the overtime calculations.

Straight Reporting Method

Use the Straight Reporting Method panel to enter the weekly number of hours for each level of overtime.

  1. Enter the number of hours worked on a weekly basis for this level in the When Hours Worked in a Week Are Greater Than field. For example, 40.

  2. In the Pay Excess Hours with Pay Code field, enter the pay code used to pay employees who work overtime at this level.

  3. Click Save.

Daily Overtime Rules

Use the Daily Overtime Rules panel to define the parameters for daily calculations.

  1. Rule for Calculating Daily Overtime:

  • Enter the number of hours worked on a daily basis for this level in the When Hours Worked in a Day Are Greater Than field. For example, 8.

  • In the Pay Excess Hours with Pay Code field, enter the pay code used to pay employees who work overtime at this level.

  • The daily level premium pay rule only applies if the weekly hours worked are less than or equal to the number of hours entered in the If Hours Worked for Weeks Are Less Than or Equal To field.

  1. Rule for Calculating Premium Pay for Consecutive Days Worked:

  • Enter the minimum number of consecutive days employees must work in one week to receive the premium pay in the When Consecutive Days Worked in a Week is GT field.

  • Enter the number of hours worked on a daily basis for this level in the When Hours Worked Those Days Are Greater Than field.

  • In the Pay Excess Hours with Pay Code field, enter the pay code used to pay employees who work overtime at this level.

  • The daily level premium pay rule only applies if the weekly hours worked are greater than the number of hours entered in the If Hours Worked for Weeks Were Greater Than field.

  1. Click Save.

Importing G/L Account Codes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/GL_Import_Entry.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/GL_Import_Entry.htm

Importing G/L Account Codes

You can use the G/L Import Entry form to quickly import account codes to the G/L setup by uploading a file for import and then viewing any errors that occurred during the import or viewing successfully imported rows.

To import G/L account codes:

  1. Enter or select the GL Template. The template name displays.

  2. Select the GL Type.

  3. Enable Overwrite Existing Account Codes to replace previously imported account codes. Otherwise, leave this field blank and the system will only import new codes.

  4. Select Download Template File to download a .txt file to your computer that contains the headings that match the selected GL Type. A separate window displays the downloaded file link.

  5. Click Open File. The spreadsheet template displays, where you can enter the G/L account codes information.

  6. Select Find File. Click Add Files and select the file to upload, then click Start Upload.

  7. Click Close. A progress window displays.

Note: If an error occurs a message displays, “It may be possible to recover from this error. Do you want to repeat your last action?” Click OK.

  1. Click Close. The import process extracts account codes from the external file.

Note: Note the following:

  • The import process skips any lines that contain invalid codes in the first column and reports them in the error report.

  • If you did not enable Overwrite Existing Account Codes, the import process skips any lines that would overwrite an existing account code and reports them in the error report.

  1. A preview of imported G/L account codes displays in the G/L Import Data panel.

Note: You can download a .csv version of this information by clicking Preview Report.

  1. If the import process encounters errors, you can select one of the following:

  • Done With Errors: Performs the import even though it contains errors.

  • Error Report: Any G/L account code errors from the import process display on this tab. Click Error Report to view them. (A browser window opens where you can download the .csv file that contains the errors.)

Defining and Applying Global PEO Accounting Templates

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Global%20PEO%20Client%20Accounting%20Templates.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Global PEO Client Accounting Templates.htm

Defining and Applying Global PEO Accounting Templates

The Global PEO Client Accounting Templates allow you the flexibility to define and apply a PEO accounting template for related clients globally without having to repeat the setup on a client-by-client basis. A service provider with a PEO Client that has sister companies might want all their accounting to be set up the same, for example, a chain of hotels. You can define a Global PEO Client Accounting Template and then select it in the Global Account Template field in the PEO Client Accounting form. From there, you will only have to enter any overrides a client might have in the individual PEO Client Accounting form for that client. These account codes can be replaced by the invoice format. If items are to be summarized on the invoice format, an account number there will replace these.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

Caution: The client accounting templates that prepare downloads must be of specific design to work correctly. Please make sure you understand the format requirements before making changes here.

To access the form, click Back Office. Under System|Change, click Global PEO Client Accounting Templates.

To change the Global PEO Client Accounting Templates:

  1. Access the Global PEO Client Accounting Templates form in the System|Change menu.

  2. Complete the following:

Field Name Description
Accounting Template ID - To create a new global client accounting template that can be shared by multiple clients, enter the name of global Accounting Template here. - To change a global client existing accounting template, enter the client accounting template ID or click the Accounting Template ID link and select the one that you want to change from the Select Global Accounting Template dialog box.
  • To create a new global client accounting template that can be shared by multiple clients, enter the name of global Accounting Template here.
  • To change a global client existing accounting template, enter the client accounting template ID or click the Accounting Template ID link and select the one that you want to change from the Select Global Accounting Template dialog box. | Template Description | Enter the description of the global client accounting template entered above. > Note: Note: For an existing global client accounting template ID, this field will auto-populate. You can edit the template description here. | | Client Accounting System | Select the client accounting system to be used for this global client accounting template from the following options: - Generic - this is the default option. - PeachTree - QuickBooks - QuickBooks Billing - Great Plains - Custom > Note: Note: For an existing global client accounting template, this field will auto-populate. You can edit the client accounting system here. |
  • Generic - this is the default option.
  • PeachTree
  • QuickBooks
  • QuickBooks Billing
  • Great Plains
  • Custom | Match Format | If present, this will test the entries to ensure they follow the format. Enter a format to ensure that the G/L Account numbers entered into each code section matches the format in this field. The options you can use in this field are N, A, or X, where N is a number, A is an alphabetic character, and X is a wildcard, which means you can use anything. A zero in front of the X (that is, 0X) indicates that section of the code can be any length and any character. (An error displays, “This entry does not match the mask pattern!”, if the Acct Format entered does not adhere to the Match Format.) For example, if you enter 4N-2N, which indicates four numbers, with two numbers in this field, so any G/L number you enter must be in that format. For example, 4321-23 is a valid Acct Format, but 64321-23 is not because its format is five numbers, with two numbers in this field. | | Earning Codes | Enter the earning code here to build the client accounting template or click the Earning Code link to select the one you want from the Pay Code Search dialog box. You can select more than one earning code for a client accounting template by clicking on the (+) sign before the Earn Code link. The Description of the earning code will auto-populate which cannot be edited. In the Earn Acct Format, enter the account number format. > Note: Note: - For an existing client accounting template ID, this field will auto-populate. - You can add or delete an earning code here which will change the existing client accounting template. - You can edit the Earn Acct Format which will override the Earn Acct Format for that earning code in the existing client accounting template. |
  • For an existing client accounting template ID, this field will auto-populate.
  • You can add or delete an earning code here which will change the existing client accounting template.
  • You can edit the Earn Acct Format which will override the Earn Acct Format for that earning code in the existing client accounting template. | Deduction Codes | Enter the deduction code here to build the client accounting template or click the Deduct Code link to select the one you want from the Deduction Codes dialog box. You can select more than one deduction code for a client accounting template by clicking on the (+) sign before the Deduct Code link. The Description of the deduction code will auto-populate which cannot be edited. In the Deduction Account Format, enter the account number format. This field does not allocate. > Note: Note: - For an existing client accounting template ID, this field will auto-populate. - You can add or delete a deduction code here which will change the existing client accounting template. - You can edit the Deduction Account Format which will override the Deduction Account Format for that deduction code in the existing client accounting template. |
  • For an existing client accounting template ID, this field will auto-populate.
  • You can add or delete a deduction code here which will change the existing client accounting template.
  • You can edit the Deduction Account Format which will override the Deduction Account Format for that deduction code in the existing client accounting template. | Tax Codes | Enter the Vertex tax code here to build the global client accounting template or click the Tax Code link to select the one you want from the Select Tax Code dialog box. You can select more than one tax code for a global client accounting template by clicking on the (+) sign before the Tax Code link. The Description of the tax code will auto-populate which cannot be edited. In the Tax Account Format, enter the account number format. > Note: Note: - For an existing client accounting template ID, this field will auto-populate. - You can add or delete a tax code here which will change the existing global client accounting template. - You can edit the Tax Account Format which will override the Tax Account Format for that tax code in the existing global client accounting template. |
  • For an existing client accounting template ID, this field will auto-populate.
  • You can add or delete a tax code here which will change the existing global client accounting template.
  • You can edit the Tax Account Format which will override the Tax Account Format for that tax code in the existing global client accounting template. | Other Bill Codes | Enter other bill code here to build the global client accounting template or click the Other Bill Code link to select the one you want from the Select Billing Code dialog box. You can select more than one bill code for a global client accounting template by clicking on the (+) sign before the Other Bill Code link. The Description of the other bill code will auto-populate which cannot be edited. In the Other Bill Account Format, enter the account number format. > Note: Note: - For an existing client accounting template ID, this field will auto-populate. - You can add or delete a bill code here which will change the existing global client accounting template. - You can edit the Other Bill Account Format which will override the Tax Account Format for that bill code in the existing global client accounting template. |
  • For an existing client accounting template ID, this field will auto-populate.
  • You can add or delete a bill code here which will change the existing global client accounting template.
  • You can edit the Other Bill Account Format which will override the Tax Account Format for that bill code in the existing global client accounting template.

  1. Click Save to either save the new global client accounting template or save the changes made to an existing global client accounting template. Upon saving, the form is cleared.

  2. Click Delete to delete an existing global client accounting template any time.

  3. Click Clear to clear this form.

Configuring Client-specific Global PTO Override Rules

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Global%20PTO%20Client%20Override.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Global PTO Client Override.htm

Configuring Client-specific Global PTO Override Rules

Use the Global PTO Client Override form to view and configure client-specific Global PTO override rules.

You can only access form using the Client Global PTO Maintenance form. Click the New Rule button on this form to open the Global PTO Client Override form. (You will not find this form from the search bar.)

To configure client-specific Global PTO override rules:

  1. Complete the following fields:

Field Name — Description

Employee Type — Select groups of employees based on their Employee Type to override the existing global pto enroll and accrual logic. Select either Include or Exclude from the drop-down for one more Employee Type. You can manually enter them here. Click the Employee Type hyperlink and select them from the Select Employee Type Codes dialog box.

Pay Method — Select groups of employees based on their pay method to override the existing global pto enroll and accrual logic. Select either Include or Exclude from the drop-down for one or more of the following pay methods: - Hourly - Salary - Variable Salary - Commission - Driver

State Code — Enter the state for which the override rule applies. Enter a two-digit State code that has NOT already been added to the Excluded Plans By State grid on the Client Global PTO Maintenance form.

PTO Benefit Plan — Select the PTO Benefit Plan that the override rule applies to. Select a Global PTO Benefit Plan ID available for the selected state from the drop-down.

Override PTO Plan ID — Select an existing Global PTO Benefit Plan to replace the Global PTO Benefit Plan set in the PTO Benefit Plan field. This is a required field unless the Exempt employees from accruals in this PTO Benefit Plan field is checked.

Exempt employees from accruals in this PTO Benefit Plan — Check this field to exempt employees from accruals in this PTO Benefit Plan for the client. Note: When you check this field, the Override PTO Plan ID field will be cleared.

  1. Click Save to save the changes for the client-specific Global PTO override rule. You cannot save this form if:

  • both the Employee Type and Pay Method fields and blank for a Global PTO override rule, OR,

  • for a specified state, the Override PTO Plan ID field is blank and also the Exempt employees from accruals in this PTO Benefit Plan field is not checked.

  1. Click Close to close this form and return to the Client Global PTO Maintenance form.

Setting Global Approval Policies

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Global_Approval_Policies.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Global_Approval_Policies.htm

Setting Global Approval Policies

There are many places in PrismHR where actions require approvals before they are finalized. Examples of this include new hires, pay rate changes, and client payroll approvals. Approval policies are defined at the global or client level. See Setting Approval Policies to learn about creating client-level approval policies.

Each approval policy specifies who must approve an action before it is finalized. There are different approval levels. Client worksite personnel can approve actions (for example, a pay rate change entered for an employee by a departmental manager), and a service provider’s internal staff can approve actions. Approval policies might also require approval from both worksite and service provider users.

Note: Note: Click View All Policies to view the policies defined for your organization, and select one to edit.

At the global level, policies for each approval type can be defined by service type. For example, you can define that all payroll approvals for PEO clients must be approved by any client worksite user who has the Payroll Authorizer role assigned to their user account.

Note: Note: When service providers enter HR-related changes, those changes go through without requiring approvals. Only payroll-related processes made by service providers are subject to approval policies.

To set global approval policies:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. Select Global Approval Policies under System|Change.

  3. Fill in the fields as required.

Field Description
Service Type Select a service type. Some of the options available are Payroll Only and Professional Employer.
Approval Type The type of action that requires approval. Some of the options available are Direct Deposit Change , ACH Maximum, Late Payroll Posting , New Hire , Position Change , and Leave of Absence . You can use the Payroll Approval (Multistep) option to set up a multi-step payroll approval process. (See the PrismHRApprovals Guide.) Note: The ACH Maximum option is only available for service providers. > Note: Note the following about the Approval Type options: - Selecting Direct Deposit Change requires approval at the client or global level to store direct deposit information in the employee details record. (After approval, the direct deposit follows the regular prenote process, if one is in place.) - Selecting Late Payroll Posting stops payrolls from being posted on or after the ACH Late Payroll Posting date and time during the finalization process, which prevents the payroll from finalizing until it is approved by a user in accordance with the applicable Approval Policy configuration. Note: To stop a payroll from finalizing, the client must have ACH billing configured on the Billing tab on the Client Details form by selecting one of the following statuses in the ACH Status field, Active, ACH by Division, or ACH by Location. In addition, the approval observes the positive or negative value in the Adjust to ACH Bill Day field, which adjusts the processing of the ACH if it is different from the employee pay date. - You can use the ACH Maximum option to create or update an ACH Maximum Approval policy at the client or global level. Note: Service providers who have Inquiry access to the Approval Policies and Global Approval Policies forms can view existing ACH Maximum Approval policies in read-only format and cannot make updates to the policy setup.
  • Selecting Direct Deposit Change requires approval at the client or global level to store direct deposit information in the employee details record. (After approval, the direct deposit follows the regular prenote process, if one is in place.)
  • Selecting Late Payroll Posting stops payrolls from being posted on or after the ACH Late Payroll Posting date and time during the finalization process, which prevents the payroll from finalizing until it is approved by a user in accordance with the applicable Approval Policy configuration.
  • You can use the ACH Maximum option to create or update an ACH Maximum Approval policy at the client or global level. | Step | For each step, set one of the following: - Enter the User ID if the step requires that a specific user approves the action. - Specify the HR Role for worksite approvers. - Specify the A/M Role, which is the service provider account management role. When you include an A/M Role, select the A/M Filter from the drop-down as your organization’s security policy requires: - All Users with designated A/M role: Any user with the account management role can see the approvals. - Only A/M Assigned to Client: Only service provider users assigned to the client can see the approvals. The system checks the account assignment in the Client DetailsAccount tab for the specified A/M Role and displays the approval for only that user. > Note: Note: PrismHR automatically assigns a number to each approval step you select. The approvals are processed in that order. |
  • Enter the User ID if the step requires that a specific user approves the action.
  • Specify the HR Role for worksite approvers.
  • Specify the A/M Role, which is the service provider account management role. When you include an A/M Role, select the A/M Filter from the drop-down as your organization’s security policy requires:
  • All Users with designated A/M role: Any user with the account management role can see the approvals.
  • Only A/M Assigned to Client: Only service provider users assigned to the client can see the approvals. The system checks the account assignment in the Client DetailsAccount tab for the specified A/M Role and displays the approval for only that user.
  1. Click Save.

Setting Global Configuration

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Global_Configuration.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Global_Configuration.htm

Setting Global Configuration

Set up system-level functionality with the Global Configuration form, which can enable or disable major features such as Onboarding and Benefits Enrollment. It also controls user home pages and some user security features. (For more information on these features, see the appropriate user guide.)

Enabling the Enhanced Dashboard

The Enhanced Dashboard provides quick access to company information and relevant features. (See Using the Enhanced Dashboard.)

To enable this dashboard:

  1. Click Back Office, then select Global Configuration on the System|Change menu.

  2. In the Home Form field, enter HRPY.WORK_ENHANCED.DASH.

  3. Click Save.

Note: Note: You can only view the Enhanced Dashboard if permissions allow you to view it. (See Defining User Roles for details on adding this menu to a user role.)

Once the dashboard is enabled, it is available through Search.

Setting Up System-level Functionality

To set up system-level functionality:

  1. Complete these fields as required.
Field Name Description
Product Version Select one of the following options: - Professional: Configures the system to provide services to clients. - Corporate: Configures the system for internal payroll and HR services (that is, for employees of your own organization). > Note: Note the following: - A warning displays if you change the Product Version. Click OK to continue. (If you did not intend to change the Product Version, you can reset it to the original version.) - If you enabled the BLENDED-STAFFING custom feature code and need to change the Product Version from Corporate to Professional, you must disable this custom feature code and log out/in again to ensure the system applies the correct version update and the Corporate/Staffing Accounting option no longer displays on the Actions menu.
  • Professional: Configures the system to provide services to clients.
  • Corporate: Configures the system for internal payroll and HR services (that is, for employees of your own organization).
  • A warning displays if you change the Product Version. Click OK to continue. (If you did not intend to change the Product Version, you can reset it to the original version.)
  • If you enabled the BLENDED-STAFFING custom feature code and need to change the Product Version from Corporate to Professional, you must disable this custom feature code and log out/in again to ensure the system applies the correct version update and the Corporate/Staffing Accounting option no longer displays on the Actions menu. | Home Form | Enter the default form that should display for Service Providers and Worksite Managers when they log in to the system. The default template IDs are HRPY.WORK_DASH for service providers and HRPY.WORK_WS.HOME for worksite managers. Note: The system validates these form names to ensure that the entry exists and is active in HRP.USER.PROCESS. If you enter an invalid form name, such as a misspelled or “junk” name or disabled/inactive user process, an error message displays, “The entry for [Home Page, Service Provider] or [Home Page, Worksite Manager] is invalid.” Click OK to continue. | | Dashboard Access | Select this field to open the Dashboard Access form, where you can control the dashboard view for your clients. (See Controlling Dashboard Views for more information.) > Note: Note the following: - This field only displays when HRPY.WORK_ENHANCED.DASH is set as the Home Form for worksite managers or worksite trusted advisors. - This field is only available for service providers. |
  • This field only displays when HRPY.WORK_ENHANCED.DASH is set as the Home Form for worksite managers or worksite trusted advisors.
  • This field is only available for service providers. | Favorites Template | Set a pre-populated favorites menu for Service Providers, Worksite Managers, or Trusted Advisors. | | Separate Print/Ship Functions | Select this option if your organization has separate processes for printing and shipping payroll advices and reports. On the Users form, under Account Management Roles, you can assign the Payroll Processor (Print/Mail) role. Note: If you enable the Separate Print/Ship Functions option, you can select Do Not Allow Self-Services Clients to Print to enable the Print feature in self-service clients’ payrolls. This enables self-service Worksite Managers to either Print or Finalize and Print payrolls from the Client Payroll form. This setting restricts user account access to service provider users with user administrator roles. If you select this option before assigning any roles, all users will be prevented from assigning the roles to user accounts! | | Manager Only Views All SuperBatch Payrolls | Select this option to only allow service providers who have the Payroll Manager A/M role to view all SuperBatch payrolls. Note: For more information on these roles, see Defining User Roles. | | Debug Printing | Select this option if you want to troubleshoot printing issues. | | Client Change Behavior | This field determines what happens when you switch from one client to another. You can either choose to Stay on the Current Form or Return to the Dashboard. When users select a different client, they stay on the current form. For example, if they are viewing Client Details and select a different client, they will see that client’s information in Client Details. When users select a different client, regardless of the form they are on, they will be taken to the Dashboard for that client. | | Enable SBEA Feature Set | Enables features related to Certified PEO reporting under the Small Business Efficiency Act of 2014. Configuring Global New Hire and Dependent Fields

For instance, fields that are not flagged as required on the New Hire and Dependent Required Fields (Global) form but have been flagged as required on the New Hire and Dependent Field Overrides form (located in the Client menu under Client|Action| New Hire and Dependent Field Overrides) override the global settings for the specified clients.

  • Required for Standard New Hire: Indicates whether the field is required when clients enter new hire information without electronic onboarding.

  • Required for Onboarded New Hire: Indicates whether the field is required when clients have their new hires onboard electronically.

  1. For each of the Dependents fields, indicate whether it is mandatory:
  • Required for Dependent: Indicates whether the field is required for data entry when clients complete the Employee Dependents form.
  1. Click Save.

Note: Clicking Cancel while editing this form reverts the form to the state it was initially in when you first accessed the form (if you have performed no Save actions) OR reverts the form to the state it was in after the most recent Save action (so that only unsaved changes are removed).
