Maintaining Global PTO Benefit Plans

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Global_PTO_Benefit_Plans.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Global_PTO_Benefit_Plans.htm

Maintaining Global PTO Benefit Plans

Use the Global PTO Benefit Plans form to set up and maintain rules for PTO carryover and accrual on the system level.

You can then assign these plans to particular states or GeoCode ranges on the State Rules form. For details about this process, see the article on Setting Up Global PTO Plans.

Setting Up Basic Rules

This panel defines the general rules for accruing and carrying over global PTO hours.

To configure a global PTO benefit plan:

  1. Click Back Office > System|Change > Global PTO Benefit Plans.

  2. Enter or select a Global PTO Benefit Plan ID. Use the Copy from another plan option if you want to use an existing plan as your template.

  3. Enter a brief Plan Description.

  4. Specify the Global PTO Register Type that will track accumulations and PTO usage under this benefit plan. You cannot assign a Global PTO Register Type to more than one global PTO benefit plan. For more information, see Setting Up Global PTO Register Types.

  5. Fill out the remaining fields as needed. These settings behave like the ones on the client-level PTO Benefit Plans form (see Defining Time Off Plans). Refer to the table for field-level guidance.

Field — Description

Annual Carryover — Enter the maximum number of unused hours that employees can carry over from one plan year to the next.

Lifetime Maximum Carryover — Enter the maximum number of unused hours that employees can carry over for the duration of their employment. This includes all plan years, starting from the employee start date.

Negative Carryover — Select this option if negative hour amounts, as recorded in the PTO register of the employee, can carry over from one year to the next.

Carryover Expiration — If you want employee PTO hours to expire a certain number of days, months or pay periods after the new year, enter that time frame here. Leave this field blank if hours do not expire.

Expiration Period — Define whether the Carryover Expiration field specifies the number of days, months, or pay periods.

Suppress Print Method — Use these fields if you want to suppress printing of PTO hours on pay stubs. For the amount of time (days or months) specified in these fields, the system will not print the PTO balance on any payroll check stubs. The balance will not display in Employee Portal either.

Add To Balance On First Accrual — Enter a flat amount to add to the accrual balance when the first accrual triggers for any employee assigned to this PTO benefit plan. Note: This amount only applies to plans with a Calculation Basis of Flat Amount or Hours Worked (by Months).

Plan Starts — Enter the date when employee paid time off begins accruing under this plan.

Plan Expires — Enter the PTO benefit expiration date. After this date, no paid time off accrues for this plan.

Usage Waiting Period — Specify the amount of time after an employee’s original hire date during which the system will suppress PTO accrual. Using the text field and the drop-down, enter the number of hours, days, or months until employees can request time off, if appropriate for this PTO benefit plan. The value must be a whole number. For the amount of time specified here, accrued time off will not display as “available” on pay stubs / advices. If an employee leaves the company and is then rehired, the system uses the original hire date, not the rehire date.

Max Usage Limit Per Plan Year — Enter the maximum number of PTO hours an employee can use in a given plan year. This works in tandem with the Stop Init If Exceed Limit setting.

Stop Init If Exceed Limit — Select this option if you want the system to stop time sheet calculation / initialization whenever one or more employees on that time sheet exceed the Max Use Limit per Plan Year.

  1. Continue to the next panel.

Hourly Accrual and Accrual Thresholds

In order to accrue hours based on hours worked, you must assign pay codes to the benefit plan.

  1. Complete the tables in this panel:

  • In the Pay Codes for Hourly Accrual table, add each pay code on which to base the PTO hour accrual (such as regular pay). You must add at least one pay code if you want PTO hours to accrue under the plan.

  • In the Pay Period Accrual Thresholds table, specify the maximum number of hours that employees in each pay period can accrue. Leave this table blank if you do not limit hour accrual.

  1. Continue to the next panel (Flat Amount per Hours Worked).

  2. Click Save when finished.

Flat Amount per Hours Worked

Use this panel to associate a certain number of hours worked with the accrual of a certain amount of PTO hours.

Setting Maximum Accruals and Stopping Accruals

The following conditions apply to the values in the Maximum Amount Accrued Per Year and Stop Accrual if Balance Reaches fields:

  • If one of these fields is blank, the system limits accrual based on the value stored in the other field.

  • If the value in both fields is the same, the system defaults to the value in the Maximum Amount Accrued Per Year.

  • If the “Maximum Value” value is greater than the “Stop Accrual” value, the system defaults to the Stop Accrual if Balance Reaches field.

List of Options

Fill out the fields in this panel, as needed:

Field or Fields — Description

Accrue a flat X hours for every Y hours worked. — X = number of PTO hours that employees can accrue after working a certain number of hours. For example, 1.00. Y = number of hours that employees must work to accrue the value in X. For example, 40.00.

If the actual hours worked are not an even multiple of YY.YY hours worked then accrue a fraction of the XX.XX hours (where X and Y are defined in the field above) — Select this option to accrue a fraction of PTO hours if employee hours worked are not an even multiple of the hours specified in the fields above.

Maximum Amount Accrued Per Year — Specify the maximum number of PTO hours to accrue in a year. See the section below for more information about the logic behind this field.

Stop Accrual if Balance Reaches — Specify the number of accrued PTO hours after which employees do not accrue any more. See the section below for more information about the logic behind this field.

Apply Carryover toward Maximum Accrual Per Year — When this field is checked, accruals will stop when Carryover Hours plus the Accrued Hours reach the Maximum Amount Accrued per Year. No additional accruals will be made for the remainder of the year. For example, if the “Maximum Amount Accrued per Year” is 40 hours, and the Carryover Hours is 39 hours, the employee can only accrue 1 hour for the current year.

Apply Current Hours Taken before applying Stop-Balance limits — Select this option to subtract the number of PTOhours used before applying a stop-balance limit to employee hour accrual. If you do not select this option, the system ignores any used PTO hours when it stops new hour accrual for an employee.

Maximum Hours That Can Be Used in a Block — Enter the maximum number of PTO hours that can be used in a single block.

Setting Up Global PTO Register Types

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Global_PTO_Register_Types.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Global_PTO_Register_Types.htm

Setting Up Global PTO Register Types

Use the Global PTO Register Types form to set up PTO register types for plans that are not client-specific. For details about the Global PTO feature set, please see Setting Up Global PTO Plans.

PTO registers track the usable hours of PTO that employees accrue over the course of the year. The events that trigger PTO accrual, and the strict definition of “year”, are defined on this form. After setting up these rules, you can assign these type codes on the Register Types table, located on the PTO Absence Codes form. For more information, see Creating Time Off Absence Codes.

Setting Up Basic Parameters

Note: Note: You cannot set up a global PTO register type code with the same ID as a client-level PTO register type.

To set up a global PTO register type:

  1. Click Back Office > System|Change > Global PTO Register Types.

  2. Enter a unique Global PTO Type Code.

  3. Enter a Description of the global PTO register type.

  4. Select the Year End Basis – the means by which the system measures the end of a year (Anniversary or Fiscal).

  5. Specify a Fiscal End Month and Day.

  6. In the Trigger Method field, select Pay Period Acrrual.

  7. Set the optional parameters below, as needed.

  8. Click Save.

Optional Parameters

Set the following parameters as needed:

Field Description
Trigger Date Select the date through which the accrual calculation is triggered. The options vary based on the selected Trigger Method.
Print on Check Select whether to print balances for this register type on employee check stubs from the following options: - Always – The Global Register will always print on the employee check when associated with the employee record. - Never - The Global Register will never print on the employee check when associated with the employee record. - If Used/Accrued Only – The Global Register will only print on the employee check if - the employee is paid in a worksite that triggers that Global Register or - a Pay Code linked to the absence code triggers that Global Register (appearing on the PTO tab of the current payroll voucher)
  • Always – The Global Register will always print on the employee check when associated with the employee record.
  • Never - The Global Register will never print on the employee check when associated with the employee record.
  • If Used/Accrued Only – The Global Register will only print on the employee check if
  • the employee is paid in a worksite that triggers that Global Register or
  • a Pay Code linked to the absence code triggers that Global Register (appearing on the PTO tab of the current payroll voucher) | Pay Stub Name | Enter a descriptive name for the PTO register type. This displays on each employee check stub and certain reports. If no check stub name is entered then the Description of the PTO Register prints. | | Inactive Register | Select if this register type is no longer used. The system will not calculate accruals or update existing employee registers associated with this register type. | | Auto-enroll Through-Date is Day Before Start Date | When the system auto-enrolls employees in plans for this register type, this option forces the PTO “accrued through date” to be the day before the employee’s start date. This can help ensure that auto-enrolled employees do not lose accrual for that day. | | Display a Warning If Employee Uses More Hours Than Available | Select to display a warning during payroll initialization if an employee uses more PTO hours than are available in the register. | ========================================================================

Importing Client Benefit Plans

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Importing%20Company%20Benefit%20Plans.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Importing Company Benefit Plans.htm

Importing Client Benefit Plans

After you complete the steps for setting up a group benefit plan at the system level (see the Benefits Administration Guide for detailed information), you can begin the steps for importing the client benefit plan. After that, you must set up a data file and a benefit import definition.Important! Client Access Group security is enabled on this form. Only service providers can use the Client Benefit Plan Import form to import client benefit plans from an external text file.

Admin Surcharge Message

If a user attempts to import client benefit plans and the import file contains data for any of the Admin Surcharge fields, the system displays the following message when the user attempts to validate the import file:

The Admin Surcharge feature is not available in this release.

This error message blocks the user from importing the file. The user must edit the file and remove the Admin Surcharge field values in order to continue with the import process.

The Admin Surcharge feature will be available in a future release.

To import client benefit plans:

  1. On the Work Centers panel, under Benefits, click Benefit Imports & Reporting.

  2. Under Benefit Imports, click Client Benefit Plan Import.

  3. Click Upload File and then Choose File to select the data file. Alternatively, you can first download a sample header file by clicking the Download Sample Header File link on the Client Benefit Plan Import.

After you click the Download Sample Header File link, the system downloads or prompts for download a sample header file that displays columns and headers that match each column and description for the import template option. Also, the file displays a title that matches the selected option.

Note: Note: The header file is in .csv format. You can save the file in .csv or .txt format. Additionally, a the sample import file also contains the a column for Only apply to S-Corp Principal Employees.

  1. Click Submit. A confirmation message displays.

  2. Click Close.

Next, validate the import:

  1. Click Validate Import File.

  2. When the process is complete, click Close.

  3. Click Import.

  4. When the process is complete, click Close. The data file imported.

  5. Click Print Import Report. The Company Benefit Plan Import Report opens.

  6. Click the XLS link to download the report.

Value Search

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Looking_Up_Values.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Looking_Up_Values.htm

Searching for Values

In PrismHR, a field or column label may provide a link that enables you to search for values. The user interface for searching depends on the selected form. For example, in some forms you can navigate through a list of available values using navigation keys. In other forms, you use scroll bars to navigate through the list of values.

Some fields accept only one value. Other fields accept multiple values.

Using Navigation Keys

This section is relevant for forms in which you select values for a field using navigation keys. The following example explains how to use navigation keys to find one or more values for the Position field.

To find available positions:

  1. Either press Ctrl + Enter while the cursor is in the field or click the Position link. The search window opens.

  2. To move through multiple pages of values, use the Pg Up or Pg Dn keys or click Previous and Next. You can go directly to a page by entering the page number in the Select Page field and then clicking Go To Page.

  3. Use the Refine Search fields to modify the search criteria. For example, enter some of the Employee ID or Sort Name.

  4. To select a value, enter the row number in the Select Row field or click the value in the list. You return to the previous screen and the selected value populates the field. If you know the value, you can simply enter it in the field instead of selecting it.

Using Scroll Bars

This section is relevant for forms in which you select values for a field using scroll bars. The following example explains how to use scroll bars to find a value for the Client ID field.

To find client IDs:

  1. Click the Client ID link. The Select Clients window opens.

  • Each page shows 100 items at a time and scroll bars are available to navigate through the page.

  • To see additional pages, click More at the bottom of the list.

  • You can filter the list by Service Type, Status, or Employer. You can also filter the list by typing text in the search box.

  1. Select one or more clients. Totals are shown for the number of available clients and the number of selected clients.

  • If a field allows only one value, the selection list closes and the value is supplied in the field.

  • If a field allows multiple values, The selected values are shown in a list at the bottom of the window. Click Done to accept them.

Employee Search

Most employee search fields enable you to search for the employee directly from the Employee field. You can also click the field label link to use a search form.

If you choose to search from the field, type the first part of the employee’s name or ID and then select the name from the list. The list filters as you type.

Using Substitution Variables

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Message_Substitution_Variables.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Message_Substitution_Variables.htm

Using Substitution Variables

Substitution variables are tags that you can use as placeholder text when building message template content. When generating the message, the system replaces the variable with data pulled from the system. Substitution variables are similar to mail merge fields in word processing programs. They give content a more personal impact and make it easier to customize and reuse content for multiple employees, clients, workflows, and enrollment periods.

Substitution variables behave differently depending on where you use them:

  • Specifying Substitution Variables for Messages

  • Working with Substitution Variables for Onboarding

  • Working with Substitution Variables for Benefits Enrollment

Specifying Substitution Variables for Messages

Substitution variables for messages behave differently based on the message type they are used for and only work in specific message types.

For example, you might set up a form for a workflow that includes text using the substitution variable for the employee’s name:

Welcome, <<EMPLOYEE.NAME>>!

When the employee views the form, the substitution variable is replaced by the employee’s name and displays as:

Welcome, Jane M. Smith!

Users can include the following substitution variables in both notifications and custom forms.

These variables are case-sensitive and you must type them exactly as shown in the Substitution Variable column.

Configuring MFA Email Templates and Services

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/MFA_Email_Templates_Services.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/MFA_Email_Templates_Services.htm

Configuring MFA Email Templates and Services

You must set up an email template before implementing MFA. This template contains the text and passcode (the <> substitution variable) that users receive by email when they attempt log in.

Note: Note: Multi-factor authentication requires a message template. You can associate the message template with the MFA passcode email service.

  1. Open Message Templates (found in [Image: screenshot] under System|Change).

  2. Enter a Message ID (for example, MFA).

  3. Enter a Description (for example, MFA Template).

  4. Select the Content Type: TEXT or HTML.

  5. Enter the Subject line for emails that use this template.

  6. Enter the Body of the message. Be sure to include the <> substitution variable in the message. The user enters this when they log in with multi‑factor authentication. [Image: screenshot]

  7. Click Save in the Message Templates form.

Setting Up Email Services

Use Email Services to maintain the information PrismHR uses to send automatic email messages.

  1. Open System Parameters (found in [Image: screenshot] under System|Change).

  2. Select Email Services from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] .

  3. Complete these fields as required:

  4. Enter the IP address or host name of the SMTP Server.

  5. Enter the SMTP Port number the server is listening on.

  6. Enter the Email Service URL.

  7. Enter the Support Email, which is the email address that recipients see for most messages.

  8. Enter an email address in sMFA Email that recipients see when they receive an email for multi‑factor authentication. This does not need to be an actual, monitored email account. However, you can use a monitored account for testing or to enable users to communicate if they have a problem.

Note: Note: The Benefits Security Email Subject field is for Benefits Enrollment. You can leave this field blank.

  1. Create a new line in the Email Templates table.

  2. Select MFA Passcode from the Template Type drop-down.

  3. Enter the ID of the template you created in the Template column (for example, MFA). The Description displays.

  4. Click Save, then click Save in System Parameters.

Enabling Multi-Factor Authentication

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/MFA_Enabling.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/MFA_Enabling.htm

Enabling Multi-Factor Authentication

Your organization can enable multi-factor authentication security at the system, client, or user level. After the number of days is specified in Authentication Services, affected users are prompted to request an authorization. This authentication applies to each device used to access PrismHR (computer, tablet, and so on).

Enabling System-Level MFA

Enabling MFA at the system level affects all service provider, worksite manager, and worksite trusted advisor users, and the period applies to all levels of authentication.

To enable MFA for the entire system:

  1. Open System Parameters (found in [Image: screenshot] under System|Change).

  2. Select Authentication Services from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] .

  3. Set the sMFA Device Expiration period.

  4. Set the sMFA Device Expiration for Employee Portal period.

  5. Set the sMFA Security Code Access method to Email (default) and/or SMS (text sent to mobile device). This determines where security codes are sent during the Account Access Confirmation process.

  • SMS is enabled - It’s enabled for all employees, service providers, managers, and trusted advisors. It cannot be enabled for individual users or clients.

  • SMS destination - For service providers, managers, and trusted advisors: authorization codes are sent as a text message to the phone number saved in the Mobile Phone field on the Users form. For employees: The phone number saved in Cell Phone on the Employee Details form (HR menu > Employee Details > Address tab) is used for text messages and authorization codes.

  1. Optional: Select IP Whitelist Skips sMFA. This feature applies only to PrismHRand not to EP.

  2. Click Save in Authentication Services.

  3. Click Save in System Parameters. After enabling MFA, whenever a service provider, worksite manager, or worksite trusted advisor logs into PrismHR, the Account Access Confirmation dialog displays: [Image: screenshot] After enabling Send SMS to, a generic message displays stating that the user will receive the security code via email. However, the code is actually sent as a text message. Once the user requests the security code, this message (or a similar one) displays: [Image: screenshot]

Enabling Client-Level MFA

Enabling MFA at the client level can affect all service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors associated with the client.

To enable client-level MFA:

  1. Select the client to enable MFA.

  2. Open Client Details (found in the Client menu under Client|Change).

  3. Select Security from the Actions menu.

  4. Set security options (under Access) as needed:

Option — Description

sMFA Device Expiration — Use the global setting, a different interval period from the global setting, or disable MFA for this client. When enabled, all users associated with this client who access the system will need to re‑authenticate their access after the specified time interval, if any, for each device they use. The system prompts them to request an authentication code, which it sends to the user’s specified email address. The user can then enter the authentication code to regain system access.

MFA Expiration for Employee Portal — Use the global setting, a different interval period from the global setting, or disable Employee Portal (EP)MFA for this client. When enabled, all users associated with this client who access EP will need to re‑authenticate their access after the specified time interval, if any, for each device they use. The system prompts them to request an authentication code, which it sends to the user’s specified email address. The user can then enter the authentication code to regain EP system access.

Note: Note: To implement MFA, your organization must set up a message template for MFA Passcode.

sMFA Enabled for Trusted Advisor Password Reset — Enable MFA for all worksite trusted advisors who have access to the client, requiring them to use MFA when the Forgot Password link is clicked.

  1. Click Accept in the Client Security form.

  2. Click Save in the Client Details form.

Enabling User-Level MFA

Enabling MFA at the user level only affects each specified user. At the user level, MFA settings apply to both PrismHR and EP.

To enable user-level MFA:

  1. Click [Image: screenshot] and open the Users form under System|Change.

  2. Enter the User ID for a service provider, worksite manager, or worksite trusted advisor user.

  3. Set sMFA Device Expiration to use the global setting, a different interval period from the global or client setting, or disable MFA for this user. When enabled, the user will need to re‑authenticate their access after the specified time interval, if any, for each device they use. The system prompts them to request an authentication code, which it sends to the user’s specified email address. The user can then enter the authentication code to regain system access.

  4. Click Save.

Multi-Factor Authentication Security

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/MFA_Overview.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/MFA_Overview.htm

Multi-Factor Authentication Security

Note: Note: As of September 2019, Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is now automatically enabled for Service Provider users.

A major challenge of system security is keeping user credentials secure. User names, passwords, and personal information such as date of birth are no longer considered secure. This is especially true for people who have ever used a public computer in a library, or accessed a secure website over a public Wi-Fi network. Community computers and public Wi-Fi are vulnerable to screen scraping or decrypting technologies which put credentials at risk.

Because many people use the same credentials across websites, phishing schemes and malicious redirects also play a part in security breaches. If a cyber-criminal has access to one set of your credentials, that criminal may have access to all of them.

MFA security for service providers, worksite managers, worksite trusted advisors, and customer users helps keep credentials secure. MFA provides an additional level of user authentication outside of the web browser. When MFA is enabled in PrismHR and a user tries to log in, the system generates an email or text message with a unique validation key. This key, or passcode, is valid for a single use and expires after a set time period. The email or text message authenticates the legitimate user. It also notifies the rightful account owner that an unauthorized user has stolen their credentials.

To begin using MFA, you must first set up a message template in PrismHR. Message templates send the emails or text messages that contain the text and unique passcode.

Note: Note: For MFA to be effective, all users must have a valid email address or mobile device number associated with their user account.

MFA requires that after a certain number of days accessing the system from a device, each user is prompted to request an authorization code. The system sends the code to the email address or mobile device number associated with the user account, after which the user enters it and can access the system.

Authentication is necessary for each device that accesses the system. For example, if a user logs in with multiple devices, they must authenticate separately on each device.

Resetting MFA Passwords For Trusted Advisors

Resetting MFA Passwords For Trusted Advisors

You can enforce MFA for worksite trusted advisor password resets. Enable this feature at the system, client, or user level.

Resetting System-Level MFA Passwords

Note: Note: Enabling MFA for password resets at the system level requires all worksite trusted advisors to use MFA when the Forgot Password link is invoked.

To enable MFA for password resets at the system level:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. Select System Parameters under System|Change.

  3. Select Authentication Services from the Actions menu.

  4. Select the Use MFA for Password Reset option for Trusted Advisors.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Save.

  2. Click Save in System Parameters.

Resetting Client-Level MFA Passwords

Enabling MFA for client-level password resets affects all worksite trusted advisors who have access to the client, requiring them to use MFA when the Forgot Password link is invoked.

To enable MFA for password resets at the client level:

  1. Select Client Details under Client|Change.

  2. Select Security from the Actions menu.

  3. Select the sMFA Enabled for Trusted Advisor Password Reset option in the Access panel.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Accept in the Security Entities form.

  2. Click Save in the Client Details form.

Resetting User-Level MFA Passwords

Enabling MFA for password resets at the user level requires that worksite trusted advisor to use multi-factor authentication when they use the Forgot Password link.

To enable user-level MFA for password resets:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. Select Users under System|Change.

  3. Open the worksite trusted advisor user account.

  4. Select sMFA Support in the Password Recovery panel.

  5. Click Save.

Reauthorizing Standard MFA Login

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/MFA_Standard_Access.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/MFA_Standard_Access.htm

Reauthorizing Standard MFA Login

Service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors are prompted to request an authorization code after a specified number of days accessing the system from a device.

The user follows this process:

  1. A message notifies the user that they will receive a security code by email (the email address is masked for security) The user must click Submit.

  2. The system sends the message with the authorization code and displays a form that allows the user to enter the security code.

  3. The user receives the email with the authorization code and enters it in the form.

  4. The user clicks Submit and is logged in to the system.

Resetting Forgotten Passwords For MFA Login (Trusted Advisors)

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/MFA_WTA_Access.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/MFA_WTA_Access.htm

Resetting Forgotten Passwords For MFA Login (Trusted Advisors)

This process applies to worksite trusted advisors who use MFA when resetting a forgotten password.

  1. Click Forgot your password? in the login form.

  2. Enter your Username and click Continue. The system sends two messages: a link to a form, and the authorization code itself.

  3. Click the link in the email to access the User Registration & Password Reset form.

  4. Enter [the] Security Code received in the second email. Manually type in the code to avoid copy and paste mistakes.

  5. Enter the New Password and Confirm New Password.

  6. Click Continue.

If there are any issues with the password, the system displays a message to try again.

  1. Once the password is successfully reset, the system returns to the login screen where you can log in with the new password.

Creating/Editing NAICS Codes

Use this form to create/edit North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) codes in PrismHR that identify various industries.

To create or edit an NAICS code in PrismHR:

  1. Complete the following fields:
Field Description
NAICS Code To create a new NAICS Code in PrismHR, enter it here. To edit an existing NAICS Code in PrismHR, enter it here or click the NAICS Code link and select it from the Select NAICS Code dialog box for example 311221.
Description To create a description for a new NAICS Code in PrismHR, enter the appropriate description here. To edit an existing NAICS Code in PrismHR, edit the description that appears here when you enter an existing NAICS Code in PrismHR above. For example the updated description for NAICS Code 311221 from 2022 onwards will be Wet Corn Milling and Starch instead of Wet Corn Milling earlier.
Obsolete This box is unchecked by default for valid codes as of 2022. For NAICS Codes obsolete as of 2022 it will be checked by default. Check this box if you need to identify an NAICS code as an obsolete NAICS code in PrismHR. For example NAICS Code 811219 is now an obsolete code as per 2022 NAICS Code. When building the EEO-1 data, you will receive an error message and the EEO-1 build will fail if: - The NAICS Code assigned to a client here or a worksite location in the Worksite Locations form is obsolete in PrismHR. - No NAICS Code is assigned to a client in PrismHR. > Note: Note: NAICS codes are not mandatory in the Worksite Locations form. You will not receive an error if there is no NAICS Code assigned to a worksite in the Worksite Locations form. This field is only necessary if the worksite location NAICS code differs from other locations.
  • The NAICS Code assigned to a client here or a worksite location in the Worksite Locations form is obsolete in PrismHR.
  • No NAICS Code is assigned to a client in PrismHR.

  1. Click Save to save the changes made to this form in PrismHR.

  2. Click Delete if you want to delete an NAICS Code from PrismHR.

  3. Click Clear to clear this form at any time.

  8. Click Send when the message is ready. | Search for messages | 1. Click Search Messages. 2. Select the message you want to view. The Message Center form populates with information from the selected message. When you are finished, click Cancel. |
  9. Click Search Messages.
  10. Select the message you want to view. The Message Center form populates with information from the selected message. When you are finished, click Cancel. | View Message History | Click Message History. The Sent Message Review form populates with the user’s sent message history. When you are finished, click Close. | Parent Topic

Scheduling ACH Processing

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Notification_Control_Panel_for_ACH_Processing.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Notification_Control_Panel_for_ACH_Processing.htm

Scheduling ACH Processing

Important! This topic refers to a feature that will be available in a future release.

You can specify the daily start time for ACH processing using the ACH Processing panel on the Notification Control Panel form, which is accessible from the Operations|Action menu. In addition, you can view the last date/time they were run.

Based on the scheduled time specified in the ACH Processing panel, the system runs multiple ACH processing by selecting all the files and then building the file.

Note: You must use the options in the ACH Processing panel in conjunction with multiple ACH processing. (See Performing Multiple ACH Processing for more information.)

To specify the daily start time for ACH processing:

  1. Click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office).

  2. From Operations|Action, select Notification Control Panel. The Notification Control Panel form displays.

Note: If the notifications engine is already running, select BE Stop, then select BE Start before using the ACH Processing panel.

  1. In the ACH Processing panel, enter the following information:
  • User ID: Define the user associated with the ACH process.

Note: This user must have access to the ACH Processing form for external payroll.

  • Daily ACH Start Time: Enter the daily start time for ACH processing. Valid entries for this field must be entered in military time. For example, to start ACH processing at 1:00AM, enter 01:00:00.

Note: The ACH processing start times only apply to the ACH Processing form for external payroll.

  1. Click Save.

To the right of the Daily ACH Start Time field a display-only process status displays, which matches the same control number that displays in the BE Notify panel. (See Using the Notification Control Panel (Benefits Enrollment).)

In addition, the display-only Last Run Date/Time field displays the last date and time the process ran.

Scheduling Payroll Reminders

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Notification_Control_Panel_for_Payroll_Reminders.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Notification_Control_Panel_for_Payroll_Reminders.htm

Scheduling Payroll Reminders

You can use the Payroll Reminders panel in the Notification Control Panel form to schedule payroll reminders for worksite advisors and worksite trusted advisors if the payroll is still in timesheet entry status as the payroll’s completion date gets closer to the cutoff date. For example, if the payroll will no longer be available to worksite advisors and worksite trusted advisors as of 4/15/2024 and it is not completed, the system sends a reminder to those users on 4/13/2024 that payroll is almost due.

Note: This feature is only available for service providers.

To schedule a payroll reminder:

  1. Click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office).

  2. From Operations|Action, select Notification Control Panel. The Notification Control Panel form displays.

  3. In the Payroll Reminders panel, enter the number of hours before the payroll cutoff date and time to send the reminder in the Payroll Reminder Timing field.

  4. Click Save.

To the right of the Payroll Reminder Timing field a display-only process status displays, which matches the same control number that displays in the BE Notify panel. (See Using the Notification Control Panel (Benefits Enrollment).)

In addition, the display-only Last Run Date/Time field displays the last date and time the process ran.

Working with ACH Impounding

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Offset_Impound_Accounts.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Offset_Impound_Accounts.htm

Working with ACH Impounding

Use the Offset Impound Accounts form to work with ACH impounding, where the system creates offset transactions for various client fund types. You can designate impound bank accounts where client net-pays, payroll taxes, and retirement contributions are deposited. The system deposits the remainder of the client invoice amount leftover after deducting for net-pays, taxes, and retirement contributions into the bank account designated by the Offset Account ID on the Bank Accounts form.

Note: Historically, PrismHR has supported generating a single ACH transaction to offset the client invoice amount. For a typical payroll, this transaction would be an ACH credit transaction. For most PEO/ASO clients, the total invoice amount is the aggregate of the client fees, employee net pays, taxes, and benefits, such as retirement. The system uses this functionality to designate the impound bank accounts where client net-pays, payroll taxes, and retirement contributions are deposited. The remainder of the client invoice amount leftover after deduction for net-pays, taxes, and retirement are deposited into the bank account designated by the “Offset Account ID” on the primary bank’s account form.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: You must enable the ACHBREAKONPRBATCH custom feature code on the System Parameters form to access the Offset Impound Accounts form on the Actions menu for the Bank Accounts form.

To set up ACH impounding for an account:

  1. Go to the Bank Accounts form on the System|Change menu.

  2. Enter or select an Account ID.

  3. Select Offset Impound Accounts on the Actions menu.

  4. Select the Fund Type to designate the billing component for which the offset credit applies on the ACH file. (You can set multiple types.)

  5. Enter or select the Bank Account to return records from the system-level Bank Accounts file.

  6. Click Close. The Bank Accounts form re-displays.

  7. Click Save.

Establishing OSHA Event Codes

  2. Complete the following fields:

Field — Description

Event Code — Enter or select an Event Code that represents an OSHA event. Use something brief but descriptive, such as PHL for permanent hearing loss.

Type — Select the Type of event, either Illness or Injury.

Event Description — Enter a short Event Description, such as Permanent Hearing Loss.

OSHA Illness Type — Select the OSHA Illness Type used for reporting purposes. If the Type is Illness, this is required.

  1. Click Save.

Activating Pending Enrollments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Part-Req-Maint.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Part-Req-Maint.htm

Activating Pending Enrollments

After you define participation requirements and medical waiver reasons, employees can submit their enrollments, which are assigned to the posting queue as pending. The Participation Requirement Maintenance form enables you to activate pending enrollments.

To activate pending enrollments:

  1. In the Back Office menu, go to Operations|Action > Participation Requirement Maintenance.

  2. In the Participation Requirement Maintenance panel, complete the following fields:

Field Action
Benefit Plan ID Enter a plan ID or click the link to select from a list.
Participation Requirement Criteria - To view posted enrollments with the start date and percentage entered at the system level on the Group Benefit Plans form, select System check. - To view posted enrollments with client overrides entered at the client level on the Benefit Plan Setup form, select a Client ID check. The Client ID field is disabled.
  • To view posted enrollments with the start date and percentage entered at the system level on the Group Benefit Plans form, select System check.
  • To view posted enrollments with client overrides entered at the client level on the Benefit Plan Setup form, select a Client ID check. The Client ID field is disabled. | Client ID | To filter between clients with system-level participation requirements, select a client from the Client ID list. |
  1. Click Search. The Search Results panel displays posted enrollments with effective dates on or before the Participation Requirement Start Date.

The table includes:

Field Description
Client The client ID number and name.
Employee The employee name and ID number.
Plan ID The plan ID.
Effective Date The plan’s effective date.
Status - Pending - Active - Waived - Terminated - Eligible
  • Pending
  • Active
  • Waived
  • Terminated
  • Eligible In the Participation Requirement Maintenance panel, information displays for posted enrollments. Enrollments currently in progress do not display.

Field — Description

Participation Requirement Needed — The total Participation Requirement percentage.

Estimated Participation Achieved — Percentage = (Pending Employee count + Active Employee count) / (Total Employee count - Waived Employee count)

Pending Employee count — The number of employees with a Pending enrollment status.

Active Employee count — The number of employees with an Active enrollment status.

Waived Employee count — The number of employees with a Waived enrollment status.

Terminated Employee count — The number of employees with a Terminated enrollment status.

Eligible Employee count — The number of employees with an eligible benefit enrollment for this plan. Note that when adding the benefit plan after entering the employee into the system, the employee is eligible, but an eligible benefit enrollment does not exist.

Total Employee count — Total of all employee counts.

  1. To activate enrollments displayed in the table, click Activate Pending Plans. A dialog displays confirming you want to change the pending enrollments to an active status.

  2. To continue, click Yes. Or, click No to return to the Participation Requirement Maintenance form.

Changing Passwords

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Password_Change_Form.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Password_Change_Form.htm

Changing Passwords

Change a user password on the Change Password form.

To change your password or that of another user:

  1. Verify the Username is correct and you are on the correct user’s page.

  2. Change your own password by entering your Current Password.

Note: If you are resetting an employee’s password, you don’t need to enter their current password.

  1. Enter a New Password. The system validates the password. If validation fails, PrismHR provides information on creating a valid password.

  2. Re-enter the password in the Confirm New Password field. The next time the user logs on, use the new password.

Note: The read-only Requires New Password field, which is enabled by default and cannot be disabled for security purposes, prompts employees to create a new password the next time they log into the system.

  1. Click Save. The next time the user logs on, use the new password.

Note: If you are resetting an employee’s password, this resets the lockout period, if any, in cases where the password is being changed because the employee was locked out of EP after too many failed login attempts.

Working with Pay Codes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Pay_Codes.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Pay_Codes.htm

Working with Pay Codes

Use the Pay Codes form to establish pay code information and processing parameters required to process pay information in PrismHR.

In addition, you can access pay code-related features and settings using the Actions menu:

  • Viewing the Audit Log

  • Defining Maximum Earnings

  • Exempting Taxes

  • Creating Weighted Average Calculations for Pay Codes

Defining Basic Pay Code Information

Use the Pay Codes panel to define the basic pay code information.

Note: Click the Data Import Tool icon (

[Image: screenshot]

) to upload a database file and import data. (This icon displays for all user roles, except “Inquiry Only.”)

Note: Note: For more information about the Data Import Tool form, see the Payroll Administration Guide.

To define basic pay code information:

Field Description
Pay Code Enter a Pay Code to use for this type of payment or click this field to display existing pay codes and select it from the list. (When creating a pay code, use a mnemonic, such as OT for overtime.) If you select this field, a selector form displays where you can search for a specific pay code or pay description or select a code from the list that displays. When this form opens, the pay code, pay description, pay type, pay class, calculation method, and obsolete date display. To filter the search further: - Select a Pay Type, Calculation Method, or Pay Class (the default is All for these fields). - Display only Obsolete codes by selecting Yes (the default is No). (Note: Codes with an obsolete date earlier than the current date do not display in the selector form.) To refresh the list, select Reset Search and Filters.
  • Select a Pay Type, Calculation Method, or Pay Class (the default is All for these fields).
  • Display only Obsolete codes by selecting Yes (the default is No). (Note: Codes with an obsolete date earlier than the current date do not display in the selector form.) | Pay Description | Enter a Pay Description for this type of earning or payroll disbursement. | | Pay Type | Select the Pay Type. In any one payroll batch, the system creates up to three payroll vouchers for one employee. Each voucher can be a different type of earning. The system processes each type differently. | | Pay Class | Select the Pay Class for this payment, which determines the tax liability. All classifications except for Expense Reimbursements are considered taxable. Payments classified as Non-Cash Fringe Benefit, Reported Tips, and Memo are considered non-cash. Most pay codes define payments made to employees for services rendered (amounts earned). You would classify such payments as Earnings. In some cases, however, you might want to include amounts on a payroll voucher that are not amounts “earned” by employees as part of their normal hourly wages or salary. > Note: Note: Changing the pay class of a pay code that has been used can cause issues with payrolls and Form W‑2s. If you need a pay code that is similar but has a different class, create a new pay code. | | Cash/Non-Cash | Select the Cash/Non-Cash method. In almost all cases, amounts paid to an employee on a payroll voucher represent actual cash earnings. However, the amount does not need to represent an actual cash payment. You would use this when you need to withhold taxes for a taxable fringe benefit, such as a company car. | | Calculation Method | Select the Calculation Method used to determine the hourly/unit rate paid with this pay code when it is entered on a time sheet. > Note: Note: For some methods, the Maximum Calc Hours/Maximum % of Gross Earnings field displays. Enter the maximum amount the system should use on a single pay voucher when calculating an amount based on hours worked, hours paid, and so on. | | Pay Reason | Select the Pay Reason, which describes whether this pay code is for hours worked or units of service. | | Print on Paystub | Select the Print on Paystub method to indicate how to print the pay code on the employee’s pay stub. | | Pay Stub Name | Enter the Pay Stub Name, which is a short description that prints on the remittance stub of a payroll check/direct deposit advice and certain other reports. | | Retirement Earnings | Select Retirement Earnings if the system should use amounts paid with this pay code to calculate the employee’s elective contribution to a retirement plan. | | Subject to Work Comp | Select the Subject to Work Comp method, which indicates whether these earnings should be used to calculate Workman’s Compensation insurance liability. | | Form W-2 Box | Select the Form W-2 Box number in which this pay code’s tax year payments should print. | | Form W-2 Code | Enter the Form W-2 Code that precedes the amount printed in Box 13 or 14 of Form W-2. | ## Viewing Calculation Rules

One of the following panels displays, which depends on the rules for the selected Calculation Method:

  • Standard Method Rules

  • Fixed Method Rules

  • Calculated Method Rules

  • Per Diem Method Rules

  • Calculated Fringe Benefit

  • Fringe Calculation Pay Codes

For detailed information about these panels, see See Defining Pay Code Calculation Rules.

Note: Note: If you import a pay code that contains a value in the Alt. Pay Rate # field in the Standard Method Rules panel, but there is no corresponding value for the employee in the Pay tab on the Employee Details form, no import occurs and the system does not display an error message.

Setting Up Billing Codes

Use these fields to determine how to bill the clients for this pay code, if appropriate. For example:

To setup billing codes:

Field — Description

Bill Code — Enter the bill code to use for this pay code. Leave this field blank if your organization does not re-bill clients for this pay code, for example, a Section 125 expense reimbursement or a PEO discretionary payment.

Bill Code Job Rate — Enter the billing code to use if you bill clients using job rates. Leave this field blank if your organization does not re-bill clients for this pay code.

Non-Cash Rebate Bill Code — Enter the billing code for pay codes classified as Non-Cash Fringe Benefits or Reported Tips. Leave this field blank if your organization does not re-bill clients for this pay code.

Setting Processing Options

The Processing Options panel controls how PrismHR processes pay code information.

To set processing options:

Field Description
Pay Code is Used to Pay Productive Work Select if this pay code represents an amount earned for productive labor. For example, do not check this box for pay codes intended for vacation or sick time.
Used to Pay Cash Wage for Tipped Employees Select to use this pay code to pay cash wages for tipped employees, usually at the minimum cash wage required by state law.
Pay Code Used to Pay Employee for Charged Tips Select if this pay code is for compensating employees for charged tips. This is valid only when the Pay Class is Earnings.
Include Hours/Amount Paid in Overtime Calculation Select to include this pay code in any overtime calculation. Note that Hours is hours worked, whereas the Amount is the paid amount.
Use Hours Paid instead of Hours Worked in Overtime Calculation If you selected the Include Hours/Amount Paid… option, you can also enable this option to use the paid hours instead of the hours worked when calculating overtime. Note: Overtime calculations require that the client has an FLSA ruleset defined. These calculations only work for scheduled payroll batches; the system does not use FLSA rulesets for manual or special payrolls. (See Overtime Calculation Examples.)
Include Amount Paid Only in Overtime Calculation Select to include only amounts paid with this pay code in any overtime calculation.
Add to O/T Hours in lieu of Threshold Calculation Select to add hours paid using this pay code to overtime hours instead of the overtime threshold calculation. You would only select this when the FLSA Ruleset is configured to report overtime hours separately. (For more information, see FLSA Ruleset.)
Round to Period Pay if Salaried Employee Select to have this pay code force time sheet pay to total period pay if salaried employee and hours paid are equal to standard hours. Note: The system uses the last detail timesheet entry for rounding.
Include when Calculating Shift Differential Pay Select if this pay code should include premium hours paid with this pay code when calculating the number of shift differential/longevity pay premium hours to be paid.
Charge Expense Admin (For Expense Reimbursements) Select if this pay code is an expense reimbursement. It is subject to the same administrative fees as a regular earning.
Third Party Administrator (Unemployment) Pay Code Enter the pay code used to report this pay type to a third-party administrator, usually an unemployment claims processor.
May Fund Voluntary Deductions Select to use the cash from this expense reimbursement pay code to fund voluntary payroll deductions.
Exclude From Payroll Overtime Recalculation Select to exclude this pay code when recalculating payroll batch overtime. Select this option if you use this pay code with a separate half-time pay code for overtime. > Note: Note: Changes made to this setting on the pay code form after processing the payroll batch will not be applied in the recalculation. For example, if the bonus/commission pay code is set to exclude when the bonus/commission payroll batch is calculated, changing the pay code to be included in overtime recalculation will not take place upon recalculation.
Qualified OT Factor This field is optional. Define the percentage of overtime pay that should be included in qualified overtime calculations by selecting the appropriate factor from the following options to ensure only eligible overtime amounts are reported in compliance with OBBBA’s rules. - – Select– (default) - 100% : Half time - Calculates at the standard 0.5 of the employee’s hourly rate. - 50% : Double Time (1x) - Calculates at the standard employee’s standard full hourly rate. - 33% : Time & A Half - Calculates at 1.5x of the employees standard hourly rate. - 25% : Double time (2x) - Calculates at 2x of the employees standard hourly rate.
Pay Code is Used to Pay Daily Overtime This field is optional. This is an informational setting that will be used in future reports to flag employees who may be receiving daily OT and require additional review for FG overtime.
Exclude from Qualified Tip Reporting This field is optional. This field is unchecked by default. Check this field if you want to exclude the pay code from Qualified Tip Reporting.
Include in Variable Salary Pay Select to include this pay code in the employee’s Variable Salary pay. Important! You must enable all pay codes within a payroll as Include in Variable Salary Pay, so the system performs the correct calculation. If you need to pay an employee with a mix of variable salary and non-variable salary pay codes, you must pay the non-variable salary pay codes in a different payroll batch. In addition, if you need to pay an employee with a mix of Pay Types for the variable salary pay codes, you must pay each Pay Type in a different payroll batch. The Variable Salary pay method accurately tracks the hours that employees actually work. For example, non-profit companies could use this pay method to track the work hours of their employees who are paid a standard salaried amount, so they can use these hours and their allocations for grant purposes. Important! When using Include in Variable Salary Pay, the pay codes paid to the employee must be set to Regular for the Pay Type. In addition, you must enable the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code on the System Parameters form to include the pay code in the employee’s Variable Salary pay.
Unpaid Variable Salary Time Select to reduce an employee’s Variable Salary pay by the percentage of unpaid hours assigned to the Unpaid Pay Code (default is disabled). For example, if an employee makes $3000 per pay period and they submit 100 hours, where 90 hours are worked and 10 hours are unpaid. This indicates that the employee’s wages should be reduced by 10 hours, so the system reduces the wages for the pay period from $3000 to $2700. This calculation works as follows: $3000/10 hours of unpaid time is $300, so $300 is subtracted from the gross pay. (On the voucher, the Unpaid Time hours display as the number of hours in the time sheet entry for the unpaid pay code, but the unit rate and amount display as zero (0).) > Note: Note the following: - The Unpaid Variable Salary Time field only displays when the Include in Variable Salary Pay field is enabled for the pay code. - The system still allocates wages for the reduced amount, except the pay is reduced by the unpaid hours.
  • The Unpaid Variable Salary Time field only displays when the Include in Variable Salary Pay field is enabled for the pay code.
  • The system still allocates wages for the reduced amount, except the pay is reduced by the unpaid hours. | Include in Certified Pay Report Detail Include in Certified Pay Report Fringe Summary | Select one of these, if appropriate: - Include in Certified Pay Report Detail: include a non-earning pay code in the Detail section of the Certified Pay Report. - Include in Certified Pay Report Fringe Summary: include any amounts paid with this pay code in the Fringe/Contribution Summary section of the Certified Pay Report. |
  • Include in Certified Pay Report Detail: include a non-earning pay code in the Detail section of the Certified Pay Report.
  • Include in Certified Pay Report Fringe Summary: include any amounts paid with this pay code in the Fringe/Contribution Summary section of the Certified Pay Report. | Certified Pay Report Fringe Class | Select the fringe class to assign to this pay code if it is included in the Certified Pay Report as a fringe benefit. The system uses this for some pay reports. | | TALX Pay Type | Select the TALX pay type download code used for employment verification. | | Pinnacle Pay Type | Select the Pinnacle Pay Type for discrimination testing against earning codes. | | Allow Description Override | Select to allow Description overrides for this pay code. | | Time Sheet Heading | Enter the heading for the Fax Back Time Sheet and the Summary Time Sheet. | | Obsolete Date | Enter the date this pay code is no longer used. | | Custom Option | Enter a custom option to enable special processing attributable to a custom feature. | | Per Diem daily rate overrides Certified Rate | Select to override the certified pay rate with the per diem rate. | | Collect Tip Sales on Time Sheet | If there is a reported tip pay code, you can select this field to display the Tip Sales column next to this pay code column in Summary Time Sheet Entry. (This is a memo field for recording the sale amount associated with the reported tip and is used for reporting purposes.) | | Exclude From ACA Hours Calculations | Select to exclude this pay code from the Large Employer Test Report and Eligibility Reports. | | Add to D/T Hours (Threshold) | Select to allow California O-type FLSA calculation of double-time hours (that is, where double-time (D/T) hours are paid at one times the regular rate of pay.) When there are more than two rates of pay or non-discretionary income, the weighted average method is used for calculation premium pay or HALF pay. (See O Method FLSA Calculation of D/T Hours.) | | Pto Wages | This field is used when building California Pay Data reporting information. Select this option if this pay code is used to compensate employees for PTO. This value will be counted as hours worked on that report. For more information about this feature, see the article on Creating California Pay Data Reporting Files. | | Total Compensation Category | Select the Direct or Indirect category to designate where the compensation displays in the total compensation statement in the Total Compensation dashboard in Employee Portal (EP). (See the Payroll Administration Guide for more information about the Total Compensation dashboard.) | | Include in Check Stub Gross Wage calculation | This field is a checkbox. On the Print Service Global Check Parameters form, under the Check Options, the Always Display Gross Wages option needs to be selected for this Include in Check Stub Gross Wage calculation field on the Pay Codes form to function. - When on the Print Service Global Check Parameters form, under the Check Options, when the - Always Display Gross Wages and the - Exclude Non-Cash Fringe from Gross Wages options are selected, then if the Include in Check Stub Gross Wage calculation field on the Pay Codes form is: - Unchecked - (default) The gross wage reflected on the check stub will exclude the non-cash fringe pay codes configured to include in gross wages. - Checked - The gross wage reflected on the check stub will include the non-cash fringe pay codes configured to include in gross wages. - When on the Print Service Global Check Parameters form, under the Check Options, when the - Always Display Gross Wages option is selected BUT the - Exclude Non-Cash Fringe from Gross Wages option is not selected, then if the Check Stub Gross Wage calculation field on the Pay Codes form is: - Unchecked - (default) The gross wage reflected on the check stub will include the non-cash fringe pay codes configured to include in gross wages. - Checked - The gross wage reflected on the check stub will include the non-cash fringe pay codes configured to include in gross wages. |
  • When on the Print Service Global Check Parameters form, under the Check Options, when the

  • Checked - The gross wage reflected on the check stub will include the non-cash fringe pay codes configured to include in gross wages. ## Defining Conditional Rules

Field Description

Defining Pay Code Calculation Rules

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Pay_Codes_Calculation_Rules.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Pay_Codes_Calculation_Rules.htm

Defining Pay Code Calculation Rules

Different pay code calculation rules are available based on the Calculation Method selected in the Pay Codes form. Refer to the relevant panel descriptions.

  • Standard Method Rules

  • Fixed Method Rules

  • Calculated Method Rules

  • Per Diem Method Rules

  • Calculated Fringe Benefit

  • Fringe Calculation Pay Codes

Standard Method Rules

The Standard Method Rules panel displays for pay codes with these calculation methods:

  • Standard

  • % of 401(k) Earnings

  • Rate x Hours Paid

  • Rate x Hours Paid (Selected Codes); also displays the Fringe Calculation Pay Codes panel

  • Rate x Full Hours Worked

  • Rate x Straight Hours Worked

  • Rate x Union Job Hours Worked

  • Rate x Union Project Hours Worked

Note: Note: The calculation methods that start with “Rate x” also display the Maximum Calc Hours/Maximum % of Gross Earnings field, which is described in Working with Pay Codes.

[Image: screenshot]

Complete the following fields:

  1. Enter the Factor to multiply against the pay rate to arrive at the actual rate used to calculate earnings. You would typically use this to define the rate to pay employees for overtime pay.

Note: A value of zero (0) or a value greater than or equal to .5 is acceptable for Standard Calculation Method pay codes. (Entering a negative value displays an error message.)

  1. Select the Rate Class:

  • For hourly or unit pay rates, select Straight or Premium time.

  • For flat pay rates, select Double Time or Other.

  1. Enter the Alt. Pay Rate #, which is the alternate employee pay rate to apply when this pay code is entered on a time sheet.

Note: If “1” displays in this field and the employee’s Sequence 1 Alternate Pay Rate is left blank, no data imports.

Fixed Method Rules

The Fixed Method Rules panel displays for pay codes with the Fixed calculation method. You can specify the amount in the Amount field or enter it directly on employees’ Other Earnings Records.

[Image: screenshot]

Complete the following fields:

  1. Select the Rate Class:

  • For hourly or unit pay rates, select Straight or Premium time.

  • For flat pay rates, select Double Time or Other.

  1. Enter the Default Pay Amount to use when this pay code is entered on employees’ Other Earnings Records.

  2. Select Default Auto Hours to automatically associate employees’ standard hours worked with this pay code. You would typically use this for a salary pay code.

Calculated Method Rules

The Calculated Method Rules panel displays for pay codes with the Calculated calculation method. The system stores the rate used as a default on the Pay Code Record instead of the Employee Payroll Record or Job Record.

[Image: screenshot]

Complete the following fields:

  1. Enter the Hourly/Unit Rate, which the system multiplies by the number of hours worked/units produced entered in conjunction with this pay code.

  2. Enter the Factor to multiply against the pay rate to arrive at the actual rate used to calculate earnings. You would typically use this to define the rate to pay employees for overtime pay.

  3. Select the Rate Class:

  • For hourly or unit pay rates, select Straight or Premium time.

  • For flat pay rates, select Double Time or Other.

Per Diem Method Rules

The Per Diem Method Rules panel displays for pay codes with the Per Diem calculation method.

[Image: screenshot]

Complete the following fields:

  1. Select the Per Diem Method used to calculate this pay code: percentage, per day, or mileage.

  2. Select the Per Diem Taxable Pay Code used for the taxable wages portion of the total wages entered when using the percentage per diem method.

If the pay code uses the per day method for per diem, this field stores the pay code which, if paid to an employee in the same batch, the amount paid using the pay code is reduced by the amount of the per day amount. For example, if regular wages are $1000, and per diem is $300, during initialization the regular wages are reduced by $300 for a net of $700.

  1. Select the Per Diem Non-Taxable Pay Code to use for the non-taxable wages portion of total wages entered when using the percentage per diem method.

  2. Select the Other Per Diem Taxable Pay Codes, which is the additional pay code for the non-taxable wages portion of total wages entered when using the percentage per diem method.

Calculated Fringe Benefit

The Calculated Fringe Benefit panel displays for pay codes with these calculation methods:

  • % of Gross Earnings

  • Rate x Hour Worked

Note: Note: These calculation methods also display the Maximum Calc Hours/Maximum % of Gross Earnings field, which is described in Working with Pay Codes.

[Image: screenshot]

Enter the Percent/Rate per Hour to calculate for the pay code.

Fringe Calculation Pay Codes

The Fringe Calculation Pay Codes panel displays for pay codes with the Rate x Hours Paid (Selected Codes) calculation method. Use this to set up employee taxable benefits such as insurance, uniforms, a company car, and so on.

[Image: screenshot]

Enter each of the Fringe Pay Codes for which hours will accumulate. The system uses these to calculate the fringe benefit amount. The Pay Description displays.

Creating Weighted Average Calculations for Pay Codes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Pay_Codes_Weighted_Average.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Pay_Codes_Weighted_Average.htm

Creating Weighted Average Calculations for Pay Codes

Your organization can create weighted average calculations for pay codes using the Weighted Average form. For example, California requires that employees be paid at their “regular rate” when using state-mandated paid time off. Other states, such as Arizona, permit a regular rate calculation rate.

Weighted averages are used for either pay codes that are set to include hours/amount paid in overtime calculations or those that include amount paid only:

[Image: screenshot]

[Image: screenshot]

When applied to a pay code, it provides a weighted average of pay over a specified time frame. You might use weighted averages when improving calculations for FLSA.

Use weighted average calculations when you need to:

  • Tie FLSA logic into weighted average pay code logic to pick up minimum wage rates when performing calculations.

  • Look at previous periods for compliance. (Typically, you would use lookback periods for salaried employees.)

Please note that you should use caution when using the pay code for tipped employees with pay rates below minimum wage. Currently the calculation does not gross all such rates up to the minimum wage. Also note that weighted averages do not include system-calculated shift differentials within the payroll that the pay code is used.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Select Calculated Weighted Average Pay Rate to indicate that the pay code will use a calculated weighted average pay rate.

  2. The Exclude FLSA Exempt Employees field is a checkbox. This field is un-checked by default. You can check it and click Accept to enable this option.

  • When unchecked, any FLSA exempt employee will have their pay rate recalculated when paid with applicable pay codes.

  • When checked, no FLSA exempt employee will have their pay rate recalculated. The pay rate will default to their standard hourly pay rate.

  1. Enter each required pay period weighted average calculations:
a. Select the Pay Period: weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly, or monthly.

The work week method can be used only with weekly and biweekly pay periods.

b. Select the weighted average Method:

  • Work Week: Based on a single payroll and the pay period is divided into seven-day increments. The weighted average is determined for the week encompassing the charge date.

  • Pay Period: Based on a single payroll. The weighted average is determined for all charge dates within the payroll.

  • Look back, full periods: Based on all vouchers with both a period start and period end date within the lookback period of the weighted average pay code’s charge date.

  • Look back, period end: Based on all vouchers with a period end date within the lookback period of the weighted average pay code’s charge date.

  1. — If you selected a look back method, enter the Lookback Period number and then indicate whether the period is Days or Months.
  1. Click Accept.
