Setting Up Pay Import Definitions

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Pay_Import_Definition.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Pay_Import_Definition.htm

Setting Up Pay Import Definitions

Use the Pay Import Definition form to set up pay data import definitions from tab-delimited, comma-delimited (CSV), or fixed-length data import files.

Note: Note: After you create a pay import definition, you assign it to the appropriate client(s) in the Time Sheet tab of the Client Details form.

Defining Time Sheet Pay Import Definition Parameters

Define the parameters required to import the pay data from the file in the Time Sheet Pay Import Definition panel.

[Image: screenshot]

To set up pay data import definitions:

  1. Enter the Definition ID for the pay import.

  • If you are creating a new import definition, use something descriptive, such as the name of the client that generates the data import file; the ID cannot include spaces. Also enter a short Description in the second field.

  • You can copy an existing definition to use as the basis for a new definition. Open the Actions menu and select Copy.

Note: You can only create and save a New Definition ID using the following characters: numbers zero through nine, lowercase letters a through z, and capitalized letters A through Z. Otherwise, an error message displays.

  1. Select Hourly Only to load only hourly employees from the import file. The system reports any salaried employees included in the file as download exceptions.

  2. In the File Format field, select a format for the data import:

  • Delimited—data is separated by a demiliter

  • Fixed‑Length—data is grouped together without spaces

If you select Delimited, select a delimiter from the Delimiter drop‑down:

  • Tab—space between data

  • Comma—comma (,) between data

  • Pipe—pipe (|) between data

  1. If necessary, enter the Number of Header Lines To Skip. This setting skips any header content lines in the import file, and begins the import after that. For example, if the first line in the file has the column headings, and the second line is the first record, enter 1.

  2. Select Rates Have Four Decimal Places if the pay rates have four decimal places.

  3. Select Allow Zero Pay On Time Sheets to pass zero amounts to the time sheet.

WARNING: Do not use the Special Processing Routine fields unless directed to do so by the PrismHR Customer Support Team.

  1. Enter the Special Processing Routine to use to convert the import file.

  2. Enter the Special Routine after Import for the system to execute immediately after importing the file from DOS; this can reformat the file.

  3. Enter the Post Processing Routine to execute at the end of the import process.

Note: Note: You must select All Special Routines Using Message Format if this is a web-based import. If this parameter is not selected, do not select it unless directed to do so by the PrismHR Customer Support Team.

  1. Select All Special Routines Using Message Format if the system uses a routine to pass back status and message information.

  2. Select Show Original File Data in Error Report if the error report should show the complete line of data from the original file.

  3. From the Use STD Allocation On drop-down, select the standard allocation to use for time.

Indicating Outcome of Existing Data After Data Import

Use the When Posting Imported Data to Time Sheets panel to indicate what happens to any existing data after a data import.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. From the Clear Existing Pay From Time Sheets for drop-down, select how to manage existing information:

  • All Employees: Clears all pay information for all employees in a batch when the file imports.

  • Employees in Import File Only: Employee data in the import file overwrites any existing data only for those employees. If other employee data exists in the payroll batch, their data is preserved.

  • None: No data is cleared.

Note: Note: If you chose to clear existing pay (All Employees or Employees in Import File Only), you can only select Overwrite existing amounts from the Update existing pay on time sheets drop-down. If you chose not to clear existing data (None), then you can choose a method for how to handle existing pay.

  1. From the Update existing pay on time sheets drop-down, select whether the imported data overwrites any existing pay data or adds to it.

  2. Select Auto Add Option (when employee is in file import but not on payroll) to have the system automatically add active employee time sheets.

  • Auto Add Active Employees to Payroll: The system automatically adds the time sheets for all active employees. There are some instances where employees will not be added:

  • The employee’s onboarding is still in progress.

  • It is a regular or special batch and the employee’s pay group is not included.

  • It is a manual batch.

  • Auto Add All Employees to Payroll: The system automatically adds all employees to the time sheet. This affects employees who were terminated and re-hired. They need to be paid but have not yet been re-hired in the system. They must also be assigned to the pay group in the import.

  • Do Not Auto Add: The system will not automatically add active employees.

  1. Select Recalculate Overtime Pay Rate to have the system recalculate overtime pay rates (based on the rate multiplier) on imported overtime hours that use the definition.

For example, an employee is included in the import with a pay rate of $10. If this option is not selected, then the employee will be paid $10. If this option is selected, then the employee will be paid at the overtime rate (such as $15 for a 1.5 multiplier).

Note: If you enable Recalculate Overtime Pay Rate, make sure the import file has a pay rate for the corresponding overtime pay code. Otherwise, an error message displays, “Recalculate Overtime Pay Rate is checked for Import Definition <import definition name> but the overtime Pay Code does not have a corresponding Pay Rate on line <letter> which will result in an incorrect pay calculation.”

Defining Standard Pay Imports

There are two methods for defining the pay import:

  • Mapping Data Import File Fields: Map pay codes from a time-keeping system to existing pay codes in PrismHR.

  • Mapping Data Import File: Import the pay data that has been prepared to match the client’s existing time sheet column headings in PrismHR.

Mapping Data Import File Fields

Use the Import Field Definitions table to map the fields of the data import file to those in PrismHR.

[Image: screenshot]

To map the data import file fields:

  1. Specify the fields in the file:

  • If the import file is tab- or comma-delimited, enter the Field #.

  • If the import file is fixed-length, enter the Start and End positions.

  1. Select the Field Name of the field into which the data imports. The system skips any missing fields or applies a default value.

  2. Use the Conversion Mask field only with direction from the PrismHR Customer Support Team. The system uses this value when data in the import file is in a non-native format.

Mapping Data Import File

Use the Import Translation Table to map the data import file codes to those in PrismHR.

[Image: screenshot]

To map the data import file codes:

  1. Enter the Foreign Code from the other system.

  2. Enter the Prism Code to use once the data imports, for example, REG.

  3. Select the PTO Type Flag if this code is for Vacation, Sick, or Other paid time off.

  4. Click Save.

Translation Code Description
V* Division
D* Department
J* Position Code
S* Shift Code
C* Project/Cost Center
L* Location Code

Note: For more information about setting pay codes, see the Importing More Than 20 Pay Codes Using Match Pay Import Method article in the Customer Resource Center.

Viewing Assigned Clients for Pay Import Definitions

Select Clients Assign To on the Actions menu to view the assigned clients for the selected pay import definition. The Clients Assigned To Pay Imports Definition form displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: If you do not select a Definition ID in the Pay Import Definition form and then select the Clients Assigned To option an error message displays, “You must enter a Definition ID first.” Click OK to continue.

The Clients Assigned to Pay Import Definition form displays all active, pending, inactive, terminated, and client-canceling clients assigned to the selected pay import definition ID.

Note: You can filter the client list by selecting an option from the Status field.

For example, Group Policy #G98787. | | Inactive | Select this if a payee is no longer used. You cannot select inactive payees. | ## Setting Up Electronic Payment to Garnishing Authority

Field Description
Transit Number The financial institution where the garnishing authority maintains the account.

Case Number Required? Optional. A case number might be required as part of the electronic file transfer addenda record layout.
Case Number Format Enter one or more codes for the SDU case number. Use any valid Basic MATCH operator. The MATCH function determines if a string matches a specific pattern of characters, numbers, or literal strings. Use a format code in the pattern, for example, len [A,N] [text] where len denotes the number of characters to match, A specifies only alphabetical characters, N specifies only numeric characters, and text specifies a literal string. Enclose literals in single quotation marks. For example, to display a Social Security number with hyphens, use 3N’-‘2N’-’4N.

Establishing Payroll Holidays

Use the Payroll Holidays form to establish the holidays when your organization does not process payrolls. Your organization must maintain these each year.

You can group holidays when you never process payrolls into a set, which allows the system to retrieve the holidays faster. This also makes it easier to set holidays in Client Details. For example, STDBANK could be for all of the bank holidays defined by the Federal Reserve. (Note: STDBANK determines bank holidays even when it is not listed in the Client Payroll Holidays Observed.)

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter a Holiday Code that represents holidays observed by your clients, for example, NYD or STD4.

  2. Enter the Holiday Description, for example, New Year’s Day or Standard 4 holidays.

  3. Click the Action icon [Image: screenshot] next to a holiday. The existing Holiday Dates for that holiday populate.

  4. Enter new Holidays Dates as required.

  5. Click Save.

Managing Payroll Option Templates

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Payroll_Option_Templates.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Payroll_Option_Templates.htm

Managing Payroll Option Templates

You can manage the payroll option templates that your organization uses to override specific calculations for one or more employees in a payroll batch using the Payroll Option Templates form. For example:

[Image: Payroll Option Templates form]

To manage payroll option templates, do the following:

  1. Enter or select the Template ID. When creating a new template, use something brief but descriptive such as SUPRETDED. You are limited to 10 characters so that it displays cleanly on the Summary Time Sheet Entry form.

  2. Enter the Description of the payroll options template that explains its purpose; for example, Suppress Retirement Deductions.

  3. Select ACH in the Suppress ACH field to prevent the generation of direct deposit transactions. (Employees normally paid by direct deposit will receive paper checks instead.) For example, you might select this option when the client wants to deliver live checks for year-end bonuses.

Note: Note the following:

  • This field applies only to employee ACH processing. It does not suppress electronic billing.

  • If you select Suppress ACH with Pay On-Demand selected, an error message displays stating that they cannot be enabled for the same payroll.

  • If you create a manual payroll with Pay On-Demand selected and then apply a Payroll Option Template with Suppress ACH selected within a timesheet, an error message displays stating that they cannot be enabled for the same payroll and the system does not apply the Payroll Option Template.

  1. Select the ACH Earn Type Limiter to specify the voucher types that will be processed as ACH transactions. Voucher types that you do not specify will be processed as paper checks. This overrides the settings defined in the Employee Details Deposit tab.

  • Blank: All checks (regular, vacation, and supplemental)

  • R: Only regular checks

  • V: Only vacation checks

  • S: Only supplemental checks

  • RV: Only regular and vacation checks

  • RS: Only regular and supplemental checks

  • VS: Only vacation and supplemental checks

  1. Select Suppress Other Earnings from the Suppress Earnings drop-down to prevent payment for other earnings.

  2. From the Suppress Deductions drop-down, select what payroll deductions (other than payroll taxes) to suppress for this payroll batch, if any. For example, you might need to suppress retirement deductions from bonus pay if employees opt not to have it deducted.

Note: Note the following:

  • When you run a supplemental batch, the system ignores voluntary deductions.

  • The system sends benefit deductions to arrears.

  1. Select Suppress Arrears to prevent the deduction of any amounts in arrears.

  2. Select Suppress Garnishments to prevent garnishment deductions.

  3. Select Suppress Benefits Calculation to suppress withholding of any benefits deductions and benefit accruals/arrears calculations. If you suppress benefits for this payroll batch, the system does not calculate benefits for the pay period, and therefore no benefit deductions go to arrears.

  4. Select Suppress Benefits Update to suppress the benefit update step that updates benefit-related deduction amounts on employee standard deduction records.

The system normally updates the benefits on the employees’ standard deduction schedules according to the parameters set at the system level. For example, if you change the amount of the employees’ contributions on the Group Benefit Plan, the system updates the employees’ standard deduction schedule to reflect the change. Use the Suppress Benefits Update option to suppress that update.

  1. Select Suppress Benefit Adjustments to suppress the processing of benefits adjustments.

  2. Select Suppress Loan Payment to prevent the loan payment from processing in the current payroll when the template is applied.

  3. Enter the Federal Tax Rate - Supplemental Pay, which is the rate to use as the federal tax percentage rate for all supplemental pay. This overrides the aggregate method.

  4. You can override the state tax percentage rate for all states, or for specific states.

  • All states: In the field, enter the State Tax Rate - Supplemental Pay, which is the rate to use for all supplemental pay. This overrides the rate for all states.

  • Specific states: In the table, enter the two-character State Code for each state that should use an override state tax rate, as well as the Supplemental Rate to use for each state.

  1. Use the Show Future Dated Checks On ESS drop-down to indicate whether employees can view paychecks in the payroll that have future dates in Employee Self Service or Employee Portal (EP). This overrides the global setting.

  • Yes: Checks in this payroll batch with dates in the future display.

  • No or Select: Future checks do not display.

Validating the Payroll Process

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Payroll_Process_Validations.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Payroll_Process_Validations.htm

Validating the Payroll Process

During the payroll process, PrismHR performs validations in the Users form. A system administrator can suppress these for payroll processors to prevent any of these validations or warning messages.

Validation and Process Step — Details

Lock Out - Calculation — This validation occurs when a system administrator has executed a system-wide lockout from the payroll calculation process. System administrators might do this when they must apply an emergency patch that affects the payroll calculation process. A system administrator can then suppress this validation and have one user test the updated process before allowing any other payroll processors to proceed.

Service Type “HRN” - Calculation — If a client’s service type is HRN (HR Services Only), the system does not allow users to calculate a payroll for the client.

Payroll Processing Through Date - Calculation/Finalization — This validation compares the value of the Payroll Processing Through Date set on the Lockout Payroll Processing Control Date form to the pay date being processed. If the payroll processing date is earlier than the pay date, the system prevents the process from continuing.

7 Days Future - Calculation — This validation does not allow the calculation to proceed if the pay date is more than seven days in the future.

ACH Days Warning - Calculation/Finalization — This is a warning that the system displays if the pay date is not far enough into the future to meet the ACH processing deadline.

Lock Out - Finalization — This validation occurs when a system administrator has executed a system-wide lockout from the payroll finalization process. System administrators might do this when they must apply an emergency patch that affects the payroll finalization process. A system administrator can then suppress this validation and have one user test the updated process before allowing any other payroll processors to proceed.

Do Not Service - Finalization — This validation does not allow the finalization process to proceed if the client is marked as Do Not Service.

Payroll Calculation Timing — This is a warning that the system displays if the payroll calculation was not completed on the same day as the finalization.

Re-Start Warning - Finalization — This is a warning that the system displays if it detects that the user is restarting the payroll finalization process.

Post Time Cutoffs - Finalization — This validation fails if the time at which the payroll finalization process starts is beyond any of the process cutoff times defined.

Terminated Client - Finalization — This validation checks the client status before termination.

Validate Pay Date (LE/LT Today) — This validation is based on the value of the Validate Pay Date Code value in System Parameters.

SUTA State Lockdown — This validation is based on the SUTA state lockdown rules defined in the system.

Payroll Finalization Warning — If this is selected, then the user can see the Finalize All button in SuperBatch.

Establishing Pay Schedules

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Payroll_Schedules.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Payroll_Schedules.htm

Establishing Pay Schedules

Use the Pay Schedules form to establish pay schedules, which users assign to pay groups. Each pay schedule determines:

  • The length of the pay period

  • The day the pay group is paid

  • The end of the pay period

This example displays a weekly pay schedule:

[Image: screenshot]

This example displays a semi-monthly pay schedule:

[Image: screenshot]

To establish pay schedules:

  1. Enter the ID for the Pay Schedule.

  2. Enter a short Description of the pay schedule.

  3. Specify the Pay Period and Pay Day(s):

Pay Period Pay Day(s) Details
Daily Daily-paid
Weekly Day of the week Select the day of the week for the pay date.
Biweekly Day of the week Select the day of the week for the pay date.
Semi-monthly Dates of the month, or the last day of the month, for first and second pay days Specify the days of the month for each pay date. You can also choose the last day of the month.
Monthly Date of the month, or the last day of the month
Monthly [Find nth Occurrence of Day of Week in Month] - Occurrence (1-5) - Day of the week Specify the occurrence of the day of the week for the pay date. For example, Third Wednesday.
Monthly [Find the Day of Week in the nth week of Month] - Day of the week - Week of the month (1-5) Specify the day of the week and the week of the month. For example, Thursday in the Second week of the month.
Monthly [Find Last Occurrence of Day of Week in Month] Day of the week Specify the last day of the month for the pay date. For example, Friday.
Monthly [Find the Day of Week after a Date in Month] - Day of the week - Date of the month Specify the day of the week for the pay date, and the date of the month after it occurs. For example, Thursday after 15.
Monthly [Find the Day of Week before a Date in Month] - Day of the week - Date of the month Specify the day of the week for the pay date, and the date of the month it precedes. For example, Monday before 20.
  1. Specify when the Pay Period Ends:

  • Daily, weekly, or biweekly pay schedules: specify the number of days before or after the pay date. For example:

  • For a weekly payroll, paid on Friday, with a period end on Wednesday of the same week, enter 2 Days Before the Pay Date.

  • Semi-monthly or any of the monthly pay periods: enter the number of days before or after the pay date, or the day of the month before or after the pay date. You can also enter EOM for the last day of the month, instead of number of days or the date. Semi-monthly requires values for each of the two pay dates. For example:

  • For a semi-monthly payroll paid on the 5th and 25th with period ends of EOM and 20th, enter 5 Days Before the Pay Date for both pay dates.

  • For a semi-monthly payroll paid on the 15th and EOM that has period ends of the 10th and 25th, you have some options for the 15th pay date: enter either 5 Days Before the Pay Date or 10 On this Day of Month Before the Pay Date. For the EOM pay date, enter 25 On this Day of Month Before the Pay Date.

  • For a monthly payroll that pays on the 15th with a period end of the 10th, enter 5 Days Before the Pay Date.

  • For a monthly payroll that pays on EOM with a period end of the 25th, enter 25 On this Day of Month Before the Pay Date.

  • For a monthly payroll that pays on the 25th but the period ends on the last day of that month, enter EOM On this Day of Month After the Pay Date.

  • For a monthly payroll that calculates the period end date as the last day of the following month, select On this Day of the Following Month. For example, if the pay date is 7/31/2025 and the pay period start date is 8/1/2025, then the period end date would equal 8/31/2025.

Important! The following options in these fields must be set to display the On this Day of the Following Month option:

  • Pay Period field: Select Monthly.

  • Pay Day field: Select End Of Month.

  • Pay Period Ends field: Enter EOM.

Note: If you try to select On this Day of the Following Month without setting the fields listed above, an error message displays.

  1. Click Save.

Maintaining Position Classifications

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Position_Classifications.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Position_Classifications.htm

Maintaining Position Classifications

You can maintain position class information, which can span multiple states, using the Position Classifications form.

To maintain position class information, do the following:

  1. Click the Back Office menu and select Position Classifications from the System|Change menu.

  2. Complete the following fields:

Field Description
Position Classification Enter or select a unique Position Classification ID.
Description Description of the position classification. For example, the job title.
EEO Position Group Enter or select the appropriate group. PrismHR automatically displays the EEO Position Class based on the EEO position group entered.
Special Requirements Select this option to indicate that this position classification involves special physical or mental requirements; the position must be closely monitored for ADA compliance when applications are accepted for any positions with this classification. The Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (ADA) prohibits employers from discriminating against qualified individuals with disabilities. Not including a particular person in the applicant pool for a certain job is nondiscriminatory only if that person does not meet any physical or mental requirements that have been identified as a essential functions of the position.
FLSA Exempt Select this option to exempt this position from the provisions of the Fair Labor Standards Act, which defines the workers who must be paid for overtime.
FLSA Type Select the type that best describes this FLSA exempt position. If the position classification is not FLSA exempt, do not select an FLSA type. - Standard Duties Test: The position satisfies standard duties test, or is exempt from duties test but still subject to standard salary test. - Exempt Executive Duties: The position satisfies the highly compensated duties test only. - Exempt Professional Duties: The position is exempt from the duties and salary tests (such as teachers, doctors, and lawyers).
  • Standard Duties Test: The position satisfies standard duties test, or is exempt from duties test but still subject to standard salary test.
  • Exempt Executive Duties: The position satisfies the highly compensated duties test only.
  • Exempt Professional Duties: The position is exempt from the duties and salary tests (such as teachers, doctors, and lawyers). | State | For each state: - Enter or select the state abbreviation. The system ties a state-specific workers’ compensation class to this position when it is performed by employees who work at a location within that state. - Enter or select the W/C Class Code applicable to the state for this position classification. The W/C Class Description displays. |
  • Enter or select the state abbreviation. The system ties a state-specific workers’ compensation class to this position when it is performed by employees who work at a location within that state.
  • Enter or select the W/C Class Code applicable to the state for this position classification. The W/C Class Description displays.
  1. Click Save.

Positive Pay Setup

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Positive_Pay_Setup.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Positive_Pay_Setup.htm

Positive Pay Setup

Use the Positive Pay Setup form to set up the positive pay file for the bank account. To access the form, open the Actions menu in Bank Accounts and select Positive Pay Setup.

The Positive Pay file is created by interpreting the specifications from the bank, entering the Header, File Header, Detail, and Trailer Record parameters, and entering the appropriate UniData Masking Codes.

[Image: Positive Pay setup]

Note: Note: Enter the masks required for the fields using standard UniData masking parameters. For example, R%10 places the item on a field of 10 zeroes. See Table 116 for a list of commonly used parameters.

To set up positive pay:

  1. Access the setup form: click the Back Office menu and select System|Change > Bank Accounts. Then, click the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] and select Positive Pay Setup.

  2. To copy existing positive pay information, click Copy From Another Bank Account. Enter the bank account ID and then click Copy.

  3. Enter a File Stub code. The system can group all accounts with the same file stub together for downloading, and it appends the year, month, and day to create the file name. For example, if you have multiple accounts with the same financial institution, enter the same File Stub for each account.

  4. Enter the positive pay File Extension that defines the file type, typically .txt.

  5. Set up the header record information, which determines the format for the header information for each record included in the overall positive pay file your organization will send to the bank:

  • Select the Header Record parameter that matches the header specification from the bank.

  • Enter the UniData Masking Parameter required for the record in the Masking Code field.

  1. Set up a detail record information, which specifies the format for the individual checks that are grouped under each header:

  • Select the Detail Record parameter that matches the detail specification from the bank.

  • Enter the UniData Masking Parameter required for the record in the Masking Code field.

  1. Set up a trailer record information; trailer records indicate the end of a group of checks:

  • Select the Trailer Record parameter that matches the trailer specification from the bank.

  • Enter the UniData Masking Parameter required for the record in the Masking Code field.

  1. Set up a file header record information, which is used for the entire file sent to the bank:

  • Select the File Header Record parameter that matches the file header specification from the bank.

  • Enter the UniData Masking Parameter required for the record in the Masking Code field.

  1. Click Save.
Parameter Definition Example
CRLF Carriage return and line feed Moves cursor to the next line
DD Converts a date format to a day of the month Converts a date format 7-14-2017 to 14.
DM Converts a date format to a numbered month Converts date format 7-14-2017 to 7.
DY Converts a date format to a numbered year Converts date format 7-14-2017 to 2017.
D4- Converts a UniData date to a date with month-date-year format Converts UniData date 14806 to 7-14-2008.
D2/ Converts a UniData date to a date with month-date-year format Converts UniData date 14806 to 7/14/08.
L#XX Left justify text and pad with spaces L#8 will cause “text” to appear as text_ _ _ _.
R%XX Right justify numbers and pad with zeros R% 8 will cause “1234” to appear as 00001234.

Note: Note: Go to http://www.ibm.com/us/ and search for the latest IBM UniData Commands Reference for additional UniData Masking parameter information.

Field Name Description
Top Margin This field is optional. Enter a number between 0 to 30 to indicate the number of blank lines to be added as part of the Top Margin on mvQuery checks.
Middle Margin This field is optional. Enter a number between 0 to 30 to indicate the number of blank lines needed to position the second section of mvQuery checks. (The default value is 3.)
Bottom Margin This field is optional. Enter a number between 0 to 30 to indicate the number of blank lines to be added as part of the Bottom Margin on mvQuery checks. (Default value is 0. Only use with third section on check.)
Test Margins? This is an optional field. You can set this flag to true when TESTING margins. You will see the number of lines and margin used when printing between each section. Select one of the following options from the drop-down: - No (default) - Yes

MICR Line Adjustments

Note: Note:

Field Name — Description

MICR Print Line — This is an optional field. Enter the line within the MICR print area to position the MICR. (Valid adjustment range is between 1 to 5. Default value is 3. Enter zero if no adjustment is required.)

MICR Indent — This is an optional field. Enter the value for the number of spaces to indent the entire MICR line from the left. (Valid indent range is between 0 to 30. Enter zero if no MICR indent is required.)

Transit Number Indent — This is an optional field. Enter the number of spaces to indent the Transit Routing Number of the MICR from the MICR indent. (Valid indent range is between 0 to 30. Enter zero if no Transit Number indent is required.)

Account Number Indent — This is an optional field. Enter the number of spaces to indent the Bank Account Number of the MICR from the MICR indent. (Valid indent range is between 0 to 30. Enter zero if no Bank Account Number indent is required.)

Special Font Adjustments

Note: Note:

  • This option will only work if mvQuery Custom Check Report field above is set to Yes.

Field Name — Description

Default Payee Font — This is an optional field. Select the font size for the Payee section on the check form. (Default value is Arial 9pt.) > Note: Note: Increased font size will affect window size adjustments.

Default Micr Font — This is an optional field. Enter the code from the table of the MICR font to use on checks. Valid range is between 1 and 7. (Default value is 1.)

Default Security Font — This is an optional field. Enter the code from table of the security font to use on checks. Valid range is between 1 and 6. (Default value is 1.)

MEMO Font Size — This is an optional field. Enter a number between 8 and 12 for the font size to display Memo field comments on customized fonts. Valid range is between 7 and 12. (Default value is 7.)

Check Stub Adjustments

Note: Note:

Field Name — Description

Current Earnings Detail Section — This is an optional field. Enter the number of lines to display on each check stub for the Current Earnings Detail section. (Valid range is between 0 and 100, Default value is 10. Zero means use the current default value.)

Deduction & Taxes Section — This is an optional field. Enter the number of lines to display on each check stub for the Deduction & Taxes section. (Valid range is between 0 and 100, Default value is 22. Zero means use the current default value.)

Direct Deposit Section — This is an optional field. Enter the number of lines to display on each check stub for the Direct Deposit section. (Valid range is between 0 and 100, Default value is 10. Zero means use the current default value.)

YTD Earnings Section — This is an optional field. Enter the number of lines to display on each check stub for the YTD Earnings section. (Valid range is between 0 and 100, Default value is 10. Zero means use the current default value.)

Paid Time Off Section — This is an optional field. Enter the number of lines to display on each check stub for the Paid Time Off section. (Valid range is between 0 and 100, Default value is 10. Zero means use the current default value.)

Employer Contributions Section — This is an optional field. Enter the number of lines to display on each check stub for the Employer Contributions section. (Valid range is between 0 and 100. Default value is 10. Zero indicates to use the current default value.)

Deduction Description Length — This is an optional field. Enter a description consisting of letters or numbers up to 15 characters. (You should test this description since it can effect how the data displays.)

Third-Party Payment Section — This is an optional field. Enter a number between 0 and 60 for the maximum number of lines to appear in the Third-Party Payment section. (Default value is 40.)

Void After _ Days Placement — This is an optional field. Enter a number between 1 and 3 to indicate the number of lines to move the “Void After <xx> Days” line up or down from its original position on the check. (Default value is 3.)

  • Click Clear STUB Values to clear the values from all fields in this section.

  • Click Reset STUB Value to Default to set the default value for all the fields in this section.

Check Window Adjustments

Field Name — Description

Address Window Indent — This is an optional field. Enter the value for the number of spaces to indent the check window address lines from the left. (Valid range is between 0 to 10. Default value is 5. A zero is considered no indent needed.)

  • Click Clear Window Values to clear the values from all fields in this section.

  • Click Reset Window Value to Default to set the default value for all the fields in this section.

Creating Payroll Processing Schedules

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Processing_Schedules.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Processing_Schedules.htm

Creating Payroll Processing Schedules

Use the Processing Schedules form to establish payroll processing information for your organization.

The processing schedule is set for each client on the Client Details Control tab.

To set up a payroll processing schedule:

  1. Enter the pay Processing Schedule ID. If you are creating a new schedule, enter something brief but descriptive, such as STD.

  2. Enter a brief Description for this pay schedule, such as Standard.

  3. Enter the Remote Entry Cutoff Days Prior to Pay Day, which is the number of days prior to the pay day when the client must submit time sheet information.

  4. Enter the Remote Entry Deadline, which is the time when the client must complete time sheet entry on the cutoff day.

  5. Enter the Delivery Days Prior to Pay Day, which is the number of days prior to the pay day that your organization must deliver checks/advices to the client.

  6. Select Skip Weekends to skip weekend days. Any count that crosses a weekend goes back two additional days.

For example, if the cutoff is five days before the pay date and the pay date is a Tuesday, then the cutoff day is the previous Tuesday (five days back, skipping the two weekend days). If the schedule does not skip weekends, the cutoff day would be Thursday (five days back, including the weekend).

  1. Click Save.

========================================================================

Creating Reason Codes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Reasons.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Reasons.htm

Creating Reason Codes

You can create codes that represent actions that Human Resources can take using the Reason Codes form. When a user performs a human resources action, such as a pay rate or position change, the system prompts you for a reason code.

To create a reason code, do the following:

  1. Click the Back Office menu and select Reason Codes from the System|Change menu.

  2. Complete the following fields:

Field — Description

Reason Code — Enter or select the Reason Code for this action. If you are creating a new reason, use something brief but descriptive, such as MI or PRO.

Reason Description — Enter the Reason Description, such as Merit Increase or Promotion.

Valid Actions — Select one or more Valid Actions to which this reason applies. For example, Promotion could apply to both Pay Rate Change and Job Change.

TPA Separation Code — Enter a TPA Separation Code if this reason code is for actions, typically terminations, used by a third-party when your organization reports the action.

Show on Web — Select Show on Web to display the reason code in Employee Portal (EP).

Obsolete On Date — Enter the Obsolete On Date when this reason code is no longer valid.

Termination Type — If this reason applies to termination, select the Termination Type.

  1. Click Save.

Globally Recalculating Workers Compensation on Vouchers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Recalculate%20Workers%20Compensation%20on%20Vouchers%20(Global).htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Recalculate Workers Compensation on Vouchers (Global).htm

Globally Recalculating Workers Compensation on Vouchers

Use this form to recalculate workers’ compensation accrual (liability) amount in payroll vouchers, for a specific date range. You can also use this form to update both vouchers and the employee workers compensation register.

Security

  • Service Provider Only.

  • Does not use Client Access Group security.

Note: Note: This utility will use the rates in effect on the voucher pay date. But, any workers’ compensation parameters taken from company records, state processing rules, or worker’s compensation policies will use current values.

Worker’s compensation will be recalculated using current values of the following parameters:

File Name Field Description
WC.RATES Gross Rate
WC.POLICIES Suppress G/L Accrual Suppress TRIA Premium Rate Template
WC.MODS Use Override Rates Override Rate
STATE.CODES W/C Wage Basis W/C Wages Sheltered Week Ends on Day Rate/Hundred
LOCATION.CODES Wc Policy Work Comp State
JOB.CODES Job Master Classification
JOB.CODE.MASTER Work Comp Class
EARNING CODES Factor Worker Comp Taxable Pay Class Rate Class Comp State
CLIENT MASTER W/C Policy Work Location Based W/c Calc Service Type
To access the form, click System. Under System Action, click Recalculate Workers Compensation on Vouchers (Global).

To globally recalculate workers’ compensation on vouchers:

  1. Enter a Start Date, which is the date from which you want to recalculate, by globally applying the changed rates, or other changed workers’ compensation parameters.

  2. Enter an End Date, which is the date up to which you want to recalculate, by globally applying the changed rates, or other changed workers’ compensation parameters.

  3. Click Update W/C Values. A job progress window displays. Select Yes to continue. (Since this is a global utility, the processing time depends on the date range selected.)

  4. Click Close. A message box appears, telling you the number of voucher records updated and number of voucher errors if any.

  5. Click OK to close the message box. The job progress window also closes now.

  6. Click Update Report. The Workers Compensation Recalculation Report opens, showing the amount of Accrual Change made for each affected employee.

  7. Click the XLS link on the Workers Compensation Recalculation Report to download the report.

  8. Click Error Report. The Workers Compensation Recalculation Error Report opens, showing the list of prior payroll vouchers not updated, and the reason thereof.

  9. Click the XLS link on the Workers Compensation Recalculation Error Report to download the report.

  10. Click Clear to clear the form.

Maintaining Relationship Codes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Relationships.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Relationships.htm

Maintaining Relationship Codes

You can maintain the codes that represent dependents’ relationships to employees using the Relationships form.

Note: Note: If your organization is an Aetna reporting PEO, you must use the two-digit code supplied by Aetna for the Relationship Code.

To maintain a relationship code, do the following:

  1. Click the Back Office menu and select Relationships from the System|Change menu, OR under Work Centers, under the Onboarding & Benefits section click Benefit Plan Maintenance. Under Group Benefit Plans (Global) click Relationships.

  2. Complete the following fields:

Field — Description

Relationship Code — Enter or select a Relationship Code that briefly represents the dependent’s relation to the employee. This field is required.

Relationship Description — Enter a description of the Relationship between a dependent and an employee.

Relationship Description (Spanish) — Enter a description of the relationship in Spanish.

Relationship Type — Specify the Relationship Type you want to use for the relationship. This field is required. Benefits Enrollment uses this setting when selecting dependents to enroll in benefit plans that include those relationships.

Plan Types — The plan types connected to the relationship allow the system to show the correct cost for employees based on the dependents specified during benefits and open enrollments. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

Obsolete — Select Obsolete if the relationship is no longer used. This hides the relationship so it cannot be selected by employees during enrollments. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

  1. Click Save to save the record.

  2. Click Delete to delete an existing relationship code. However, please note that:

  • If an existing Relationship Code is tied to a Dependent ID on the Employee Dependents form, then you cannot delete that Relationship Code on the Relationships form. You will receive an error stating Dependents are associated with . Code cannot be deleted.

  • If an existing Relationship Code is NOT tied to any Dependent ID on the Employee Dependents form, then you can delete that Relationship Code on the Relationships form without any error.

  1. Click Cancel to clear this form at any time. All unsaved changes will be lost.

Configuring an Invoice Logo Override for Sub-Cost Centers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Report_Print_Options.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Report_Print_Options.htm

Configuring an Invoice Logo Override for Sub-Cost Centers

You can use the Report Print Options form to add an override to the Print Service Report Logo Filepath when configuring a sub-cost center, which helps manage branding for all clients within the same cost center.

Note: Note the following:

  • This feature is only available for service providers.

  • When Sub-Cost Center is enabled on the Cost Centers form and you add a Print Service Report Logo Filepath override for this sub-cost center, the system produces invoices using this logo for clients with the assigned sub-cost center.

  • Configuring an Invoice Logo in this form overrides any configuration at the system level, unless there is an override in place that was configured at the client level in the Print Service Report Logo Filepath field on the Report Print Options form, which is accessible by selecting Report Print Options on the Actions menu in the Client Details form.

To configure an Invoice Logo override for a sub-cost center:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change, select Cost Centers.

  3. Enter or select a cost center that is a sub-cost center.

  4. Select Report Print Options on the Actions menu. The Report Print Options form displays.

  5. Specify the complete path to the location on the mvQuery print server for report logo images in the Print Service Report Logo Filepath field. For example, C:.gif.

  6. Click Accept.

Note: If you selected a cost center that is not a sub-cost center (Sub-Cost Center is not enabled on the Cost Centers form) or you did not select any sub-cost center an error message displays, “Print Service Report Logo Filepath override is only available for Sub-Cost Center.” Click OK to continue.

In this Field — Enter or select this

Client ID — The ID for the client whose information you want to capture. After entering or making a selection, the client’s name displays. (You can select multiple clients at once by selecting them from the list that displays and then click Done.) Note: You can only select clients in your client access group.

User ID — The ID for the user whose information you want to capture.

Start Date — This field is required. Enter or select a date to limit the report to a specific date or to use as the start date in the date range. Note: The total date range cannot be greater than one year.

End Date — This field is required. Enter or select a date to limit the report to a specific date or to use as the last date in the date range. Note: You cannot enter an End Date that is prior to the Start Date.

Identifying Employee Status

The Reason Code Report displays all the reasons that your client has entered into PrismHR. These reasons identify why employees are in a certain status. For example, if an employee terminated their employment, the reason code provides additional information such as whether the termination was voluntary or involuntary. To run the report:

  1. Click Back Office.
  2. From System|Change, select Reasons.
  3. Select a Reason Code
  4. Select Reason Code Report from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] .

The report columns are:

The system chooses the logo to display in the invoice header based on the following hierarchy:

Employer invoice logo the Invoice Logo File Path field in in Employer Details - The employer invoice logo displays in the invoice header; - Otherwise, the system checks to see if the global invoice logo is available.

  • Otherwise, the system checks to see if the client’s print service report logo is available. | Client’s print service report logo in the Print Service Report Logo Filepath field in Report Print Options | - The client’s print service report logo displays in the invoice header; - Otherwise, the system checks to see if the global mvQuery report logo is available. |

  • Otherwise, the system checks to see if the global mvQuery report logo is available. | Global mvQuery report logo in the mvQuery Report Logo Filepath field in the mvQuery Image Path Maintenance form in the backend system for PrismHR | - The global mvQuery report logo displays in the invoice header; - Otherwise, the system checks to see if the global blank image logo is available. |

PEO and non-PEO clients use different logic to define the employer whose information is included in the invoice. Whether the client is PEO or non-PEO is defined by the Service Type selected in the Contract panel in Client Details.

[Image: Service Type field set to “Professional Employer” in the Contract panel]

If the Service Type selected is … Then …
Professional Employer The client is a PEO client.
Any other value in the drop-down The client is a non-PEO client.

PEO Clients

If the client is a PEO, it uses the employer associated with the invoice. Typically this is the Employer specified in the Contract panel in Client Details.

[Image: Employer ID entered in the Contract panel]

Non-PEO Clients

If the client is non-PEO, it uses the Non-PEO Invoice Employer specified in the Billing Tab in Client Details.

Note: Note: The Non-PEO Invoice Employer field only displays in Client Details if the client is non-PEO.

[Image: Non-PEO Invoice Employer field in the Billing panel]

  • If the client does not specify a Non-PEO Invoice Employer, the Non-PEO Invoice Global Employer specified in Logo Path Maintenance is used.

[Image: Non-PEO Invoice Global Employer field under Invoice Parameteres]

  • If the client does not specify a Non-PEO Invoice Employer and does not specify a Non-PEO Invoice Global Employer, the Employer specified in the Contract panel in Client Details.

Once the system determines an employer to use in the invoice, it uses the employer name, address, and other information entered in Employer Details.

Employer Name

The Employer Print Name displays in the invoice as entered in Employer Details. If an Employer Print Name is not entered, the Employer Name is used.

[Image: Employer Details form with Employer Name and Print Name highlighted]

Employer Address

If an employer has return address information entered in the Invoice Information Maintenance panel in Employer Details, this is the address that displays in the invoice. If an address is not specified in the Invoice Information Maintenance panel, the employer’s standard address as entered in the Employer Details panel displays.

Note: Note: If the first return address field in the Invoice Information Maintenance panel does not have a value entered, the system uses the employer’s standard address.

[Image: Invoice Information Maintenance panel]

Other Employer Information

If any of the following fields have information entered in the Invoice Information Maintenance panel in Employer Details, the information displays in the PDF version of the invoice (it is not included in the display version).

  • Contact Name

  • Invoice Contact Phone

  • Invoice Contact FAX Number

  • Invoice Email Address

  • Invoice Website

Field Description
Category Select from display categories, such as Report.

Creating S-Corp Benefit Tax Adjustments

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/S-Corp%20Benefit%20Tax%20Adjustment.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/S-Corp Benefit Tax Adjustment.htm

Creating S-Corp Benefit Tax Adjustments

Use the S-Corp Benefit Tax Adjustments form to calculate and create tax adjustments to Federal Income Taxable wages ONLY (no state or local income tax) for S-Corp owner employees for the amount of company paid benefit plans (up until the date the utility ran).

The process selects the records in the Employee Benefits Register for each employee that fits the criteria and totals the company contributions to any or all benefit plans for the selected insurance class. Once the process has completed the calculation and accumulation of fringe pay amounts, a report is generated that details the fringe benefit amounts for each employee.

Fringe benefits are often considered extra benefits outside of a company’s standard health insurance offerings. The employer is the provider of the fringe benefit, even if a third party provides the actual benefit. For example, an employee may receive legal services through an attorney that is paid by the employer, but the employer is still the provider of the fringe benefit. Before using this process, ensure that a Fringe Pay Code was set up. The total amount paid by the client for the applicable benefits will be assigned to this pay code and appear on each adjustment voucher. The pay code must be a non-cash fringe benefit type, otherwise, taxes will be deducted if the wrong pay code is selected.

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form click Back Office > Employer|Action > S-Corp Benefit Tax Adjustments.

To calculate and create S-Corp benefit tax adjustments:

  1. Complete these fields as required:

In this field — Enter this

Year — The year for the download. Defaults to the current year.

Quarter — The quarter for the download. Select 1, 2, 3 or 4 depending for which quarter you want to calculate.

Insurance Class Code — Click the link and select the insurance classes to include in the report. Employer contributions for plans with these classes will be calculated. When selection is complete, click Done to close the Select Insurance Classes list.

Fringe Pay Code — Click the link and select the fringe pay code.

Tax Adjustment Date — Click in the field and select the adjustment date for the report.

Employer ID — Click the link and select the employer or leave blank to select all employers.

Client ID — Click the link and select the client for the report or leave blank to select all clients.

State Income Tax Code — If you want to change the tax adjustment amount to consider that state income tax, enter the state income tax codes. Otherwise, the system does not take the state income tax into account when calculating the Tax Adjustment.

  1. To see a preview of the report, click Preview Changes. The system displays the processing status and notifies you when it is complete.

  2. Click Close. The system displays a preview and provides a Download Report link.

  3. When you are ready to make the adjustments, click Generate Adjustments.

Search

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Search_Field.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Search_Field.htm

Searching Techniques

The Search field at the top of the PrismHR window enables you to search for forms, employees, and other items. This field gives you quick access to features without needing to navigate to them in the menus.

To initiate a search, start entering to do a broad search or narrow the search using an initial letter followed by a colon:

  • A: Application Search (Features/Forms)

  • C: Client Search

  • E: Employee Search

  • R: Report Search

To initiate a broad search:

  1. Enter the text of the item you want to find. As you type, the system presents a list of suggestions.

  2. Click an item to open it. If there is an arrow next to the item [Image: screenshot] , click it to open the form as a layer over the current page. This makes a second form available while continuing to display the main form.

To search for a feature or a form (application):

  1. Type A: and then enter the name of the feature you want to access. As you enter, the list filters to the features that match your search.

  2. Click the feature’s name to open the form or click the arrow to open the form in a new window and layer it over the current page.

To search for a client:

  1. Enter C: and then type the name of the client. As you type, the list filters client records that match your search. The Search field lists only clients to which you have access.

  2. Click the client name to open the Employee Details form.

To search for an employee:

  1. Enter E: and then enter the name of the employee. As you enter, the list filters to employee records that match your search. (The Search field lists only employees to which you have access.)

Note: Note the following:

  • If an employee works for more than one client, the Search field displays each client ID and name in the preview list, so you can easily distinguish which employee/client match to select.

  • If relatives who work for the same client have the same first and last name, such as a father and son, the system lists the middle initial for these employees, so you can easily distinguish between them.

  • An employee’s termination date displays in the results, so you can quickly verify whether the employee currently works for the client.

  • You can enter an employee’s preferred name, if applicable, the same way that you would search for their first or last name. (Note: If you enter an employee’s legal first name in the Search field and they have a preferred name, the preferred name displays first in the search results with the legal first name displaying in parentheses.)

  1. Click the employee name to open the Employee Details.

Note: Note: To see employees with an onboarding status displayed, you must be enrolled in the Onboarding module.

To search for a report:

  1. Type R: and then type the report name. As you type, the list filters reports that match your search. The Search field lists only reports to which you have access.

  2. Click the report name to open the report’s selection criteria screen.

  3. Make your selections and then run the report.

Configuring System-Level Settings for Coronavirus-Related Paid Leave

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/SP-Coronavirus_Setup.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/SP-Coronavirus_Setup.htm

Configuring System-Level Settings for Coronavirus-Related Paid Leave

Note: Note: Known Issue with Billing - Workarounds are now available for this issue. See the article Compliance with COVID-19-Related Legislation on the CRC for more information.

The Families First Coronavirus Response Act establishes coverage rules for employees who must take time off due to the COVID-19 outbreak. Use this form to configure system-level settings for paid leave defined by this act.

For detailed, step-by-step instructions on setting up COVID-19 features, please see the article Setting Up Coronavirus-Related Paid Leave on the Customer Resource Center.

Note: Note: Please ensure that you set up all necessary COVID-19 pay codes and bill codes before you edit this form.

To set up pay codes for emergency paid leave:

  1. Select the bill codes you want to assign for system-level COVID-19 leave tracking.

  2. Select one or more pay codes to associate with emergency FMLA, self care-related paid sick leave, and dependent care-related paid sick leave. See the table below for descriptions of each field.

  3. Set the wage and tax cap logic, as appropriate.

  4. When you finish, click Save.

Assigning Pay Codes for Emergency Paid Leave

Pay and Billing Event Settings

Field — Description

Emergency Tax Credit Rebate Billing Event — Select the billing event you set up to track COVID-19 paid leave credits.

Emergency Medicare Credit Rebate Billing Event — Select a billing event to track employer-side Medicare tax credit rebates for COVID-19 leave.

Emergency Paid Sick Leave (Self-Care) Pay Code — Select or enter a pay code to use for COVID-19-related sick leave payments when the employee takes time off to care for themselves.

Emergency Paid Sick Leave (Dependent-Care) Pay Code — Select one or more pay codes to use for COVID-19-related sick leave payments when the employee takes time off to care for a dependent.

Emergency FMLA Pay Code — Select one or more pay codes to use for COVID-19-related FMLA payments. For example, you can enter one pay code with a Factor of 1.00 and another with a Factor of 0.67.

Cap and Credit Settings

You can configure credit cap settings according to your needs. Refer to the following table for descriptions of the fields and their settings. The federal legislation defines the creditable wage limits as follows:

Aggregate

  • FMLA: $10,000

  • Sick (Dependent-Care): $2000 OR $5110 minus credits from Sick (Self-Care), whichever is less

  • Sick (Self-Care): $5110 minus credits from Sick (Dependent-Care)

  • If an employee works 8 hours or fewer per day, there is a $200/day cap

Daily

  • FMLA: $200 per time sheet line item

  • Sick (Dependent-Care): $200 per time sheet line item

  • Sick (Self-Care): $511 per time sheet line item

Note: Note: We strongly recommend setting wage cap and tax credit cap logic to the same value. Using different settings can cause serious irregularities.

Field — Description

Default Wage Cap Logic — The federal legislation specifies the legal extent to which employers must compensate workers for coronavirus-related leave. Employers can pay employees more, but they only receive credit up to the defined limits. Select whether to use the daily caps or overall (aggregate) caps specified in the legislation. This setting reduces employee pay to the appropriate limits, if it exceeds those limits. While we strongly recommend against using this setting in general, you can select No Limits if you don’t want employee pay reduced in this way.

Default Tax Credit Cap Logic — Select whether to enforce the federally defined tax credit caps. You can limit based on either the aggregate or daily cap. This should use the same setting as Default Wage Cap Logic.

Default Suppress Client Rebate — The client rebate is reflected as a separate bill pending entry in an invoice line item. The line item shows total credits accumulated this pay period, along with the rebate associated with this invoice. If the entire rebate is not owed at once, the system tracks rebates that are owed and that can be taken, based on the limit structure. If you don’t want the system to automate the rebate process, select this option. Otherwise, select an option for Default Client Tax Credit Rebate Cap Logic, below.

Default Client Tax Credit Rebate Cap Logic — If you choose not to suppress the client tax credit rebate, you can select an option for applying caps to this rebate. You can either apply No Limits (the system bills the client and subtracts all credit accrued ) or you can cap at the client’s Form 941 liability, where the rebate for this pay period is calculated based on whether there is 941 liability from prior payrolls against which it can rebate. In other words, the amount available to rebate for a payroll = QTD 941 Liability minus QTD system-generated rebates. For example, if you have $1,000 in creditable wages and Medicare tax for a payroll (no 941 liability) and, quarter-to-date, you have $5,000 in un-rebated 941 liability, you can rebate the full $1,000 for the payroll because there is enough liability to rebate against. > Note: Note that if the rebate for a payroll is higher than the 941 limit, the system creates a client bill pending entry with a date of 10/14/2114. This is an intentional programming decision to prevent the entry from being pulled into the next payroll. For more information about this setting, see the Known Issues section at the top of this document.

Setting Up Client-Specific Overrides

Use the COVID-19 Emergency Processing Parameters Client Overrides form to establish client-specific settings, if necessary. These fields mimic the system-level fields for COVID-19 credit logic.

To set up client overrides:

  1. On the COVID-19 Emergency Processing Parameters form, select the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] .

  2. Select Client Overrides. A new form displays.

  3. Add clients to this form as needed. To add clients, enter the Client ID. The Client Name populates automatically.

  4. Select the appropriate options for each client override parameter. These are identical to the system-level settings.

  5. When you finish, click Save.

Creating 1095-C Election Text

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/SP_1095C_Election_Text.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/SP_1095C_Election_Text.htm

Creating 1095-C Election Text

This is the first step in setting up employee access to Forms 1095-C (See Giving Employees Access to Form 1095-C).

Set up the Early 1095-C Election page in Employee Portal (EP) with the 1095C Election Configuration form. This lets employees choose to receive their Form 1095-C electronically and saves money on printing and mailing costs. Employees also receive their Forms 1095-C earlier than a form sent by mail.

  1. In PrismHR, open System > Change > System Parameters and select 1095C Election Text from the Actions menu.

  2. Complete these fields as required.

Field — Description

Lockout Period — Period during which employees are unable to access their 1095-Cs. Set 1095C Elect Disable From and 1095C Elect Disable To to set this lockout period. Outside of these dates, employees are able to access the Early 1095-C Election page.

1095C Elect Intro — Displays text in the Introduction field.

1095C Elect Terms — Displays terms to help employees understand how to use the page.

1095C Disabled Message — Displays when the page is not available.

1095C Elected Message — Displays when employees return to the page after electing to receive 1095-Cs electronically.

1095C Elect Accept — Statement that displays above the Click Here to Accept check box on the page. This implies that an employee agrees with the terms and conditions established by your organization.

  1. Click Save.

Set up information to the Corporate Edition with the Corporate Edition form. Fill in the fields as required.

Defining a Custom Process

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/SP_Custom_Process.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/SP_Custom_Process.htm

Defining a Custom Process

Custom processes allow your organization to define your own menu items with in PrismHR.

To access this form:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change, select System Parameters.

  3. From the Actions menu, select Custom Process.

  4. Complete these fields as required.

Item — Description

Process ID — Enter a unique process ID.

Name — Process name that displays in menu and search.

Category — Menu where the custom process belongs.

Sub-Category — Indicates where the custom process belongs within the selected menu. If you select Other, you can enter a custom sub-category.

Disabled — Suppresses the display of custom processes.

Display in Menus — Displays the custom process in the menu to users who have access to it.

Display in Search — Displays the custom process to users who have access to it and use the search field to find it.

Disable Resizing — Enable to prevent the custom process from adjusting its size based on the browser window.

Role Specific — If the menu item is limited to a specific user role, select Service Provider or Worksite Manager as appropriate. If the menu item should be available to user roles of either type, leave this drop-down set to Select.

Version Type — For future development. Does not currently impact the functionality of PrismHR.

  1. Click Save.

SSO Forms

You can enter single sign-on information in the SSO Forms panel if the custom process is for something defined in SSO Services.

To access this form:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change, select System Parameters.

  3. From the Actions menu, select Custom Process.

  4. From SSO Forms, select SSO Service.

  5. Leave the SSO Action field blank for tandem SSO. Only enter an SSO Action if you know the specific value that should go in this field for a legacy SSO service.

  6. Select the appropriate option from Use SSO Init:

  • SSO: Use the legacy SSO code. This is used only for products developed a while ago.

  • Tandem SSO: Use the SSO methods in the PrismHR Services API. This is the typical selection.

  1. External App indicates whether this was defined as an external application in SSO Services. You cannot edit it here.

  2. Click Save.
