Setting General System Parameters

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/SP_Details.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/SP_Details.htm

Setting General System Parameters

You can set up general parameters on the System Parameters panel.

To set up general system parameters:

  1. Complete these fields as required.
Field Description
Installed Company Name Business where the software is installed. This name displays at the top of some reports.
Custom Options Suffix Read-only field used if a system has custom processing installed.
Weeks In Year for Benefit Calculations Calculates payroll deduction amounts for employee benefit contributions. Options are 48 or 52 weeks, but you can override this setting for individual clients. This setting has consequences for the calculation of weekly, bi-weekly,semi-monthly, or monthly premiums. Typically, 48 weeks is recommended because the total amount deducted from the client and employee always equals the same monthly premium (and invoice) from the insurance carrier. You can override this at the client level (Client\ Change\ Benefit Plan Setup).
Minimum Check Amount Validation amount used during payroll calculation that flags checks with gross pay amounts less than this value. (This dollar amount is per pay period with a recommended amount of 0.00.) If a check does not meet this minimum amount, the system flags it and may require manager approval before finalization. Note: This minimum amount can be set at both the system level and the client level, with the client-level setting overriding the system-level setting. You can update or remove this limit as needed, or process the required approval if a check does not meet it.
Maximum Check Amount Validation amount used during payroll calculation that flags checks with gross pay amounts greater than this value. (This dollar amount is per pay period.) If a check exceeds this maximum amount, the system flags it and may require manager approval before finalization. Note: This maximum amount can be set at both the system level and the client level, with the client-level setting overriding the system-level setting. You can update or remove this limit as needed, or process the required approval if a check exceeds it.
Tax Calculation Lock (Formerly “Cross-Company Tax Calculation Lock”) > Note: Note: This field was renamed from “Cross-Company Tax Calculation Lock” to “Tax Calculation Lock,” and the “No” setting was renamed to “Yes, Lock on Client.” However, the functionality of this setting has not changed. Tax calculation locking mechanism used when many employees work for multiple clients. This ensures that calculations such as retirement plan contribution limits are handled correctly. Options are: - Yes, Lock on Client: This is the equivalent of the old “No” feature. It has the same exact functionality: it locks payrolls when multiple payroll batches within a single client include the same employee. Payroll processors can only process the batches one at a time, rather than simultaneously. - Yes, Lock on Employee: Locks payrolls when one or more payroll batches include the same employee. Users can only process those payrolls one at a time rather than simultaneously. This lock applies even if the employee is being paid on batches under two different employers or clients. - Yes, Lock On Employer: Locks the calculation at the employer level. If an employee works for two or more clients of the same employer, users can only process those clients’ payrolls one at a time. If the employee is in payroll batches for different clients and those clients have different employers, calculations are not locked and payrolls can be processed simultaneously.
Automatic Mail Code An existing delivery code to set automatic mailing capability, when items in a payroll batch are shipped. When a delivery method code is entered in this field, the system sets all payrolls that use the same delivery method to Mailed. Payrolls with different delivery methods must have their status manually set to Mailed. For example, if USPS is entered as a code, the system sets all payrolls sent by US mail to Mailed. Payrolls sent by FedEx must have their status manually set so that the tracking number or other information is logged. Enter ALL to set all payrolls to Mailed status, regardless of the Delivery method. A blank entry means users must manually change the status for every payroll.
Consolidated ACH File Processing Used Type of Automated Clearing House (ACH) processing method used. Options include: - No: Uses the non-consolidated method which processes one ACH file for each individual checking account as if they were separate ACH originators. This requires that ACH is processed in the backend system for PrismHR. - Yes: Uses the consolidated method which processes multiple checking accounts for one ACH originating bank. ACH is processed using the features in PrismHR. - Company: Employs the consolidated method with company batching, which processes multiple checking accounts for one ACH originating bank and sorts by client.
  • No: Uses the non-consolidated method which processes one ACH file for each individual checking account as if they were separate ACH originators. This requires that ACH is processed in the backend system for PrismHR.
  • Yes: Uses the consolidated method which processes multiple checking accounts for one ACH originating bank. ACH is processed using the features in PrismHR.
  • Company: Employs the consolidated method with company batching, which processes multiple checking accounts for one ACH originating bank and sorts by client. | Standalone FSA Reimbursement | Processes FSA reimbursements in standalone batches. If you manage your own FSA, check this box which allows you to do standalone payroll batches for FSA Reimbursements. This is a global setting and will be applied to all clients. | | Use Legacy W/C Rate Tables | Enables legacy Workers’ Compensation Rate Table Maintenance methodology. The system then employs template-based W/C calculations that incorporate policy and rate group designations. Note: You cannot select this option until you have all the codes required to support it. Otherwise, payroll processors cannot initialize payroll batches. | | SSN Mask Option | Displays employee social security numbers in PrismHR and Employee Portal (EP). Review these SS masking options before making a selection. Results are the same for PrismHR and Employee Portal (EP) unless otherwise specified. - Leave Blank ( ): Appears blank. - Show All (123-45-6789): Full SS# is displayed. - Show Last Four (###-##-6789): Masks all but the last 4 digits. - Mask All (###-##-####): Masks all the digits. - Show EE ID if Active Client(X12345): Show employee ID for active client in PrismHR and masks all but the last 4 digits in Employee Portal (EP). - Don’t Mask If DIF download: DIF downloads are not masked in PrismHR and all but the last 4 digits are masked in Employee Portal (EP). - Show EE NUMBER if Active Client: Displays the employee number for an active company in PrismHR and masks all but the last 4 digits in Employee Portal (EP). | | New Hire Proper Case Conversion Option | Converts new employee names and addresses to the proper case when they are hired. Options are: - Employee Name - Employee Address - Both Name and Address |
  • Employee Name
  • Employee Address
  • Both Name and Address | Third Party Check Printing Mode | Configures Third Party Check Printing Mode: - –Select–: Third party checks are not processed. - Batch Mode: Consolidates liabilities and prints third party checks in batch mode. - Real Time: Prints third party checks when a payroll batch posts with other payroll reports. If you have deductions for consolidated garnishments, when you post payroll the system will print checks for the payee. Important! If you do not select an option in the Third Party Check Printing Mode field (that is, this field selection remains “–Select–”), the system processes as though it was in Batch Mode. However, to access third party check processing, you must set this field to Batch Mode. > Note: Note: You can also manage Third Party Check Printing Mode using the Third Party Check Maintenance section in the Print Service Global Check Parameters form (see Setting Up Default Global Check Printing Parameters), along with the third party check format, logo, and signature. The setting is always the same setting in both forms. | | Void Lockout Year | Prevents pay date voids in that year and all previous years. The system tests Void Lockout Year before it tests Void in Current Period and fails first. | | Validate Pay Date Code | The method that PrismHR uses to validate the pay date. Options include: - No Validation: No pay date validation. - Pay Date < Curr Date, Auth Code Required: If the pay date is before the current date, an authorization code is required. - Pay Date < Curr Date, Approval Required: If the pay date is before the current date, the payroll requires user approval. - Pay Date < Curr Date, Warning Only: If the pay date is before the current date, payroll processors see only a warning. - Pay Date <= Curr Date, Auth Code Required: If the pay date is on or before the current date, an authorization code is required. - Pay Date <= Curr Date, Approval Required: If the pay date is on or before the current date, the payroll requires user approval. - Pay Date <= Curr Date, Warning Only: If the pay date is on or before the current date, payroll processors see only a warning. | | Maximum ACH Batch | Amount processed in a single ACH transaction batch. Any amount in excess of this is moved to the next batch in the file. | | Minimum ACH Window | Minimum number of days required to process ACH transactions. Any payroll batch with an ACH transaction must be at least this many days in the future. If not, the system will generate paychecks to print instead of ACH transactions. For example, let’s say you put a 0 (zero) in this field. If you run a payroll dated today and the employee has direct deposit, that direct deposit item would go as a direct deposit when you build the file tonight. It would go the bank now, but it will not get to the employee’s account until tomorrow because the day has already passed. However, let’s say you put a 1 (one) in this field. If you run a payroll dated today and the employee has direct deposit, the system will give you a message that says this will be a live check. | | ACH Billing Days Offset | Number of days to offset ACH for invoicing. For example, if the system drafts the ACH the day before the payroll, enter -1 in this field. > Note: Note that all ACH files are date-sensitive, so you can post a payroll and create/send the NACHA file several days before the effective date. The funds for both paying and collecting will follow the effective date of each transaction. - A negative number indicates the number of days before the pay date - Zero (0) indicates on the pay date - A positive number indicates the number of days after the pay date If you enter a negative number, you will draw the funds that number of days before the pay date. You can override this setting at the client level. |
  • A negative number indicates the number of days before the pay date
  • Zero (0) indicates on the pay date
  • A positive number indicates the number of days after the pay date | Days Into Future for ACH Selection | Number of days into the future for ACH selection after which PrismHR selects ACH transactions to submit to the ACH originating bank. Check with your financial institution to make sure they allow you to send transactions no matter what the date is. Some institutions restrict you to a certain number of days. For example, if you enter 99 in this field, you may build the ACH file up to 99 days ahead of today’s date. However, if you enter 2 in this field, you may only build the ACH file 2 days ahead. This is important for organizations that build ACH files and run payroll on Monday or Tuesday for a Friday pay date. | | | | Suppress Automatic Benefit Adjustment | Suppresses automatic calculation of benefit adjustments on a global basis. This is not recommended because all Benefit adjustments (which are automatically created by the system) would be suppressed. You can set up overrides at individual benefit or client level, if applicable. | | | | Suppress Arrearage Vouchers | Suppresses the global creation of arrearage vouchers. This is a zero voucher, created when an employee is active, but they do not get paid. This is a global setting that may be overridden at the client level (Client | Change | Client Controls). > Note: Note: The PrismHR Customer Support Team strongly recommends that you do not select the Suppress Arrearage Vouchers option. | | Suppress Billing In Initialization/Post | Suppresses the call to the billing routines in the payroll batch calculation and finalization processes. Select this field only if you have consulted with your Implementation Specialist or the PrismHR Customer Support Team. | | | | Suppress TEBA (Accelerated Billing) | Suppresses accelerated billing of benefit premiums when an employee is terminated. For example, if an employee is terminated mid-month and coverage goes to the end of the month, the system will accelerate the billing to the client and bill the client for any deductions that have not yet been taken from the employee. When you take the deductions from the employee, the client receives a credit. | | | | Suppress Benefits Billing Thru Date | Suppresses benefits billing. This is used for a short time after a conversion to not bill for benefits already billed on a prior system. | | | | Pay Card Account | Defines a global pay card account for all clients. Instead, a message displays to indicate that all of the new hire’s net pay will be deposited into their direct deposit account. | | | | Company Name Display for Employee Experience Header | The client name to display in all employee experience products (Onboarding, Benefits Enrollment, and Employee Portal). Note: The Enable payroll live check calculation warning field is disabled by default at the system level, but can be overridden at the client level. | | Supplemental Tax Override Rules | This field has the following drop-down options: - Respect Employee Override: When you select this option, the system will apply the employee level income tax overrides to calculate taxes to supplemental wages regardless of the override type selected on the Employee Details (Tax) form. - Ignore Employee Overrides except Block Withholding: When you select this option, the system will ignore any employee level income tax calculation override other than Block Withholding and those which are supplemental tax specific overrides. > Note: Note: This does not work if custom feature code VSUPPLEMENTAL is enabled in the System Parameters form. |

The system will attempt to take the full flat amount child support on both the regular payroll batch and any special or manual batches for the same pay period. - Checked: If an employee with a flat sum child support garnishment or creditor wage garnishment, is paid both in a regular payroll batch and one or more special or manual payroll batches for the same pay period, then the system will automatically deduct only up to the full amount of that flat child support garnishment amount between all regular, special, and manual payroll batches. No adjustments are needed for the special or manual payroll batches. When enabling this logic, the standard garnishment deduction report has been enhanced to provide information on the subsequent batch deduction amounts. Also when this field is checked, the system will ensure that the garnishment amount for a State Levy docket does not exceed the flat amount of a given State Levy docket minus the sum of all garnishment deductions made for said docket, during the applicable pay cycle. If an employee has been paid in a previous payroll batch for the same pay period with garnished wages, the State Levy garnishment will only deduct the difference of the total flat amount less the amount garnished on a prior batch for that period. If the State Levy garnishment is reduced to zero, then the system will not calculate garnishment fee for the State Levy as the garnishment for State Levy on current payroll is not deductible. > Note: Note: Now when you process a manual or a special payroll batch, and if any employee has a flat amount as a garnishment which is not for child support, then the system will provide a warning for the same indicating the Employee ID and the docket number so that you can review and make adjustments as needed. (This will work only if the Enhanced Garnishment Capping field is checked.) | | |

This is used to complete tax processing or daily reporting before the check is posted. If clients are doing same day checks, payroll must be done by this time to process the ACH and positive pay files to send to the bank. This uses the Central Time Zone and Military Time. | | | | Lockout | Method used to temporarily lock users out of certain types of processing. Setting Up Documentation Servers and Directories

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/SP_Documents.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/SP_Documents.htm

Setting Up Documentation Servers and Directories

Establish webserver IP addresses and directories that contain client documentation with the Document Services form.

To access this form:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change, select System Parameters.

  3. From the Actions menu, select Document Services.

  4. Enter the Webserver IP Address.

  5. Enter the Webserver Directory path that contains client documentation.

  6. Enter the Secure Server IP Address.

  7. Enter the Secure Server Directory.

  8. The Downloads Directory is a holding area where files are stored during a download before displaying in the internet browser.

  9. Click Save.

Setting Up Automated Email Messages

You can maintain the information used in automatic email messages using the Email Services form.

To maintain the information in an automatic email message:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change, select System Parameters.

  3. From the Actions menu, select Email Services.

  4. Complete these fields as required.

Field Description
SMTP Server IP address or host name of the SMTP server
SMTP Port Port number the server listens on
Email Service URL URL where the email application is stored
Support Email Email address that recipients see for most messages
sMFA Email Email address that recipients see when they receive MFA email
Benefits Secure Email Subject Field that activates the option to email confirmation statements to employees. This field has no character limits.
Email Templates Select from these template types (maintained in the Message Templates form): - ACH Maximum Approval: Notification of approval action required for ACH process - ACH Maximum Resolution: Notification of an approved or denied action for ACH process - Password Reset: Password reset notice for PrismHR users - User Registration: EP user registration notice - Password Reset Confirmation: Confirmation notice of successful password reset - Password Reset ESS: Password reset notice for EP users - MFA Passcode: Passcode notice for multi-factor authentication - HR Actions Approval: Notification of approval action required for HR process - HR Actions Resolution: Notification of an approved or denied action for HR process - Payroll Approval: Notification of approval action required for Payroll process - Payroll Calculation: Notification that payroll is calculated for a process - Payroll Finalization: Notice that a payroll has reached the finalization step of payroll processing - Benefits Enrollment Approval: Notification of approval action required for Benefits Enrollment process - Employee Termination Approval: Notification of approval action required for Employee Termination process - Pay Card Account: Needs a definition - Payday Email: Notification that a payment was processed - Payroll Approved - Service Provider: Notification that payroll was approved - Payroll Denied - Service Provider: Notification that payroll was denied - Payroll Reminder Email: Notification that payroll is due for processing - Direct Deposit Change: Notification that a direct deposit was changed when an approval policy is in place - Leave Approval: Notification that an employee’s leave is ready for approval - Late Payroll Posting Approval: Notification that payroll was prevented from being posted on or after the Late Payroll Posting date and time during the finalization process, which prevents the payroll from finalizing until it is approved by a user in accordance with the applicable Approval Policy configuration

  • Payroll Denied - Service Provider: Notification that payroll was denied

Setting Global Accounting Parameters

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/SP_Global_Accounting.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/SP_Global_Accounting.htm

Setting Global Accounting Parameters

Configure the required accounting parameters on the Global Accounting panel.

  1. Complete these fields as required.

Field — Description

Accounting Interface Type — This is the accounting program type used with PrismHR. Build Account # options automatically create accounts for your accounting system’s chart of accounts. - Great Plains/Dynamics - Build Account # - Intacct - Build Account #s - Peach Tree/Sage- Build Account #s - QuickBooks - Build Account #s - Custom Layout - Build Account #s Accounting system options include: - No Accounting: No accounting interface. - Great Plains/Dynamics: Use Great Plains/Dynamics. - Intacct: Use Intacct. - Peach Tree/Sage: Use Peach Tree/Sage. - QuickBooks: Use QuickBooks. - Custom Layout: Create a custom layout. > Note: Note: Automatically building the chart of accounts is useful because it does not stop payroll processing if a G/L account is not in the Chart of Accounts. It adds the G/L number to the chart. However, It can also add “bad” G/L numbers and not all accounting programs can handle these errors. You can remove account numbers added in error.

Export Path — Defines the complete export paths for these options: - Export Path For Cash Receipts - export path for cash receipts. - Export Path For Receivables - export path for receivable data. - Export Path For Journals - export path for general journal data. - Export Path for CustMast - export path for customer data. - Export Path For CompanyAcctng - export path to a client’s accounting download files.

Import Path For Chart — The complete import path for chart of accounts data.

Consolidate Cost Accounting — Consolidates costs by date.

Use PrismHR Accounts Receivable — Enable if your organization is using PrismHR Accounts Receivable and it needs to be the primary accounts receivable. (If you select this option, the system will not track accounts receivable information in your accounting software.)

Suppress File Transfer Message — Suppresses the message that appears when accounting files are successfully transferred to your computer.

W/C General Ledger by State/Policy — Sets up workers’ compensation general ledger accounts by State or Policy. If you do not specify, the system defaults to State.

Require Prepay Benefit Account No. — Selects how PrismHR handles prepaid benefits. Options are: - Yes: Sends liability amounts for prepaid benefit plans to another account. This forces the use of the prepaid account. - No: Uses the same account for all benefit plans. - Setup: Allows setup transition For example, if a single plan has prepaid clients, you would put the current clients into the liability and prepaid clients into a prepaid account that you would manually “sweep” at the end of the month into the liability account for the next month.

Debit Account for EE Paid Tax Adjustment — The account used to record debits to G/L accounting for refunds that are paid out in relation to tax refunds.

  1. Click Save.

  2. Click Yes to confirm you want to save the system parameters.

Setting Up Global Codes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/SP_Global_Codes_Setup.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/SP_Global_Codes_Setup.htm

Setting Up Global Codes

Define the deduction, pay, and bill codes in PrismHR on the Global Codes Setup panel.

  1. Complete these fields as required.

Field — Description

401(k) Pre-Tax Deduction Code — 401(k) elective contributions deducted before taxes.

401(k) Loan Deduction Code — 401(k) loan payments.

401(k) Post-Tax Deduction Code — 401(k) elective contributions deducted after taxes.

Garnishment Fee Deduction Code — Garnishment fees that must be set up as voluntary type deduction codes.

Automatic Loan Deduction Code — Automatically converts deductions entered on the Other Deductions form to employee loan deductions.

Employee Loan Deduction Code — Automatically creates employee loan deductions.

Employee Catch-up Deduction Code — Code used for employee’s catch-up retirement deduction.

Roth Post-Tax Deduction Code — Roth contributions deducted after taxes.

Roth Catch-up Deduction Code — Code used for Roth catch-up contributions.

Employer Match Billing Code — Code used for billing employer match.

ACH To Deduction Code — Creates a payroll deduction instead of an ACH direct deposit transaction.

Group Term Life Fringe Pay Code — Group term life insurance over 50K that is a taxable fringe benefit.

Dependents GTL Fringe Pay Code — Group term life insurance for employee dependents.

Tip Credit Make Up Pay Code — Pays tip credit make-up wages.

Calculate Tip Credit Make Up Daily in — Calculates tip credit make up wages for different states on a daily basis.

Auto Term Employee Status Code — Used in employee records when employees are automatically terminated because a client was terminated. This is the status code assigned to all employees.

Auto Term Reason Code — Provides a reason when employees are automatically terminated because a client was terminated. This code is used when you do a “mass termination” of a client. The system prompts you if you want to terminate all employees. If you select Yes, the system automatically assigns this reason code to all employees.

Transfer Term Reason Code — Provides a reason when employees are terminated after being transferred to a different client. When you transfer all employees to a client, this code is assigned to all employees at transfer.

FSA Match Bill Code — Code used for billing client contributions to employee flexible savings accounts.

HSA Match Bill Code — Code used for billing client contributions to employee health savings accounts.

PFML ER Pickup Fringe Pay Code — When this field is selected, then on the State Tax Rates (SUTA) form, in the Rate Breakdown section, the field named PFML Employer Pickup will display. You can click the hyperlink and select a pay code with a pay class of non‑cash fringe benefit from the Select fringe benefit dialog box or you can manually enter a valid pay code with a pay class of non‑cash fringe benefit here. If you manually enter an invalid (non‑fringe or non‑existing) pay code here, and click Save, you will receive an error message stating is not a non-cash fringe benefit. The invalid value will be cleared from this field.

Refund Tax Pay Code — Code used when refunding a tax amount over-withheld from an employee.

Code Test Employer — ID that validates items (such as billing codes) that do not have a particular employer tied to them. This ID must exist in Employer Details. The system validates accounts, sub-accounts, cost centers, and sub-cost centers against the accounting master file. Since this accounting validation requires employer information, PrismHR uses the employer in this field when no other is available. > Note: Note: Since the system performs the validation only for this company, other company flows might be incorrect. The PrismHR Customer Support Team strongly recommends that you test any new code you add for each employer that uses the code.

  1. Click Save.

Field Description

This is a global setting, and there are also client and employee settings. Options are: - Use Worksite GeoCode as listed: Uses the worksite location GeoCode and performs no overrides. - Override Work GeoCode with Resident GeoCode: Overrides the standard GeoCode values that are sent to the Vertex tax calculation engine for processing. This is typically selected when employees work from home. - Override Work GeoCode with Home Location GeoCode:Uses the employee’s “home” location assignment to supply a GeoCode for the location-based portion of taxes. Establish Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) fiscal year information using the FMLA panel.

To establish FMLA information:

  1. Complete these fields as required.

Field — Description

FMLA Year Basis — Establishes the Family and Medical Leave Act year basis that the calculation is driven by. Options are: - Calendar Year - Fiscal Year - Anniversary Year - First Leave Date

Fiscal End Month — Month when the fiscal year ends. Only enter a month if you select Fiscal Year for FMLA Year Basis

Fiscal End Day — Day when the fiscal year ends. Only enter a day if you select Fiscal Year for FMLA Year Basis

  1. Click Accept. The System Parameters form displays.

  2. Click Save.

Establishing SSO Services

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/SP_SSO_Services.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/SP_SSO_Services.htm

Establishing SSO Services

Use this form to establish the single sign-on service names and URLs that the system uses to negotiate with other web-based software products.

For complete details about setting up SSO services, please review the Single Sign-On Guide.

To set up single sign-on services for this system:

  1. Click Back Office and select System Parameters under System|Change.

  2. Click the Actions menu and select SSO Services.

  3. In a new row, enter a unique Service ID.

  4. Enter a service Description.

  5. Select the service Type, which is typically External for a vendor and Internal for services hosted on your organization’s servers.

  • Internal: This opens the target service in an inline frame (iframe), which displays within PrismHR.

  • External: This opens the target service in a separate window or tab (depending on your browser settings).

  1. In the Service Destination field, select whether single sign-on with this service will be Inbound (to PrismHR) or Outbound (from PrismHR).

  2. Enter the Service URL, which is the web location of the “destination” product.

  3. Click Save.

Maintaining Tax Rates

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/SP_Tax_Rate.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/SP_Tax_Rate.htm

Maintaining Tax Rates

You can maintain federal tax rates, state tax rates for Nevada and NY, and limit rates used to calculate payroll for a specific year with the Tax Rate Maintenance form.

[Image: screenshot]

Setting Federal Tax Rates

Complete the fields as required in the Tax Rates panel.

Field — Description

Year — Four-digit calendar year when the federal tax rates are in effect.

OASDI Rate — Annual Old Age, Survivors, and Disability Insurance (OASDI) rate for the year, including the decimal point. For example, enter 6.2% as .062.

OASDI Limit — Annual taxable OASDI limit for the year in total dollars.

Medicare Rate — Medicare rate for this year, including the decimal point. For example, enter 1.45% as .0145.

Med Tier 1 Limit — Medicare tier 1 rate limit.

FUTA Rate — Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) rate for this year, including the decimal point. For example, enter 6% as .060.

FUTA Limit — FUTA limit for the year in total dollars.

Configuring State-Specific Tax Rates

Configure certain state tax rates for New York, Nevada, and Puerto Rico in the fields below the Tax Rates panel.

Note: If you are entering New York SDI Tax information, see the Setting up the New York State Disability Insurance Tax article in the Customer Resource Center for complete information.

Field Name — Field Description

Default Nevada Modified Business Tax Rate — Sets the default rate (both accrual and billing) for the State of Nevada business tax.

New York SDI Max Per Week — Amount deducted each week from an employee who lives in New York.

New York SDI Percent — New York taxable gross rate.

New York SDI Employer Rate (EE/Month) — New York employer taxable gross rate (calculated for each employee). Note: This amount occurs in full on the first payroll of each month.

Allow Override by Client — Allows overrides of the NY SDI tax.

Puerto Rico Chauffeur Tax (EE) Per Week — Employee rate for this tax. Note that the Puerto Rico Chauffeur Tax is not calculated by Vertex and must be manually maintained. The tax is triggered for the employee based on a Job Code that is assigned on the Employee Master form.

(ER) Per Week — Employer rate for the Puerto Rico Chauffeur Tax.

Note: The Puerto Rico Chauffeur Tax is not calculated by Vertex and must be manually maintained. The tax is triggered for the employee based on a Job Code that is assigned on the Employee Master form.

Establishing Tax Year Limits

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/SP_Tax_Year_Limit.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/SP_Tax_Year_Limit.htm

Establishing Tax Year Limits

Tax Year Limits are not maintained by PrismHR. Every year in December, PrismHR sends you a Year-End File Maintenance document that outlines the new year tax year limits. You can use these limits for guidance or consult with a tax expert.

Before starting this process, note that the values entered on this form are applied globally. Enter them manually on the Tax Year Limits Maintenance form before the first payroll of the new year.

Note: Note: To access this form, go to the System Parameters form and select Tax Year Limits from the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

.

This form captures tax year limits for compensation, contribution, catch-up, funding, and FSA deposits. Set limits, percentages, and contributions as needed.

To establish tax year limits, do the following:

  1. Complete these fields as required.
Field Description
Limits Limit settings include: - Year - Specifies the year for the statutory limit. - Comp Limit - The maximum annual compensation limit for a given tax year, which is the compensation limit defined in Section 401(a)(17) for qualified retirement plans. - Contribution Limit - Maximum contribution an employee can make to qualified 401(k) or Roth 401(k) plan for this tax year. - Catch-Up Limit - Maximum catch-up contribution limit for this tax year. The limit applies to participants 50 years or older. When the Disable Accelerated Catchup? field on the Client Details form is checked, and when Catch Up Limit is applied at the system level on this Tax Year Limits Maintenance form only, Vertex limits the sheltered amount based on IRS limits. - 60-63 Catch Up - This field is optional. As a result of the Secure 2.0 Act of 2022, effective 1/1/2025, for employees who will turn 60, 61, 62 or 63 as of 12/31 of the defined tax year, are permitted to contribute an additional amount to their catch-up contribution. The increased contribution amount should be entered in the 60-63 Catch Up field on the following forms for the employee contribution to be treated as a pre-tax amount: - Benefit Plan Maintenance / Retirement Plans / Retirement Plans (under section Plan Year Deferral Limits) - Benefit Plan Maintenance / Retirement Plans / Tax Year Limits Maintenance - The value entered in this field will be the total amount such employees can contribute for the tax year. - For tax year 2025, it is the greater of 150% of Catch-Up Contribution limit OR $10,000. - This field will only accept numerical values. - The 60-63 Catch Up amount must be equal to or greater than the value entered in the corresponding Catch Up Limit field. If not, you will receive an error message stating Amount must be equal to or greater than Catch Up Limit. - The Catch Up Limit amount must be equal to or less than the value entered in the corresponding 60-63 Catch Up field. If not, you will receive an error message stating Amount must be equal to or less than 60-63 Catch Up. - If the Catch Up Limit field is empty, any value in the 60-63 Catch-Up field will present an error stating 60-63 Catch-Up limits must be defined. - Funding Limit - Maximum Section 415 contribution limit for this tax year. - HPE Threshold (Prior Year) - This column was added to support Secure Act 2.0 requirements; however as the implementation timeline of this functionality was delayed, there will be no current functionality around this column. More information will be available in a future release. - FSA Dep Limit - Maximum Flexible Spending Account employee contribution for dependent care. - PEO Tax Basis - Determines the taxable limit basis used for PEO Client billing.
  • Year - Specifies the year for the statutory limit.
  • Comp Limit - The maximum annual compensation limit for a given tax year, which is the compensation limit defined in Section 401(a)(17) for qualified retirement plans.
  • Contribution Limit - Maximum contribution an employee can make to qualified 401(k) or Roth 401(k) plan for this tax year.
  • Catch-Up Limit - Maximum catch-up contribution limit for this tax year. The limit applies to participants 50 years or older. When the Disable Accelerated Catchup? field on the Client Details form is checked, and when Catch Up Limit is applied at the system level on this Tax Year Limits Maintenance form only, Vertex limits the sheltered amount based on IRS limits.
  • 60-63 Catch Up - This field is optional. As a result of the Secure 2.0 Act of 2022, effective 1/1/2025, for employees who will turn 60, 61, 62 or 63 as of 12/31 of the defined tax year, are permitted to contribute an additional amount to their catch-up contribution. The increased contribution amount should be entered in the 60-63 Catch Up field on the following forms for the employee contribution to be treated as a pre-tax amount:
  • Benefit Plan Maintenance / Retirement Plans / Retirement Plans (under section Plan Year Deferral Limits)
  • Benefit Plan Maintenance / Retirement Plans / Tax Year Limits Maintenance
  • The value entered in this field will be the total amount such employees can contribute for the tax year.
  • For tax year 2025, it is the greater of 150% of Catch-Up Contribution limit OR $10,000.
  • This field will only accept numerical values.
  • The 60-63 Catch Up amount must be equal to or greater than the value entered in the corresponding Catch Up Limit field. If not, you will receive an error message stating Amount must be equal to or greater than Catch Up Limit.
  • The Catch Up Limit amount must be equal to or less than the value entered in the corresponding 60-63 Catch Up field. If not, you will receive an error message stating Amount must be equal to or less than 60-63 Catch Up.
  • If the Catch Up Limit field is empty, any value in the 60-63 Catch-Up field will present an error stating 60-63 Catch-Up limits must be defined.
  • Funding Limit - Maximum Section 415 contribution limit for this tax year.
  • HPE Threshold (Prior Year) - This column was added to support Secure Act 2.0 requirements; however as the implementation timeline of this functionality was delayed, there will be no current functionality around this column. More information will be available in a future release.
  • FSA Dep Limit - Maximum Flexible Spending Account employee contribution for dependent care.
  • PEO Tax Basis - Determines the taxable limit basis used for PEO Client billing. | Percentages | Percentage settings include: Safe Harbor Type 1 Percentage - Percentage of the match for type 1 plans. For example, enter 3.5% as 3.50. Safe Harbor Type 2 Percentage - Percentage of the match for type 2 plans. For example, enter 5% as 5.00. Safe Harbor plans are ones that the employee must contribute to in order to receive the match. | | Contributions | HSA Maximum Annual Contribution (single coverage) - Maximum annual HSA contribution (single). HSA Maximum Annual Contribution (dual coverage) - Maximum annual HSA contribution (dual). HSA Maximum Annual Contribution (family coverage) - Maximum annual HSA contribution (family). > Note: Note: A warning message displays if you access any of the HSA Maximum Annual Contribution fields, “HSA Annual Contribution limits for the upcoming year should not be updated until after the final payroll of the current year has been processed.” This message indicates that updating an employee’s HSA Maximum Contribution amount beforethe year-end payroll is processed results in imbalanced deduction amounts. |

  1. Click Accept.

  2. Click OK in the confirmation message.

  3. Click Save in the System Parameters form.

  4. Click Yes in the message to confirm that you want to save the parameters.

State Garnishment Rules

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/State_Garnishment_Rules.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/State_Garnishment_Rules.htm

Creating State Garnishment Rules

Establish the manner in which PrismHR processes state garnishment rules with the State Garnishment Rules form.

The FG state garnishment rules record is for the federal government, and is the default template for all other states. You only need to enter the values that are different for a particular state. Everything else defaults to the values for the federal garnishment rules.

To create state garnishment rules:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. Select State Garnishment Rules under System|Change.

  3. Enter the two-character State Code, or FG for Federal Government.

  4. Define the Rules for Calculating Withholding for Creditor Garnishments:

Field Description
Maximum Percent of Select either Disposable Pay or Gross Pay, depending on the state rule you are setting up. Enter the maximum amount that can be withheld in the second field.
Minimum Wage Rate Multiplier The multiplier is the number of hours multiplied by an employee’s minimum wage to calculate the maximum disposable earnings that standard creditors can garnish. This is overridden if the garnishment maximum is lower. For example, if the multiplier is 40, the system multiplies the minimum wage by this number. The result is the minimum pay that an employee has after taxes and garnishments. Standard creditors can garnish amounts left after subtracting taxes and the minimum pay amount from an employee’s gross pay. From 1/1/2025 up to 06/30/2027, Oregon Creditor Garnishment calculations have been programmed by effective date to use the following exempt amounts as defined by Oregon State Law based on the pay period for each of the effective dates. These amounts will be applied when the Minimum Wage Rate Multiplier field for the state of Oregon is set to 30. \ Pay Period \ Weekly \ Bi-Weekly \ Semi-Monthly \ Monthly \ \ — \ — \ — \ — \ — \ \ 01-Jan-2025 thru 30-Jun-2025 \ $305 \ $611 \ $655 \ $1309 \ \ 01-Jul-2025 thru 30-Jun-2026 \ $338 \ $675 \ $737 \ $1458 \ \ 01-Jul-2026 thru 30-Jun-2027 \ $400 \ $832 \ $912 \ $1792 \ On July 1, 2027, calculations will default to State Garnishment Rules for the state of Oregon: > Note: Note: It is recommended that for the state of Oregon, on the State Garnishment Rules form, the Minimum Wage Rate Multiplier field be set to 30 until July 2027.
Pay Period Weekly Bi-Weekly Semi-Monthly Monthly
01-Jan-2025 thru 30-Jun-2025 $305 $611 $655 $1309
01-Jul-2025 thru 30-Jun-2026 $338 $675 $737 $1458
01-Jul-2026 thru 30-Jun-2027 $400 $832 $912 $1792
Minimum Wage Rate Source The source that determines the minimum hourly rate for creditor garnishment maximum calculations.
Hours Calculation Method The method that calculates minimum net pay for semi-monthly or monthly pay periods under CCPA rules for creditor garnishments: - Factored – Multiplies the weekly hours by either a factor of 2.16 (for semi-monthly) or 4.33 (for monthly). The factor method may be less accurate because of rounding errors, but some states specify its use. - Annualized – Multiplies the weekly hours by 52 and then divides by the number of pay periods in the year. For example, for semi-monthly, the calculation is ( (30.00 x 52)/24 ).
- Factored – Multiplies the weekly hours by either a factor of 2.16 (for semi-monthly) or 4.33 (for monthly). The factor method may be less accurate because of rounding errors, but some states specify its use.
- Annualized – Multiplies the weekly hours by 52 and then divides by the number of pay periods in the year. For example, for semi-monthly, the calculation is ( (30.00 x 52)/24 ).
Administrative Processing Fee The fee applied per pay period to process creditor wage garnishments.
Maximum Monthly Fee The maximum monthly fee collected from employees for processing creditor wage garnishments.
Reduce Limit by Fee Amount There are two options: - Yes – Reduces the CCPA limit by the administrative processing fee for this state. This is only for non-consumer garnishments. - No –The system does not reduce the limit.
- Yes – Reduces the CCPA limit by the administrative processing fee for this state. This is only for non-consumer garnishments.
- No –The system does not reduce the limit.
Non Consumer Min Wage Multiplier The multiplier is the number of hours multiplied by an employee’s minimum wage to calculate the maximum disposable earnings that creditors can garnish in case of a judgment or non-consumer garnishment. This is overridden if the garnishment maximum is lower. For example, if the multiplier is 30, the system multiplies the minimum wage by this number. The result is the minimum pay that an employee has after taxes and garnishments. A non-consumer creditor can garnish amounts left after subtracting taxes and the minimum pay amount from an employee’s gross pay.
HOH Maximum Percent Enter a value if the state has a maximum allowed creditor garnishment percentage rule for heads of households.
State Tax Levy Maximum Percent of Select whether the state tax levy maximum should be a percent of: - Disposable Pay – income after taxes are deducted - Gross Pay – total income
- Disposable Pay – income after taxes are deducted
- Gross Pay – total income
Allow Creditor Garnishment deduction before State Levy Certain states have varying requirements on how to calculate a State tax levy when an employee has other garnishments. This option allows you the flexibility to better support states allowing other garnishments including creditor garnishment deduction before calculating the amount due to the state levy. If for a selected state, this field is: - Enabled– then the order of priority for deduction of garnishments will be as follows: 1. Child Support (Spousal Support) 2. Bankruptcy 3. Levies (IRS Tax Levy, FTB) 4. Creditor Wage Garnishment / Student Loan 5. State Tax Levy - Disabled – then the order of priority for deduction of garnishments will be as follows: 1. Child Support (Spousal Support) 2. Bankruptcy 3. Levies (IRS Tax Levy, FTB) 4. State Tax Levy 5. Creditor Wage Garnishment / Student Loan > Note: Note: When using this option to prioritize Creditor Wage Garnishments prior to the State Tax Levy, you should ensure that the State Tax Levy maximum percent has been entered for the applicable State Code on this form.
- Enabled– then the order of priority for deduction of garnishments will be as follows:
1. Child Support (Spousal Support)
2. Bankruptcy
3. Levies (IRS Tax Levy, FTB)
4. Creditor Wage Garnishment / Student Loan
5. State Tax Levy
- Disabled – then the order of priority for deduction of garnishments will be as follows:
1. Child Support (Spousal Support)
2. Bankruptcy
3. Levies (IRS Tax Levy, FTB)
4. State Tax Levy
5. Creditor Wage Garnishment / Student Loan
Multiple Order Priority Method This field helps you manage the varying rules for different states for creditor garnishments like child support. Select one of the following options from the drop-down: - First In, First Out – earliest dated garnishment will be deducted first. This is the same as the default behavior. - Prorate Allocation – proportionally deduct creditor garnishments based on wage to garnishment ratio. - Equal Share Allocation – equal and simultaneous deductions for multiple creditor garnishments are in place. > Note: Note: If a Creditor Garnishment has an override state, it will follow the rules for the override state. This feature will work with or without enabling the Enhanced Garnishment Capping field on the System Parameters form.
- First In, First Out – earliest dated garnishment will be deducted first. This is the same as the default behavior.
- Prorate Allocation – proportionally deduct creditor garnishments based on wage to garnishment ratio.
- Equal Share Allocation – equal and simultaneous deductions for multiple creditor garnishments are in place.
Additional Disposable Deductions Other deductions that are removed from gross earnings to calculate disposable income for the purpose of computing creditor wage garnishments.
  1. Define Rules for Calculating Withholding for Child Support Payments.

Processing Taxes for a Specified State

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/State_Rules.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/State_Rules.htm

Processing Taxes for a Specified State

You can maintain the information required to process taxes for a specified state using the State Rules form.

Note: Note: The processing rules that come with PrismHR may not be current. PrismHR is not liable or responsible for the accuracy of these rules. It is your responsibility to verify and update state processing rules according to the laws and statutes of the states where you conduct business.

Establishing Basic State Tax Rules

You can establish basic state tax rules using the State Rules panel.

Important! Do not change the default values in the FIPS 5 Code and Vertex Code fields. This can cause system-wide errors in tax processing.

Note: Note: The Client State Unemployment Tax (SUTA) Rate setting is valid only when the Service Type field in Maintaining Client Details is set to PEO.

Field Name Description
State Code Two-letter abbreviation for state tax information. Enter a code to populate the form with tax information for that state.
State Name Name of the state that corresponds to the State Code.
FIPS 5 Code Do not change this field. This is a default value.
Vertex Code Do not change this field. This is a default value used during state tax calculations.
SUTA PEO/Client Based Select whether SUTA is reported at the PEO level or at the client level.
Client SUTA Report Only Select this option if SUTA rates are set at the PEO level, but reported at the client level. For example, Kansas and Missouri require this type of reporting.
SIT Combined Reporting This field only appears for the state of Oregon. This field is used during payroll processing to force the tax basis for specific state taxes to be assigned the same tax entity (PEO or Client) as is assigned for SUTA. Oregon is a combined reporting state that has historically always been PEO report only. To support Oregon HB 2263(Permits professional employer organizations (PEOs) to report payroll information in aggregate on behalf of their clients) this new option has been added. For combined reporting, all state taxes must report on the same level including SIT. While we support this today for SUTA and SUTA Components, SIT could previously only be set to an override on the employer level. With this option, for pay dates starting 1/1/2026, Oregon employers now can change the PEO/Client reporting designation for additional Oregon state taxes that do not naturally follow the client reporting dates within the client detail tax tab. - This is not a required field. - Unchecked - This field is unchecked by default. When this field is not set on Oregon, AND for all client types other than PEO, AND for all states other than Oregon, there will be no change in tax basis. - Checked - When this field is checked for OREGON PEO CLIENT TYPES, all of the following taxes will report using the same tax basis P or C for PEO Clients: - 38-23 (WBF) - Employee - 38-24 (SUTA) - Employer - 38-26 (WBF) - Employer - 38-27 (State transit) - Employee - 38-28 (SUTA offset) - Employer - 38-20 (SIT) - Employee - 38-40 (PFML) - Employee - 38-41 (PFML) - Employer - 38-51 (Lane Transit) - Employer - 38-52 (TRI COUNTY TRANSIT) - Employer - When you select this field, you will receive a warning stating Warning, payroll processing will use the SUTA tax entity for other state taxes with the tax IDs 20,23,26,27,28,40,41,51,52. Are you sure? You can click Yes or No. - The existing tax basis designation hierarchy Tax Deduction → State Rule → Employer Detail → Client Detail is extended to the State Tax Deduction codes that are currently excluded such that: - If SUTA is configured to be PEO or Client, all of the above tax codes follow the SUTA Reporting designation. - Not all Oregon tax codes will follow the new SIT setting. For example, the following state and local tax codes are excluded from this logic: - 38-46 (Portland Metro SHS). - Any County or Local tax codes.
Client SUTA Rate Select this field to include the client-level SUTA rate during reporting. This option is only available if Service Type on the Client Details form is set to PEO.
Officer SUTA Client Based Select this option to report SUTA for company officers separately from other employees.
Electronic Pay Stubs Allowed Select one of the following options according to state laws for electronic pay stubs: - Allowed, Employee may not un‑enroll: The state allows electronic pay stubs. You can configure direct deposit to disable employees from un‑enrolling. - Allowed, Employee may un‑enroll: The state allows electronic pay stubs. You can configure direct deposit to enable employees to un‑enroll. - Not allowed by the State: The state does not allow electronic pay stubs. - Allowed, Employee must Opt‑In: The state allows electronic pay stubs, but employees must select electronic pay stub when setting up their direct deposit. Employees defaults to paper pay stubs. For more information on how these settings relate to the client‑level settings, See Configuring Electronic Pay Stubs.
  • Allowed, Employee may not un‑enroll: The state allows electronic pay stubs. You can configure direct deposit to disable employees from un‑enrolling.
  • Allowed, Employee may un‑enroll: The state allows electronic pay stubs. You can configure direct deposit to enable employees to un‑enroll.
  • Not allowed by the State: The state does not allow electronic pay stubs.
  • Allowed, Employee must Opt‑In: The state allows electronic pay stubs, but employees must select electronic pay stub when setting up their direct deposit. Employees defaults to paper pay stubs. | Print Legal Name On Check | If the state requires you to print legal names on checks, instead of DBAs, select this option. | | Client State Tax ID required for PEO to withhold tax | Select this option if the state requires PEO clients to have state tax IDs before the PEO can withhold taxes. | | Local Allowances Never Default to State Allowances | Select this option if a state has local tax authorities and the system should never assume the same withholding allowances as the state withholding. | | Direct Deposit Mandatory Allowed | Select this option if a state allows mandatory direct deposit (100% of pay must be direct deposit). | ## Establishing Additional Rules

Field Description

Local Income Tax Select if the state levies local income taxes on residents. When users hire employees who live in this state, the New Hire Form displays the Local Form W4 Details panel if this option is selected.
Allow 1099 Income Tax Withholding You will need to first enable the custom feature code 1099WITHHOLDING to display these new options. You will need to enable each state in which you wish to withhold income tax from a 1099 contractor. To support 1099 contractor Federal and State Income Tax reporting, when the Custom Feature Code 1099WITHHOLDING is enabled, the wages and tax withholdings for a 1099 contractor will NOT be included in the Employer 941 Quarterly Report for any 1099 contractor with tax withholding. Additionally, release enhancements for the PTS and RTS to support 1099 withholding will only be present in the files using the NEC tax code when the Custom Feature Code 1099WITHHOLDING is enabled. This box is unchecked by default. - When unchecked, no taxes are withheld for any employee who is a 1099 Contractor in PrismHR. - When checked: - PrismHR will withhold state and federal income tax for 1099 contractors hired for the selected client only. - PrismHR will only withhold federal and state income tax for that state (FG and all other states) if the field Allow 1099 Income Tax Withholding under State Tax Parameters section in the State Rules form is also checked. - PrismHR will honor any tax overrides for the 1099 contractors including Add to, Block, Percentage, and Fixed. > Note: Note: You should NOT have 1099 withholding from a contractor if you do not have the Custom Feature Code 1099WITHHOLDING in place. When leveraging the Custom Feature Code 1099WITHHOLDING, you will need to have a separate Employee ID for any 1099 contractor who has tax withheld. Previously, the system allowed a 1099 Contractor in one client and a W-2 employee in a second client using the same Employee ID. For purposes of 1099 income tax withholding and reporting, the 1099 contractor must NOT be a W2 employee in any other client.

SuperView

Use the SuperView to review payroll batches that are in process.

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the fields at the top of the form to filter the list of payrolls:

  • Enter the Through Date to select batch control with a call-in date less than or equal to the through date. (The default is the current date.)

Maintaining System Parameters

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/System_Parameters.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/System_Parameters.htm

Maintaining System Parameters

Maintain system-wide settings for PrismHR with the System Parameters form.

Note: Note: Some features are not available to all users.

  • Setting General System Parameters: Sets parameters such as mail codes and company IDs

  • Setting Up Global Codes: Defines deduction, pay, and bill codes

  • Setting Global Accounting Parameters: Sets parameters such as accounting interface and export paths

  • Customizing My Support Team Dashboard Contacts: Customizes the contacts that display on your My Support Team Dashboard

Using the Actions Menu

You can perform additional tasks using the options on the Actions menu.

Menu Item — Description

Creating 1095-C Election Text — Defines the text that displays on the Early 1095C Election page.

Viewing the Audit Log — Displays all changes made to a form.

Enabling Multi-Factor Authentication — Sets up basic security at the system, client, or user level. After the number of days is specified in Authentication Services, impacted users are prompted to request authorization.

Configuring System-Level Settings for Coronavirus-Related Paid Leave — Configures system-level setup for coverage related to the 2020 COVID-19 outbreak, as described in the Families First Coronavirus Response Act.

Clearing Backup Account Assignments — Clears all backup account assignments regardless of which clients are listed in the import file. Important! This process cannot be reverted.

Defining a Custom Process — Configures custom menu items.

Specifying Direct Deposit Terms and Conditions — Sets the effective date and any terms and conditions that display before accepting direct deposit information.

Setting Up Documentation Servers and Directories — Establishes the web server IP address and directory that contains client documentation

Selecting Default Menus with ESS Menu Builder — Sets up default menus for Employee Self Service.

Setting Up Automated Email Messages — Maintains automatic e-mail information and sets up email message templates.

Setting Enrollment Options — Configures online benefits enrollment settings in EP.

Printing Setup for Global Payroll Reports — Selects reports that print during regular, special, manual, or special/manual payroll runs.

Maintaining Global mvQuery Image Path — Specifies the logos that appear on checks and reports that use mvQuery.

Logo Path Maintenance — Specifies the logos that display in PEO and non-PEO invoice headers.

Setting Miscellaneous Parameters — Sets up tax codes and FMLA parameters.

Managing Next Number Control — Controls the next number types that appear on checks.

Maintaining Global Onboarding Options — Sets global parameters such as enabling benefit enrollment after final submittal.

Establishing SSO Services — Creates and maintains single sign-on names and URLs.

Maintaining Tax Rates — Creates and maintains federal tax rates and rates for Nevada and New York as well as limit rates.

Establishing Tax Year Limits — Adds and maintains tax year limits for compensation, contribution, catch-up, funding, and FSA deposits. Safe Harbor percentages and HSA maximum annual contributions are also maintained here.

Controlling Employee Termination Messages — Provides a method for controlling system messages related to employee termination.

Creating W-2 Election Text — Sets up the Early W‑2 Election page in Employee Self-Service (ESS) so employees can obtain their Form W‑2 electronically.

Maintaining Web Extensions — Creates and maintains custom web scripts and HTML tags.

Maintaining Web Service Users — Creates web service user profiles with allowed or restricted IP addresses and methods (for example, sign-on service methods).

Shelter Bill Code — Controls the sheltered billing amount if Discount Shelter is not selected for bundled billing. If left blank, the system uses the active tax billing code.

  1. Click Save.

Tax Deduction Administrative Fund

Establish the tax deduction information with the Tax Deduction Administrative Fund panel.

Note: Note: The information on the Tax Deduction Administrative Fund panel is for reporting purposes only. The system does not perform calculations on this information.

  1. For the deduction administrative fund:

  • Enter the Admin Tax Year.

  • Enter the Admin Tax Rate.

  1. Click Save.

Determining Total Compensation Setup

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Total%20Compensation%20Report%20Setup.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Total Compensation Report Setup.htm

Determining Total Compensation Setup

Use the Total Compensation Report Setup form to determine how the screen is configured on the Total Compensation Dashboard in PrismHR. This form contains the following three sections:

  • Pay Code Allocation

  • Retirement Tax Allocation

  • Benefit Plan Allocation

Note: Note: Client Access Group Security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, click the Back Office menu. Under System|Change, click Total Compensation Report Setup.

To set up the Total Compensation Report:

  1. Complete the following sections:

Field Name — Description

Pay Code Allocation Allocate pay codes and assign descriptions for up to 4 rows on the report.

Row 1

Pay Description — Enter the description of the first pay row on the report. For example Hours Worked Plus Holiday Hours.

Pay Codes — Enter the pay codes to be included in the first row of pay amounts on the report, or click the Pay Codes link and select the appropriate pay codes from the Select Pay Code dialog box. For example REG - Regular Pay.

Suppress description if amount is zero — Check this box if you want to suppress a pay code if the amount is zero.

Row 2

Pay Description — Enter the description of the second pay row on the report. For example Non-Worked Hours (PTO annual entitlement).

Pay Codes — Enter the pay codes to be included in the second row of pay amounts on the report, or click the Pay Codes link and select the appropriate pay codes from the Select Pay Code dialog box. For example VAC - Vacation.

Suppress description if amount is zero — Check this box if you want to suppress a pay code if the amount is zero.

Row 3

Pay Description — Enter the description of the third pay row on the report. For example Bonus (Incentive, referral, commission).

Pay Codes — Enter the pay codes to be included in the third row of pay amounts on the report, or click the Pay Codes link and select the appropriate pay codes from the Select Pay Code dialog box. For example BON - Bonus.

Suppress description if amount is zero — Check this box if you want to suppress a pay code if the amount is zero.

Row 4

Pay Description — Enter the description of the fourth pay row on the report. For example Overtime.

Pay Codes — Enter the pay codes to be included in the fourth row of pay amounts on the report, or click the Pay Codes link and select the appropriate pay codes from the Select Pay Code dialog box. For example OT - Overtime.

Suppress description if amount is zero — Check this box if you want to suppress a pay code if the amount is zero.

  • Insert Column Before - This button will remain inactive if you already have four columns in this section. If there are less than four columns, then button will remain active and you can insert a column before an existing column.

  • Delete Column - Use this button to delete an existing column in this section.

Field Name — Description

Retirement Tax Allocation Allocate tax codes and assign a description for retirement taxes.

Tax Description — Enter the description of the retirement tax on the report, for example Social Security/Medicare & Other Tax.

401(k) Description — Enter the description for the 401(k) on the report, for example Employer Match into the 401(k) Plan.

Retirement Tax Codes — Enter the retirement tax codes here or click the Retirement Tax Codes link and select them from the Select Tax Deduction Code dialog box, for example 00-17 FUTA.

Field Name — Description

Benefit Plan Allocation Allocate benefit plans and assign descriptions for up to 8 rows on the report.

Row 1

Benefit Description — Enter the description of the first benefits row on the report. For example Medical.

Benefit Codes — Enter the benefit codes to be included in the first row of benefit amounts on the report, or click the Benefit Codes link and select the appropriate benefit codes from the Select Plan dialog box. For example BCBS - Blue Cross Blue Shield.

Row 2

Benefit Description — Enter the description of the second benefits row on the report. For example Dental.

Benefit Codes — Enter the benefit codes to be included in the second row of benefit amounts on the report, or click the Benefit Codes link and select the appropriate benefit codes from the Select Plan dialog box. For example DENAET - AETNA Dental.

Row 3

Benefit Description — Enter the description of the third benefits row on the report. For example Vision.

Benefit Codes — Enter the benefit codes to be included in the third row of benefit amounts on the report, or click the Benefit Codes link and select the appropriate benefit codes from the Select Plan dialog box. For example JDSVSP - JDS VSP Vison.

Row 4

Benefit Description — Enter the description of the fourth benefits row on the report. For example Life Insurance.

Benefit Codes — Enter the benefit codes to be included in the fourth row of benefit amounts on the report, or click the Benefit Codes link and select the appropriate benefit codes from the Select Plan dialog box. For example VSPKC - VSP Kansas City.

Row 5

Benefit Description — Enter the description of the fifth benefits row on the report. For example Other Benefits.

Benefit Codes — Enter the benefit codes to be included in the fourth row of benefit amounts on the report, or click the Benefit Codes link and select the appropriate benefit codes from the Select Plan dialog box. For example CBOTHER - CB Other Benefits.

Row 6

Benefit Description — Enter the description of the sixth benefits row on the report. For example Short-Term Disability.

Benefit Codes — Enter the benefit codes to be included in the fourth row of benefit amounts on the report, or click the Benefit Codes link and select the appropriate benefit codes from the Select Plan dialog box. For example STD - Short Term Disability.

Row 7

Benefit Description — Enter the description of the seventh benefits row on the report. For example Long-Term Disability.

Benefit Codes — Enter the benefit codes to be included in the fourth row of benefit amounts on the report, or click the Benefit Codes link and select the appropriate benefit codes from the Select Plan dialog box. For example LTD - Long Term Disability - Salary Banded.

Row 8

Benefit Description — Enter the description of the eighth benefits row on the report. For example Tuition Assistance.

Benefit Codes — Enter the benefit codes to be included in the fourth row of benefit amounts on the report, or click the Benefit Codes link and select the appropriate benefit codes from the Select Plan dialog box.

  • Insert Column Before - This button will remain inactive if you already have eight columns in this section. If there are less than eight columns, then button will remain active and you can insert a column before an existing column.

  • Delete Column - Use this button to delete an existing column in this section.

  1. Click Save to save the changes.

Importing Multiple Unbundled Billing Rules

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Unbundled_Billing_Rules_Import.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Unbundled_Billing_Rules_Import.htm

Importing Multiple Unbundled Billing Rules

Use the Unbundled Billing Rules Import form to import multiple unbundled billing rules for clients associated with a specific bill code. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

To access the form, click the Back Office menu. Under Operations|Action, click Unbundled Billing Rules Import.

Note: This form is only available for service providers.

To import unbundled billing rules:

  1. In the Generate Import Spreadsheet section, create an import spreadsheet by entering or selecting the Client IDs and Bill Codes. (You can select multiple clients from the Select Clients list at once.) The Client Name and Bill Description display next to each client. (If left blank, the system selects all clients and bill codes.)

  2. Select Download Spreadsheet. The system creates a spreadsheet that displays in a separate window, which is suitable for editing.

  3. In the Import Data section, enter an Import Name. (This is a required field; you cannot import a file without this information.)

  4. Select Upload File. Click Add Files and select the file to upload, then click Start Upload. (This file must be in .csv format.)

  5. Click Close. A separate Downloads window displays the name of the .csv file that the system created. (Click Open file to view the downloaded file.)

Note: The first row in the downloaded file displays information about the first rule and the multi-value fields, which are separated by a pipe delimiter (|).

  1. Click Import. Processing steps describe the information saved and include a date and time stamp. You can view this as a report or download in PDF or XLS format by clicking Report.

  2. Click Close.

  3. Click Transaction Report to display a link to a report that contains the unbundled billing rules transactions.

Note: The Transaction Report displays “Skipped” for any column in a row that has valid data but was not imported because a required row contained invalid data. (All invalid data displays in the Transaction Report.)

  1. Click Error Report to display a link to a .csv file that details the errors that occurred during the import. (The system does not import any rows listed in the error file and only imports rows where all data in the row is valid.)

Note: The Error Report link only displays if errors occurred during the import, which confirms that the system is unable to perform the import.

Note: Note the following:

  • You can only select active clients in the Client ID field.

  • If a Per Active Employee Per Month (PAEPM) rule is already active for a client, you cannot import another active PAEPM rule for that client. (A warning displays if you try to import another PAEPM rule using the same rule dates, which would make them active at the same time.)

  • If you enter an inactive client or a client that you are not allowed to access the following error message displays, “Invalid Client ID.”

Adding New Rules to an Import

Using the import process, you can define new rules that the system adds to the Billing Rules (Unbundled) form. To do this, you must enter the rule as NEW. For example:

  • Row 1 - NEW: Contains all the rule details and all the multi-value details associated using a pipe delimiter

  • Row 2 - NEW: Contains all the rule details and all the multi-value details associated using a pipe delimiter

Note: Note the following:

  • Rules display one row after another using sequential numbers. Therefore, do not use a numeric value after each row.

  • If there are any errors, they display in the error report. (You can view errors by clicking Error Report.)

Define the following information for the import:

Field Details Description
Client ID Unique identifier for the client.
Rule This field is pre-defined. Note: If you create a NEW rule, the next sequential value is selected. Existing Billing Rule ID, or New Rule to create a new unbundled billing rule. The system automatically assigns an ID.
Rule Description This is a free-form field where you can enter the description. Describes the rule. (This description cannot exceed 40 characters.)
Rate Allows numeric value up to 4 decimal places. Billing Rate. The system uses this in conjunction with the Based On value.
Based On Codes used as basis for calculating unbundled billing rules. Based On value, which represents the logic to use when calculating the rate.
Rule Start Date Date format MM/DD/YYYY. Rule Start Date when this rule begins.
Rule End Date Date format MM/DD/YYYY. Rule End Date when this rule ends.
Voucher Types Allowed types: - R: Regular - V: Vacation - S: Supplemental - A: Arrearage - H: Adjustment > Note: Note: - If only Regular applies, use R. - If all types apply, use RVSHA. Voucher Types to which a billing rule applies.

  • M: Manual
  • If only Regular applies, use R.

Note: Obsolete types are not allowed. | Employee Type to which this billing rule applies, if any. For example, FT is a full time employee. | | Pay Group | Can vary by client (W, BW, and so on). Setup: Payroll | Change | Pay Groups. | Pay Group to which this billing rule applies, if any. When you update an existing rule in the Unbundled Billing Rules Import form, the import must identify the rule number being updated and include details that for the updated rule. For example, Rule 1 defines Pay Group A. If the updated rule then lists Rule 1 as Pay Group B, after the import finishes Rule 1 now uses Pay Group B.

After you import the updated rule, you can view the Transaction Report to determine which values were imported. (You can view errors by clicking Error Report.)

Note: Note the following:

  • Anything included in the file updates the current rule.

  • Running the import updates the rule or adds to the rule depending on the fields completed in the file.

  • Using a blank field removes any existing data. (If you only want to change one field, then you should download the rule, make the update to that field, and then re-import.)

To add form access to user roles in bulk:

  1. Open the User Roles form by clicking [Image: screenshot] (Back Office) and locating the form name under System|Change.

  2. Open the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] and select Bulk Role Update. The Bulk Role Update form displays.

  3. Click Form to view a list of all available forms and select a form name, or enter the desired form name (for example, BILLING.CODES*MAINT).

Maintaining User Roles

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/User_Role_Maintenance.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/User_Role_Maintenance.htm

Maintaining User Roles

User Role Maintenance lists the forms and features that are not currently associated with the role. You can add any of these forms to a user role by clicking Add in the User Roles form.

Forms may not display in the list for the following reasons:

  • Added recently to PrismHR

  • Not added to the role

  • Removed from the role.

Note: Note: Forms with the word details in the Description sometimes apply only to the first tabs of Employee Details (Name) and Client Details (Detail), not all tabs in the forms. Each tab has its own security setting. For example, Employee Work (EMPLOYEE.PER*MAINT.WORK) is the Work tab in Employee Details.

  1. Use Type Filter to limit to forms of a specific type.

  2. To select forms:

  • Choose Select All to add all forms visible in the list. Deselect the option to deselect all forms.

  • Check Select next to each form to select or deselect it.

  1. Click Accept. All selected forms are added to the user role.

  2. Click Save in the User Roles form.
