Defining User Roles

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/User_Roles.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/User_Roles.htm

Defining User Roles

Define the forms and fields in PrismHR that users with a specific role can access on the User Roles form. Provide either full access to a form (including editing form data) or read-only access. Your organization should have a well-planned strategy for applying role-based security.

Using the Actions Menu

From the Actions menu:

  • Select the option to create, copy, or delete a user role.

  • Control document management access (upload, delete, move, rename, and other updates) for your Service Providers, Worksite Trusted Advisors, and Worksite Managers. To access these settings, select a role ID and click Document Security (See Maintaining Document Security). See Viewing the Audit Log for information on the Audit function.

Note: Note: The User Report and the User Roles Report (available from theReports menu) display valuable information about how users and user roles are currently set up.

Viewing Role Information

Enter the Role ID or click the field title and select the role from a list. The form populates with specific information on that role.

Filtering Form Types

Filter the form access list by form Type by selecting an option from the Type Filter field. For example, select Payroll to view payroll-related forms.

Obsoleting a User Role

Obsolete a user role that is no longer in use by enabling Obsolete. (Selecting Role ID displays the User Role Search list, where the Obsolete column indicates whether the user role is obsolete (Y) or not obsolete (N).)

Note: Note the following:

  • You cannot assign an obsoleted role to a user or obsolete a user role that is currently assigned to active users. If this occurs an error message displays, “This role must be removed from all active users before it can be obsoleted!”

  • Once a user role is obsolete, you cannot manually enter an obsoleted role for a user.

Searching for Forms

Search for a particular form in the list by entering a query in the Search for Description field.

User Role Tasks

You can perform a variety of tasks on the User Roles form and itsActions menu

[Image: screenshot]

:

  • Creating a New Role

  • Editing a User Role

  • Copying a User Role

  • Deleting a Role

  • Maintaining Document Security

========================================================================

Copying a User Role

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/User_Roles_Copy.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/User_Roles_Copy.htm

Copying a User Role

Create a new user role based on an existing one with the Role Copy form.

Note: Note: The new role will be identical to the role you copied, except for its Role ID and Description.

  1. Select the Role ID of the role you want to copy. The list includes all user types, both service providers and worksite managers. Be sure that you know the name of the role you want to copy.

  2. Enter a new Copy To Role ID. The role ID should indicate its purpose (for example, BENADM).

  3. Enter a Description that clearly describes its purpose ( for example, Benefits Administrator).

  4. Click Save.

========================================================================

Deleting a Role

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/User_Roles_Delete.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/User_Roles_Delete.htm

Deleting a Role

Delete an existing user role with the Role Delete form.

Note: Note: You cannot delete any roles that have users associated with them.

To delete a user role:

  1. Select Delete Role from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] in User Roles.

  2. Select a Role ID from Role ID to Delete.

  3. Click Delete. A pop-up window opens.

  4. The system checks to see whether the user role is associated with any user accounts:

  • If not, click Yes to confirm that you want to delete the user role.

  • If one or more accounts are assigned to the user role, the system displays a message: “This role must be removed from all users before it can be deleted!” You can see what users have what roles with the User Report.

Editing a User Role

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/User_Roles_Edit.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/User_Roles_Edit.htm

Editing a User Role

Edit new and existing user roles directly from the User Roles form. When you finish editing information on the form, click Save.

Adding and Removing Forms

You can add and remove forms as needed:

  • Click Add to add form access and to select that form in User Role Maintenance. For more information, see Maintaining User Roles.

  • Click Remove [Image: screenshot] to remove form access from a role.

Changing User Access to a Form

Configure user access to a form by selecting the text in the Access column until the correct setting displays. There are three access settings:

  • Full: Users can view and edit information but cannot see fields that are denied in the field-level security settings.

  • Inquiry: Users can view information but cannot edit the form.

  • Deny: Users cannot see the form.

Note: Note: If one role permits access to a feature and another role prohibits access, the system denies access in both instances. Avoid this by removing the denied form from that user role. If one role permits access and the other role does not include the feature, the user will have appropriate access.

Configuring Field-Level Access

Select the Field option in the Security column to set field-level access to a form. This only applies to certain forms. For more information, see Configuring Field Security.

========================================================================

Configuring Field Security

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/User_Roles_Field_Security.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/User_Roles_Field_Security.htm

Configuring Field Security

Your organization can set field-level security for some forms, as indicated in the Security column of the User Roles form. Some fields are required by the system and cannot be customized.

  • Field indicates that field-level security is available.

  • Field Set indicates that security is established for the form.

Setting Field Security

To access field security for a form:

  1. Click Field or Field Set in the Security column on User Roles. The Field Security Maintenance form opens.

Note: Note: If no fields display, field-level security is not set up.

  1. Locate the permission you want to configure, and set Permissions by clicking the link until one of the following displays:

  • Enable: Users can edit the field

  • Disable: Users cannot edit the field.

  • Hidden: Users will not see the field (available for certain fields).

  1. Select Y (required) or N (not required) in the Required column. Only enabled fields can be set to required.

  2. When you are finished, click Save.

  3. Click Save in the User Roles form.

A service provider can hide fields that are required by Worksite Managers or Worksite Trusted Advisors. In these cases, a message displays to warn you that hiding a required field could prevent the user from saving the form.

Adding Fields for Security

To require security for a field:

  1. Click Add on the Field Security Maintenance form. This opens the Field Security Selection form, which lists fields without security.

  2. Click Select next to the field that requires security.

  3. Click Accept. The Field Security Maintenance form displays again.

  4. Locate the permission you want to configure, and set Permissions by clicking the link until one of the following displays:

  • Enable: Users can edit the field

  • Disable: Users cannot edit the field.

  • Hidden: Users will not see the field (available for certain fields).

  1. Select Y (required) or N (not required) in the Required column. Only enabled fields can be set to required.

  2. When you are finished, click Save.

  3. Click Save in the User Roles form.

Note: Note: If a user has two roles with different field security settings, the system honors the settings for the first role assigned to the account. The administrator must take this into consideration when designing and assigning roles.

Creating a New Role

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/User_Roles_New.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/User_Roles_New.htm

Creating a New Role

Create and configure new user roles with the Role Maintenance form.

Note: You cannot use a different case structure of an existing Role when creating or copying a new user role. For example, you cannot create the user role glsp if the user role GLSP already exists. If you try to create or copy a new user role using an existing role but with a different case structure, an error message displays.

To create a new user role:

  1. Enter a unique Role ID that briefly indicates its purpose (for example, PAYPROC).

  2. Enter a role Description that clearly describes its purpose (for example, Payroll Processor).

  3. Select a User Type:

  • Service Provider: PEO employee or other user at an organization.

  • Worksite Manager: Manager for a client, or trusted worksite advisors.

  1. Click Save to create the new user role.

Note: Note: By default, no forms are assigned to the role.

Defining Users

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Users.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Users.htm

Defining Users

You can define user access to clients and system features on the Users form. Also, you can copy or delete existing user accounts, view a user’s login history, and set other information on this form.

Note: Note: Service providers whose user role provides access to the Users form can also access this form by selecting the User Record option on the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

in the Employee Details form.

PrismHR users are one of the following types:

  • Service Provider: PEO employee or other user at your organization.

  • Worksite Manager: Manager for a client.

  • Worksite Employee: Employee for a client.

  • Worksite Trusted Advisor: User who works for one or more clients, and is not necessarily an employee.

  • I-9 Approver: User that secures who can approve I-9 Section 2.

  • Pay Card Account Approver: User that secures who can enter Pay Card account numbers.

  • Employee Manager (Leave Request only): User who has access to direct employees listed in the Reports To field on the employee record.

  • PTO Administrator: User who has access to the full list of Planned Time Off Requests.

  • Worksite Manager Proxy: User who can proxy into the system as a worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor by selecting the Worksite Manager Proxy option on the Actions menu. (See Defining the Worksite Manager/Trusted Advisor Proxy Role for Service Providers.)

  • Employee Portal Proxy: Provides user with read-only access to employees’ Employee Portal records by selecting Employee Portal Proxy in the Account Management Roles panel (service providers only). (Note: The system bypasses any field-level security when using this role.)

  • Enrollment Proxy: User who can act as an employee and execute the employee’s enrollment selections (Benefits Enrollment only).

  • Onboarding Proxy: Provides user with read-only access to employees’ full onboarding workflows by selecting Onboarding Proxy in the Account Management Roles panel (service providers only) or in the Human Resource Roles panel (worksite managers/worksite trusted advisors only). (Note: The system bypasses any field-level security when using this role.)

  • Benefits Approver: User who can approve benefits-related actions for clients assigned in Data Security (Benefits Enrollment only).

  • Client Manager: User who can receive notifications (make this assignment in the Notifications Recipients form).

  • Direct Deposit Approver: User who can approve direct deposit updates stored in the employee details record.

Note: You can only assign this role to service providers.

To do this Perform these steps
Create a user See Creating a New User
Copy a user See Copying a User
Edit a user After entering a user’s basic information, your next steps depend on the type of user you need to create. Click a link below to read the topic that covers the relevant user type, and then proceed to step 3 within those topics: - Editing a Service Provider User - Editing a Worksite Manager User - Editing a Worksite Trusted Advisor - Editing a Worksite Employee User
  • Editing a Service Provider User
  • Editing a Worksite Manager User
  • Editing a Worksite Trusted Advisor
  • Editing a Worksite Employee User | Delete a user | See Deleting a User | | Record commission details | Service providers who are set up with the Sales Representative role in the Account Management Roles panel can use the Commission Details option on the Actions menu. Selecting Commission Details opens a form where you can record the Client ID and Employee Identifier. (This information helps the system capture additional salesperson details to create an import pay file.) Note: To begin using this form, you must first add it to the user role(s). (See Defining User Roles.) | ========================================================================

Changing the User Type

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Changing_User_Type.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Changing_User_Type.htm

Changing the User Type

You can use the Users form to change a Worksite Employee user to a Worksite Manager, or a Worksite Manager user to a Worksite Employee.

To change a user from one type to the other:

  1. Open the user account on the Users form.

  2. Open the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] and select Change to a Worksite Manager or Change to a Worksite Employee.

  3. Click Yes in the confirmation message.

  4. The User Type field changes.

  • If you changed an employee to a manager, the User Roles, Human Resource Roles, and Current Access panels display. Enter the appropriate information in those fields. You can also set Data Security at this time.

  • If you changed a manager to an employee, only the fields related to employee user accounts display, and the system deletes the Data Security information. Make edits as needed.

  1. Click Save.

Copying a User

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Copying_Users.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Copying_Users.htm

Copying a User

Copy an existing user account to create a new one with the same or similar access privileges.

To copy a user, do the following:

  1. Open the Actions menu and select Copy User. The User Copy form opens.

  2. Enter or select the User ID of the user you want to copy.

For worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors, you can copy clients, client access, and data security entities to a new user ID by selecting the Copy all client and data security settings field, which displays when you enter a user ID or select one in the Search users list. After selecting this field, a confirmation message displays, “This will copy over all client access and data security settings from the existing user to the new user. Do you want to continue?” Click Yes to continue. (Clicking No closes the message and returns to the User Copy form, where the field is now unchecked.)

  1. Enter the User ID of the new user.

  2. Click Save.

Creating a New User

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Creating_New_User.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Creating_New_User.htm

Creating a New User

Create a new user directly from the Users form. This procedure describes the steps common to all PrismHR user types.

To create a new user, do the following:

  1. Enter a unique User ID and press Tab. User IDs may not contain special characters such as slashes, brackets, apostrophes, or other symbols.

Note: Note: If there is an existing user with this ID, the user account information displays. Click Cancel and enter a different User ID. Select the User ID link to view existing IDs exist to help avoid creating a duplicate ID. In the Search users list that displays, select the User Type and the Status. The field defaults, All User Types and All, allow you to search Active and Disabled user records for all user types.

  1. Select the User Type. The Users form displays the fields and panels appropriate to that type of user. (Note: After selecting the Service Provider, Worksite Manager, or Worksite Trusted Advisor option from the User Type field, the sMFA Device Expiration setting automatically defaults to 30 Days.)

Note: Note the following:

  • Service providers can create worksite managers even if the employee is not associated with the active client.

  • The system displays a warning when you create a new worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor with No Access set for their Data Security access if the client is set to No Access for its Default Access and Default Access when Blank settings on the Client Security form. Click Yes to confirm the user will not have access to any employees for this client. (Select the user’s security settings by selecting Data Security on the Actions menu.)

  1. Enter the user’s full Name.

  2. Enter the user’s initial Password. This can be changed later.

  3. Enter the user’s primary Email Address. The system uses this for communications such as password resets.

Note: Note the following:

  • You cannot enter an invalid character in this field. For example, if you enter a left bracket ([) in the user name segment in this field and then move away from the field an error message displays, “Email address cannot contain illegal character: [.” (Note: The system does not remove the invalid character, so you need to make the correction.)

  • If you try to save an email address that contains an invalid character, the system disables the save function and an error message displays.

  1. (Optional) Enter the user’s Mobile Phone number.

  2. Enter the user’s Notification Email.

Establishing User Data Security

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Data_Security.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Data_Security.htm

Establishing User Data Security

You can establish security for worksite manager and worksite trusted advisor users to specify the user’s access to companies, divisions, departments, locations, shifts, and so on.

[Image: screenshot]

The following chart displays a high-level overview of the Data Security access hierarchy:

[Image: screenshot]

To establish security:

  1. While editing the user account in the Users form, open the Actions menu and select Data Security. The Data Security window opens.

  2. Maintain the companies that the user can access:

  • To add access to a client:

  1. — Click Add Company and then select the client the user can access. Typically, this is the client that employs the user. The Access is set to Pending.

  2. — Return to the Users form to select the employee ID. If you select an employee that is employed by the client, then the Access changes to Granted.

  • For clients already assigned to the user, the access you can set depends on whether the user is employed by that client. If the user is, then you can set the access to Granted or a thru date, otherwise you can set only a thru date.

  • To change from Granted or Pending to a thru date:

i. Click the link.
ii. Enter the Optional Override Access Thru date.
— —
  1. — Click Submit. The user’s access to the client expires after 11:59:59 p.m. on that date (Central Time).
  • To change from a thru date to Granted:
i. Click the link.
ii. Delete the Optional Override Access Thru date.
— —
iii. Click Submit. The access is set to Granted.
— —
  • To remove access completely, click the Delete icon [Image: screenshot] in the company row.
  1. Configure a user’s Data Security access hierarchy by setting one of the following options in the Security by field:

  • Entity (default): User is granted access to all entries.

  • Manager Direct Reports: User is only granted access to their direct reports.

  • Manager Full Hierarchy: User is granted access to their direct reports and any employees that are assigned to or inherited by their direct reports.

  • PTO Approver Direct Reports: User is only granted access to their direct reports.

  • PTO Approver Full Hierarchy: User is granted access to their direct reports and any employees that are assigned to or inherited by their direct reports.

Note: The Security by field is available for service providers with access to configure a worksite manager’s (WSM) Data Security.

  1. The entities are for the selected client and are set in Client Details. Using the drop-down, you can choose to show All Defined Entities or limit the list to specific entities.

  • To configure access for entries in the All Defined Entities table, ensure that you set the Security by field to Entity.

  • If you select options other than Entity, the table displays the list of employees that are directly related to the selected data security option in read-only format.

  1. For each defined entity, you can set the access by clicking the row:

  • Full Access: User can view, edit, and save data.

  • No Access: User cannot see any information associated with the entity.

  1. When you are finished, click Save. You return to the Users form where you can complete the necessary steps for editing the user.

Deleting a User

Use the delete function to permanently remove a user from the system.

Editing a Worksite Employee User

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Editing_Employee.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Editing_Employee.htm

Editing a Worksite Employee User

Worksite Employees are workers at client locations. The Worksite Employee form provides access to Employee Portal (EP).

To set up basic employee information:

  1. Enter or select the User ID. The Users form displays the information for the Worksite Employee.

  2. Select Worksite Employee from the User Type drop-down menu.

  3. Update the user’s First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Mobile Phone, Notifications Email, or Registration Email, if required.

Note: You cannot edit the Email Address after the first time the record is saved. If the user updates his or her primary email address through Employee Portal (EP) or through the Employee DetailsAddress tab, the system displays that in the Email Address field.

  1. Enter the Employee ID to link the user account to the appropriate employee record.

  2. You can include a photo of the user. Mouse over the image and then select Upload to add an image, or select Delete to remove an existing image.

  3. Click Save.

Worksite Employee Settings

Configure these optional settings to control employee password, multi-factor authentication, and activity behavior.

Field — Description

Active User — Deselect if you want to remove system access for this user without deleting their user record.

Requires New Password — Select this option to prompt the user for a new password the next time they log in. This feature works even if passwords are set to never expire on the Authentication Services form.

Logging Enabled — Do not select this option unless you know it is necessary, as it adds overhead and slows the system. This option enables back end logging to assist with troubleshooting.

Last Changed On — This field displays the date and time of the most recent change to the user account.

sMFA Device Expiration — This field determines the amount of time until a user is prompted to verify their login using multi-factor authentication. You can use the global MFA setting for MFA expiration, select a different time interval, or disable it entirely. PrismHR highly recommends that you do not disable MFA expiration. See the previous warning.

Setting User Details (PrismONE ID)

Configure these settings to control the user’s registration with PrismONE ID.

Field — Description

Registration Status — This field displays the user’s PrismONE registration status.

Registration Email — Enter the user’s email address that is used as the registration message’s destination.

Require This Email for PrismONE ID — Select this option to require the user to use the Registration Email address for their PrismONE ID address.

Registration Code — This field displays the status of the PrismONE registration code sent to the user’s Registration Email.

Send Code via Mobile Phone — Select this option to send the registration code as an SMS/Text message.

Editing a Service Provider User

Configure accounts for the users who work for your organization with the Service Provider form.

Note: If an existing email address contains an invalid character and you do not remove it, when you click Save the system displays a warning message, but still allows you to save the information, “Warning! Email address cannot contain illegal character: ‘X’. It should be updated to a valid email address.” Click OK to save the other information in the form (the invalid email address remains in the field).

  1. Enter a Client Access Group. This determines the client companies that the user can access (See Defining Client Access Groups).

Setting User Details (Status and Password Recovery)

Configure these optional settings to control service provider password, multi-factor authentication, and activity behavior.

Important! For service provider users, sMFA Device Expiration is set to 30 days by default. For your organization’s security, disabling sMFA Device Expiration is highly discouraged.

Field — Description

Active User — Deselect to remove system access for this user without deleting their user record.

Requires New Password — Select this option to prompt the user for a new password the next time they log in. This feature works even if passwords are set to never expire on the Authentication Services form.

Logging Enabled — Do not select this option unless absolutely necessary, as it adds overhead and slows down the system. This option enables back-end logging to assist with troubleshooting.

Last Changed On — This field displays the date and time of the most recent change to the user account.

sMFA Device Expiration — This field determines the amount of time until a user is prompted to verify their login using multi-factor authentication. You can use the global MFA setting for MFA expiration, select a different time interval, or disable it entirely. PrismHR highly recommends that you do not disable MFA expiration. See the previous warning.

sMFA Support — This field determines if multi-factor authentication is supported for password recovery.

Birth Date — This field is used to enter the user’s birth date for use in password recovery.

ZIP Code — This field is used to enter the user’s ZIP code for use in password recovery.

Configure these settings to control the user’s registration with PrismONE ID.

Field — Description

Registration Status — This field displays the user’s PrismONE registration status.

Registration Email — Enter the user’s email address that is used as the registration message’s destination.

Require This Email for PrismONE ID — Select this option to require the user to use the Registration Email address for their PrismONE ID address.

Registration Code — This field displays the status of the PrismONE registration code sent to the user’s Registration Email.

Assigning User Roles

The User Roles panel maintains the roles that apply to this user. Each role determines what forms and fields a user can access.

  • Click the + button and then click Role ID to select and add the user role.

  • Click the x for that row to remove a role.

Note: Note: If a user is assigned more than one user role, and one role allows access to a feature while another denies it, the system does not allow the user to access the feature. This safeguards your organization’s information and that of your clients. Alternatively, if one role allows access and another role does not define access to the form, the user can access it.

Note: Note: If a user has two roles with different field security settings, the system honors the settings for the first role assigned to the account. The administrator must take this into consideration when designing and assigning roles.

Note: Note: A warning message displays on the User Role form if the following occurs:

  • A user who has access to the Transfer Downloads File to PC menu is switched to a new User Role BUT,

  • is also restricted from clients via client access security.

The message states:

The user role has access to the Transfer Downloads File to PC menu. This form does not utilize client access group security so it is possible that maybe be able to download files that contain data they should not be allowed to access. Do you wish to continue?

  • If Yes is selected, then user record is saved, and the screen is cleared.

  • If No is selected, then user record is not saved, and the data is left as is on the screen.

Setting Account Management Roles

Account Management roles determine what the user can do in PrismHR.

Setting Client-Related Roles

These roles determine what actions the user can perform, and what assignments they can have in the Client Details Account tab.

Note: Note the following:

  • If your organization separates the print and ship function from the payroll processing function, you can choose one of the Payroll Processor roles. Otherwise, use the Payroll Representative role. See Setting Global Configuration to learn about separating the functions.

  • If the user is a Payroll Representative or Payroll Processor, you can Suppress Payroll Validations. The system does not perform the selected validations or display the selected warnings for that user. See Validating the Payroll Process to learn about each of the validations.

Account Management Role Details
Benefits Representative The user can be assigned as a Benefits representative. (This user can also approve benefit-related actions for clients in the assigned Client Access Group.)
Billing Representative The user who can approve ACH Billing threshold approvals for global-level and client-level approval policies. Users can set the Billing Representative Account Management Role as follows: - Users with Full access to the Users form can set up a service provider user with the Billing Representative A/M Role, so they can approve ACH Billing threshold approvals. - Users with Full access to the Global Approval Policies form can create an approval policy and assign Billing Representative to the A/M Role. When the approval policy is triggered, a user with the Billing Representative A/M Role can successfully approve the action. - Users with Full access to the Approval Policies form can create a client-level approval policy and assign Billing Representative to the A/M Role. When the approval policy is triggered, a user with the Billing Representative A/M Role can successfully approve the action.
  • Users with Full access to the Users form can set up a service provider user with the Billing Representative A/M Role, so they can approve ACH Billing threshold approvals.
  • Users with Full access to the Global Approval Policies form can create an approval policy and assign Billing Representative to the A/M Role. When the approval policy is triggered, a user with the Billing Representative A/M Role can successfully approve the action.
  • Users with Full access to the Approval Policies form can create a client-level approval policy and assign Billing Representative to the A/M Role. Account Management Role — Details

Service Provider User Administrator — This role allows the service provider user to make changes to other service provider user accounts.

Worksite User Administrator — This role allows the service provider user to make changes to worksite manager, worksite trusted advisor, and employee user accounts.

Report Center User Administrator — This role allows the service provider to access the field-level Security Administration page in the Report Center, which grants access to Report Center administrator rights.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Editing_Users.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Editing_Users.htm

Editing a User

Edit an existing user to configure that user as one of the user types.

To edit a user:

  1. Enter the User ID of the user you want to edit.

  2. Follow the edit user type instructions in the appropriate topic (See Defining Users).

This section discusses:

========================================================================

Editing a Worksite Trusted Advisor

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Editing_WSA_User.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Editing_WSA_User.htm

Editing a Worksite Trusted Advisor

Worksite Trusted Advisors work for one or more clients but are not necessarily employees of those clients. These are typically consultants who are expected to view information but not perform actions like those done by a service provider or worksite manager.

Use the Worksite Trusted Advisor form to edit settings for these users.

To set up a worksite trusted advisor:

  1. Enter the User ID. The Users form displays the information for the worksite trusted advisor.

  2. Select Worksite Trusted Advisor from the User Type drop-down menu.

  3. Update the user’s First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Mobile Phone, Notifications Email, or Registration Email, if required.

Note: If an existing email address contains an invalid character and you do not remove it, when you click Save the system displays a warning message, but still allows you to save the information, “Warning! Email address cannot contain illegal character: ‘X’. It should be updated to a valid email address.” Click OK to save the other information in the form (the invalid email address remains in the field).

  1. You can include a photo of the user. Mouse over the image and then select Upload to add an image, or select Delete to remove an existing image.

  2. Click Save.

Configuring Data Security

Manage data and client security for the user account by opening the Actions menu and selecting Data Security. The Data Security form opens.

[Image: screenshot]

To add companies that the user can access:

  1. Click Add Company and then select the client the user can access. Typically, this is the client that employs the user. Access is set to Pending.

  2. Click Save to return to the Users form to select the employee ID. If you select an employee that is employed by the client, Access changes to Granted. If the employee is not employed by the client, the status remains Pending.

Note: Note: For clients already assigned to the user, the access you can set depends on whether the user is employed by that client. If so, set the access to Granted or a thru date, otherwise you can set only a thru date.

To change from Granted or Pending to a thru date:

  1. Click the link.

  2. Enter the Optional Override Access Thru date.

  3. Click Submit. The user’s access to the client expires after 11:59:59 p.m. on that date (Central Time).

To change from a thru date to Granted:

  1. Click the link.

  2. Delete the Optional Override Access Thru date.

  3. Click Submit. The access is set to Granted.

To remove access completely, click Delete

[Image: screenshot]

in the company row.

Displayed entities are specific to the selected client and are set in Client Details. Using the drop-down, you can show All Defined Entities or limit the list to specific entities.

Note: Note: See Managing Client Security Settings to learn about defining entities for a client.

For each entity, you can set the access by clicking the row:

  • Full Access: User can view, edit, and save data.

  • No Access: User cannot see any data associated with the entity.

When you are finished, click Save. You return to the Users form where you can complete the necessary steps for

editing the user.

Worksite Trusted Advisor Settings

Configure these optional settings to control worksite trusted advisor password, multi-factor authentication, and activity behavior.

Field — Description

Active User — Deselect to remove system access for this user without deleting their user record.

Requires New Password — Select this option to prompt the user for a new password the next time they log in. This feature works even if passwords are set to never expire on the Authentication Services form.

Logging Enabled — Do not select this option unless absolutely necessary, as it adds overhead and slows down the system. This option enables back-end logging to assist with troubleshooting.

Last Changed On — This field displays the date and time of the most recent change to the user account.

sMFA Device Expiration — This field determines the amount of time until a user is prompted to verify their login using multi-factor authentication. You can use the global MFA setting for MFA expiration, select a different time interval, or disable it entirely. PrismHR highly recommends that you do not disable MFA expiration. See the previous warning.

Birth Date and ZIP Code — The system uses these fields during password recovery to verify a user’s identity.

Note: Note: Password recovery always requires message templates for Password Reset and Password Reset Confirmation. If you are also using sMFA Support, it requires a message template for MFA Passcode.

Setting User Details (PrismONE ID)

Configure these settings to control the user’s registration with PrismONE ID.

Field — Description

Registration Status — This field displays the user’s PrismONE registration status.

Registration Email — Enter the user’s email address that is used as the registration message’s destination.

Require This Email for PrismONE ID — Select this option to require the user to use the Registration Email address for their PrismONE ID address.

Registration Code — This field displays the status of the PrismONE registration code sent to the user’s Registration Email.

Send Code via Mobile Phone — Select this option to send the registration code as an SMS/Text message.

Assigning User Roles

Maintain the user roles that apply to this user with the User Roles panel. Each role determines what forms and fields the user can access.

  • Click + to add a new role and then click Role ID to select the User Role.

  • Click x to remove a role for that row.

Note: Note: If a user is assigned more than one user role, and one allows access to a feature while another denies it, then the system does not allow the user to access the feature. This is to ensure the security of your organization’s information and that of your clients. If instead one role allows access and another role has simply removed it, the users can access it.

If a user has two roles with different field security settings, the system honors the settings for the first role assigned to the account. The administrator must take this into consideration when designing and assigning roles.

You can also select the Human Resource Roles for this user.

Human Resource Roles

Human Resource roles determine what the user can do in PrismHR. The user can only perform actions for client companies assigned in Data Security.

Note: Note the following:

  • The Payroll Processor can perform all payroll tasks.

  • If your organization separates the time sheet entry and check printing tasks, you should assign some worksite users as Time Sheet Entry types and other users as Payroll - Prints Checks and Payroll - Print Garnishment Checks.

Human Resource Role — Details

Employee’s Manager (Leave Request Only) — User can approve employee leave requests.

H/R Action Approver — User can approve human resource actions for clients assigned in Data Security.

Payroll Approver — User can approve payroll-related actions for clients assigned in Data Security.

Payroll Processor — User can process payroll information for clients assigned in Data Security. (Applies to Portal Time Sheet Entry.)

Time Sheet Entry (w/ Pay Rates) — User can enter time sheet data, including pay rates. (Applies to Portal Time Sheet Entry.)

Time Sheet Entry (w/o Pay Rates) — User can enter time sheet hours, but cannot see or enter pay rate information. (Applies to PrismHR Core and Portal Time Sheet Entry.)

Payroll - Prints Checks — User can view and print regular paychecks. Note: If a user’s role is only set to the Payroll - Prints Checks role, they cannot print garnishment paychecks.

Payroll - Print Garnishment Checks — User can view and print garnishment paychecks. Note: If a user’s role is only set to the Payroll - Print Garnishment Checks role, they cannot print regular paychecks.

Enrollment Proxy — User can act as an employee and execute the employee’s enrollment selections. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

Onboarding Proxy — User can read employees’ full onboarding workflows. (Note: The system bypasses any field-level security when using this role.)

Benefits Approver — User can approve benefits-related actions for clients assigned in Data Security. (PrismHR Benefits Enrollment only.)

PTO Administrator — User can see all employees in the Planned Time Off Requests form, regardless of whether they are restricted by Data Security settings, not only direct reports.

Client Manager — User can be assigned to receive notifications in the Notification Recipients form.

I-9 Approver — User can approve Form I-9s for employees during the onboarding process.

Pay Card Account Approver — User can approve pending pay card account approvals.

Manager User Setup — Worksite managers can set up other worksite managers.

Custom HR role (defined by your organization)— If your organization has defined custom human resources roles using the Custom HR Approval Roles form, you can add them to the user. These roles are for customizing global or client-specific approval policies.

Setting Client Device IP Range

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Setting_Client_Device_IP_Range.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Users_Setting_Client_Device_IP_Range.htm

Setting Client Device IP Range

Restrict a user to a specific IP address or range of addresses using the Client Device IP Range form, which you can access on the Actions menu in the Users form. For example, you can grant users access only at a specific location, such as an office or home.

To set a client device IP range:

  1. Select Client Device IP Range from the Actions menu on the Users form. The IP Restrictions form opens.

  2. Enter each Acceptable IP Address Range. Users can only access anything IP addresses or ranges in the list.

  3. Click Close.

  4. Click Save in the Users form.

Examples

In this example, the user can only access PrismHR from the listed IP addresses (123.123.123.101, 123.123.123.102, and 123.123.123.103).

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: Your organization can also specify a range of permitted IP addresses.

In this example, the user can only access PrismHR from IP addresses that begin with 123.123.123.

[Image: screenshot]

In this example, the user can only access the system from IP addresses in the range (123.123.123.100, 123.123.123.101, 123.123.123.102, and so on).

If you enter a range, you must separate the first and last addresses with a dash and the first three numbers must match. The system will ignore it if the first three numbers are different.

[Image: screenshot]

Set the default printers available to a user for specific items by selecting Printer Setup from the Actions menu in the Users form.

  2. Select the Default Code, which is the type of item to print on the printer (for example, Reports).

  3. Click Accept.

  4. Click Save in the Users form.

Using Tables

You enter some information in tables.

Defining W/C Classification Rates

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/WC_Classification_Rates.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/WC_Classification_Rates.htm

Defining W/C Classification Rates

You can use the W/C Classification Rates form to maintain workers’ compensation classification rate information. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: Click the Data Import Tool icon (

[Image: The Data Import Tool icon.]

) to import W/C rates at the system level. (See the Payroll Administration Guide for more information about using the Global W/C Classification Rates Import Template option to perform this import.)

To define workers’ compensation classification rate information, do the following:

  1. Go to the W/C Classification Rates form and complete the following fields:
Field Description
Rate Template Select the Rate Template.
State Select the State.
Effective Date Enter a new Effective Date for this rate template, or select an existing date from the table at the right.
Time sheet based WC tax calculations Only for the State of Washington, this field will appear. This field is a checkbox which is unchecked by default. - Not checked (default) - Payroll programs calculate the Washington State Workers’ Compensation (WC) tax using standard Vertex processing - Checked - When checked: 1. Employee Payroll Vouchers store the following data based on the timesheet positions used in the payroll: \ a. \ WC Hours by position WC Class \ \ — \ — \ \ b. \ EE Charged WC Tax Rate \ \ — \ — \ \ c. \ ER Charged WC Tax Rate \ \ — \ — \ 2. Stored EE Charged WC Tax Rate and ER Charged WC Tax Rate honor the following logical criteria: a. — For exempt/salaried employees only: caps WC hours to 160 hours worked/month for tax calculation purposes b. — Uses the EE and ER Tax rates related to the WC Class code implicated by the time sheet level positions (not the employee’s assigned position) c. — For employees with more than 1 WC class codes on a given charge date, the EE and ER Tax rates reflect the highest Rate for the date, applied to all hours reported on the charge date
  • Not checked (default) - Payroll programs calculate the Washington State Workers’ Compensation (WC) tax using standard Vertex processing

Defining W/C Classifications

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/WC_Classifications.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/WC_Classifications.htm

Defining W/C Classifications

Use the W/C Classifications form to define the workers’ compensation class information for a state.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: Click the Import icon (

[Image: screenshot]

) to import W/C codes and descriptions by state or to import multiple rate templates and effective dates all at once. (See the Payroll Administration Guide for more information about using the Global W/C Classifications Import Template option to perform this import.)

To define workers’ compensation class information for a state, do the following:

  1. Enter the two-character State code where this workers’ compensation classification applies.

  2. Enter the workers’ compensation Class Code used by the state for this classification. To enter a sub-class code, precede it with a period.

  3. Enter a Class Description for this classification.

  4. Select Ohio Construction Class if the classification pertains to a construction trade class in Ohio. The system uses this in the Ohio Weekly Construction Cap calculation.

  5. Click Save.

Establishing Workers’ Compensation Insurance Policy and Carrier Information

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/WC_Policies.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/WC_Policies.htm

Establishing Workers’ Compensation Insurance Policy and Carrier Information

If your organization services clients with employees in various states, be sure to use the correct workers’ compensation (W/C) policies for each state where you do business. Use the W/C Policies form to establish workers’ compensation insurance policy and carrier information.

Policy Information

Use the Policy Information panel to maintain basic information about the W/C insurance policy.

Field — Description

Policy ID — Workers’ compensation insurance policy ID.

Description — Description of the insurance policy.

Policy Start Date — Date when coverage begins under this policy. This is the beginning of the policy year.

Policy Type — Select Primary if the policy is maintained by the PEO. Select Individual if the policy is carried by the client.

Rate Template ID — If you use a table-based approach for maintaining W/C insurance rates, enter the appropriate rate template ID.

Suppress Billing — Select this option to suppress billing in cases where the client pays the policy premiums.

Suppress G/L Accrual — Select this option to suppress the generation of a general ledger account for any pay associated with this policy.

Company Mod/Discount — Select this option to use client-level W/C accrual modifiers when calculating W/C liability for this policy.

Use Company Level Override Rates — Select this option to use the rate overrides set at the client level.

Suppress TRIA Premium — Select this option to suppress the calculation of the state-based terrorism risk insurance act premium.

Suppress Shelter for Billing — Select this option to bill on gross W/C taxable wages in states that allow Section 125 to shelter W/C wages.

Carrier Information

Use the Carrier Information panel to establish the W/C insurance carrier information for this policy, including:

  • Carrier ID

  • Carrier Name, Address, City, State, and ZIP Code

  • Carrier Phone Number

  • Worker’s compensation insurance Policy Number assigned by the carrier

  • Whether worker’s compensation is Self-Insured

  • Self-Insure Certificate Number for consent to self-insure

Establishing Workers’ Compensation Rate Templates

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/WC_Rate_Templates.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/WC_Rate_Templates.htm

Establishing Workers’ Compensation Rate Templates

Use the W/C Rate Templates form to establish workers’ compensation rate templates in PrismHR.

To set up a template:

  1. Enter the unique Template ID.

  2. Enter a descriptive Template Name.

  3. Click Save.

Your organization can use templates to group multiple W/C classification rates. This is useful when you want to offer different rate tiers to your clients, for example, “Good”, “Better”, and “Best”. Then, in the W/C Classification Rates form, you could use the “Good” template to set the classification rate for MA.8810 to 2.00, and the “Better” template to set a rate of 1.50. See Defining W/C Classification Rates.

Work Centers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Work%20Centers.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Work Centers.htm

Work Centers

Work Centers are groups of forms that let you complete related HR tasks such as Benefits, Compliance, Time Off (formerly PTO), or Taxes. Each Work Center provides a single location from which you can open the forms required to perform a specific task.

The Work Centers panel displays on the PrismHR Dashboard. You can also access Work Centers in the following ways:

  • Click Work Centers on the menu bar.

  • Click the PrismHR logo on the menu bar.

Navigating

The Work Centers panel is organized into categories from which you can select a specific type of processing. Let’s say you open the Quarterly Tax Processing Work Center from the Tax category.

Next, open the Employer Quarterly SUTA Tax Export link from the Government Exports heading. To return to the Quarterly Tax Processing page, you can click

[Image: screenshot]

in the header area of the form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Providing Access to Work Centers

Only Service Providers can access Work Centers. You must give users access to the Work Center form to enable them to see it on the home page or under the Work Center menus. You must also give access to each individual form that is located under a Work Center.

  • Work Center access must be given to any user who has access to forms in that Work Center. Work Centers to which a user does not have access are not shown on the dashboard.

  • A user who has access to a form but not to the Work Center where it is located can still access the form by searching.

  • Each Work Center displays, even if a user does not have access to any forms in it.

  • Client Access Group security is not used for Work Centers.

To assign Work Center access to a role:

  1. On the Back Office menu, select System|Change > User Roles.

  2. Select a Role ID.

  3. Click Add.

  4. Select the type and category for the Work Center, and then click Accept.

  5. Click Save.

Maintaining Zip Code Networks

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/ZIP_Code_Network_Maintenance.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/ZIP_Code_Network_Maintenance.htm

Maintaining Zip Code Networks

View or delete networks from a zip code with the ZIP Code Network Maintenance form.

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From System|Change, select Zip Codes.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter a five-digit ZIP Code for the location whose networks you want to view.

  2. Select Benefit Networks from the Actions menu [Image: screenshot] . This is only visible if the Zip Code has at least one network assigned to it. The ZIP Code Network Maintenance form opens and displays the networks associated with the selected location. [Image: screenshot]

  3. Remove a network from the location by clicking Network ID. An alert displays.

  4. Click Yes to confirm.

  5. Click Close.

Setting Up Zip Codes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Maintenance/System/Zip_Codes.htm Path: PD/Maintenance/System/Zip_Codes.htm

Setting Up Zip Codes

Create and maintain zip codes with the ZIP Codes form. Users can also view and delete networks from a zip code in the ZIP Code Network Maintenance form, accessed by selecting Benefit Networks in the Actions menu

[Image: screenshot]

(see Maintaining Zip Code Networks).

Note: Note: The ZIP Code must have at least one network assigned for this to be visible.

  1. Complete these fields as required.

Field — Description

Zip Code — A location’s five-digit zip code.

City/Town — Name of the location covered by the zip code. > Note: Note: City & State displays the combined information.

State — Two-character state code.

OR Transit Tax — Indicates the type of transit tax that applies to this zip code. Options include TriMet Transit District and Lane Transit District.

  1. Click Save.
